You’ll work on detection models for particle contamination, cosmetic defects, and closure
items.desc: Now Hiring: Data Scientist in high-tech scale-up Location: Delft, on-site At Luo, we build machines that automate quality inspections of medicine. In many pharmaceutical environments, people still spend hours manually checking products for particles, cosmetic defects, and packaging integrity issues. It’s tedious, and humans make mistakes. Our machines do this job more accurately, faster, and more consistently. The brains of our machines are the detection models: algorithms that decide in real time whether a product passes inspection. We’ve proven the technology works. Now we’re scaling, which means more clients, more applications, and higher accuracy. For that, we need someone who builds, improves, and pushes these models to the next level. Our office is located at YES!Delft, surrounded by dozens of other tech start-ups and scale-ups, right next to TU Delft. Much of the work happens hands-on, with our machines, test setups, and the teams around them. The Role We are looking for a Data Scientist who enjoys developing and optimizing machine learning models for real-world applications. Not just running models and reporting results, but understanding what has impact and executing what must be done to make it better. Most of the time, that is more than just re-training. You’ll work on detection models for particle contamination, cosmetic defects, and closure integrity problems. You stay on top of the latest developments in the field, translate them into concrete improvements, and ensure our models meet the strict requirements of the pharmaceutical industry. You work closely with the Software, Quality Support, and Machine Vision teams, who support you as you grow in the role. What you’ll work on Staying up to date: Following the latest developments in detection models and AI, assessing what’s relevant for our custom models, and translating this into concrete research actions. Building and improving detection models: Adapting existing models to new clients, improving detection, and qualifying model performance offline. Orchestrating data strategy: Managing and executing dataset annotation for model training and defining which data needs to be available to build and improve the best detection models. What we are looking for Education: A bachelor’s (HBO) or master’s degree in data science, AI, Computer Science, or a related field. Strong ML foundation: You have hands-on experience with Python and machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, gained at work or during your studies, graduation project, or internship. Data analysis: You have a strong focus on analyzing image data, understanding patterns, and extracting meaningful insights to improve model performance. Experience with medical or industrial datasets is a plus. Hands-on experience: You are comfortable owning the full pipeline, including data collection, annotation, and running experiments independently, or you’re eager to learn this quickly. Analytical and communicative: You can explain complex findings clearly to non-technical people and know how to tailor your message to your audience. Languages: Professional fluency in English, both written and spoken, is required. Dutch language skills are considered a plus. Eye for quality: You recognize that accuracy is critical in the pharmaceutical industry and understand the real-world impact of your models, especially when it comes to patient safety. Direct and transparent: You communicate openly about challenges. If a model underperforms or data is insufficient, you raise your concerns early so we can solve them together. Office-based work is required , allowing for fast communication and close collaboration with your team. Dutch/EER working permit What it’s like to work here Real impact: Your models run in real machines at real client sites. When you improve something, you directly see the effect! Flat structure, short lines: Good idea? Go for it. Our structure is simple to encourage involvement, creativity, and innovation. Interesting challenges: Detection problems in the pharmaceutical industry are complex and demanding. You’ll work at the edge of technology, where quality standards are high. A solid team: You work alongside engineering, operational, and commercial teams who all share the same goal. Cooperation and teamwork are key to building and delivering machines that actually work. Ready to build detection models that make a difference? Send your CV and a short intro to jobs@luoautomation.com

Based in our London office, this role is designed for a unique technical practitioner who enjoys owning the complete lifecycle of a feature. Working collaboratively with various stakeholders, you won’t be isolated to just model training or just infrastructure configuration; you will help translate product briefs into algorithmic solutions, train deep learning models, engineer algorithmic pipelines, and deliver optimised, production-ready deployable artifacts that power analytics used by professional sports teams and elite athletes around the world. What You’ll Do End-to-End Pipeline Contribution: Collaborate with senior data scientists, computer vision engineers and vertical teams to translate product requirements into practical computer vision solutions, helping design the pipeline from raw video ingestion to production inference. Algorithm & Model Development: Design, train, and evaluate deep learning architectures alongside classical computer vision pipelines (e.g., feature tracking, optical flow, and spatial filtering via OpenCV). Geometric Computer Vision: Develop robust mathematical pipelines for camera calibration, homography estimation, and coordinate mapping to ensure model spatial outputs are accurate and stable. Modern Cloud & Containerised Deployment: Focus on architecting and containerising Python-based cloud microservices (via Docker) as our primary, future-facing deployment model. Desktop Applications Support: Assist in compiling cross-platform native binaries or shared libraries linking against the ONNX Runtime C++ API to support and maintain our existing Windows/macOS desktop application footprint. Automated Data Curation: Help build intelligent, automated data-ingestion pipelines that utilise model-assisted pre-labeling to continuously clean and version high-throughput training datasets. Interface & Boundary Design: Participate in defining clean API boundaries and interface contracts to ensure our core data science modules integrate seamlessly into downstream vertical applications. What You’ll Need Core Algorithmic Background: Foundational knowledge of classical computer vision (multi-view geometry, object tracking, spatial transformation) and modern deep learning architectures (object detection, semantic/instance segmentation, transformer-based vision models). Production Model Training: Experience sourcing, structuring, training, and benchmarking deep neural networks using PyTorch or TensorFlow. Hybrid Language Skills: High proficiency in Python for prototyping, training, scripting, and deployment pipelines, combined with a practical, supporting capability to read, build, and debug existing C++ codebases (including exposure to build management tools like CMake). Execution Graph Optimisation: Familiarity with optimising model runtimes and inference execution graphs for real-time applications using TensorRT or ONNX Runtime (e.g., quantisation, layer fusion). Modern Infrastructure: Practical experience with Docker containerisation, version control (Git), and cloud platform execution (AWS). NICE TO HAVE Neural Architecture Customisation: Experience modifying, adapting, or designing custom neural network components (e.g., specialised backbones, attention mechanisms, or custom loss functions) rather than just implementing standard off-the-shelf models. Advanced Mathematical Foundations: A strong intuitive grasp or academic background in applied linear algebra and matrix calculus, particularly as it relates to 3D spatial transformations and projective geometry. items.card: Your role as a Computer Vision Engineer at Xsens As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will lead camera-based perception for Xsens motion capture. Your role is to establish Deep Learning and Computer Vision pipelines to turn camera images into human pose estimate. You will learn from the highly-skilled team of sensor fusion experts, biomechanists and mathematicians. You will be its computer vision specialist, and
items.desc: Do you get excited about building cutting-edge perception systems that work reliably in the real world? Do you have a strong foundation in computer vision, robotics, or sensor fusion? Are you interested in shaping new technology capabilities within a growing and innovative high-tech company, where people and fun are part of our core values? We’d love to have you! Who is Xsens Xsens is a leading full-stack provider of sensors, software, and analytics that enable the digitization of movement. Xsens serves entertainment, humanoid robotics, health & sports and automation & mobility markets. By turning complex motion data into actionable insight, we help our partners accelerate development, improve control and learning, and bring physically intelligent systems to life. We collaborate with leading global innovators including Boston Dynamics, Toyota, Siemens, Electronic Arts, Epic Games, Netflix, and 20th Century Studios, alongside more than 1,000 research institutions, humanoid robotics companies and universities worldwide. Your role as a Computer Vision Engineer at Xsens As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will lead camera-based perception for Xsens motion capture. Your role is to establish Deep Learning and Computer Vision pipelines to turn camera images into human pose estimate. You will learn from the highly-skilled team of sensor fusion experts, biomechanists and mathematicians. You will be its computer vision specialist, and report to the Technology Manager. The position is open to hybrid / remote working. Key challenges: Select, adapt and fine-tune deep learning models for 2D and 3D human pose estimation from cameras, that perform robustly in challenging real-world conditions. Develop camera models and calibration routines for a range of camera and lens configurations. Evaluation of motion capture output and developing compensatory algorithms and techniques to handle camera /vision failure modes. Build training and evaluation pipelines from camera and optical motion capture recordings. Use synthetic data where real data is insufficient. Track the computer vision research landscape and assess whether new techniques are feasible for Xsens products. Xsens is looking for a hands-on Computer Vision Engineer who combines strong theoretical foundations with a proven ability to build and ship working systems. Required MSc/PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics or a related field, with years of relevant industry or applied research experience. Hands-on experience training and fine-tuning deep learning models for human pose estimation, with results evaluated on public benchmarks. Solid understanding of camera and lens models, including wide field-of-view optics, intrinsic and extrinsic calibration, and multi-view geometry. Familiarity with the output representations of common pose models, such as keypoint sets and SMPL-family parameters. Experience with tools in markerless eco-system such as OpenCV, Sapiens, and SAM3D. Proficiency in Python. Working knowledge of C++ for integrating models into an existing C++ codebase. Preferred Experience with synthetic data generation and rendering pipelines. Experience optimizing models for real-time deployment, for example with ONNX, TensorRT or quantization. Experience building datasets and benchmarks for human motion. Working at Xsens We value ingenious ideas, no matter where they come from. We believe diverse thoughts, voices, and backgrounds make us stronger as a company. We know that it is through collaboration with people from all walks of life that we make the most positive impact as an organization. Join Xsens’ innovative, ambitious, and international team, where your ideas and talents make an impact. Along with a competitive compensation package, we offer a range of benefits designed to support your well-being and help you thrive. 28 paid vacation days with an option to buy, sell, or carry over days, giving you flexibility to manage your time off as appropriate to your situation Tax perks for your sports memberships and bicycle purchase; so staying active is easier than ever. Flexible working hours and the option to work from home, helping you balance life and work Paid volunteer time: Through our partnership with Stichting Present, you have the opportunity to give back to the community during office hours Our partnership with Equip gives you on-demand access to a dedicated financial planner who provides clear guidance and a concrete plan for wealth building, pensions, and major life events. Enjoy company social events as well as fun, informal activities organized by our staff association. From movie nights and sports clinics to cooking classes and LAN parties, there’s always something happening to connect and have fun

 Your impact

They also dive into the deepest level of detail – taking the system piece-by-piece and defining its design to the finest point.  As a Graduate Systems Engineer, you will work on real engineering problems within either the Radar or the Advanced Targeting business area. You will have the opportunity to be involved in supporting a wide range of tasks across multiple projects/products, such as:
 The radar for the Typhoon fighter jet
 The radar for the SAAB Gripen fighter
 Our family of Surveillance AESA (Active Electronically Scanned Array) radars
 An IRCM (Infra-Red Counter Measures) system
 Our laser target designator or laser ranging systems
 Key Responsibility Areas 
 Requirements capture, design documentation, verification and validation
 Algorithm design and test
 Performance modelling; building physics-based models to test our designs through computer simulation
 Data analysis; end-to-end systems analysis using synthetic and ‘real world’ data
 Applied research; from product improvements to blue-sky thinking
 You will join a dynamic and innovative team who will provide day-to-day guidance and on-the job training, introducing you to systems engineering processes, methods, technology and tools. You will also receive targeted training, developing the engineering skills and necessary domain knowledge required to achieve technical excellence and be a successful Systems Engineer.
 What you’ll bring 
 All of our roles require (a) a minimum of a 2:2 Bachelors/Integrated Master’s degree, or (b) a higher degree, such as a MSc or PhD in a STEM related subject.
 In addition to this, we would be interested in hearing from you if you have experience in:
 Coding/programming.
 Relevant project work and/or placements in industry.
 Solving problems as part of a team
 Applying your science and technology knowledge to solve a real-world problem
 Security Clearance 
 Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years. 
 For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV). As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment. 
 To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years. In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks. Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

PhD fellow in Molecular biology, Biotechnology and Genomics - IT | Lifetech 
 PhD fellow in Molecular biology, Biotechnology and Genomics 
 Italy 
 IIT invites excellent candidates to apply to its PhD program organized in collaboration with the Open University; this international PhD program confers Doctorates in Health, Sustainable and Human Technologies .
 In order to be admitted into the ARC program, the minimum requirements are
 a Masters-level degree, which broadly corresponds to a 4/5-year undergraduate MSc/MChem/Meng-style degree or to a postgraduate Masters in the British system, or to a second level University degree in Italy;
 a grade corresponding to an upper second class (2.1) or a merit in the UK system or 100/110 in the Italian system. Candidates with lower grades but redeeming features (publications, specific expertise) are requested to contact the potential supervisors before applying;
 where English is not the applicant’s first language, a valid IELTS (International English Language Testing System) certificate. The minimum acceptable score is an overall 6.5, with no less than 6.0 in any of the four categories
 One PhD fellow position will be available from 1st of January 2027 in the Non-coding Genomics research Line led by Stefano Gustincich .
 Title of the project : The SINEUPOME . 
 Background : SINEUPs are a class of natural and synthetic antisense long non-coding RNAs that selectively increase the translation of a target mRNA without altering its transcription or stability. They were discovered through the mouse antisense Uchl1 transcript (Carrieri et al., Nature 2012), whose activity depends on an embedded inverted SINEB2 repeat, the origin of the name.
 SINEUPs have a modular architecture. A binding domain, antisense to the 5′ region of the target mRNA (typically overlapping the start codon), confers specificity. An effector domain, containing the inverted SINEB2 element or minimal functional fragments of it, drives translational enhancement. Swapping the binding domain lets SINEUPs be designed against virtually any gene of interest.
 Their effect is moderate (about 1.5- to 3-fold protein increase) and stays within physiological ranges. This makes them attractive for haploinsufficiency disorders and other conditions caused by insufficient protein dosage. They are also useful for biotechnological protein production. They can be delivered as plasmids, viral vectors such as AAV, or synthetic RNA.
 Description: 
 Rationale . Only a handful of natural SINEUPs are known, yet inverted SINE elements are abundant in antisense transcripts across mammals. A systematic analysis would reveal how widespread translational enhancement by antisense lncRNAs really is.
 Aim 1 – Computational catalogue. Mine CAGE (FANTOM5/6), total RNA-seq and nanopore long-read datasets from human, mouse and non-model mammals to annotate lncRNAs with an embedded inverted SINE (SINEB2, MIR, Alu, FLAM).
 Aim 2 – PARIS analysis. Identify lncRNA/mRNA pairs in PARIS data from a diverse array of dataset. List which candidate SINEUPs from Aim 1 are part of the duplex.
 Aim 3 – Functional validation. Test 50–100 top SINEUP candidates in HEK293 and neuronal cells, measuring protein over mRNA ratio of the targets by western blot, qRT-PCR and polysome profiling.
 Impact . A validated atlas of natural SINEUPs and their targets, plus rules linking sequence architecture to activity, would provide both a new layer of post-transcriptional gene regulation and design principles for synthetic SINEUP therapeutics.

items.desc: About Voodoo Voodoo is a consumer tech company founded in Paris in 2013, with one mission: entertain the world. Today we are 1,000 people, generating $1b+ in annual revenue, profitably. Our games and apps have passed 7 billion downloads and reach 200 million+ active users every month, making Voodoo the #3 mobile publisher worldwide in downloads, after Google and Meta. We were backed by Goldman Sachs, Tencent and GBL along the way. Team Blitz is a gaming platform launched by Voodoo in 2021, allowing players to compete on mobile games for real cash prizes (head-up, tournaments, leagues, etc.). It is leveraging Voodoo's unique game portfolio to engage users in a fun and rewarding way. Role This role sits at the intersection of the Data and Gaming teams. You'll be the analytical partner to game designers and product managers, owning the measurement and tuning of the games themselves — from difficulty and game parameters to matchmaking fairness and the in-game economy. Your work directly shapes what players experience and how the games perform. Missions Own the A/B testing cycle for games and game parameters — designing experiments, validating changes, and reading out results that drive core KPIs (engagement, RTP, rake, fairness, retention). Analyze and calibrate game parameters — difficulty, scoring, completion rates, seed selection, and payout structures — to hit target player experience and economic goals. Translate analyses into clear, actionable recommendations that shape game design and the product roadmap. Build simulations and prototypes to pressure-test parameter and economy changes before rollout, then monitor them live once shipped. Collaborate closely with game designers and engineers to embed data-driven decisions across the full game lifecycle. Build and maintain dashboards and reports that keep the Gaming and Data teams aligned on critical game and economy metrics. Profile 3+ years in analytical roles, ideally within gaming or a data-intensive product environment, comfortable working directly with product and design teams. Skilled in SQL and Python; experience with large, complex datasets. Strong grasp of A/B testing and statistical methods. Comfortable with simulation and modeling to reason about game parameters, difficulty, and game economy outcomes. Thrives in a fast-paced environment with rapid iteration. Player-first mindset with genuine curiosity about games, player behavior, and game balance. Benefits Competitive salary based on experience Swile Lunch voucher Gymlib (100% covered by Voodoo) Premium healthcare coverage with SideCare, 100% covered for you and your family Wellness activities in our Paris office Remote days on Fridays

Location This role is fully remote. We are currently accepting applicants based in: United States, Canada, Puerto Rico, Mexico, United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, and Argentina.

items.desc: Software Developer — Build Your Own Project with an AI Coding Assistant About The Role What if you could get paid to work on the project you've been meaning to build — with a state-of-the-art AI coding assistant at your side, completely free of charge? We're looking for software developers in the Lisbon area to bring their own projects and build them using an AI-powered coding assistant. You write real code on real projects you care about. We learn from your expert judgment on how the assistant performed. You keep full ownership of everything you build. This is a fully remote, flexible contract role designed for developers who want to ship their own work — and get compensated for it. Organization: Alignerr Type: Hourly Contract Location: Fully Remote Commitment: Flexible What You'll Do Bring a software project you personally own — a side project, a tool, an open-source library, or something you've been meaning to finish Build features, fix bugs, refactor code, write docs, or do whatever your project needs — using an AI coding assistant At each step, compare two versions of the assistant's response, choose the better one, and write a brief explanation of your reasoning Work in your own environment, on your own schedule, with your own tools Who You Are A developer with a software project you personally own, stored in a git repository Comfortable working in the terminal and with git-based workflows Running macOS, Linux, or Windows with WSL2 Able to write clear, honest evaluations — you'll explain your choices in a few sentences Self-motivated and reliable when working independently Open-source maintainers are especially welcome What's Eligible Software projects that you personally and solely own Open-source projects with an approved license If your project has other maintainers, mention it in your application — we'll confirm eligibility What's Not Eligible Work owned by an employer, client, university, company, or startup Projects under NDA AI model training or evaluation projects; ML infrastructure Security exploit tooling Projects that process other people's personal data Good to Know Before starting, you'll sign short contributor terms and we'll approve your project Transcripts of your coding sessions are used to improve AI models and cannot be withdrawn after submission — this covers sessions only, not the rest of your codebase Your ratings and written feedback become part of the project's deliverables During sessions: no passwords, API keys, or other people's personal data — and you write your ratings yourself, without AI help Why You'll Love This Your project, your code — you keep full ownership of everything, including code the assistant writes for you Free AI tokens — your AI usage during sessions is fully covered, no subscription or API bill needed Paid to build what you'd build anyway — real compensation for real development work on your own project Fully remote and flexible — work from your own computer, on your own schedule Shape the future of AI-assisted coding — your expert judgment directly improves the next generation of developer tools Spots are limited — the first cohort is small and starting soon

items.title: AI Data Trainer - Remote
items.card: Responsibilities Review robotic-arm videos and identify key actions, events, and outcomes. Apply detailed guidelines to tag and annotate video events accurately. Mark precise start and end timestamps for actions, transitions, and outcomes. Verify annotations for timing accuracy and correct inconsistencies or drift. Use video annotation tools to create and submit high-quality datasets. Collaborate with project teams
items.desc: Senior AI Trainer Role Type: Contractor, Remote Location: North America, Latin America, Europe, UK, Oceania We're seeking Senior AI Trainers to support a customer project focused on improving AI systems through expert-level video annotation and data labeling. You'll review robotic-arm footage, create precise annotations, and provide high-quality data to support AI model training. No prior AI experience is required. Key Responsibilities Review robotic-arm videos and identify key actions, events, and outcomes. Apply detailed guidelines to tag and annotate video events accurately. Mark precise start and end timestamps for actions, transitions, and outcomes. Verify annotations for timing accuracy and correct inconsistencies or drift. Use video annotation tools to create and submit high-quality datasets. Collaborate with project teams to resolve ambiguities and maintain annotation consistency. Participate in quality reviews and incorporate feedback to maintain standards. Required Qualifications Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy when reviewing visual data. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Excellent time management and ability to work independently in a remote environment. Analytical and problem-solving mindset. Preferred Qualifications Experience in video annotation, data labeling, or similar projects. Familiarity with video annotation and timeline-based labeling tools. Experience with frame-level or timecode-based annotation. Background in AI training, machine learning data preparation, or robotics is strongly preferred.

items.desc: Turn computational work from your own engineering research into paid evaluation tasks for AI models. Open to research-track Bachelor's students, Master's and PhD students, postdocs, and recent graduates. AfterQuery is building a network of researchers to author and validate research-grade scientific-computing tasks for AI models. A strong task is a real piece of computational work from your own research, something you've actually run and debugged: a finite-element or CFD solver, a reaction-engineering model, a physiological model, or a structural or electromagnetic simulation you implemented and validated. Each task has a main problem, a few connected subproblems, a Python reference solution, and tests that check the result. The difficulty should come from the engineering science itself, not from withheld information. We're looking for researchers in: computational mechanics and finite-element methods; computational fluid dynamics; aerospace numerical modeling; chemical and reaction engineering; biomedical and physiological modeling; civil and structural computational mechanics; environmental modeling; and computational electromagnetics. Requirements Education: A Bachelor's student on a research track or with research experience (such as an REU, a thesis, or an RA or lab role), a Master's or PhD student, a postdoc, or a recent graduate in mechanical, aerospace, chemical, biomedical, civil, environmental, or electrical engineering with a computational focus. Technical: Hands-on experience writing your own code, preferably Python, to implement or validate engineering models and solvers. Using commercial software (such as ANSYS, COMSOL, or Abaqus) without your own code isn't enough. Work authorization: Must be able to work as an independent contractor without visa sponsorship. Students on F-1 visas (including OPT/CPT) are not eligible. items.desc: Position description Category Thermohydraulics and fluid mechanics Contract Internship Job title Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions H/F Subject Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions Contract duration (months) 6 Job description The Critical Heat Flux (CHF) is a physical phenomenon that may cause the deterioration of the heat transfer in the core of nuclear reactors, potentially leading to core damage. Its accurate prediction is therefore a crucial issue in nuclear reactor safety. The internship deals with the prediction of the CHF through the development of machine learning techniques and the quantification of the associated uncertainty. It will be realized in the framework of an international OECD/NEA project on the development and application of artificial intelligence methodologies for nuclear engineering. Within this framework, the intern will: Perform a preliminary literature review on the topic and get familiar with the previous works performed at CEA, based on experimental data in tubes with uniform axial heat flux profiles Analyse the new experimental CHF database (e.g., tube with non-uniform heat flux, rod-bundle, rectangular channel, …) to understand the physical phenomenon and to verify the coherence and exploitability of the experimental data. Perform an initial assessment of previously developed machine learning models to the new database. Develop transfer learning to predict as accurately as possible the CHF for the new experiments. If time allows it, investigate the explainability issue and quantify the uncertainty of the models developed during the internship applying different state-of-the-art methodologies such as conformal prediction, hierarchical models and other coverage-driven techniques. Present and discuss the work during technical meetings and write a final report. Applicant Profile The ideal candidate is a MSc. student (in French system: M2 level or Ecole d’ingénieur) who has a good knowledge of artificial intelligence and neural networks with an interest in fluid mechanics. Knowledge of the physics processes underlying the CHF phenomenon will be considered a plus. Good skills in Python coding and code management are required. We welcome previous experience with any major deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, Tensorflow) and with uncertainty quantification approaches. Given the international context of the OECD/NEA project, fluency in English is considered necessary (French will be considered a plus). Position location Site Saclay Job location France, Ile-de-France Location Saclay Candidate criteria Prepared diploma Bac+5 - Diplôme École d'ingénieurs PhD opportunity Non Requester Position start date 01/02/2027 General information Organisation The French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA) is a key player in research, development and innovation in four main areas : defence and security, nuclear energy (fission and fusion), technological research for industry, fundamental research in the physical sciences and life sciences. Drawing on its widely acknowledged expertise, and thanks to its 16000 technicians, engineers, researchers and staff, the CEA actively participates in collaborative projects with a large number of academic and industrial partners. The CEA is established in ten centers spread throughout France Reference 2026-42162 Description de l'unité The internship will be conducted at the Department of Thermal-hydraulics and Fluid dynamics (STMF – Service de Thermohydraulique et de Mécanique de Fluide) within the Energy Division (DES - Direction des Énergies). The department develops and qualifies the simulation tools for the design and the safety analysis of the French nuclear power systems, such as the system thermal-hydraulic code CATHARE. These studies are performed within the framework of internal CEA projects or in collaboration with several industrial partners (e.g., EDF, Framatome and TechnicAtome) and international partners. The internship is in collaboration with the Department of Software Engineering and for Simulation (SGLS - Service de Génie Logiciel pour la Simulation).

items.desc: Summary You will become part of the newly established AI Threat Research and AI Conversation Security team within the Technology Division in Bratislava. As a founding member, you have a unique opportunity to shape the team's direction and methodology from the ground up. The team researches attacks against conversational AI systems — probing and breaking them to understand how adversaries exploit large language models. Job Description Beyond research, the team designs and implements detection mechanisms and translates these defenses into shipping products across endpoint, cloud, and standalone form factors. As a Conversational AI Security Engineer, you bridge adversarial research and production engineering — building detection mechanisms to defend conversational AI systems and shipping those defenses as products. Your work spans the full lifecycle, from breaking models to running detection in production. About The Role Research attacks against conversational AI systems — exploring, probing, and breaking them to discover vulnerabilities before adversaries do. Design and propose mitigations, protections, and detection strategies based on findings from adversarial research. Build a multilayered detection core, combining different approaches to identify malicious prompts and attempts to manipulate AI systems. Productize detection capabilities — packaging and deploying them across endpoint, cloud, and standalone environments. Collaborate with the broader threat detection department, product teams, and endpoint teams to integrate defenses into shipping security solutions. Evaluate and experiment with open-source and proprietary AI tooling to stay current with the rapidly evolving attack surface. Shape the team's technical direction and methodology as a founding member, with the opportunity to grow into a Team Lead role over time. Essential Requirements Strong software engineering background — ability to build production systems, not just prototypes. Proficiency in Python for building detection and security tooling. Understanding of how large language models work and how they can be manipulated or attacked, including prompt injection, jailbreaking, and adversarial inputs. Ability to work independently in a newly forming team with minimal defined processes. Desirable Requirements Experience with machine learning and AI, including fine-tuning and deploying language models. C++ for performance-critical detection components. Background in cybersecurity or threat research. Technologies Python, C++, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, scikit-learn, vLLM, Ollama, ONNX, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Git, JIRA, Confluence Compensation Basic wage component (brutto): from 2800 EUR/m. (brutto) * The final basic wage component can be increased accordingly to individual skills and experience of the selected candidate. * Performance bonus 2 times per year up to 10% of the basic salary paid for the evaluation period(usually 6 months). #medior At ESET, diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) are integral to our corporate culture. We believe in creating a respectful environment, where everyone feels valued and respected, welcoming applications from individuals of all backgrounds, including race, gender, age, religion, disability, and sexual orientation.

items.desc: Starting date: 16/10/2026Job Reference 446_26_ES_AC_RE2Position Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2)Closing Date Monday, 19 October, ****Reference: 446_26_ES_AC_RE2Job title: Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2)About BSCThe Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over **** staff from 60 countries.Look At The BSC ExperienceBSC-CNS YouTube ChannelLet's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured.We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences.If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team.Context And MissionWe are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic research engineer to join the Atmospheric Composition (AC) group within the Earth Sciences department at the BSC-CNS. The AC group is currently composed of about 50 people among researchers, engineers and students of different nationalities. It aims at better understanding and predicting the spatio-temporal variations of atmospheric pollutants along with their effects upon air quality, weather and climate. This is addressed through the continuous development and application of numerical models over multiple scales, from weather to climate and from global to urban scales.The AC group develops and maintains its own forecast model MONARCH, which is a coupled meteorological-chemistry model that can be run at global and regional scales to simulate gaseous chemistry and aerosols plus their feedbacks on radiation. MONARCH is also coupled to a data assimilation scheme for gases and aerosols that is used to initialize forecasts or produce reanalyses of the atmospheric composition. The AC group operates several operational forecasting systems in the framework of the World Meteorological Organization Sand and Dust Storm Advisory System (SDS-WAS, ), the Copernicus atmospheric monitoring services (CAMS, ), the Spanish air quality forecasting system CALIOPE (), and the International Cooperative for Aerosols Predictions (ICAP). The successful candidate will join the Data Assimilation Forecasting and Application team of the AC group and will play a key coordinating role in the production and continuous improvement of the team's operational forecasting and reanalysis systems. The activities will be carried out mainly in the framework of the Copernicus CAMS2_40bis international project, with contributions to the CAMS2_82bis project and to the activities of the Barcelona Dust Regional Center (BDRC). The candidate will work in a highly collaborative environment, with tight links with researchers and engineers in the AC group. The candidate will have the opportunity to follow multiple training activities, including those aimed at improving coding and data analysis, project writing abilities, or project management. All this will be implemented via the formal courses organized by the Education and Training team and Human Resources, and the participation in the regular seminars organized by the department.Key DutiesManage the team's technical activities within CAMS2_40bis and its contributions to CAMS2_82bis and the BDRC, including planning, follow-up of tasks and milestones, and reporting.Coordinate the preparation and timely delivery of project deliverables, and represent the team in international project meetings.Coordinate the upgrades of the production systems: define and evaluate target model configurations, organize the e-suite experiments, and ensure successful operational deployments.Coordinate the production of atmospheric composition reanalyses, from planning and set-up to monitoring, validation and dissemination.Oversee the overall quality assurance of the forecast and reanalysis products, including routine evaluation against in-situ and satellite …

items.desc: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role As a Research Software Engineer on the Sandboxes team, you will design, build, and operate the platform that runs isolated environments for untrusted code at massive scale. Our work spans distributed systems, low-level virtualization, and product-minded platform design. Engineers on this team move between deep infrastructure work and understanding how researchers actually use the platform. This is a software engineering role, not an ML research role. You do not need prior ML experience; what matters is writing clean, reliable systems code that scales. You will join a small, senior team where the wrong hire is worse than no hire. What You Will Do Design, build, and operate the sandboxing platform that runs untrusted code at scale across multiple Kubernetes clusters, from our own bare metal data centers to hyperscalers. Develop the sandbox runtime leveraging Firecracker, enabling fast startup, snapshotting, and efficient scheduling without blocking expensive hardware. Obsess over performance and latency optimisation allowing us to reach millions of concurrent sandboxes. Write robust, well-tested systems code in Rust and Python; review code, CI/CD, and observability across the platform. Own cross-cluster networking, security boundaries, isolation guarantees and monitoring for suspicious activity. Collaborate with researchers and ML engineers who use sandboxes for synthetic data generation and RL training, turning their needs into platform features. What We're Looking For A strong background in software engineering and distributed systems, with experience building and operating large-scale infrastructure. Deep expertise in at least one of: Kubernetes and cluster operations, cross-cluster networking, observability, or low-level virtualization. Fluency in Python or Rust; comfortable writing systems code where performance and security matter. Strong software-design instincts: modular code, testing, CI/CD, observability, and a bias for reliability. A self-starter who learns fast. Core skills matter more than specific tools — we value meta-learning ability and motivation highly. Low-ego, collaborative, and comfortable with ambiguity in a small, high-ownership team. Nice-to-haves Experience with Firecracker, microVMs, or similar virtualization technologies. Product-mindedness: understanding of how sandboxes are used for synthetic data generation or RL training. Experience with GPU clusters, CUDA, or ML workloads. Prior SRE or platform engineering experience at scale. Open-source contributions or widely used internal tools. What we offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page. Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

items.desc: APPLY NOW! Intact Insurance is the new name for RSA in the UK, Ireland, and across Europe. It’s a new name and a new way to do business. Backed by global expertise and a commitment to service that feels different, we’re focused on making insurance simpler, faster, and more responsive. Shape The Future We’re leading a transformation in insurance helping people, businesses and society prosper in good times and be resilient in bad times. When you join us, you’re not just taking a job, you’re stepping into a career where you can make a real difference. Grow With Us We’re customer-driven, community-focused, and committed to helping our people grow. Whether you’re early in your journey or bringing years of experience, we’ll support you with the tools, flexibility, and opportunities to thrive. Win As a Team We’re looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to help build and run production-ready ML systems that make a real impact across the business. You’ll work closely with Data Scientists and engineering teams, shaping the ML roadmap, developing scalable solutions, and driving innovation while growing your career. You’ll Make An Impact By Office location – London or Horsham, 3 days a week. Build and automate ML pipelines for feature engineering, model training, and model scoring using Python, PySpark, Databricks, and MLflow. Productionise Data Science models, converting notebooks into modular, tested, production-ready code. Deploy models into batch and real-time environments, managing versioning, promotion, rollback, and scheduled workflows via MLflow and APIs. Implement monitoring and observability, including data and model drift detection, performance alerts, logging, and automated retraining. Collaborate with Data Engineering and Platform teams on CI/CD integration, pipeline performance, compute optimisation, and secure deployment patterns. Maintain engineering standards, ensuring high-quality testing, documentation, code quality, reproducibility, and operational reliability. Your Skills And Experience Experience with ML platforms including Databricks, MLflow, Delta Lake, and cloud environments. Proficient in Python, PySpark, and SQL, following production coding best practices. Understanding of data, distributed ML pipelines, and model deployment patterns, including monitoring, drift detection, and lifecycle operations. Exposure to CI/CD, containerisation, and API integration, with the ability to build scalable, production-ready ML systems. Comfortable working technically while communicating effectively with Data Scientists, stakeholders, and cross-functional teams. Why You’ll Love It Here Being part of our team means you’ll have the support and freedom to bring your best self to work each day. As a permanent member, here’s what you can look forward to Annual discretionary bonus Up to 11% pension contributions Hybrid working + flexible hours 25 days annual leave + bank holidays + buy/sell options Health & wellbeing + virtual GP Career development and mentoring Inclusive culture + employee networks Share investment options Our DEI Commitment We celebrate individuality and believe our differences make us stronger. We’re proud to foster a culture where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to thrive. As an Equal Opportunity and Disability Confident Employer, we ensure fair consideration for all applicants and offer interviews to all disabled candidates who meet the essential criteria. We understand that everyone’s circumstances are different and are happy to explore flexible working options such as reduced hours or job shares to support work–life balance. If you meet the core criteria but not every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Let’s explore how this role could support your next career step. If you need adjustments during the recruitment process, just let us know we’re here to support you.

items.card: Responsibilities Chemiluminescent Sensor Development and Characterisation Prepare, refine and evaluate candidate chemiluminescent sensing materials and formulations in collaboration with the project team. Develop experimental methods to quantify sensor response under controlled temperature and relative-humidity conditions. Characterise sensor sensitivity, repeatability, variability, response behaviour and stability
items.desc: Description Role Title: Research Associate in Sensor Development & Electronic Device Characterisation Grade and Salary: Grade 7, £38,448 - £48,337 per annum FTE and working pattern: Full-time (35hrs per week) Fixed Term until 31st March 2027. Reward and Benefits : 33 days annual leave, plus 9 buildings closed days for all full time staff. Use our total rewards calculator: https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University. Purpose of Role Applications are invited for a five-month Research Associate position at Heriot-Watt University to support an interdisciplinary ARIA-funded research programme developing highly miniaturised sensing and wireless technologies for bio-inspired aerial platforms. The project is a collaboration between Heriot-Watt University and the University of Edinburgh and brings together expertise in sensing, functional materials, electronic systems, microdevices, wireless technologies and bio-inspired engineering. The successful applicant will contribute to two equally important experimental activities within the project: Chemiluminescent sensor development and characterisation - This will include preparation and evaluation of candidate sensing materials, development of optical measurement methods, and assessment of temperature and relative-humidity response, repeatability and stability. Electronic device and high-frequency/RF characterisation - This will include development of suitable measurement arrangements for externally fabricated micro- and nanoscale devices, acquisition and analysis of electrical signals, and evaluation of device performance within the wider electronic and wireless system. The position therefore requires an interdisciplinary experimental researcher with practical experience spanning both sensor/materials development and electronic or high-frequency characterisation. The successful candidate will develop experimental methods, establish and troubleshoot measurement systems, analyse results and contribute to technical decisions across both workstreams. Fabrication of the micro- and nanoscale electronic devices will be undertaken by specialist external facilities. The focus of this appointment is experimental development, characterisation and validation rather than cleanroom fabrication. Given the short duration of the appointment, we are particularly interested in candidates with strong practical laboratory skills who can work independently, adapt quickly to new techniques and deliver experimental results within a defined project timescale. Key Duties And Responsibilities Chemiluminescent Sensor Development and Characterisation Prepare, refine and evaluate candidate chemiluminescent sensing materials and formulations in collaboration with the project team. Develop experimental methods to quantify sensor response under controlled temperature and relative-humidity conditions. Characterise sensor sensitivity, repeatability, variability, response behaviour and stability using appropriate reference measurements. Compare candidate formulations and sensor configurations and identify promising approaches for further development. Establish and use suitable optical measurement methods for quantitative sensor evaluation. Analyse results, identify experimental limitations and provide recommendations for subsequent sensor development. Electronic Device and High-Frequency/RF Characterisation Develop and implement experimental procedures for the electrical and high-frequency/RF characterisation of externally fabricated micro- and nanoscale electronic devices. Establish suitable test arrangements and interfaces between devices and electronic measurement equipment. Acquire and analyse transient and high-frequency electrical signals using appropriate laboratory instrumentation. Characterise device performance, repeatability and device-to-device variability, and compare different device designs or fabrication variants. Identify and minimise measurement artefacts associated with noise, grounding, shielding, bandwidth and parasitic effects. Support evaluation of signal detectability and device performance within the wider electronic and wireless system. Activities Across Both Research Strands Analyse experimental data using MATLAB, Python or equivalent computational tools. Develop appropriate quantitative methods for comparing experimental results. Maintain clear and accurate laboratory records and prepare concise technical reports. Provide technical feedback to project collaborators and external partners and contribute to decisions on subsequent experimental iterations. Develop appropriate risk assessments and COSHH documentation and work within established laboratory health and safety procedures. Present research findings and experimental plans at project meetings and contribute to reports, publications and presentations. Work effectively with researchers at Heriot-Watt University, the University of Edinburgh and …

items.desc: About ION We are a Software Product Company with a global footprint in the FinTech sector. With more than 10,000 professionals across 40+ offices worldwide, we provide solutions combining trading and workflow automation , market data , and advanced business intelligence. Our Graduate Development Program is a three-year journey designed for recent graduates who look beyond the obvious, challenge existing processes, and are driven to automate and reinvent the way things work. The program is structured into 4 progressive phases, each with distinct learning objectives. Tasks evolve according to your abilities and interests, ensuring the experience is as individual as you are. From day one, you join ION on a full‑time permanent contract , carry real accountability on live projects, and be paired with senior professionals who guide your development throughout the entire journey. What You'll Do Across phases, you will become the owner of full data transformation and reporting pipelines, working at the intersection of business processes and technology. items.desc: Orcrist is building a next generation data intelligence platform using cutting-edge technologies. We're handling petabyte-scale data with sub-second queries. Our product is a Kubernetes‑based platform delivered as B2B SaaS or as a self‑hosted on‑prem solution, including air‑gapped deployments. We enable customers across defense, law enforcement, and enterprise to turn mission-critical data into actionable intelligence. Role We are looking for a hands-on ML Engineer to build and productionize modern AI capabilities across text, vision, audio, and other applied ML use cases. You will work directly with state-of-the-art and open-source models — testing, evaluating, optimizing, and fine-tuning them for real product use cases. This is not a role focused on training foundation models from scratch or building data pipelines only. You will work closely with Research, Product, and Data Engineering teams to take promising models and ideas from experimentation to reliable, production-ready systems. What you'll do Evaluate, compare and integrate open-source models for concrete product and customer use cases. Build and improve LLM-based applications. Extend and improve AI and ML models using inference optimization, evaluation, and fine-tuning where appropriate. Work with NLP, translation, speech-to-text / ASR, image and document understanding, and related applied AI models. Design evaluation frameworks covering model quality, latency, reliability, and cost. Take models from experimentation into production, including packaging, deployment, monitoring, and iteration. Optimize inference performance and operational cost. Collaborate with Research and Product teams to turn prototypes and experiments into scalable product capabilities. Contribute to modern ML infrastructure and MLOps while remaining hands-on with models and model behaviour. About You 4+ years of experience in Machine Learning Engineering, Applied AI, or a similar hands-on ML role. Strong Python skills and practical experience with modern ML frameworks and libraries such as PyTorch, Transformers, and Hugging Face. Experience working with LLMs, NLP models, speech models, or other modern generative AI systems. Hands-on experience evaluating and experimenting with existing models rather than only building ML infrastructure. Experience with inference engines like vLLM or SGLang, and platforms like NVIDIA Triton or Ollama. Familiarity with fine-tuning, prompting, model evaluation, inference, and deployment. Working understanding of AI model encoding and quantization formats, and the tradeoffs thereof. Strong engineering mindset and ability to turn experiments into reliable, reproducible systems. Eligible to work in Germany; export-control screening required for certain programs. Nice-to-haves Hands-on experience with model serving and production deployment, using technologies such as Kubernetes, KServe, NVIDIA Triton, and/or Ray Serve. Knowledge of inference optimization techniques, including batching, quantization, ONNX, or TensorRT. German language skills (B1+) and/or familiarity with defense or public safety datasets. Exposure to geospatial AI, satellite imagery, or remote sensing. Experience working in constrained or regulated environments with infrastructure, security, or deployment requirements. What we offer Remote-first, Germany-wide: Work from wherever you do your best work, with regular team gatherings in Berlin and other off-site locations. Flexibility by default: Flexible working hours help you make work fit your life. Your setup, your way: Get a personal home-office equipment budget to create a workspace that works for you. 30 days of vacation: Take the time you need to recharge and come back with fresh energy. Keep growing: We invest in your personal and professional development. Get rewarded for impact: Performance bonuses are tied to agreed objectives and key results. A warm welcome: Every new team member gets a welcome goodie bag. Good people, good times: From summer and Christmas parties to regular team gatherings, we make time to celebrate together. items.desc:
The Amazon Web Services Professional Services (ProServe) team is seeking a skilled Delivery Consultant to join our team at Amazon Web Services (AWS). In this role, you'll work closely with customers to design, implement, and manage AWS solutions that meet their technical requirements and business objectives. You'll be a key player in driving customer success through their cloud journey, providing technical expertise and best practices throughout the project lifecycle.
Possessing a deep understanding of AWS products and services, as a Delivery Consultant you will be proficient in architecting complex, scalable, and secure solutions tailored to meet the specific needs of each customer. You’ll work closely with stakeholders to gather requirements, assess current infrastructure, and propose effective migration strategies to AWS. As trusted advisors to our customers, providing guidance on industry trends, emerging technologies, and innovative solutions, you will be responsible for leading the implementation process, ensuring adherence to best practices, optimizing performance, and managing risks throughout the project.
The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts that help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute enterprise cloud computing initiatives. Our team provides assistance through a collection of offerings which help customers achieve specific outcomes related to enterprise cloud adoption. We also deliver focused guidance through our global specialty practices, which cover a variety of solutions, technologies, and industries.

As an experienced technology professional, you will be responsible for:
- Designing, implementing, and building complex, scalable, and secure GenAI and ML applications and models built on AWS tailored to customer needs
- Providing technical guidance and implementation support throughout project delivery, with a focus on using AWS AI/ML services
- Collaborating with customer stakeholders to gather requirements and propose effective model training, building, and deployment strategies
- Acting as a trusted advisor to customers on industry trends and emerging technologies
- Sharing knowledge within the organization through mentoring, training, and creating reusable artifacts

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS? Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Inclusive Team Culture - Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
Mentorship & Career Growth - We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Work/Life Balance - We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

- Experience developing software code in one or more programming languages (typescript, python, etc.)
- Experience scripting for automation (e.g., Python, Perl, Ruby)

 The Position
 RWD Scientist in Ophthalmology 
 A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.

 You support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement in RWD methodology and delivery 
 You continuously look for opportunities to broaden knowledge, capabilities and skill set

 You exhibit Excellent strategic agility including problem-solving and critical thinking skills, and agility that extends beyond technical domain 
 You demonstrate respect for cultural differences when interacting with colleagues in the global workplace 
 You possess excellent verbal and written communication skills, specifically in the areas of presentation and writing, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts in clear language 
 Preferred: 
 Experience working in Ophthalmology related data / projects 
 Experience working in agile project teams or regulated environments 
 Exposure to pharmacoepidemiology or HEOR 
 Location 
 This position is based in Welwyn, UK 
 Relocation Assistance is not available 
 Who we are
 A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




THE ROLE

As a Research Software Engineer on the Sandboxes team, you will design, build, and operate the platform that runs isolated environments for untrusted code at massive scale. Our work spans distributed systems, low-level virtualization, and product-minded platform design. Engineers on this team move between deep infrastructure work and understanding how researchers actually use the platform.

This is a software engineering role, not an ML research role. You do not need prior ML experience; what matters is writing clean, reliable systems code that scales. You will join a small, senior team where the wrong hire is worse than no hire.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Design, build, and operate the sandboxing platform that runs untrusted code at scale across multiple Kubernetes clusters, from our own bare metal data centers to hyperscalers.

 - Develop the sandbox runtime leveraging Firecracker, enabling fast startup, snapshotting, and efficient scheduling without blocking expensive hardware.

 - Obsess over performance and latency optimisation allowing us to reach millions of concurrent sandboxes.

 - Write robust, well-tested systems code in Rust and Python; review code, CI/CD, and observability across the platform.

 - Own cross-cluster networking, security boundaries, isolation guarantees and monitoring for suspicious activity.

 - Collaborate with researchers and ML engineers who use sandboxes for synthetic data generation and RL training, turning their needs into platform features.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A strong background in software engineering and distributed systems, with experience building and operating large-scale infrastructure.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of: Kubernetes and cluster operations, cross-cluster networking, observability, or low-level virtualization.

 - Fluency in Python or Rust; comfortable writing systems code where performance and security matter.

 - Strong software-design instincts: modular code, testing, CI/CD, observability, and a bias for reliability.

 - A self-starter who learns fast. Core skills matter more than specific tools — we value meta-learning ability and motivation highly.

 - Low-ego, collaborative, and comfortable with ambiguity in a small, high-ownership team.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with Firecracker, microVMs, or similar virtualization technologies.

 - Product-mindedness: understanding of how sandboxes are used for synthetic data generation or RL training.

 - Experience with GPU clusters, CUDA, or ML workloads.

 - Prior SRE or platform engineering experience at scale.

 - Open-source contributions or widely used internal tools.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.




PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



As a Research Engineer on the Orchestral team, you will help build the agentic platform we use to train and evaluate our models. Orchestral is the system our researchers rely on to run training and evaluation at scale — from the rollout engine that powers agentic workflows to the infrastructure that keeps their workloads running reliably. What you build becomes the foundation the whole science team works on.

Your work will span the platform's core: the library, tooling, abstractions and rollout engine — including new capabilities like long-running tasks, subagents and RL features — and the machinery that runs data and jobs at scale, with a focus on resiliency, routing and request handling. You will own significant pieces end to end, from design to production.

This is a software engineering role rather than an ML or infrastructure-operations one: RL or PyTorch experience is not required, and you will spend your time building the platform, not operating it. You will be building a distributed RL system, with the scientists as your users.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Design and build the core of the Orchestral platform: the library, abstractions and tooling researchers use to train and evaluate models.

 - Build and evolve the rollout engine, shipping new capabilities such as long-running tasks and subagents.

 - Run Orchestral as a production system: keep training and evaluation workloads reliable at scale.

 - Improve how data and jobs flow through the platform as usage grows — scheduling, routing and request handling.

 - Treat researchers as your users: understand their workflows and turn recurring needs into robust, shared tooling.

 - Raise the bar on engineering quality across the platform: testing, code review, CI/CD, observability and documentation.

 - Contribute to open-source rollout-engine and agent-infrastructure projects where it benefits the platform.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience directly building and debugging complex distributed systems at scale, with an emphasis on reliability and scalability.

 - Strong Python skills and solid software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD.

 - A builder mindset: you have constructed systems from the ground up, not just operated polished ones.

 - A track record in small teams running complex systems at scale — for example in finance, crypto or ad tech.

 - Self-starter, low-ego and collaborative, with a product mindset toward your users.

 - Curiosity about ML and RL — this experience is not required, but a desire to learn is.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Hands-on experience with Ray or similar distributed-computing frameworks.

 - Open-source contributions, especially to rollout-engine or agent-infrastructure projects such as SLIME, verl or PrimeRL.

 - Experience building or working with agentic workflows and environments.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

items.desc: At ZEISS Corporate Research & Technology, we work at the frontier of science and technology to identify emerging computing architectures and translate them into future technology opportunities for ZEISS. We are looking for a Research Scientist who understands accelerator architectures and fundamentally new computing concepts driven by the latest AI developments – from CPUs, GPUs and TPUs to custom accelerators, optical and analog computing, novel memory architectures and new forms of heterogeneous computing. The position combines strategic technology exploration with hands-on technical work. You will build targeted proof-of-concepts to validate promising architecture concepts, while engaging with startups, research groups and technology partners to understand emerging solutions first-hand, assess their maturity and identify the most promising approaches for ZEISS Your role Analyze AI computing systems end-to-end: Understand how training and inference workloads run on modern data-center architectures and identify the fundamental bottlenecks in compute, memory, interconnects and energy efficiency. Explore next-generation computing architectures: Evaluate established, emerging and fundamentally new concepts – custom accelerators, chiplets, in- and near-memory computing, optical and analog computing and heterogeneous systems. Build and benchmark proof-of-concepts: Translate architectural hypotheses into hands-on demonstrators and assess their potential quantitatively against the state of the art. Scout and recommend: Engage with startups, research groups and technology providers, judge maturity and differentiation, and distinguish fundamental technology shifts from incremental improvements. Your profile A university degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering with a focus on digital systems or computer architecture, or a closely related discipline. A PhD or equivalent research experience is welcome. Expertise in at least two of the following areas: computer architecture and systems; machine-learning systems and AI infrastructure; heterogeneous accelerators and emerging computing architectures. A systems-level understanding of modern AI technology stacks – training and inference workflows, numerical kernels, memory hierarchies, data movement, interconnects, accelerator hardware and system software – and the ability to explain where bottlenecks occur, why, and which architectural approaches can address them. Programming skills in Python and/or C/C++; experience with GPU computing, parallel programming, distributed systems, compilers, runtimes or HPC environments is an advantage. Curiosity and openness toward external technology developments, and the ease to engage directly with startups, research groups and technology providers, understand their approaches in technical depth and assess their relevance. An analytical eye for technology trends, the flexibility to revise your view when the evidence changes, and the ability to present complex topics clearly. Business-fluent English is required. Your tasks: Collaboration in the externally funded DFG project “Mestizo as a Transimperial Categorization in the Early Modern Greater Caribbean and Mexico City”.
