This role balances hands-on data workflow engineering with policy experimentation. You
items.desc: Founding Robot Learning Engineer | YC-Backed Physical AI & Robotics Startup | London (Remote) | Full-Time | Up to £150K + Equity About the Company Our client is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) physical AI data company building the foundational human video and motion datasets for leading robotics and embodied-AI teams. Focused on egocentric first-person video and UMI demonstration data, the company turns real-world capture operations into high-precision, versioned data products that foundation-model and VLA teams rely on to train physical robots. Backed by a freshly closed seed round, their core constraint is supply, not demand. They are actively scaling deployment engineering, field operations, and capture hardware to keep up with massive customer demand. The founders are building a three-person founding engineering team to set the technical standards, tooling, and evaluation methodology behind the world's reference dataset for robot learning. About the Role Reporting to the Engineering Lead (and working directly with partners and founders), the Founding Robot Learning Engineer bridges human demonstration data and real-world policy performance. You will decide, with empirical evidence, what datasets the company should collect and how that data should be represented. This role balances hands-on data workflow engineering with policy experimentation. You will build task segmentation and assisted-labeling workflows, construct policy data loaders, and execute policy training and evaluation experiments using egocentric and UMI datasets to prove that the company's data directly improves robot task success. Key Responsibilities Turn long recordings into useful task intervals, define annotation schemas for specific customer needs, and ensure every label remains frame-locked to the source video. Deploy AI models to propose task boundaries and labels, route uncertain results for human review, write labeling instructions, and measure reviewer consistency. Build custom data loaders and transformations that format video, labels, and motion trajectories (including human hand motion and UMI gripper paths) into policy-ready inputs. Fine-tune and evaluate robot policies on human demonstration data, running controlled baseline comparisons, held-out split tests, and task performance evaluations under realistic test conditions. Translate policy evaluation insights into precise data recommendations—guiding perception and capture teams on which tasks, viewpoints, and annotations yield the highest policy improvement. Skills & Competencies Demonstrated experience training, fine-tuning, and evaluating robot manipulation or imitation learning policies (e.g., Diffusion Policies, VLAs, ACT). Strong Python and PyTorch capability with comfort building dataset interfaces, loaders, and annotation tooling alongside ML research. Deep understanding of evaluation leakage, dataset confounders, and the gap between offline loss metrics and physical robot task success. Experience working with temporal action segmentation, video annotations, spatial trajectories, and human-to-robot data transfer. Qualifications & Experience Background as a Robot Learning Engineer, Embodied AI Researcher, or Robotics ML Engineer. Proven track record of personally preparing training data, training or fine-tuning robot policies, and evaluating physical or simulated task performance. Hands-on implementation experience connecting dataset decisions directly to policy improvements, identifying confounders, and preventing data leakage. Background in physical robot manipulation, diffusion policies, vision-language-action models, or human-to-robot transfer is highly desirable. Role Details Timing: Immediate Start. Location: London (Remote). Package: Competitive base salary up to £150K + significant founding-engineer equity with absolute ownership over policy evaluation and dataset standards.

items.desc: Do you want to contribute to improving human health? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The Baranello Lab: Drawing from our expertise in the fields of topoisomerase and cancer biology, we aim to answer fundamental questions about how transcription, replication and DNA topology are functionally coordinated in human cells. We use state-of-the-art approaches to assess transcriptomic, epigenomic and topoisomerase activity profiles, as well as bioinformatics, advanced microscopy and drug screens to understand how topoisomerase regulation affects fundamental nuclear processes (key lab references: Baranello et al. Cell 2016; Wiegard et al. Molecular Cell 2021; Das et al. Molecular Cell 2022, Cameron et al. Nature Communications 2026). The overall aim of our research is to reveal novel cancer dependencies and develop new anti-cancer strategies more specific towards tumor cells and with fewer side-effects. We are a young and dynamic research team with a well-established collaborative network. The group is also associated to the laboratory of Dr. Levens at the National Institutes of Health in the US and Prof. Shirahige at the Institute of Quantitative Biology (IQB), Tokyo University, Japan. The successful applicant will thus be part of multiple networks of recognized scientists. The group is located in the Biomedicum, a top modern research building with a large repertoire of researchers and access to state-of-the-art infrastructure and facilities. Laura Baranello Lab The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student Topoisomerases are essential enzymes that regulate the topology of DNA favoring replication and transcription by cleaving/resealing DNA strands. Because cancer cells have higher rates of proliferation compared to normal cells, they are highly dependent on topoisomerase activity. Therefore, strategies to target topoisomerases could provide a mean to selectively affect cancer cells. The focus of this research project is to understand how topoisomerases are regulated during transcription to develop new ways to target these regulatory mechanisms and affect the viability of cancer cells. Recent evidence show that topoisomerases execute their function through interactions with partner proteins that modulate their activity to affect transcription (Baranello et al. Cell 2016; Das et al. Molecular Cell 2022, Cameron et al. Nature Communications 2026). Using biochemical and molecular biology approaches, DNA and RNA sequencing, and advanced microscopy, this project investigates how the transcription machinery controls topoisomerase activity in physiological and pathological conditions, and how this regulation affects topoisomerase nuclear dynamics. The PhD includes several short research stays (~3 months each) in the lab of Prof. Mazza (Hospital San Raffaele, Italy), where the student will learn and apply key techniques for the project. The findings are expected to open new strategies for targeting topoisomerases in cancer therapy, offering the student broad training across molecular biology, genomics, and advanced microscopy in an international collaborative setting. The PhD program at the Karolinska Institutet corresponds to 4 years full time studies. The project is a combination of practical laboratory work (wet-lab work) and computational analysis (programming in R and/or Python). The program also includes attendance to seminars, courses, and conferences. The PhD student will plan and execute experiments, analyze data, interpret, and present the results as well as write scientific articles, initially under supervision but with greater independence going forward. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. items.desc: The Mobile Robotics research line of the Robotics and Automation Unit at Eurecat Technology Center (Barcelona) is seeking a SLAM & Autonomous Navigation Researcher with a strong background in robotics software, localization, mapping and autonomous navigation, together with hands-on experience deploying and validating navigation algorithms on real mobile robotic platforms, including AMRs, agricultural robots and tractors, quadrupeds, and other autonomous vehicles. The selected candidate will focus on the development and integration of autonomous navigation technologies, with particular emphasis on SLAM, localization and multi-sensor state estimation, as well as path planning, reactive navigation and obstacle avoidance. We are particularly looking for a software-oriented robotics profile, with strong experience in ROS/ROS2, C++ and Python, capable of understanding, adapting and extending existing robotics software, developing new algorithms, and integrating navigation solutions across different robotic platforms and sensor configurations. The selected candidate is expected to work on: SLAM, localization and multi-sensor state estimation. 2D/3D mapping and navigation in GNSS-denied environments. Global and local path planning. Develop and integrate global/local planning, reactive navigation and obstacle avoidance capabilities. Integrate LiDAR, cameras, IMUs, GNSS, wheel odometry and other sensors into navigation stacks. Analyze, debug and improve navigation performance using datasets, simulation and real-world experiments. Contribute to national and European R&D projects, technical reports and scientific publications. Requirements: REQUERIMENTS: Academic Background MSc, PhD, or equivalent experience in Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Vision, Automation, Control Engineering, or related fields. Mandatory Strong background and hands-on experience in SLAM and robot localization, including the development, integration or modification of LiDAR-based and/or visual approaches, odometry and sensor fusion. Strong background in autonomous mobile robot navigation, including global/local path planning, reactive navigation and obstacle avoidance. Experience with ROS/ROS2 navigation frameworks such as Nav2 or equivalent custom navigation stacks, and good understanding of the different components of a complete autonomous navigation pipeline. Good understanding of robotic state estimation and sensor integration, including coordinate frames, transformations, calibration and synchronization. Proficiency in ROS/ROS2, C++ and Python. Experience understanding, debugging and modifying robotics software and adapting it to different platforms and sensor configurations. Hands-on experience integrating and validating navigation algorithms on real robotic platforms, including outdoor, unstructured and/or GNSS-denied environments. Nice to Have Experience with perception for autonomous navigation, including object/person tracking and perception-driven reactive navigation. Experience with LLMs, VLMs and/or VLAs for robotic autonomy, including natural-language commands and mission execution. Experience with Behaviour Trees for navigation and autonomous mission execution. Experience with SLAM frameworks such as Cartographer, RTAB-Map, LIO-SAM, FAST-LIO, ORB-SLAM or similar. Experience with LiDAR-inertial, visual-inertial or other advanced multi-sensor localization approaches. Experience with simulation environments such as Gazebo or Isaac Sim. Experience with aerial robotic platforms. Soft Skills & Practical Aspects Strong analytical, problem-solving and debugging skills. Ability to work autonomously and within a multidisciplinary robotics team. Good communication and teamwork skills. Fluent English; other languages are a plus. Availability to travel occasionally for integration and field-testing activities. WORKING ENVIRONMENT AND BENEFITS: Our laboratory is located in Cerdanyola del Vallès, just outside Barcelona (Spain). Barcelona, besides being easily connected to the rest of Europe, offers excellent quality of life and a vibrant robotics ecosystem rich with initiatives, research groups, robotics companies, and engaging events—with many more opportunities emerging continuously! items.desc: Join our Team About The Opportunity We are establishing a new AI-driven Digital ASIC research activity inside Ericsson Research. Our research thesis is that AI-driven design methodology is mandatory from day one — and that we drive the evolution of those tools rather than wait for it. The methodology itself is a research deliverable. This is a single-tier contributor role. Everyone works on the shared research threads, participates in challenge, and contributes to delivery. What differentiates contributors is the expert area(s) each of us brings to the team — the deep technical specialism that anchors our personal contribution. What You Will Do Drive the AI-driven methodology research deliverable: characterized AI-driven design flow, quantified PPA / lead-time / closure-effort deltas vs. a controlled traditional baseline, failure-mode taxonomy of AI-EDA tools, and the methodology playbook. Apply your expert area(s) inside the threads — both as the depth that makes the research credible, and as the lens through which you characterize AI-driven tooling at your part of the chain. Contribute to the controlled traditional baseline in your area(s) — without the baseline anchor, the team's PPA and lead-time claims aren't falsifiable. Co-design across the chain. The boundary between architecture, RTL, verification, physical design, test and packaging is fluid here; contributors are expected to engage beyond their primary area. Engage with Ericsson's product organizations, tool vendors and external research partners as the work and the rotation calls for it. Maintain cross-site presence (Lund / Lindholmen). Contribute openly to the team's culture. Work on shared research threads — typically 2–3 active at any time. Take rotating turns on delivery lead and operations. The Skills You Bring Genuine enthusiasm for AI-driven design and confidence that AI-assisted methods are the right direction for silicon and systems. Demonstrated depth in at least one primary expert area, with working competence in one or two adjacent areas, evidenced through tape-outs, open-source contributions, publications, hands-on projects, joint academic roles, or comparable experience. Typical expert areas include: Software, SW architecture, SW stack and low-level drivers EDA tools and design environment CPU architecture, compute architecture, packet routing, accelerators DSP, signal chains, hardware-efficient algorithms, AI accelerators Verification — model to RTL, RTL to gates, SW emulator RTL implementation — model to RTL, RTL to gates Physical design — P&R, low power ASIC production test Packaging, chiplet, integration, interfaces, DC-DC power Comfort with a peer-led, one-tier research culture: you challenge and accept challenge openly, and align once decisions are made. Ability to work in a cross-site rhythm (regular remote sessions, periodic co-location, strong async collaboration). Strong curiosity and rigour, treating methodology evolution as part of the research, and willingness to work beyond your core discipline when the problem demands it. Why join Ericsson? At Ericsson, you´ll have an outstanding opportunity. The chance to use your skills and imagination to push the boundaries of what´s possible. To build solutions never seen before to some of the world’s toughest problems. You´ll be challenged, but you won’t be alone. You´ll be joining a team of diverse innovators, all driven to go beyond the status quo to craft what comes next. What happens once you apply? We truly believe that by collaborating with people with different experiences we drive innovation, which is essential for our future growth. We encourage people from all backgrounds to apply and realize their full potential as part of our Ericsson team. Ericsson is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. learn more. items.desc: As a Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence Engineer within the Image Processing UK department, you will play a critical role in the development of MBDA products and technologies. You will be an important member of a department that produces world-beating algorithms. Salary : Up to £58,000 depending on experience Dynamic (hybrid) working : 4 - 5 days per week on-site due to workload classification Security Clearance : British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team. What we can offer you: Company bonus: Up to £2,500 (based on company performance and will vary year to year) Pension: maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14% Overtime: opportunity for paid overtime Flexi Leave: Up to 15 additional days Flexible working: We welcome applicants who are looking for flexible working arrangements Enhanced parental leave: offers up to 26 weeks for maternity, adoption and shared parental leave -enhancements are available for paternity leave, neonatal leave and fertility testing and treatments Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more… The opportunity: As a Computer Vision and Artificial Intelligence Engineer, you will be an essential team member at an exciting time of growth and opportunity. The algorithms that you will research, develop and evaluate will form part of the next generation of complex weapon systems. You will be an important member of a department that produces world-beating algorithms that use imaging sensors to provide situational awareness, and guide weapons to their target with maximum precision. We have a detailed understanding of the interaction between missile subsystems and have a direct influence on meaningful design decisions. We are a firm supporter of equal opportunity for all, and are proud to be a diverse engineering team. Image Processing UK is an innovative, cohesive department where the contributions of each individual have real value. As part of our team you will benefit from an excellent working culture built on individual empowerment and mutual support. What we're looking for from you: Preferably PhD qualified in a related area, either holding or completing the PhD, or relevant Post-Doctoral or Industry experience would be highly beneficial A degree with strong mathematical content e.g. Mathematics, Engineering (e.g. Aeronautical, Mechanical, etc), Physics, Computer Science, or similar A keen curiosity about cutting-edge technologies and their applications Specific knowledge in any of the following areas is of benefit: Image Processing Algorithms: Segmentation, Filter Design, Noise Removal, Compression, Super Resolution Computer Vision Algorithms: Tracking, Optical Flow, Particle Filtering, Pose Estimation Deep Learning techniques: Detection, Classification, Tracking, Siamese Networks Inverse Problems / Computational Imaging: Sparse Coding, Compressive Sensing Machine Learning: Support Vector Machines, Neural Networks Domain Specific Signal Processing: Multi/Hyper-Spectral, RF, IR, SAR, STAP The primary development environments used within the department are Matlab/Simulink and Python (including PyTorch Deep Learning libraries). What's in it for you? Every day you will work in a friendly and motivated team You will play a key role in the development of our complex weapon systems, and gain in-depth knowledge of their design and functionality You will collaborate with other engineers from a broad range of subject areas You will be working on cutting-edge technological innovations You will have the opportunity to work within an international field that has strong links to MBDA sites in France and Germany that will provide the opportunity for European travel You will have the opportunity to attend workshops and conferences both nationally and internationally We invest in your success and have development, leadership and mentorship programmes available Our company: Peace is not a given, Freedom is not a given, Sovereignty is not a given MBDA is a leading defence organisation. We are proud of the role we play in supporting the Armed Forces who protect our nations. We partner with governments to work together towards a common goal, defending our freedom. We are proud of our employee-led networks, examples include: Gender Equality, Pride, Menopause Matters, Parents and Carers, Armed Forces, Ethnic Diversity, Neurodiversity and more… We recognise that everyone is unique, and we encourage you to speak to us should you require any advice, support or adjustments throughout our recruitment process. Follow us on LinkedIn (MBDA), X (@MBDA_UK), Instagram (MBDA_UK) and Glassdoor or visit our MBDA Careers website for more …

items.desc: At ZEISS Corporate Research & Technology, we work at the frontier of science and technology to identify emerging computing architectures and translate them into future technology opportunities for ZEISS. We are looking for a Research Scientist who understands accelerator architectures and fundamentally new computing concepts driven by the latest AI developments – from CPUs, GPUs and TPUs to custom accelerators, optical and analog computing, novel memory architectures and new forms of heterogeneous computing. The position combines strategic technology exploration with hands-on technical work. You will build targeted proof-of-concepts to validate promising architecture concepts, while engaging with startups, research groups and technology partners to understand emerging solutions first-hand, assess their maturity and identify the most promising approaches for ZEISS Your role Analyze AI computing systems end-to-end: Understand how training and inference workloads run on modern data-center architectures and identify the fundamental bottlenecks in compute, memory, interconnects and energy efficiency. Explore next-generation computing architectures: Evaluate established, emerging and fundamentally new concepts – custom accelerators, chiplets, in- and near-memory computing, optical and analog computing and heterogeneous systems. Build and benchmark proof-of-concepts: Translate architectural hypotheses into hands-on demonstrators and assess their potential quantitatively against the state of the art. Scout and recommend: Engage with startups, research groups and technology providers, judge maturity and differentiation, and distinguish fundamental technology shifts from incremental improvements. Your profile A university degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering with a focus on digital systems or computer architecture, or a closely related discipline. A PhD or equivalent research experience is welcome. Expertise in at least two of the following areas: computer architecture and systems; machine-learning systems and AI infrastructure; heterogeneous accelerators and emerging computing architectures. A systems-level understanding of modern AI technology stacks – training and inference workflows, numerical kernels, memory hierarchies, data movement, interconnects, accelerator hardware and system software – and the ability to explain where bottlenecks occur, why, and which architectural approaches can address them. Programming skills in Python and/or C/C++; experience with GPU computing, parallel programming, distributed systems, compilers, runtimes or HPC environments is an advantage. Curiosity and openness toward external technology developments, and the ease to engage directly with startups, research groups and technology providers, understand their approaches in technical depth and assess their relevance. An analytical eye for technology trends, the flexibility to revise your view when the evidence changes, and the ability to present complex topics clearly. Business-fluent English is required. Your ZEISS Recruiting Team Friederike Kirklar-Harms

items.desc: AI-udvikler søges til Dansk Center for Partikelterapi, AUH, Dansk Center for Partikelterapi (DCPT) søger en fysiker, hospitalsfysiker, datalog, softwareingeniør eller lignende profil til softwareudvikling inden for adaptiv protonterapi. DCPT er et nationalt center, der giver strålebehandling med protonterapi. Vores mission er at levere protonterapi af højest mulig kvalitet til alle relevante danske kræftpatienter. Alle vores udviklingsopgaver er forankret i brede tværfaglige, lokale, nationale og/eller internationale udviklings- og forskningsgrupper. I denne nyoprettede stilling er der fokus på at løse de kliniske behov bl.a. gennem forskning, som bliver en vigtig del af din dagligdag. Du vil blive tilknyttet gruppen af fysikere og dosimetrister, hvis driftsopgave er at planlægge individuelle protonbehandlinger og kvalitetssikre behandlinger og tilhørende udstyr. Gruppen udvikler behandlingsteknikker i tæt samarbejde med læger, sygeplejersker, radiografer, m.fl., samt de ansatte i vores forskningsafdeling. DCPT har udviklet kunstig intelligens til at forbedre billedkvaliteten af de billeder vi anvender til at adaptere patientbehandlingen, samt til segmentering af medicinske billeder. Vi ønsker at styrke denne indsats og målrette den mod udviklingen af adaptiv protonterapi, hvor den individuelle tilpasning af behandlingen sker hurtigere og på daglig basis. Det er afgørende, at du har følgende kompetencer solid erfaring med maskinlæring og deep learning anvendt på billeddata - gerne 3D medicinsk billedbehandling: segmentering, registrering eller billede-til-billede-modeller rutine i PyTorch eller tilsvarende, og erfaring med at træne, evaluere og fejlsøge modeller på virkelige datasæt håndværksmæssig disciplin i kodning: versionsstyring, test, dokumentation og kodegennemgang. Du skal kunne bygge noget, som andre end dig selv kan overtage og videreudvikle evnen til at arbejde tæt sammen med fysikere og klinikere, og til at sætte dig ind i et domæne du ikke selv er uddannet i. Derudover er det en fordel, hvis du har kendskab til medicinsk billedbehandling i praksis: DICOM og DICOM-RT, strålebehandlingsplanlægning, scripting mod et planlægningssystem erfaring med at drifte modeller i produktion: containere, inferensservere, versionering af modeller og data og overvågning serverdrift og databaser kendskab til softwareudvikling under EU's forordning om medicinsk udstyr, herunder undtagelsen for egenudviklet software, samt kvalitetssystemer, risikostyring og validering baggrund som fysiker eller erfaring fra stråleterapi. Med ansættelse ved DCPT skal du være indstillet på at kunne brede dig ud over flere forskelligartede opgaver, der vil veksle mellem udviklingsopgaver og driftsorienterede opgaver. Din opgave- og projektportefølje vil udvikle sig over tid, og afhængigt af dine kompetencer vil den komme til at indeholde forskning, udvikling og drift. Uanset hvor vægten kommer til at ligge, skal du konstruktivt, effektivt og aktivt kunne indgå i samarbejder med forskere og klinikere kunne sætte dig ind i brugeres og domænets behov være ambitiøs og have lyst til at fuldføre dit arbejde med både praktiske og akademiske resultater være indstillet på at løse mangeartede opgaver. Det forventes, at du i samarbejde med DCPT's øvrige akademiske medarbejdere deltager aktivt i forsknings- og udviklingsopgaver. Du kommer til at indgå i et tværfagligt miljø med fysikere, læger, sygeplejersker, radiografer og andre, der ligeledes arbejder for at udvikle teknologi og klinisk udnyttelse af protonterapi. Er du kandidat, der opfylder indgangskrav til uddannelse som hospitalsfysiker, så vil centeret tilbyde dig uddannelsen. Hvis ikke, vil vi tilbyde lignende skræddersyet uddannelse og træning. For yderligere information om stillingerne kontakt hospitalsfysiker, lektor Jesper Kallehauge på mail jespkall@rm.dk eller cheffysiker Ole Nørrevang på tlf. 2117 4193. Bemærk at Jesper Kallehauge ikke er tilgængelig for yderligere information før efter den 27. oktober. Stillingen er som udgangspunkt en fuldtidsstilling. Da Region Midtjylland løbende gennemfører besparelser og omorganiseringer, vil medarbejdere i omplacering, der søger stillingen, have fortrinsret. Region Midtjylland er jf. EU’s løngennemsigtighedsdirektiv, der trådte i kraft 7. juni 2026 forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startløn eller et interval for startløn for en stilling inden du tilbydes ansættelse. Her finder du Region Midtjyllands lønkatalog for de fleste faggrupper og stillinger, som findes i Region Midtjylland: Gennemsigtighed forud for ansættelse - Medarbejder.rm.dk

items.desc: Dans le cadre du laboratoire commun "AI-Native Communications" lancé par Orange et le CEA, dédié à la recherche sur les communications sémantiques pour les réseaux 6G et futurs, nous recherchons un ingénieur en communication sémantique 6G . Ce programme vise à concevoir des réseaux plus intelligents, sobres et efficaces, en intégrant de nouvelles approches où le sens de l’information prime sur la transmission exacte des données. Intégré dans le Service Technologies Sans Fil (STSF) et sous la responsabilité du chef de projet, vous aurez pour principales missions de : Concevoir et valider des algorithmes novateurs destinés aux futurs standards 6G, avec un focus spécifique sur les communications sémantiques. Développer des méthodes et solutions visant à optimiser les performances des systèmes, tout en respectant des contraintes strictes en matière: d’efficacité énergétique, de consommation des ressources réseau, Piloter la mise en œuvre d’une plateforme numérique de validation, intégrant :l’interfaçage de chaînes de traitement (Python/Matlab) avec des plateformes matérielles et logicielles haut de gamme, la validation expérimentale des concepts développés, dans un contexte représentatif des communications 6G. Profil du candidat Vous êtes diplômé d'un Master of Science (ou équivalent) en traitement numérique du signal, communications sans fil, ou domaine connexe. Dans l'idéal vous disposez d'un doctorat dans l'un de ces domaines. Compétences techniques requises Expertise avérée en traitement numérique du signal appliqué aux communications sans fil, Maîtrise du machine learning et de l’intelligence artificielle dans le contexte des systèmes de communication sans fil, Solide expérience en développement d’algorithmes de traitement du signal, avec une pratique confirmée de Python ou Matlab, Compétences techniques souhaitées Expérience en prototypage matériel sur SoC ARM/Xilinx (notamment plateformes RFSoC), constituant un atout important pour le poste, Expérience appréciée Publications scientifiques dans des revues ou conférences, ainsi que participation à des colloques ou séminaires. Expérience en dépôt de brevets ou en gestion de portefeuille de propriété intellectuelle Vous avez encore un doute ? Nous vous proposons : Un environnement unique de recherché dédié à des thématiques à fort enjeu sociétal, Une expérience sur des thématiques à la pointe de l’innovation, liées à des développements industriels concrets, Des formations pour renforcer vos compétences ou en acquérir de nouvelles, Un équilibre vie privé – vie professionnelle reconnu, Un compte épargne temps afin de gérer au mieux vos congés et RTT, Une épargne entreprise abondée par le CEA, Un poste au cœur de la métropole grenobloise, facilement accessible via la mobilité douce favorisée par le CEA, Une rémunération selon vos diplômes et votre expérience, bénéficiant d’une progression régulière, Un environnement propice aux évolutions professionnelles, Un CSE actif en termes de loisirs et d’activités extraprofessionnelles, Une politique diversité et inclusion : nous sommes engagés depuis plus de 30 ans dans l’inclusion et le maintien dans l’emploi des personnes en situation de handicap Conformément aux engagements pris par le CEA en faveur de l'intégration des personnes en situation de handicap, cet emploi est ouvert à toutes et à tous. Le CEA propose des aménagements et/ou des possibilités d'organisation pour faciliter l'intégration de tous les candidats. items.desc: Job Description Position Details School of Engineering University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK As this vacancy has limited funding the maximum salary that can be offered is Grade 7, salary £36,636 Grade: 7 Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to October 2027 Closing date: 25th October 2026 Background To create and contribute to the creation of knowledge by undertaking a specified range of activities within an established research programme and/or specific research project. This Research Fellow position is based in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Birmingham and will support an industry-funded research project focused on engines operating on non-fossil fuels and their integration into hybrid electric vehicle powertrains. The research will involve engine modelling and simulation, intelligent control strategy development, and data-driven calibration, applying AI and optimisation techniques, including machine learning and metaheuristic algorithms, to improve engine performance and efficiency and reduce emissions. Control strategies will be implemented and validated using Pi OpenECU and Cosworth ECU platforms, supported by engine test bench experiments. The project will also address hybrid powertrain development, including engine–electric motor integration, coordinated torque control, and energy management optimisation, in close collaboration with industrial partners. Summary Of Role Develop and apply AI and optimisation techniques, including machine learning and metaheuristic algorithms, to engine modelling, intelligent control strategy development, and data-driven calibration for engines operating on non-fossil fuels. Conduct engine test bench experiments, analyse experimental data, and implement and validate engine control strategies using Pi OpenECU and Cosworth ECU platforms. Contribute to hybrid powertrain development, including engine–electric motor integration, coordinated torque control, and energy management optimisation to improve efficiency and reduce emissions. Develop and validate vehicle-level torque distribution control strategies to optimise traction, vehicle stability, and energy efficiency. Work closely with industrial collaborators, support student supervision, and contribute to research publications, technical reports, and funding applications. Main Duties The responsibilities may include some but not all of the responsibilities outlined below. Develop research objectives and methodologies for engine modelling, intelligent control, and calibration for engines operating on non-fossil fuels. Develop, calibrate, and validate engine, powertrain, and vehicle models using tools such as AVL CRUISE, IPG CarMaker, and MATLAB/Simulink, supported by experimental data and system identification methods. Investigate the effects of non-fossil fuels on combustion characteristics, engine performance, fuel consumption, and emissions through modelling and engine test bench experiments. Develop and apply Artificial Intelligence and optimisation techniques, including machine learning and metaheuristic algorithms, to data-driven engine modelling, intelligent control strategy development, and automated calibration. Implement, test, and calibrate engine control strategies using Pi OpenECU and Cosworth ECU platforms, including sensor and actuator integration, CAN communication, and data acquisition. Plan and conduct engine test bench experiments under steady-state and transient conditions representative of real-world driving cycles, and analyse experimental data to refine models and control strategies. Contribute to hybrid powertrain development, including system integration, coordinated torque control, and energy management optimisation to improve efficiency and reduce emissions. Develop and validate vehicle-level torque distribution control strategies to improve traction, vehicle stability, and energy efficiency using learning-based methods. Support related experimental research in fuel sprays, combustion, and proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells. Contribute to research funding applications, technical reports, and project deliverables. Disseminate research findings through publications, presentations, and seminars. Provide technical support and training to PhD students working on related research topics. Work closely with academic and industrial partners to coordinate research activities, review progress, and deliver project objectives. Participate in public engagement, enterprise, and knowledge transfer activities as required. These indicative responsibilities may also be included in a research role at grade 6. Person Specification A PhD (or thesis submitted) in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Solid experience in engine modelling, simulation, and calibration using IPG CarMaker, AVL tools, or MATLAB/Simulink, with knowledge of non-fossil fuels. Experience in intelligent control and data-driven calibration, with practical …

items.desc: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. As a Research Engineer on the Orchestral team, you will help build the agentic platform we use to train and evaluate our models. Orchestral is the system our researchers rely on to run training and evaluation at scale — from the rollout engine that powers agentic workflows to the infrastructure that keeps their workloads running reliably. What you build becomes the foundation the whole science team works on. Your work will span the platform's core: the library, tooling, abstractions and rollout engine — including new capabilities like long-running tasks, subagents and RL features — and the machinery that runs data and jobs at scale, with a focus on resiliency, routing and request handling. You will own significant pieces end to end, from design to production. This is a software engineering role rather than an ML or infrastructure-operations one: RL or PyTorch experience is not required, and you will spend your time building the platform, not operating it. You will be building a distributed RL system, with the scientists as your users. What You Will Do Design and build the core of the Orchestral platform: the library, abstractions and tooling researchers use to train and evaluate models. Build and evolve the rollout engine, shipping new capabilities such as long-running tasks and subagents. Run Orchestral as a production system: keep training and evaluation workloads reliable at scale. Improve how data and jobs flow through the platform as usage grows — scheduling, routing and request handling. Treat researchers as your users: understand their workflows and turn recurring needs into robust, shared tooling. Raise the bar on engineering quality across the platform: testing, code review, CI/CD, observability and documentation. Contribute to open-source rollout-engine and agent-infrastructure projects where it benefits the platform. What We're Looking For Experience directly building and debugging complex distributed systems at scale, with an emphasis on reliability and scalability. Strong Python skills and solid software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD. A builder mindset: you have constructed systems from the ground up, not just operated polished ones. A track record in small teams running complex systems at scale — for example in finance, crypto or ad tech. Self-starter, low-ego and collaborative, with a product mindset toward your users. Curiosity about ML and RL — this experience is not required, but a desire to learn is. Nice-to-haves Hands-on experience with Ray or similar distributed-computing frameworks. Open-source contributions, especially to rollout-engine or agent-infrastructure projects such as SLIME, verl or PrimeRL. Experience building or working with agentic workflows and environments. items.desc: Research Associate (m/f/d) Institute for Embedded Systems Remuneration EG 13 TV-L ID 23726WE13 Start of employment as soon as possible Application deadline 30.11.2026 Scope full time and fixed term until 3 years The Computer Engineering group at the Institute of Embedded Systems, Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) is looking for a dedicated PhD researcher. We are a dynamic, international team focused on advancing Electronic Design Automation (EDA) for embedded and cyber-physical systems. Our goal is to develop tools and methodologies that rigorously yield high-quality, reliable results for increasingly complex system designs. Specifically, we are having ongoing projects in security analysis, testing of digital systems and AI-based modelling of cyber-physical systems. Our group is tightly coupled to the research training group CAUSE that studies the design of self-explaining systems. As a researcher and PhD candidate in our group, you will drive state-of-the-art research in modeling, testing, verification, diagnosis, and debugging. A uniquely exciting aspect of your research will be the incorporation of recent Generative AI (GenAI). You will investigate novel design automation methods to improve efficiency and quality while adhering to rigorous guarantees on correctness. YOUR TASKS Conduct independent and collaborative research projects Design and implement new software tools for system design Present research results at conferences and publish articles in peer-reviewed academic journals Engage in the teaching activities of the group Contribute to third-party funding applications YOUR PROFILE Requirements Completed scientific university studies (masters degree or equivalent) in Computer Science or a tightly related field Desired knowledge and personal skills Strong skills in software engineering and computer science theory Interest in system and automation tool development with background in dependability Proficiency in both German and English to effectively participate in our bilingual teaching environment A rigorous, independent work ethic paired with a collaborative mindset to thrive in our international team OUR OFFER Scientific qualification with the opportunity to pursue a PhD A job in an interesting, friendly and appreciative working environment Intensive introduction and onboarding Internal offers for health promotion and special conditions in gyms At the heart of TU Hamburg’s research, teaching and transfer of technology is the guiding principle of developing technology for people. The TU Hamburg sees itself in this context as a family-friendly and sustainable university with high performance and quality standards that strives for excellence in all its research fields. Interdisciplinarity, innovation, regionality and internationality are binding principles in our actions. With currently around 8.000 students, 110 professors and 1.650 employees, the TU Hamburg is characterised by short decision-making processes and close cooperation between the board, the institutes, the deans of studies, the research areas and the administration. We identify ourselves with a modern leadership culture and cultivate appreciative interaction. Note regarding the Standard Enquiry under Section 34a of the Hamburg Security Clearance Act: The department will submit an enquiry to the State Office for the Protection of the Constitution regarding any information it holds on the person selected in the recruitment process, provided that the legal requirements are met (information on the Standard Inquiry and data protection notices ). For further information please contact Prof. Görschwin Fey, Tel.-Nr. +49 40 30601 3697, Email: goerschwin.fey@tuhh.de We value diversity, therefore all applications are welcome, regardless of gender, gender identity, ethnic origin, nationality, age, religion and belief, disability, sexual orientation and identity or social background. items.desc: Description De L'entreprise Ubisoft est une référence mondiale du jeu vidéo, avec des équipes réparties aux quatre coins du monde qui créent des expériences de jeu originales et mémorables, de Assassin’s Creed à Rainbow Six en passant par Just Dance et bien d’autres encore. Nous croyons que la diversité des points de vue fait progresser à la fois les joueurs et les équipes. Si vous êtes passionné·e par l’innovation et que vous souhaitez repousser les limites du divertissement, rejoignez notre aventure et aidez-nous à créer l’inconnu ! Studio pionnier d’Ubisoft, le studio de Paris est à l’origine des premiers succès de l’éditeur suite à sa création en 1992. Il est aujourd’hui à la tête de licences incontournables comme Just Dance, Ghost Recon ou Mario + The Lapins Crétins. Ubisoft Paris s’est également construit une solide réputation comme partenaire de choix dans les collaborations inter-studios comme Watch Dogs, Skull & Bones, Beyond Good & Evil 2 ou encore Star Wars. Fort de cette expérience, le studio continue d’aller plus loin en termes de créativité en travaillant sur des projets très prometteurs encore non-annoncés. Regroupant 750 talents de 35 nationalités, Ubisoft Paris est aujourd’hui le plus grand studio de France et l’un des plus expérimentés de l’industrie. Les jeunes talents peuvent bénéficier de la présence importante de profils seniors, dans les métiers créatifs, techniques ou artistiques. Chacun·e reste animé·e par la même passion : repousser les limites du possible et proposer de nouvelles expériences à nos joueurs et joueuses. Prêt·es à rallier l’aventure ? Rejoignez-nous au Studio de Paris ! Description Du Poste En nous rejoignant sur ce poste, vous intégrerez une équipe multidisciplinaire (data, programmation, game & narrative design, animation, etc.), guidée par une question simple et ambitieuse : parmi toutes les possibilités offertes par l’IA générative, lesquelles sont réellement intéressantes et fun pour le gameplay ? L’équipe a pour mission de tester de nouvelles expériences auprès de joueurs et joueuses, et d’équiper les créateur·rices pour imaginer des interactions plus dynamiques, immersives et surprenantes — jusqu’à faire émerger des features impossibles à réaliser autrement. Son quotidien s’inscrit à la croisée de la R&D, du développement produit, de la création de jeux courts et de la collaboration multi-studios, au service des gameplays de demain. Au sein de l’équipe responsable de l’analyse des données et des projets data science, détachée dans une production de jeu vidéo, vous apportez vos connaissances en Machine Learning et en analyse de données en général aux équipes de développement afin d’exploiter le potentiel de l’Intelligence Artificielle au sein du design de nos jeux. Vos missions seront les suivantes : Contribuer à la faisabilité technique des systèmes gameplay basés sur l’IA. Identifier des algorithmes pertinents (génératifs, information retrieval, classification…) et les adapter pour un usage production (fine-tuning, optimisation, intégration). Mettre en place les processus d’évaluation pertinents Déployer ces algorithmes sur des cloud internes ou externes de manière robuste et scalable, en suivant les meilleurs pratiques en terme de développement et de MLOps, en collaboration avec les ingénieurs du projets Implémenter des techniques à partir de papiers de recherche dans une démarche d'innovation/R&D Qualifications Vous disposez d’une première expérience significative en tant que Machine Learning Engineer et avez mis en production différents algorithmes de Generative AI, Vous avez une connaissance poussée des algorithmes de NLP (comme SentenceBERT, Llama 2, Mistral ou Qwen 3) et vous savez les fine-tuner, Vous avez une bonne maitrise de Python et de Tensorflow ou PyTorch, Vous avez une première expérience avec Docker, Le jeu vidéo est une passion pour vous, Votre très bonne capacité d’écoute et de compréhension vous permet de traduire facilement les besoins des clients en spécifications, Vous êtes en mesure d’adapter vos analyses et votre discours pour atteindre un large public, Vous faites preuve d’autonomie et de curiosité. Enfin, votre aisance en anglais vous permet d’échanger à l’écrit comme à l’oral avec des interlocuteurs variés. Ce sont des + : Vous avez une bonne maitrise du C++, C# ou Rust Vous savez comment utiliser des LLM (du prompt engineering aux approches plus complexes comme Tree of Thoughts) Vous savez comment optimiser la taille et le temps d’inférence des modèles (ex : quantization, LoRA…) Vous avez une affinité avec les jeux de rôle, les jeux narratifs... Informations supplémentaires En tant qu’employeur, Ubisoft offre à tous les mêmes opportunités d’accès à l’emploi, sans distinction notamment de genre, ethnicité, religion, orientation sexuelle, statut social, handicap et d’âge. Ubisoft veille à développer un environnement de travail inclusif qui reflète la diversité de sa communauté de joueurs dans ses équipes.

items.card: About The Role, Shortlisting And Interviews Email Address: bsfellowships@manchester.ac.uk. General enquiries and administrative support recruitmentservices.people@manchester.ac.uk Technical and job portal support https://jobseekersupport.jobtrain.co.uk/support/home Applications close at midnight on the closing date. Further particulars (with person specification) linked below.
items.desc: Applications are invited for a research fellowship focused upon how people and AI can and should work together in a collaborative partnership. The fellowship is jointly hosted by the University of Manchester, Manchester Metropolitan University and the University of Salford, and supported by the UK Government. The fellowship is initially through until March 2028, with the possibility of an extension. Applicants are requested to submit a brief research proposal addressing the topic of human-AI collaboration with their application. If successful they will be required to revise this proposal, in consultation with colleagues from UK Government, both to address government priorities and to improve the fit of the proposal with the demands of the National Security context, where advances in AI capability could give significant efficiency gains but must be balanced against a strong regulatory regime. Some of the research will assume a standard academic form and fellows will be expected to pursue publication in relevant academic journals, subject to approval from the government sponsor. Some may be classified and intended for use by UK Government and their partner organisations only. Fellows will therefore gain experience of two very different research environments and of negotiating the complexities of working between them. The Fellow will have a base within one of the partner universities. They will have mentors both within their University and UK Government, to offer guidance and support. Mentors from the organisations will work together to ensure coherence and consistency in their advice and support. Fellows will be required to be in Manchester several days a week and so are expected either to be located in the North-West or willing to relocate. Applicants should have completed or at least submitted a relevant PhD and have expertise in computer science, AI, machine learning and/or an intersection of those fields. This expertise should be explained in a letter of application and demonstrated in the abovementioned proposal, which short-listed candidates will be expected to present at interview. The fellow must be eligible and willing to apply for national security clearance at a minimum level of Enhanced Security Clearance (eSC) and a preferred level of Enhanced Developed Vetting (eDV), making them subject to the provisions of the Official Secrets Act (which includes restrictions on travel to certain countries). UK nationals currently resident in the UK will normally be eligible, but all applicants should carefully consider their eligibility before applying for the fellowship. Information about vetting and clearance can be found on the UK Government Security Clearance website. The employer reserves the right to terminate a fellowship in the event of a loss of security clearance. Our benefits include: Generous employer contribution pension 29 days annual leave plus bank holidays, along with Christmas closure Ride to work and EV car scheme available For more information, please see University of Manchester Benefits. You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working here. We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our Freedom of Speech Policy. Enquiries About The Role, Shortlisting And Interviews Email Address: bsfellowships@manchester.ac.uk. General enquiries and administrative support recruitmentservices.people@manchester.ac.uk Technical and job portal support https://jobseekersupport.jobtrain.co.uk/support/home Applications close at midnight on the closing date. items.card: ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Computational Biology & AI Solutions Specialist to help translate scientific and business needs into practical, responsible and scalable data and AI solutions. items.desc: COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY & AI SOLUTIONS SPECIALIST Driving bioinformatics and AI adoption across R&D and business functions _________________________________________________________________________ Cantanhede, Portugal | Computational role - hybrid ABOUT EXOGENUS THERAPEUTICS Exogenus Therapeutics is a biotechnology company developing multifactorial, disease-modifying biologics for regenerative medicine. Our lead programme, Exo-101, is an extracellular-vesicle-enriched secretome in development for knee osteoarthritis. We are also exploring applications in cisplatin-induced hearing loss and other regenerative medicine indications. We combine scientific rigour, collaboration and responsible innovation to advance new therapies for patients. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Computational Biology & AI Solutions Specialist to help translate scientific and business needs into practical, responsible and scalable data and AI solutions. Working across R&D and business development, you will combine hands-on bioinformatics with the evaluation, implementation and adoption of AI-enabled tools for data analysis, knowledge management and competitive intelligence. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys working with complex biological datasets, applying emerging technologies to research challenges and collaborating across scientific disciplines. WHAT YOU WILL DO Computational Biology and Bioinformatics: Develop and maintain pipelines for transcriptomic, proteomic and other omics data analyses. Integrate and analyse datasets from multi-omics experiments. Establish appropriate standards for data quality, documentation, version control and reproducibility. Translate analytical results into clear outputs for multidisciplinary R&D teams. AI solutions and cross-functional enablement: Identify and implement AI-based tools and platforms to enhance the company’s’ activities, including research and innovation workflows and business development. Develop guidance, training and reusable workflows to support effective adoption. Implement and maintain platforms for competitive intelligence, including monitoring of scientific publications, patents, clinical trials and market developments. Contribute to the establishment of best practices for data management, reproducibility and analytics. ESSENTIAL EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS MSc or PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Data Science, Biotechnology, Life Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Proven background in bioinformatics and computational data analysis. Hands-on experience evaluating, implementing or integrating AI-enabled tools into scientific or business workflows, including the ability to define use cases, test outputs, document limitations and support user adoption. Experience using AI-powered platforms and tools for data analysis, information retrieval or decision support. Experience analysing biological datasets, particularly omics data. Knowledge of data integration methodologies and workflows. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with attention to detail. Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary R&D teams. Self-initiative and ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Curiosity and enthusiasm for applying emerging technologies to research challenges. Excellent proficiency in English (mandatory); knowledge of Portuguese (desirable). WHAT WE OFFER Work with a multidisciplinary team developing innovative medicines, with a special focus on extracellular vesicle-enriched secretome technologies. Annual gross salary within the range of €30.000–€40.0000, depending on the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications, plus meal allowance. Flexible working arrangements, including the possibility of hybrid work. Professional development through internal learning, workshops, conferences and relevant training. An open, respectful working environment where people are encouraged to contribute ideas and different perspectives. Informal team activities and opportunities to connect across the company. INCLUSION AND ACCESSIBILITY At Exogenus Therapeutics, we are not just a team, we are a family that values innovation, collaboration, and the drive to revolutionize healthcare. Our culture thrives on teamwork, mutual respect, and a shared passion for making a significant impact in the EV field. We believe that our employees are our greatest asset, and we are committed to supporting their professional and personal growth. Exogenus Therapeutics is committed to creating equal opportunities and an inclusive recruitment process and workplace. We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. HOW TO APPLY Please email your CV and motivation letter explaining your interest in the role and the most relevant experience for the role, in a single pdf document titled Computational Biology & AI Solutions …

Fort de cette expérience, le studio continue d’aller plus loin en termes de créativité en travaillant sur des projets très prometteurs encore non-annoncés. Regroupant 750 talents de 35 nationalités, Ubisoft Paris est aujourd’hui le plus grand studio de France et l’un des plus expérimentés de l’industrie. Les jeunes talents peuvent bénéficier de la présence importante de profils seniors, dans les métiers créatifs, techniques ou artistiques. Chacun·e reste animé·e par la même passion : repousser les limites du possible et proposer de nouvelles expériences à nos joueurs et joueuses. Prêt·es à rallier l’aventure ? Rejoignez-nous au Studio de Paris ! Description Du Poste En nous rejoignant sur ce poste, vous intégrerez une équipe multidisciplinaire (data, programmation, game & narrative design, animation, etc.), guidée par une question simple et ambitieuse : parmi toutes les possibilités offertes par l’IA générative, lesquelles sont réellement intéressantes et fun pour le gameplay ? L’équipe a pour mission de tester de nouvelles expériences auprès de joueurs et joueuses, et d’équiper les créateur·rices pour imaginer des interactions plus dynamiques, immersives et surprenantes — jusqu’à faire émerger des features impossibles à réaliser autrement. Son quotidien s’inscrit à la croisée de la R&D, du développement produit, de la création de jeux courts et de la collaboration multi-studios, au service des gameplays de demain. Dans le cadre de ce poste, vous rejoindrez une équipe développant un produit technologique favorisant l'intégration de l’IA au sein des fonctionnalités de nos jeux. Au sein de nos studios de production, vous pourrez apporter vos connaissances en Data Science afin de construire des expériences de jeux uniques. Missions Au sein de l’équipe du produit technologique intégrant l’IA générative dans nos gameplays, vous apportez vos connaissances en Data Science et Machine Learning afin de prototyper et modéliser des solutions permettant la création de nouvelles expériences de jeu: Identifier des objectifs en fonction des spécifications partagées par les équipes de design et à travers l’analyse des données joueurs et définir des protocoles d’évaluation Concevoir des prototypes et entrainer des modèles pour répondre à ces objectifs Collaborer avec les Machine Learning Engineers pour transférer les prototypes et définir les critères de succès en vue de leur intégration. Collaborer avec les designers pour analyser les comportements de vos IA et identifier des pistes d’améliorations du jeu. Identifier les opportunités d’expérimentation et d’innovation. Communiquer sur vos travaux et vos résultats de façon pédagogique pour un public varié. Qualifications Vous disposez au moins d’une première expérience significative en tant que Data Scientist, durant laquelle vous avez pu mener des projets sur des produits interactifs (jeux, apps, systèmes temps réel …), Vous avez une bonne maitrise de Python ainsi que Tensorflow ou PyTorch (avoir une expérience en pyspark est un +), Vous disposez de solides bases en statistiques et méthodes d’évaluation (analyse exploratoire, tests statistiques, A/B testing), Vous êtes à l’aise avec l’analyse de données complexes et séquentielles issues de systèmes interactifs et avez de bonnes connaissances des LLM, Vous êtes une personne dotée d’une bonne capacité d’écoute, de compréhension et vous savez traduire les besoins des clients en spécifications, Vous faites preuve d’autonomie et de curiosité et avez un véritable intérêt pour le jeu vidéo. Enfin, votre maîtrise de l’anglais vous permet d’être à l’aise dans les échanges écrits et oraux avec des interlocuteurs de différents pays. Informations supplémentaires En tant qu’employeur, Ubisoft offre à tous les mêmes opportunités d’accès à l’emploi, sans distinction notamment de genre, ethnicité, religion, orientation sexuelle, statut social, handicap et d’âge. Ubisoft veille à développer un environnement de travail inclusif qui reflète la diversité de sa communauté de …

items.desc: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. As a Research Engineer on the Orchestral team, you will help build the agentic platform we use to train and evaluate our models. Orchestral is the system our researchers rely on to run training and evaluation at scale — from the rollout engine that powers agentic workflows to the infrastructure that keeps their workloads running reliably. What you build becomes the foundation the whole science team works on. Your work will span the platform's core: the library, tooling, abstractions and rollout engine — including new capabilities like long-running tasks, subagents and RL features — and the machinery that runs data and jobs at scale, with a focus on resiliency, routing and request handling. You will own significant pieces end to end, from design to production. This is a software engineering role rather than an ML or infrastructure-operations one: RL or PyTorch experience is not required, and you will spend your time building the platform, not operating it. You will be building a distributed RL system, with the scientists as your users. What You Will Do Design and build the core of the Orchestral platform: the library, abstractions and tooling researchers use to train and evaluate models. Build and evolve the rollout engine, shipping new capabilities such as long-running tasks and subagents. Run Orchestral as a production system: keep training and evaluation workloads reliable at scale. Improve how data and jobs flow through the platform as usage grows — scheduling, routing and request handling. Treat researchers as your users: understand their workflows and turn recurring needs into robust, shared tooling. Raise the bar on engineering quality across the platform: testing, code review, CI/CD, observability and documentation. Contribute to open-source rollout-engine and agent-infrastructure projects where it benefits the platform. What We're Looking For Experience directly building and debugging complex distributed systems at scale, with an emphasis on reliability and scalability. Strong Python skills and solid software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD. A builder mindset: you have constructed systems from the ground up, not just operated polished ones. A track record in small teams running complex systems at scale — for example in finance, crypto or ad tech. Self-starter, low-ego and collaborative, with a product mindset toward your users. Curiosity about ML and RL — this experience is not required, but a desire to learn is. Nice-to-haves Hands-on experience with Ray or similar distributed-computing frameworks. Open-source contributions, especially to rollout-engine or agent-infrastructure projects such as SLIME, verl or PrimeRL. Experience building or working with agentic workflows and environments. What we offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page. Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

items.desc: About SPAICE SPAICE is building the autonomy operating system that empowers satellites and drones to navigate and interact with the world – regardless of the environment. From GPS-denied zones on Earth to the unexplored frontiers of space, our Spatial AI delivers unprecedented levels of autonomy, resilience, and adaptability. At SPAICE, you’ll work on real missions alongside leading aerospace and defense contractors, shaping the future of space and autonomous systems. If you're looking for a place where your work has a real, tangible impact – SPAICE is that place. About The Role Satellites that detect & avoid threats on their own. Drones that collaborate in GPS‑denied fields. Spacecraft that rendezvous with tumbling targets in orbit. All of these feats demand robust scene understanding from multiple sensors. That’s where you come in. As a Computer Vision Engineer (Multimodal Sensing) you’ll implement and refine perception algorithms that fuse cameras, LiDAR, radar, event sensors, and beyond. Working shoulder‑to‑shoulder with a top‑tier team of CV scientists, you’ll translate cutting‑edge research into flight‑ready code for space and defense missions. What you might work on Implement perception pipelines for situational awareness, collision detection & avoidance, formation flying, surveillance and terrain mapping across satellites and drones operating in GPS‑denied, dynamic environments. Build the Perception stack of our Spatial AI architectures, fusing visual, inertial, and depth cues for robust, multi‑sensor scene understanding. Integrate sensor fusion & neural representations to create dense onboard world models that run in real time on resource‑constrained hardware. Deploy semantic scene understanding, visual place recognition, pose estimation, and monocular depth estimation on embedded or edge‑AI processors. Collaborate with a top‑tier team of CV scientists and cross‑disciplinary engineers, delivering well‑tested, high‑performance code into flight processors, Hardware‑in‑the‑Loop (HIL) and Software‑in‑the‑Loop (SIL) setups, and real missions. What we are looking for M.S. in Computer Vision/Robotics, or a related field. Expertise in at least two of the following: multimodal perception & sensor fusion, neural representations, semantic scene understanding, SLAM / camera‑pose estimation, monocular depth estimation, visual place recognition. Strong software engineering skills in C++ and Python, including performance‑critical CV/ML code on Linux or embedded platforms. Familiarity with GPU or edge‑AI acceleration (CUDA, TensorRT, Vulkan, or similar). Demonstrated ability to deliver production‑quality, well‑tested code in collaborative, fast‑moving environments. Preferred Qualifications Industry placements/working experience. Familiarity with GPU or edge‑AI acceleration (CUDA, TensorRT, Vulkan, or similar). Experience deploying perception pipelines on resource‑constrained hardware. Publications in multimodal sensing/neural representations/SLAM for robotics or autonomous navigation in journals and conferences (e.g. CVPR, ICRA, ECCV/ICCV, NeurIPS). Perks & Benefits Competitive salary commensurate with experience and impact. Equity options – you will join us at the ground floor and share in the upside. Well‑being perks – access to premium gyms, climbing centers, and wellness programs. Team retreats & offsites – recent adventures include a half‑marathon in Formentera and a Los Angeles retreat during Oscars weekend.

Det du bygger kommer användas direkt i BookBeats app och har direkt och stor påverkan på hela tjänsten. Mitt mål är att bygga små team, med hög kompetens som kan röra sig snabbt med utvecklare som söker ansvar och har en stor påverkan på vad vi bygger och hur vi jobbar både inom och utanför teamet. Med över 1 miljon användare i 30 länder är datamängderna allt annat än triviala. Det gör arbetet väldigt omväxlande och utmanande. I korthet kan man beskriva BookBeats kultur som startup-lik med få inslag av "corporate" även om det till viss del behövs med 170 anställda. Ekonomiskt står vi på egna ben och är lönsamma med Bonnier som ägare. Jag vill att du är väldigt nyfiken, inte bara på teknik och matematik, utan även på hur och varför saker görs. Det kan handla om allt ifrån teknik och domän till människor, team och organisation. Du förstår att det är helheten som spelar roll i slutändan. Du förstår att man måste vara öppen för nya idéer och dela med sig av sina kunskaper med andra utvecklare och specialister för att både BookBeat och du själv ska kunna utvecklas. Jag tror också du är engagerad i det du gör och i ditt yrke, du bryr dig på riktigt om det som du och ditt team skickar till produktion och vilken effekt det ger. Tillsammans är vårt gemensamma mål på BookBeat att bygga Europas bästa tjänst för att hitta och uppleva digitala böcker. Vårt kontor ligger på Sveavägen 56, typ mitt emot Webhallen. items.desc: Graham Capital Management, L.P. (collectively with its affiliates, "Graham") is an alternative investment manager founded in 1994 by Kenneth G. Tropin. Specializing in discretionary and quantitative macro strategies, Graham is dedicated to delivering strong, uncorrelated returns across a wide range of market environments. As one of the industry's longest-standing global macro and trend-following managers, Graham remains committed to innovation, evolving its strategies through a robust investment, technology, and operational infrastructure. Graham harnesses the synergies between its discretionary and quantitative trading businesses to offer a broad suite of complementary alpha strategies, each built on the principles of thoughtful portfolio construction, active risk management, and diversification by design. Graham invests significant proprietary capital alongside its clients – including global institutions, endowments, foundations, family offices, sovereign wealth funds, investment management advisors, and qualified individual investors – reinforcing alignment of interests across all strategies. The foundation of Graham's sustainability and success is the experience and contributions of its people. The firm seeks to cultivate talent, encourage the diversity of ideas, and respect the contributions of all. In turn, each employee shares in the responsibility of strengthening those around them. Description Graham is seeking a ML Engineer to join our Data Science team, a future-looking technical arm of Graham. We envision, design, prototype and implement the processes that feed Quantitative Research and Discretionary Trading teams as well as the broader firm. We are passionate about what we do and welcome every opportunity to prove it. The Data Science department straddles traditional Data Science and Engineering roles as well as the application of Machine Learning & AI. We work closely with Quant Researchers, Portfolio Managers, Operations and Execution to continuously improve upon our offering. Every day we work to transform our business through data, technology, and the insights we provide our stakeholders. At Graham, our systems feed live models around the clock, span billions of market data ticks, an ever-increasing corpus of news and other texts as well as a broad spectrum of financial and alternative data. Our objective is to support the research process by providing our stakeholders with all the right pieces to succeed in their jobs. Responsibilities You will be part of a growing team within Data Science. You will work alongside world-class talent to find innovative solutions to some of the most interesting problems on the buy-side. You will work closely with other areas such as Technology, Quantitative Research and Portfolio Manager groups as well as Risk and Operations to learn about problems they face with respect to data and ultimately develop cutting edge solutions. Your focus will be to dive deep into multiple data sets to understand relationships, develop time series, forecasting models, and support quant strategies, and provide new insights and leverage state-of-the-art machine learning and advanced statistical methods to produce the best data sources for the fund. Requirements Undergraduate or higher degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Operations Research, or other quantitative discipline 3+ years of hands-on experience with Machine Learning and Statistics on large, unstructured, data sets Experience writing production code for multi-client systems serving model results is a great plus Ability to clearly communicate research findings to technical and nontechnical stakeholders Full-stack experience with Python (preferred) or C++, Spark/Scala, SQL or other distributed data processing technologies as well as experience working comfortably building and deploying services and models in containerized environments Experience with scientific computing, statistics, optimization, time series, panel data, etc. Comfortable handling multiple projects to solve varied problems working with multiple teams Detail-oriented mindset Sense of ownership of his/her work, working well both independently as well as collaboratively This role requires commuting into our London office Mondays through Fridays.

items.desc: About Zego 🚀 At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing. Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive. We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖 For us, AI isn't a line on a roadmap or a buzzword on a slide. It's our operating reality, and it's how we build products that back drivers instead of the old insurance playbook. We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers. Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor. If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring. About The Team We don’t build pricing models, we build the driving intelligence that feeds them. Our mission is to drive safer roads and fairer insurance through data. The Telematics team transforms raw phone sensor data into meaningful insights about how people drive. Using advanced signal processing and machine learning, we process high-frequency data to extract behavioural signals that power our understanding of driving quality, context, and risk. About The Role As a Data Scientist, you’ll contribute to the future of behaviour-based insurance. You’ll contribute to the development of features and algorithms that detect driving patterns from sensors, test new hypotheses, and help bring impactful insights into production.
