items.desc: Job Description Position Details Department of Cancer and Genomic Sciences, School of Medical Sciences, College of Medicine and Health Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Full time starting salary is normally in the range £36,636 to £46,049 with potential progression once in post to £48,822 Grade: 7 Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to November 2029 Closing date: 25th October 2026 Background This job is part of an Advanced Research + Invention Agency-funded project. "Hephaisteion: Direct Lithium Extraction using inorganic membranes made by proteins" is a highly interdisciplinary 36-month project within ARIA's Universal Fabricators programme. The project will use self-assembling S-layer proteins to programme the manufacture of large-area inorganic membranes with tightly controlled pores, with direct lithium extraction as the first demanding application. It links protein design, high-throughput screening, cell-based expression, biomineralisation, microscopy, process scale-up, membrane manufacture and performance testing. The post will be based in the research group of Professor Steve Smerdon and will work closely with Professor Tim Knowles, project lead Dr Dominik Kubicki and the wider Hephaisteion team. The Research Fellow will take promising proteins emerging from computational and cell-free screening into cellular expression systems; design and construct expression vectors; optimise expression in appropriate bacterial hosts; recover and purify proteins using standard molecular biology and protein-biochemistry techniques; and establish refolding routes where required. Crucially, the Research Fellow will determine whether purified proteins retain the ability to self-assemble into ordered two-dimensional lattices. They will use appropriate biochemical and biophysical assays, work with the microscopy team to validate assembly, and provide well-characterised protein to the biomineralisation, membrane-manufacturing and process-scale-up workstreams. The postholder will analyse sequence-expression-assembly relationships and contribute evidence to the project's design-build-test decisions and major programme milestones. This is an opportunity to engage in a unique interdisciplinary project spanning protein science, materials chemistry, electron microscopy, bioprocessing and membrane engineering. The postholder will collaborate closely with ARIA, participate in frequent programme workshops and meet other ARIA Creators developing ambitious protein-programmed manufacturing technologies. They will be supported in their professional development while contributing to ARIA's ambition to deliver world-changing impact. items.desc: Position description Category Thermohydraulics and fluid mechanics Contract Internship Job title Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions H/F Subject Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions Contract duration (months) 6 Job Description The Critical Heat Flux (CHF) is a physical phenomenon that may cause the deterioration of the heat transfer in the core of nuclear reactors, potentially leading to core damage. Its accurate prediction is therefore a crucial issue in nuclear reactor safety. The internship deals with the prediction of the CHF through the development of machine learning techniques and the quantification of the associated uncertainty. It will be realized in the framework of an international OECD/NEA project on the development and application of artificial intelligence methodologies for nuclear engineering. Within this framework, the intern will: Perform a preliminary literature review on the topic and get familiar with the previous works performed at CEA, based on experimental data in tubes with uniform axial heat flux profiles Analyse the new experimental CHF database (e.g., tube with non-uniform heat flux, rod-bundle, rectangular channel, …) to understand the physical phenomenon and to verify the coherence and exploitability of the experimental data. Perform an initial assessment of previously developed machine learning models to the new database. Develop transfer learning to predict as accurately as possible the CHF for the new experiments. If time allows it, investigate the explainability issue and quantify the uncertainty of the models developed during the internship applying different state-of-the-art methodologies such as conformal prediction, hierarchical models and other coverage-driven techniques. Present and discuss the work during technical meetings and write a final report. Applicant Profile The ideal candidate is a MSc. student (in French system: M2 level or Ecole d’ingénieur) who has a good knowledge of artificial intelligence and neural networks with an interest in fluid mechanics. Knowledge of the physics processes underlying the CHF phenomenon will be considered a plus. Good skills in Python coding and code management are required. We welcome previous experience with any major deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, Tensorflow) and with uncertainty quantification approaches. Given the international context of the OECD/NEA project, fluency in English is considered necessary (French will be considered a plus). Position location Site Saclay Job location France, Ile-de-France Location Saclay Candidate criteria Prepared diploma Bac+5 - Diplôme École d'ingénieurs PhD opportunity Non Requester Position start date 01/02/2027

items.desc: Övergripande beskrivning Examensarbetet genomförs i samarbete med ett hållbarhetsföretag med målet att använda maskininlärning för att förbättra statistiken över produkter som anländer till en återvinningsanläggning. Företaget har tillgång till en produktdatabas med individuella SKU:er (Stock Keeping Units), ett mindre manuellt annoterat dataset från produkter som identifierats på transportbandet samt en omfattande samling oannoterade bilder som kontinuerligt samlas in av ett kamerasystem. Kombinationen av dessa datakällor skapar förutsättningar för att utveckla automatiserade metoder för produktidentifiering baserade på datorseende och djupinlärning. En central utmaning är det stora antalet produkter som kan förekomma i avfallsflödet, där många SKU:er dessutom uppvisar små visuella skillnader. För att möjliggöra detaljerad och skalbar statistikinsamling undersöker arbetet hur moderna bildklassificeringsmodeller kan användas för att identifiera produkter på olika detaljnivåer, från produktkategori till enskild SKU. Projektbeskrivning Målet med examensarbetet är att utveckla en pipeline som automatiskt kan generera statistik över de produkter som anländer till en återvinningsanläggning. För detta finns idag tre datakällor tillgängliga. Den första består av en produktkatalog med individuella SKU:er. Den andra är en annoterad datamängd som har samlats in genom manuell provtagning, där produkter från transportbandet har identifierats och märkts över tid. Den tredje datakällan utgörs av ett kamerasystem som kontinuerligt fotograferar inkommande produkter på transportbandet, vilket har resulterat i en omfattande mängd oannoterade bilder från verklig drift. Uppgiften är att utveckla och utvärdera datorseendemodeller som automatiskt kan klassificera produkter utifrån bilder. En central utmaning är det stora antalet SKU-klasser samt den höga visuella likheten mellan många produkter. I takt med att antalet klasser ökar blir klassificeringsuppgiften allt mer komplex, vilket gör skalbarhet till en viktig forskningsfråga. Examensarbetet kommer att undersöka följande frågeställningar: Hur påverkas klassificeringsnoggrannheten när antalet produktklasser ökar? Kan en hierarkisk klassificeringsmodell, där produkttyp identifieras först och därefter varumärke, förbättra prestandan vid identifiering på SKU-nivå? Hur skiljer sig olika datorseendemodeller och hyperparameterkonfigurationer åt vad gäller klassificeringsprestanda och robusthet? Vem söker vi? Vi söker en masterstudent inom datavetenskap, datateknik, teknisk fysik, data science, maskininlärning, artificiell intelligens eller närliggande område. Erfarenhet inom computer vision, AI och maskininlärning Planerad examen under 2027 Förväntas kunna arbeta självständigt och ha god analytisk och problemlösande förmåga Flytande i svenska och engelska Meriterande: Pytorch, Finetuning and cloud experience Syfte Syftet med examensarbetet är att undersöka hur datorseende kan användas för att automatisera produktidentifiering i återvinningsanläggningar och därigenom möjliggöra mer detaljerad och skalbar statistik över inkommande avfallsflöden. Studien fokuserar särskilt på utmaningen att klassificera ett stort antal SKU:er där många produkter uppvisar betydande visuell likhet. Arbetet syftar till att analysera hur klassificeringsprestanda påverkas av ett ökande antal klasser samt att utvärdera om hierarkisk klassificering kan utgöra ett effektivt alternativ till traditionella klassificeringsmetoder. Genom att jämföra olika datorseendemodeller, arkitekturer och hyperparameterinställningar avser studien att identifiera metoder som kan förbättra både noggrannhet och skalbarhet vid produktigenkänning. Resultaten förväntas bidra med kunskap om storskalig visuell klassificering samtidigt som de kan skapa praktiskt värde genom att stödja automatiserad datainsamling och analys inom återvinningssektorn. En spännande resa med Knightec Group Knightec Group är idag en av Norra Europas ledande strategiska partners inom produkt- och digital tjänsteutveckling – hur häftigt är inte det? Genom att förena ingenjörskompetens, digital expertis och affärsförståelse hjälper vi våra kunder att omvandla ny teknik till verkliga lösningar som skapar värde. Vi arbetar i skärningspunkten mellan affärsstrategi och teknikutveckling och stöttar våra kunder genom hela resan – från de första idéerna till utveckling, implementering och vidare utveckling. På Knightec Group samlas människor med olika perspektiv, erfarenheter och specialistområden. Tillsammans skapar vi innovation som gör verklig skillnad – för företag, människor och samhället i stort. För våra medarbetare innebär det stora möjligheter att vara med och forma framtidens lösningar genom meningsfulla projekt i teknikens absoluta framkant. Här får du inte bara utvecklas och växa i din roll – du blir också en del av ett team där nyfikenhet, samarbete och modet att utmana driver oss framåt. items.desc: Structure d'accueil The Curie Institute Research Center France’s leading cancer research and treatment centre, Institut Curie unites a renowned research centre and a specialist hospital, fostering close collaboration between scientists, clinicians and healthcare professionals. It offers an environment of excellence where expertise comes together around shared values: care, humanity, openness, collaboration, efficiency, innovation, solidarity and commitment. Missions Activités principales Laboratory The RACER (Rare Cancers Exploration and Research) team, led by Dr. Sarah Watson within the Chemical Biology of Cancer Unit (INSERM U1339/CNRS UMR3666, Institut Curie , Paris), conducts translational research on rare cancers, with a particular focus on sarcomas . The team combines multi-scale molecular profiling, preclinical models, and direct access to patient cohorts from Institut Curie. This position is part of the ATTILAS project ( Addressing and Targeting Tumor and Immunological Vulnerabilities in Dedifferentiated Liposarcomas ), funded by the French National Research Agency (ANR, JCJC program, 36 months) and coordinated by Dr. Watson. The project aims to identify actionable tumor and immune vulnerabilities in dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS) through the integration of multi-omics analyses and functional validation. The successful candidate will contribute to the bioinformatic analyses of a unique dataset including bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and whole-exome sequencing (WES) data. The position involves close interaction with researchers within the team and with the Bioinformatics Hub at Institut Curie. Missions Transcriptomic Analysis Analyze bulk RNA-seq datasets, including quality control, normalization, differential expression, and functional enrichment analyses. Perform cell-type deconvolution of bulk transcriptomic data. Process and integrate scRNA-seq and snRNA-seq datasets, including cell-type annotation, CNV inference, trajectory analysis, and cell-cell communication analyses. Integrate transcriptomic findings with functional data generated within the project. Biostatistics and Biomarker Correlate molecular profiles with clinical outcomes using appropriate statistical approaches. Optimize and validate prognostic signatures. Identify signatures associated with therapeutic response or resistance from single-cell data and apply these signatures to bulk transcriptomic datasets. Data Management and Scientific Dissemination Develop, maintain, and document reproducible bioinformatics pipelines. Ensure data management, traceability, and deposition. Collaborate closely with biologists, engineers, and clinicians to translate biological questions into actionable analyses. Present results at team meetings and contribute to publications, reports, and grant deliverables. Contraints and risks Opportunities for occasional travel to national and international scientific conferences. Profil du candidat Savoirs et compétences attendus Training And Experience Required Education and qualifications: Master’s degree (MSc) or Engineering degree in Bioinformatics, Biostatistics, Data Science, or a related field; alternatively, a PhD in one of these disciplines or involving substantial transcriptomic data analysis. Professional experience: At least 2 years in the analysis of high-throughput sequencing data, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) experience. Required expertise: Strong knowledge of bulk and single-cell RNA-seq analysis, from raw data processing to biological interpretation; integration methods and batch-effect correction; survival statistics; and functional enrichment analyses. A background in cancer biology is expected, while prior experience in sarcoma research is not required. Desirable skills: Experience in cellular deconvolution, cell-cell communication inference, spatial omics data analysis, and copy-number alteration (CNA) analysis. Skills Required Computational skills: Proficiency in R and Python, as well as Bash and Unix/Linux environments; routine use of Git for version control; experience working on high-performance computing clusters (SLURM); familiarity with workflow management systems such as Nextflow and reproducible computational environments including Conda, Docker, and Singularity. Language skills: Excellent written and spoken scientific English Personal qualities: Strong commitment to methodological rigor and reproducible research practices; ability to work independently while maintaining a critical perspective on the robustness of analyses; excellent communication skills to interact effectively with biologists and clinicians and present complex analytical results in an accessible manner; and a strong collaborative mindset. Contract information Type of contract : Fixed-term contract Starting date: as soon as possible Duration : 18 months, renewable Working time : full time 39 hours per week Annual Gross Salary : from 32480€ to 39459€ …

items.desc: Structure d'accueil Le Centre de recherche de l’Institut Curie Premier centre français de recherche et de lutte contre le cancer, l'Institut Curie associe un centre de recherche de renommée internationale et un hôpital de pointe. Il offre un environnement d’excellence, où les expertises se mêlent autour de valeurs communes : bienveillance, humanité, ouverture, partage, efficacité, innovation, solidarité et engagement. Missions Activités principales Laboratoire - Service L’équipe RACER (Rare Cancers Exploration and Research) , dirigée par le Dr Sarah Watson au sein de l’unité Chemical Biology of Cancer (INSERM U1339/CNRS UMR3666, Institut Curie, Paris), conduit des recherches translationnelles sur les cancers rares, dont les sarcomes. Elle combine profilage moléculaire multi-échelle, modèles précliniques et accès direct aux cohortes et échantillons biologiques de l’Institut Curie. Le poste s’inscrit dans le projet ATTILAS ( Addressing and Targeting Tumor and Immunological Vulnerabilities in Dedifferentiated Liposarcomas ), financé par l’ANR (JCJC, 36 mois) et coordonné par le Dr Watson. Ce projet vise à identifier des vulnérabilités tumorales et immunitaires du liposarcome dédifférencié (DDLPS) grâce à l’intégration d’analyses multi-omiques et de validations fonctionnelles. La personne recrutée contribuera aux analyses bioinformatiques d’un jeu de données comprenant RNA-seq bulk, scRNA-seq, WGS et WES. Elle travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les chercheurs de l’équipe et les bioinformaticiens du Hub de bioinformatique de l’Institut Curie. Missions Description Des Activités Analyse transcriptomique Analyser les données RNA-seq bulk : contrôle qualité, normalisation, expression différentielle et analyses fonctionnelles. Réaliser la déconvolution des données bulk à partir des références scRNA-seq de l’équipe. Traiter et intégrer les données scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq : annotation cellulaire, inférence de CNV, analyses de trajectoire et de communication intercellulaire. Intégrer les données transcriptomiques aux résultats fonctionnels du projet. Biostatistique et biomarqueurs Corréler profils moléculaires et données cliniques à l’aide de modèles statistiques adaptés Optimiser et valider des signatures pronostiques. Identifier des signatures de réponse ou de résistance thérapeutique à partir des données single-cell puis les appliquer aux cohortes bulk. Gestion des données et valorisation Développer des pipelines reproductibles et documentés. Assurer la gestion et le dépôt des données selon les principes FAIR et les exigences ANR. Collaborer avec biologistes, ingénieurs et cliniciens pour transformer les questions biologiques en analyses exploitables. Présenter les résultats et contribuer aux publications et rapports scientifiques. Spécificités du poste - Possibilité de déplacements ponctuels pour des congrès nationaux et internationaux. Profil du candidat Savoirs et compétences attendus Formation et expérience Niveau et diplômes : Master 2 ou diplôme d'ingénieur en bioinformatique, biostatistique, science des données ou discipline connexe ; ou doctorat dans l'un de ces domaines, notamment en analyse transcriptomique. Expérience professionnelle : au moins 2 ans d'expérience dans l'analyse de données de séquençage à haut débit. Expérience documentée du scRNA-seq. Connaissances attendues : RNA-seq bulk et en cellule unique, de la donnée brute à l'interprétation biologique ; méthodes d'intégration et de correction des effets de lot ; statistiques appliquées à la survie, analyses d'enrichissement fonctionnel. Connaissance de la biologie du cancer ; Atouts : déconvolution cellulaire, inférence de communication intercellulaire, analyse de données spatiales, exploitation de données de nombre de copies. Compétences et qualités requises Compétences informatiques : maîtrise de R, Python, bash et de l'environnement Unix ; usage courant de Git ; travail sur cluster de calcul (SLURM) ; gestionnaires de workflow (Nextflow ) et environnements reproductibles (conda, Docker, Singularity). Compétences linguistiques : anglais scientifique écrit et oral courant, indispensable. Aptitudes : rigueur méthodologique et sens de la reproductibilité, autonomie dans la conduite des analyses, esprit critique sur la robustesse des résultats, capacité à dialoguer avec des biologistes et des cliniciens et à restituer des analyses complexes de façon accessible, goût du travail collaboratif Informations sur le contrat Type de contrat : CDD, niveau ingénieur d'études ou ingénieur de recherche selon le profil Date de démarrage : dès que possible Durée du contrat : 18 mois, renouvelable Temps de travail : temps complet, 39 h par semaine Rémunération annuelle : de32480€ to 39459€ selon les grilles en vigueur Avantages : Restauration collective, prise en charge du titre de transport annuel à 70%, mutuelle d’entreprise Localisation du poste : Paris Contact Pour postuler, merci d’envoyer CV et lettre de motivation : 18/10/2026 Date de publication : …

items.desc: Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle L’Inria est l’Institut national de recherche en sciences du numérique, dont le centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur fait partie. Avec une forte expertise en informatique et mathématiques appliquées, les projets de recherche du centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur touchent toutes les dimensions des sciences et technologies du numérique, et génèrent de l’innovation. Implanté principalement à Sophia Antipolis, mais également à Nice ou Montpellier, il regroupe 47 équipes de recherche et neuf services d’appui. Il est présent dans les domaines de l’intelligence artificielle, la science des données, la sécurité des systèmes informatiques, la robotique, l’ingénierie de réseaux, la prévention des risques naturels, la transition écologique, la biologie numérique, les neurosciences computationnelles, les données de santé… Le Centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur est un acteur majeur en termes d'excellence scientifique par les résultats obtenus et les collaborations tant au niveau européen qu'international. Contexte et atouts du poste Ce poste s’inscrit dans un projet porté par OnTheFly (onthefly3d.com), projet entrepreneurial issu de l’équipe-projet GraphDeco (inventrice du 3D Gaussian Splatting) et accompagné par Inria Startup Studio. Le projet vise à développer des outils de capture 3D sur smartphone à destination des professionnels, associant reconstruction immédiate et analyse automatisée de l’évolution des sites réels dans le temps. Mission confiée Développer des méthodes de comparaison automatique entre des reconstructions 3D issues de captures réelles et des données de référence, comme des maquettes numériques ou des captures antérieures d’un même site. Les travaux porteront sur l’alignement de représentations 3D hétérogènes, ainsi que sur la détection et la segmentation de changements de manière robuste dans des conditions de capture réelles. Principales activités Concevoir et implémenter des méthodes d’alignement 3D combinant correspondances visuelles ou sémantiques et informations géométriques rendues. Développer des approches de décomposition géométrie-matériaux-éclairage pour les représentations par Gaussian Splatting. Mettre en place des méthodes de détection et de segmentation des différences entre captures ou entre reconstruction et maquette numérique, en exploitant images, profondeur, normales et modèles de vision. Entraîner et évaluer les modèles sur des données réelles et synthétiques, puis intégrer les méthodes développées dans des outils de visualisation. Compétences Requises Diplôme d’ingénieur, master ou doctorat en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe Solides compétences en programmation Expérience en entraînement et en évaluation de modèles de deep learning, avec des frameworks de programmation différentiable tels que PyTorch Solides bases en vision par ordinateur, des fondamentaux comme la géométrie multivue aux modèles de vision modernes (par ex. vision transformers, modèles vision-langage) Intérêt pour les projets entrepreneuriaux et les environnements de start-up Appréciées Expérience en programmation de shaders ou en programmation parallèle (par ex. GLSL, CUDA) Expérience en 3D Gaussian Splatting, rendu neuronal ou rendu inverse Une expérience avec les données BIM Avantages Restauration subventionnée Transports publics remboursés partiellement Congés: 7 semaines de congés annuels + 10 jours de RTT (base temps plein) + possibilité d'autorisations d'absence exceptionnelle (ex : enfants malades, déménagement) Possibilité de télétravail et aménagement du temps de travail Équipements professionnels à disposition (visioconférence, prêts de matériels informatiques, etc.) Prestations sociales, culturelles et sportives (Association de gestion des œuvres sociales d'Inria) Accès à la formation professionnelle Participation mutuelle (sous conditions) Rémunération A partir de 2692 € brut mensuel (selon diplôme et expérience) Informations générales Thème/Domaine : Interaction et visualisation Ingénierie logicielle (BAP E) Ville : Sophia Antipolis Centre Inria : Centre Inria d'Université Côte d'Azur Date de prise de fonction souhaitée : 2026-12-01 Durée de contrat : 5 mois Date limite pour postuler : 2026-11-15 Attention : Les candidatures doivent être déposées en ligne sur le site Inria. items.desc: Job Reference 457_26_CS_HAM_RE1 Position Research Engineer - HPC memory systems (RE1) Closing Date Friday, 30 October, 2026 Reference: 457_26_CS_HAM_RE1 Job title: Research Engineer - HPC memory systems (RE1) About BSC The Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over 1000 staff from 60 countries. Look at the BSC experience: BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission The Memory Systems group in the Computer Science Department at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center is offering a full-time research engineer position for a project that explores advanced memory systems for AI applications. The performance of AI models is typically limited by the memory wall. In this project, we aim to (re)move this wall by designing memory systems tailored to the requirements of AI models. We will explore systems based on HBM, DDR, GDDR devices, and Compute Express Link (CXL) memory expanders. Additionally, we will consider near-data processing architectures that offload part of the CPU/GPU processing to the memory system. The project is conducted in close collaboration with a major memory manufacturer. Most of the development will take place on high-end hardware products and industrial prototypes. We strongly encourage applications from candidates interested in joining a research team with over a decade of experience in industrial projects with major hardware companies from the US, China, and Korea. Key Duties Profiling and performance modeling of HPC applications running on high-end servers with advanced memory systems: HBM, DDR4/5, CXL memory expanders. Exploration of Processing in Memory for HPC and AI applications. Prototyping of industrial products and tools. Close interaction and reporting to industrial partners. Benchmarking and performance analysis of high-end hardware products and industrial prototypes. Requirements Education BSc, MSc or PhD in Computer Science Essential Knowledge and Professional Experience Good knowledge of computer architecture Experience with Unix/Linux environments Experience with profiling tools: Hardware counters, PAPI interface Programming languages (C/C++, Python) Additional Knowledge and Professional Experience Understanding of memory systems and memory technologies (e.g. DRAM, HBM) is a plus Experience with hardware/system simulators is a plus Fluency in English is essential Competences Good written and verbal communication skills Ability to take initiative Conditions The position will be located at BSC within the Computer Sciences Department We offer a full-time contract (35h/week), a good working environment, a highly stimulating environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure, flexible working hours, extensive training plan, restaurant tickets, private health insurance, support to the relocation procedures Duration: Open-ended contract due to technical and scientific activities linked to the project and budget duration Holidays: 22 days of holidays + 6 personal days + 24th and 31st of December per our collective agreement Salary: we offer a competitive salary commensurate with the qualifications and experience of the candidate and according to the cost of living in Barcelona Starting date: Nov 2026 Applications procedure and process All applications must be submitted via the BSC website and contain: A full CV in English including contact details A cover/motivation letter with a statement of interest in English, clearly specifying for which specific area and topics the applicant wishes to be considered. items.title: PICs@ICFO Strategic Initiative: Research Engineer in Materials Structuring and Characterization of Photonic Integrated Circuits
items.card: Responsibilities: The selected candidate will be expected to: Set-up, run and consolidate some nanofabrication techniques for PIC development within the PIXEurope Pilot Line. Set-up, run and consolidate the characterization techniques for PIC development within the PIXEurope Pilot Line. items.desc: As part of the PICs@ICFO Strategic Initiative , ICFO coordinates PIXEurope, a flagship Pilot Line funded under the European Chips JU program focused on Advanced Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) through which ICFO is advancing frontier technologies, including optical interposers for Co-packaged optics for next-generation optoelectronic and photonic devices. To strengthen this initiative, ICFO is seeking PIC Nano-structuring and Nano-characterization Research Engineer with a strong technical background in materials research, characterization of morphology and interfaces, failure analysis, and photonic integrated circuits characterization. Position Overview: We offer a research engineer position to an experienced engineer with demonstrated expertise in integrated photonics and material research, especially characterization of PICs and their related materials. The successful candidate will contribute to both technical innovation and Pilot Line development in collaboration with academic and industrial stakeholders. Key Responsibilities: The selected candidate will be expected to: Set-up, run and consolidate some nanofabrication techniques for PIC development within the PIXEurope Pilot Line. Set-up, run and consolidate the characterization techniques for PIC development within the PIXEurope Pilot Line. Contribute to characterization and application-oriented activities of PIXEurope Pilot Line and other projects related to PICs. Interface with multidisciplinary teams and contribute to the establishment of high-quality characterization workflows. This position is hosted by the Optoelectronics group , led by Prof Valerio Pruneri , and the Nanocharacterization lab , led by Dr. Johann Osmond. PIXEurope is co-funded by the Chips Joint Undertaking and national funding authorities of the Participating States, Spain, Ireland, The Netherlands, Finland, Belgium, Portugal, Poland, Austria, France, Italy, United Kingdom. In particular, it is co-funded by Spain through the Ministry for Digital Transformation and Civil Service under reference CJU-010000-2025-0005, as part of the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (PRTR). Applicants must hold an engineer degree or a master degree Science or Engineering, preferably in fields related to nanoscience and nanotechnology, photonics, materials science, or electrical engineering. Candidates should demonstrate strong expertise in the following areas: Fabrication and characterization of devices made of materials used in PICs, such as semiconductors, 2D materials, colloidal quantum dots, or thin films. Metrology characterization in a 200 mm diameter wafer capabilities environment Nanofabrication process development Characterization of defects and their automatic detection in the different processes of nanofabrication. Defect and failure analysis ranging from material structure to PIC devices. Metrology and nanoscale characterization of PICs. Materials research and chemical analysis of materials Expertise, or at least exposure, in the following technique will be evaluated: Nanofabrication techniques such as photoresist deposition, Electron beam lithography, optical lithography, Reactive Ion Etching, thin film deposition, Atomic Layer deposition, Chemical Vapour Deposition) Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and Focused Ion Beam to perform CD metrology, to realize some cross-sections and later observe the different transitions and interfaces of layers with integrated SEM, preparation of TEM lamellas. Atomic Force Microscopy, especially applied to large wafers for automatic detection of CDs, line edge, surface and sidewall roughness, and electrical characterization Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) to characterize interfaces and map atomic elements by Energy Dispersive Microscopy. Raman spectroscopy for material characterization. Nano-infrared characterization using Scanning Probe Microscopy to provide chemical information in the infrared range at nanoscale dimension. Desired (but not required) skills: Proven track record in industry-oriented research, ideally involving joint R&D&E projects with end-users. A dynamic work environment at the interface of fundamental research and industrial innovation, with opportunities for leadership and visibility. Competitive compensation aligned with ICFO’s internal scales. A family allowance may be granted to candidates with dependents, according to ICFO policies. Equal Opportunity ICFO is an equal opportunity employer. We hire based solely on merit and potential, regardless of gender, nationality, or disability. ICFO fully endorses the European Charter for Researchers and Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers, ensuring a transparent and supportive recruitment process. Your core responsibility is designing, building and operating the system landscape in the NeuraGym so that recording and
items.desc: Your mission & challenges As Compute Infrastructure Engineer – NeuraGym you work at the intersection of server architecture, virtualisation, container orchestration and data processing, with a strong focus on building a scalable compute and storage infrastructure for multimodal robot data. Your core responsibility is designing, building and operating the system landscape in the NeuraGym so that recording and processing on large data volumes run reliably, performantly and reproducibly. You play a decisive role in enabling high-quality embodied AI systems by turning individual servers, workstations and edge devices into a distributed, maintainable and extensible compute system. Server infrastructure planning: You plan and design the NeuraGym server infrastructure, including sizing of compute, GPU, storage and network, rack layout, power and cooling concept, and procurement in coordination with the team. Virtualisation: You build and operate virtualisation environments based on hypervisors such as Proxmox and provide development, test and production environments. Kubernetes & GPU scheduling: You design and operate Kubernetes clusters (or comparable orchestration) for data preprocessing workloads, including GPU scheduling, monitoring and logging. Distributed processing: You intelligently distribute compute- and data-intensive processes across multiple machines, from edge devices on the robot via local servers to central storage systems, and make sure bottlenecks are detected and removed. Network design: You design the NeuraGym network infrastructure: VLANs, switching, bandwidth planning for camera and sensor streams, firewall rules and secure integration with the rest of the company IT. Storage & data pipelines: You build storage and data pipelines for high data volumes (e.g. object storage, distributed file systems, streaming ingest) and ensure that data is reliably captured, stored, versioned and made available for model training. Automation: You automate provisioning, deployment and operations with infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD tooling and document the system landscape in a traceable way. Stability & security: You identify and resolve performance, stability and security issues in the infrastructure and develop backup, recovery and access concepts. What we can look forward to Education: Degree in computer science, systems engineering, engineering or a related field, or comparable vocational training with relevant practical experience. Experience: 4+ years in system administration, infrastructure engineering, DevOps or platform engineering. Server infrastructure: Solid experience planning, designing and operating server infrastructure (sizing, rack build-out, hardware selection, procurement). Virtualisation: Hands-on experience with hypervisors and virtualisation (e.g. Proxmox, KVM, VMware), including storage and network integration. Containers: Strong knowledge of container technologies and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes or comparable platforms), ideally with GPU workloads. Distributed systems: Understanding of how processes, data and compute load are sensibly distributed, synchronised and monitored across multiple machines. Linux & scripting: Confident with Linux systems, shell scripting and at least one scripting language (e.g. Python, Bash). IaC & CI/CD: Experience with infrastructure as code and automation (e.g. Ansible, Terraform) as well as CI/CD tooling (e.g. GitLab CI). Working style: A structured, self-driven way of working and enjoyment in building infrastructure from the ground up together with an interdisciplinary team. Nice to have: Experience with monitoring and logging stacks (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana).

À la croisée de la recherche appliquée et du génie logiciel, votre tâche principale consistera à valider les concepts ML prometteurs sur des cas industriels et à les transformer rapidement en composants logiciels C++/CUDA/Python performants, fiables, génériques et prêts pour la production. A ce titre vous effectuez les actions suivantes : Prototypage rapide & Validation : Expérimenter et adapter des architectures de Machine Learning (Neural Operators, Geometric Encoding, IA basée sur la physique...) pour vérifier leur faisabilité sur des cas d'usage industriels au sein de notre infrastructure logicielle d’entraînement (Python, C++, CUDA). Développement & Implémentation C++ : Participer au développement de l’infrastructure d'inférence et des structures de données en C++ moderne / CUDA pour intégrer ces modèles dans notre plateforme logicielle d’exécution pour IA Physique. Optimisation des Performances : Assurer l'efficacité computationnelle (temps d'exécution, gestion mémoire, parallélisation) de nos moteurs ML. Traitement de Données 3D : Développer des pipelines en C++/Python pour l'extraction, le prétraitement et la structuration des données géométriques et physiques CAD/CAE (maillages, champs de scalaires/vecteurs, conditions limites...) Qualité & Intégration : Garantir la robustesse du code (tests unitaires, intégration continue, documentation technique) au sein d'un environnement R&D Agile à grande échelle. Collaboration & Rayonnement : Interagir avec des experts métiers, des équipes R&D pluridisciplinaires et nos partenaires académiques/industriels internationaux (veille technologique, rédaction de documentation technique et valorisation de vos travaux). Vos Qualifications De formation BAC+5 (école d’ingénieur, université) ou doctorat, avec une spécialisation en Mathématiques Appliquées, Informatique, Machine Learning, Physique Numérique ou domaine connexe. Vous avez idéalement une expérience supérieure à 3 ans (post-doctorat ou industrie). Solide expertise en Apprentissage Profond appliqué aux EDP / équations physiques et à l'encodage géométrique. Maîtrise d'un framework ML principal (PyTorch, JAX ou TensorFlow) et de Python. Bonnes compétences en C++ moderne et en développement logiciel scientifique dans un environnement Agile. Rigueur scientifique, autonomie et capacité à résoudre des problèmes complexes et non structurés. Anglais courant (écrit et oral), au vu de notre environnement international. Des connaissances pratiques en simulation numérique (FEA, CFD, CAD/CAE) ainsi que des formats et structures de données CAD/CAE (Abaqus odb/inp/sim, CAA, HDF5, ...) seraient un réel plus pour mener à bien votre mission. Des connaissance des architectures GPU et de la programmation parallèle (CUDA, HIP/ROCm) également. Nous rejoindre c'est aussi Intégrer une entreprise scientifique au cœur de l’innovation technologique, portée par une forte croissance depuis plus de 40 ans Principaux avantages et bénéfices : Environnement multiculturel Cadre de travail convivial axé sur le bien-être et la santé (salles de sport & de musique, conciergerie…) Engagement en faveur de la diversité et de l’inclusion Politique dynamique de développement de carrière : plan de formation, mobilités internes, etc Inclusion statement As a game-changer in sustainable technology and innovation, Dassault Systèmes is striving to build more inclusive and diverse teams across the globe. We believe that our people are our number one asset and we want all employees to feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work every day. It is our goal that our people feel a sense of pride and a passion for belonging. As a company leading change, it’s our responsibility to foster opportunities for all people to participate in a harmonized Workforce of the Future.

items.desc: Programista AI / inżynier oprogramowania Projekt:FENG.01.01-IP.02-0224/25 Opracowanie prototypu innowacyjnego systemu wspierającego proces ekoprojektowania oświetlenia miejskiego, który łączy dane przestrzenne, semantykę urbanistyczną oraz metody sztucznej inteligencji w celu optymalizacji decyzji projektowych. STUDIO DL to biuro projektowo-badawcze z blisko 30-letnim doświadczeniem na rynku międzynarodowym w projektowaniu oświetlenia i badaniach na rozwiązaniami IT dedykowanemu oświetleniu. Zespół IT pracuje nad produktem, który łączy oprogramowanie, bazy danych, GIS, integracje oraz rozwiązania dla infrastruktury miejskiej. Tworzymy interdyscyplinarny zespół, w którym programiści współpracują z projektantami oświetlenia, architektami, geoinformatykami i specjalistami zajmującymi się infrastrukturą miejską. Dzięki temu rozwijane przez nas rozwiązania mają bezpośrednie przełożenie na rzeczywiste projekty i funkcjonowanie miast. Do naszego zespołu IT zapraszamy osoby, które chcą mieć wpływ na rozwój własnego produktu technologicznego i pracować przy projektach łączących IT z GIS, danymi przestrzennymi oraz nowoczesnym zarządzaniem infrastrukturą. O projekcie Realizujemy projekt badawczo-rozwojowy dotyczący opracowania prototypu systemu wspierającego ekoprojektowanie oświetlenia miejskiego. System ma łączyć dane przestrzenne, semantykę urbanistyczną, algorytmy obliczeniowe i metody sztucznej inteligencji, wspierając planowanie oraz optymalizację oświetlenia w skali miasta. Rola Osoba na tym stanowisku będzie odpowiadać za rozwój modeli AI/ML, integrację danych GIS i miejskich oraz optymalizację algorytmów wykorzystywanych w kolejnych modułach systemu, a także badanie, projektowanie i testowanie interfejsów użytkownika dla systemu wykorzystującego złożone dane przestrzenne, modele 2D/3D, algorytmy optymalizacyjne oraz moduły wspierające decyzje projektowe. Zakres prac przewidziany dla tego stanowiska: Analiza danych o pokryciu terenu oraz kryteriach decyzyjnych. Modelowanie i trenowanie algorytmów uczenia maszynowego (ML) oraz głębokiego uczenia (DL) wykorzystywanych do mapowania miasta pod kątem masterplanu oświetlenia. Implementacja rozwiązań AI. Optymalizacja modeli. Analiza danych o infrastrukturze oświetleniowej oraz danych o oprawach od producentów. Modelowanie i trenowanie algorytmów integrujących dane z inwentaryzacji z danymi od producentów oraz uzupełniających brakujące dane w oparciu o uczenie maszynowe i statystykę. Analiza danych o oprawach oświetleniowych od producentów i warunkach doboru najbardziej efektywnego rozwiązania dla oświetlenia trójwymiarowej przestrzeni. Opracowanie potoku danych dla algorytmów uczenia się optymalizacji światła. Tworzenie narzędzi opartych na sztucznej inteligencji do oceny różnych konfiguracji przekrojów drogowych i ich wpływu na oświetlenie. Zbudowanie powiązań pomiędzy rozwiązaniami AI dla poszczególnych modułów systemu. Optymalizacja algorytmów pod względem relacji pomiędzy poszczególnymi komponentami. Opracowywanie technik przetwarzania równoległego i rozproszonych rozwiązań obliczeniowych w celu zwiększenia wydajności algorytmów. --------------------------------------------------------- Projektowanie i implementacja algorytmów mapujących miasto. Opracowanie funkcji wspierających implementację algorytmów mapowania miast. Opracowanie szczegółów modelu danych na podstawie diagramu. Opracowanie funkcji umożliwiających zapisywanie i pobieranie danych 3D i semantycznych w dużych zbiorach danych. Analiza danych w celu identyfikacji wzorców i trendów przydatnych w zastosowaniach projektu. Projektowanie i implementacja algorytmów integrujących dane od producentów oraz dane o infrastrukturze w mieście. Opracowanie funkcji oceniających jakość danych, zapewniających dokładność i niezawodność optymalizacji oświetlenia. Uproszczenie geometrii LOD w celu zmniejszenia złożoności modelu przy zachowaniu szczegółów potrzebnych do analizy oświetlenia. Zaprojektowanie wydajnej struktury danych do organizowania i zarządzania różnorodnymi danymi wejściowymi, wspierającej obliczenia oświetlenia oparte na AI. Projektowanie i implementacja algorytmów obliczających oświetlenie dla trójwymiarowej przestrzeni. Zintegrowanie różnych parametrów oświetlenia (np. jasność, kąt i pokrycie) z algorytmem w celu dokładnej optymalizacji. Wdrożenie technik przetwarzania równoległego w celu przyspieszenia optymalizacji 3D na dużą skalę. Opracowanie i udoskonalenie procedur optymalizacyjnych dla optymalizacji częściowych. Badanie metod analiz stanu infrastruktury oświetleniowej pod kątem m.in. obciążenia obwodów, zużycia energii, potencjału oszczędności, benchmarków i priorytetów modernizacyjnych przy zadanym budżecie. Optymalizacja wydajności systemu. Profilowanie algorytmów w celu identyfikacji komponentów wymagających dużych zasobów i optymalizacji. Refaktoryzacja kodu w celu poprawy wydajności i zarządzania czasem wykonania oraz zasobami. Ocena skuteczności istniejących potoków danych. Wymagania …

items.desc: Die Sektion für Klinische Forschungs-IT (SKFIT) wird am UKSH Campus Lübeck eine eigene Plattform für ML-getriebene klinische Entscheidungsunterstützung aufbauen – von der Forschung bis in die Versorgung. Dafür suchen wir eine (Medizin-)Informatikerin/einen (Medizin-)Informatiker im Bereich der KI/ML-getriebenen Datenanalyse für klinische Entscheidungsunterstützungssysteme. Warum diese Stelle besonders ist Als Teil des UKSH dürfen wir Patientendaten inhouse analysieren und eigene klinische Entscheidungsunterstützungssysteme (CDSS) nicht nur erforschen, sondern nach 6 GDNG und Art. 5 Abs. 5 MDR (VO (EU) 2017/745) auch vereinfacht in die Versorgung überführen. Dadurch können innovative Lösungen vergleichsweise schnell von der Idee bis in die klinische Anwendung gebracht werden, ein Umfeld, das in dieser Form bisher nur wenige Forschungsgruppen in Deutschland bieten. Die SKFIT betreibt die langfristig angelegte klinische Forschungs-IT-Infrastruktur für Kliniker:innen und Forschende am UKSH Campus Lübeck und an der Universität zu Lübeck (Schwerpunkt Biobank- und Studienmanagement) und forscht zu KI-/ML-getriebener medizinischer Datenanalyse. Mit dieser Stelle zielen wir darauf ab, eine eigene ML-getriebene CDSS-Plattform aufzubauen. Start in unserem Team Kommen Sie in unser Team und unterstützen Sie uns zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, zunächst für drei Jahre. Das bieten wir Ihnen: Möglichkeit zur Promotion (Die Stelle ist als Promotionsstelle angelegt, die Betreuung erfolgt direkt im Haus. Prof. Dr. Fudickar ist Zweitmitglied der Sektion MINT der Universität zu Lübeck (inkl. The work will contribute to evidence-based decision-making, the development of practical solutions and the advancement of
items.desc: Liverpool John Moores University (LJMU) is a distinctive, unique institution, rooted in the Liverpool City Region and with a global presence. Our students and staff, past, present, and future, are the beating heart of our city and can be found in every corner of every industry and community. We couldn’t exist anywhere else and have shaped the city in which we belong. Working with the people of Liverpool to improve lives and support communities is at the heart of why we were founded and why we exist today. We are now looking for highly motivated Research Fellow (PDRA) to develop and conduct individual and/or collaborative research projects. This is a 24-month fixed-term appointment supported by the EPSRC-funded Maritime and Last Mile Net Zero (MaLaMi) Place Based Impact Acceleration Account, under the supervision of Professor Zaili Yang, offering an opportunity to contribute to innovative research and practical solutions for maritime and last-mile decarbonisation. You will support the development and application of quantitative and data-driven approaches to address challenges in maritime transportation, sustainable logistics and decarbonisation, with particular focus on Engineering Net Zero, Artificial Intelligence (AI), digitalisation and data. The work will contribute to evidence-based decision-making, the development of practical solutions and the advancement of sustainable transport systems. Key responsibilities include: 1) contributing to scoping, feasibility assessment and proof-of-concept development for maritime and last-mile decarbonisation projects; 2) supporting the development and application of quantitative and data-driven models, including modelling, simulation, optimisation and machine learning; and 3) assisting in the development, testing and evaluation of analytical tools, prototypes and demonstrators, working collaboratively with academic researchers and external partners. You should possess a good honours degree and a PhD (or equivalent professional experience) in transport, logistics, engineering, operations research, data science or a relevant discipline. You must demonstrate strong quantitative research and data-analysis capabilities, proficiency in programming or analytical tools, and the ability to disseminate research findings through high-quality publications in international journals and refereed conferences. Experience with research or innovation projects related to maritime decarbonisation, sustainable logistics, AI, digitalisation or proof-of-concept development is preferred. You will work as part of the EPSRC-funded MaLaMi programme, collaborating with an interdisciplinary team of researchers, investigators and external partners, within the Liverpool Logistics Offshore and Marine Research Institute (LOOM) at Liverpool John Moores University, UK. LOOM enjoys an international research reputation in maritime risk studies, https://www.ljmu.ac.uk/research/centres-and-institutes/loom . In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies. This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do. If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you. The School/department is committed to promoting equality and diversity, including the Athena SWAN Gender Equality charter for promoting the career of women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) in higher education. We particularly welcome applications from women for this post and all appointments will be made on merit. Please note all of our vacancies will be closed to applications at midnight on the advertised closing date, unless otherwise stated.

items.desc: Chi siamo Dal 2007, coltiviamo talenti con idee innovative, incentiviamo il gioco di squadra e promuoviamo una lunga esperienza operativa e strategica basata su ricerca e sviluppo. L’entusiasmo, le idee e il dinamismo sono il nostro faro: poniamo al centro i bisogni dei nostri clienti e lavoriamo per rispondere al meglio alle loro esigenze. Oggi, la nostra sfida è accompagnare i clienti nella Digital Transformation, integrando sistemi connessi, tecnologie intelligenti, realtà virtuale e aumentata, IoT e Big Data, per offrire soluzioni avanzate e competitive. Con sedi a Roma, Milano e Torino ci avvaliamo di professionisti altamente specializzati, utilizziamo tecnologie all’avanguardia e anticipiamo le richieste di mercato. Chi stiamo cercando Siamo alla ricerca di un/una Data Scientist che contribuisca alla progettazione, allo sviluppo e alla validazione di componenti algoritmiche. La figura ideale possiede solide competenze in Python e interesse per l’analisi e la risoluzione di problemi complessi, preferibilmente in ambito di ottimizzazione matematica e Ricerca Operativa. Attività principali Progettazione, implementazione e validazione di componenti algoritmiche. Sviluppo di servizi e API REST per l’integrazione tra applicazioni e algoritmi. Gestione e interrogazione di database relazionali per l’elaborazione dei dati. Sviluppo e sperimentazione di soluzioni basate su modelli di ottimizzazione matematica e algoritmi di Ricerca Operativa. Integrazione e supporto alla distribuzione dei componenti sviluppati tramite tecnologie di containerizzazione. Requisiti Solida conoscenza del linguaggio Python . Esperienza nell’utilizzo di API REST e nello sviluppo di servizi per l’integrazione tra applicativi e algoritmi. Buona conoscenza di SQL e familiarità con database relazionali, in particolare PostgreSQL . Conoscenza di base di Docker e dei principali concetti di containerizzazione. Esperienza nella formulazione e risoluzione di problemi di Ricerca Operativa , ottimizzazione combinatoria e programmazione matematica. Conoscenza di framework e solver per l’ottimizzazione, quali Pyomo, GLPK, IPOPT o equivalenti. Esperienza con Google OR-Tools , in particolare con il solver CP-SAT . Conoscenza di PyTorch e degli Autoencoders . Esperienza nell’utilizzo di servizi AWS . items.desc: At Cadence, we hire and develop leaders and innovators who want to make an impact on the world of technology. Join BETA CAE Systems, Greece, as a Physics-AI Engineer and become part of Cadence Design Systems, the pivotal leader in mechanical and electronic systems design. Leveraging Cadence’s Intelligent System Design strategy and BETA CAE’s innovative engineering solutions, we deliver advanced products that empower some of the world’s most forward-thinking companies across diverse industries such as consumer electronics, hyperscale computing, communications, automotive, aerospace, and healthcare. In this role, you will operate at the intersection of engineering, numerical simulation, and machine learning. You will work to bridge current CAE workflows with the next generation of AI-enabled engineering products. We are seeking an AI Engineer with a strong background in Mechanical or Civil Engineering to work on our simulation pipelines around material modeling and process simulations. You will design, train, and deploy AI models and surrogate systems that drastically reduce computation time for structural analyses, while maintaining high physical accuracy. Your focus will be on developing results prediction for structures, considering their manufacturing processes and methods. You will be working to capture the physics of stamping simulations, composite materials and laminated structures, and integrate them into finite element models or deliver as direct results to the analysts. Your Day-to-day Will Include AI surrogate modeling, where you will develop reduced-order models and deep learning-based surrogates to approximate high-fidelity finite element analyses (FEA) Work on the physics of stamping simulations and composite materials, predicting manufacturability and key results for educating engineers’ decisions Develop AI models to predict structural simulation results while incorporating physical laws to ensure physically consistent predictions Integrate and deploy machine learning models within engineering workflows, developing APIs and software interfaces for use by design and simulation teams Synthetic data generation, using existing simulation frameworks to create, label, and optimize datasets for deep learning models Develop validation pipelines that rigorously test the accuracy, latency, and failure modes of AI approaches against traditional numerical solvers Qualifications & Experience Bachelor of Science, Master of Science, or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a closely related field Experience with commercial and open-source CAE/FEA software (e.g., NASTRAN, Abaqus, ANSYS). Solid understanding of continuum mechanics, and numerical methods AI/ML Proficiency and background in Python and deep learning frameworks like PyTorch or TensorFlow Familiarity with concepts of generative modeling applied to physical sciences Software Engineering skills in C++ and basic understanding of deploying models into production Proficiency in the English language What We Offer Permanent employment contract following a six-month evaluation period Competitive salary package State-of-the-art and continuously updated equipment (hardware and software) Ongoing training in the latest technologies related to the field Opportunities for professional growth and skill enhancement Comprehensive private health insurance Employee Assistance Program Complimentary breakfast and lunch at the company dining hall Company-provided transportation to and from the premises Fully equipped on-site gym Participation in the company’s Private Pension Fund (T.E.A.) Ample parking facilities with electric car charging Comfortable and modern working environment Apply now for a place in our team! We’re doing work that matters. Help us solve what others can’t.

items.desc: En decisiOM.ai desarrollamos software para la orquestación de decisiones. Nuestra plataforma ayuda a las organizaciones a gobernar las decisiones que toman sus sistemas, garantizando que cada acción automatizada sea trazable, consistente y explicable. Nuestra tecnología es independiente de la plataforma y se adapta a distintos sectores, en cualquier contexto donde las decisiones deban automatizarse y, al mismo tiempo, ser auditables y responsables. Buscamos Machine Learning Engineers con sólida experiencia en el desarrollo, despliegue y orquestación de modelos predictivos y de decisión , así como en su integración en procesos de negocio reales. El objetivo es garantizar soluciones escalables, confiables y orientadas a generar valor medible para el negocio. Responsabilidades Diseñar, desarrollar y optimizar modelos de Machine Learning para resolver problemas de negocio. Implementar modelos de decisión para evaluar escenarios, generar recomendaciones y automatizar acciones. Desarrollar y administrar pipelines para la ejecución, integración y orquestación de modelos. Gestionar el entrenamiento, la validación, el despliegue y el monitoreo de modelos en entornos productivos. Integrar soluciones de Machine Learning mediante APIs, microservicios y plataformas en la nube. Aplicar prácticas de MLOps para el control de versiones, monitoreo y gestión del ciclo de vida de los modelos. Evaluar el desempeño de los modelos mediante métricas técnicas y de negocio. Colaborar con los equipos de Data Science, Data Engineering y áreas de negocio para desarrollar soluciones escalables. Requisitos técnicos Lenguajes de programación: Python y SQL. Machine Learning: Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, TensorFlow o PyTorch. Modelado de decisiones: Árboles de decisión, analítica predictiva, optimización y análisis de escenarios. Orquestación: Apache Airflow, Prefect, Dagster o herramientas equivalentes. MLOps: MLflow, pipelines de Machine Learning, CI/CD, monitoreo y control de versiones de modelos. Integración: APIs REST, FastAPI y microservicios. Plataformas en la nube: Experiencia con AWS, Azure o Google Cloud Platform. Contenedores: Docker y Kubernetes. Control de versiones: Git, GitHub o GitLab. Experiencia requerida Más de 4 años de experiencia en Machine Learning en modelos de decisión y predictivos. Experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo, despliegue y operación de modelos en entornos productivos. Experiencia en la automatización y orquestación de datos y pipelines de Machine Learning. Conocimientos en optimización de modelos, evaluación del desempeño y mejora continua. Capacidad para traducir requerimientos de negocio en soluciones técnicas escalables. Inglés conversacional avanzado, con capacidad para comunicarse eficazmente en entornos profesionales. Competencias clave Sólido pensamiento analítico y habilidades para la resolución de problemas complejos. Orientación a resultados y toma de decisiones basada en datos. Capacidad para diseñar soluciones técnicas y trabajar colaborativamente en equipo. Comunicación efectiva con equipos multidisciplinarios. Requisitos deseables Experiencia en Inteligencia de Decisiones ( Decision Intelligence ) o automatización de decisiones. Conocimientos de investigación de operaciones y optimización matemática. Experiencia con motores de reglas de negocio y plataformas de toma de decisiones automatizada. Familiaridad con técnicas de explicabilidad y gobernanza de modelos, como SHAP, gestión del riesgo de modelos y trazabilidad de auditoría. Experiencia en industrias reguladas. ¿Te interesa esta oportunidad? Si tienes experiencia en Machine Learning, automatización y despliegue de modelos, y buscas contribuir a proyectos de alto impacto, te invitamos a postularte y compartir tu experiencia con nosotros. Si has llevado modelos de Machine Learning a producción y te interesa desarrollar soluciones que permitan gobernar y explicar las decisiones automatizadas, nos gustaría conocerte . Postúlate y cuéntanos sobre tu experiencia.

items.desc: ATG has a wealth of data, with millions of guests visiting, eating, and drinking in our theatres every year, and there is a growing need to bring machine learning and data-driven decision-making into our core business processes. The focus of this role is to improve revenue, customer satisfaction, retention, and acquisition by delivering production-ready machine learning solutions and actionable insights from our customer data. You will join a small, growing ML team at a pivotal time for ATG, taking ownership of defined parts of our ML estate, and working towards wider ownership as you grow. We have built a Data Platform that collates our rich transactional and behavioural data in a cloud-based environment (Snowflake and AWS), enabling scalable analytics and machine learning across the business. You will contribute to the development, deployment, and continuous improvement of machine learning systems, including a revenue management application used by teams across the UK, USA, and Europe. Working alongside other ML Engineers, you will take ownership of defined workstreams (for example, a regional pipeline, a monitoring layer, or a model component), progressively taking on more of the end-to-end lifecycle: data ingestion, model training and evaluation, deployment, pricing recommendations and production monitoring. You will also have the opportunity to help design and implement AI/LLM-powered solutions, such as internal tools, decision-support systems, or workflow automation, ensuring they are well-evaluated, cost-effective, and integrated with our data platform. You will work closely with Data Science, Technology, Product, and commercial teams, helping to bridge the gap between models, AI systems, and real business decisions. Key Responsibilities You will help us maximise the value we derive from our data, building and iterating machine learning models, propensity models, and audience segmentations. You will collaborate across technical and business teams to create assets that can be used and understood. Take ownership of defined components of the revenue management application (i.e. regional pipelines, seat map and pricing data pulls, or model inference), including their reliability and ongoing improvement. Productionise and automate machine learning models end-to-end, including data ingestion, feature engineering, model training and evaluation, inference, and delivery of pricing recommendations. Build and maintain data pipelines and MLOps workflows (CI/CD, model versioning, reproducibility, runtime handling) in AWS and Snowflake. Support the diagnosis and resolution of production issues, including on-call style triage of failed pipeline runs and data quality problems, escalating to the Lead ML Engineer where needed. Design and implement monitoring for model outputs (data drift, prediction drift, anomaly detection) and build dashboards to track model behaviour and recommendation quality daily. Implement guardrails for pricing recommendations (thresholds, overrides, fallback logic) in line with agreed designs. Write well-tested, documented, maintainable Python and SQL, following team conventions and taking part in peer code review. Work with Data Science to take experimental models and prototypes into production, and with commercial teams to translate business needs into technical requirements. Document systems, runbooks, and model behaviour so that knowledge is shared across the team. Contribute to the design and build of LLM-powered solutions (e.g. internal tools, decision-support systems, automation workflows), including prompt management, versioning, and evaluation. Use our data platform to support and automate decision-making across the business, bringing data together to constantly improve our understanding of our products and customers. Be an active part of our data community as we build new capability across disciplines, sharing learning and contributing to team standards. Your Skills, Qualities, And Experience. If you have most of the essential criteria, we encourage you to apply, and welcome transferable skills from other industries or backgrounds. We can give experience of any desirable criteria but may also use them to decide between candidates for this role. Essential Proven experience as a machine learning engineer, data scientist, or similar role, with a track record of delivering ML work into production. Experience of building and optimising data science workloads in cloud environments (AWS preferred). Strong Python and SQL, including writing complex queries and well-structured, tested code. Experience deploying and maintaining ML models in production, with a working understanding of MLOps (CI/CD, versioning, reproducibility). Experience building monitoring, alerting, and observability for data or ML systems. Cytomos has developed a disruptive, IP-protected technology platform that provides label-free cell analytics to support the discovery, development, and manufacture of next-generation biologic and cell-based therapies. items.desc: Founding Robot Learning Engineer | YC-Backed Physical AI & Robotics Startup | London (Remote) | Full-Time | Up to £150K + Equity About The Company Our client is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) physical AI data company building the foundational human video and motion datasets for leading robotics and embodied-AI teams. Focused on egocentric first-person video and UMI demonstration data, the company turns real-world capture operations into high-precision, versioned data products that foundation-model and VLA teams rely on to train physical robots. Backed by a freshly closed seed round, their core constraint is supply, not demand. They are actively scaling deployment engineering, field operations, and capture hardware to keep up with massive customer demand. The founders are building a three-person founding engineering team to set the technical standards, tooling, and evaluation methodology behind the world's reference dataset for robot learning. About The Role Reporting to the Engineering Lead (and working directly with partners and founders), the Founding Robot Learning Engineer bridges human demonstration data and real-world policy performance. You will decide, with empirical evidence, what datasets the company should collect and how that data should be represented. This role balances hands-on data workflow engineering with policy experimentation. You will build task segmentation and assisted-labeling workflows, construct policy data loaders, and execute policy training and evaluation experiments using egocentric and UMI datasets to prove that the company's data directly improves robot task success. Key Responsibilities Turn long recordings into useful task intervals, define annotation schemas for specific customer needs, and ensure every label remains frame-locked to the source video. Deploy AI models to propose task boundaries and labels, route uncertain results for human review, write labeling instructions, and measure reviewer consistency. Build custom data loaders and transformations that format video, labels, and motion trajectories (including human hand motion and UMI gripper paths) into policy-ready inputs. Fine-tune and evaluate robot policies on human demonstration data, running controlled baseline comparisons, held-out split tests, and task performance evaluations under realistic test conditions. Translate policy evaluation insights into precise data recommendations—guiding perception and capture teams on which tasks, viewpoints, and annotations yield the highest policy improvement. Skills & Competencies Demonstrated experience training, fine-tuning, and evaluating robot manipulation or imitation learning policies (e.g., Diffusion Policies, VLAs, ACT). Strong Python and PyTorch capability with comfort building dataset interfaces, loaders, and annotation tooling alongside ML research. Deep understanding of evaluation leakage, dataset confounders, and the gap between offline loss metrics and physical robot task success. Experience working with temporal action segmentation, video annotations, spatial trajectories, and human-to-robot data transfer. Qualifications & Experience Background as a Robot Learning Engineer, Embodied AI Researcher, or Robotics ML Engineer. Proven track record of personally preparing training data, training or fine-tuning robot policies, and evaluating physical or simulated task performance. Hands-on implementation experience connecting dataset decisions directly to policy improvements, identifying confounders, and preventing data leakage. Background in physical robot manipulation, diffusion policies, vision-language-action models, or human-to-robot transfer is highly desirable. Role Details Timing: Immediate Start. Location: London (Remote). Package: Competitive base salary up to £150K + significant founding-engineer equity with absolute ownership over policy evaluation and dataset standards.

Job Description: 
 Your impact 
 Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one? 
 At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something extraordinary - shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety. 
 We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical or business professionals, and as such we will also support you through your preferred route for professional development. 
 Our 18-month Graduate Programmes give you the opportunity to work on exciting and challenging projects alongside industry leaders. 
On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum, plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria. 
 We encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience. 
 We have a fantastic new opportunity for a graduate to join the Advanced Targeting line of business as an Optical Engineer. Your role as a Graduate Optical Engineer will be solve real-world engineering challenges, designing and developing mission-critical solutions that power some of the world’s most advanced defence and security systems under the guidance and support of experienced Optical Engineers. The Graduate programme will offer you 18 months of development, with placements in three phases of the product life cycle. You will learn how to use state-of-the-art tools and technology to explore all aspects of the development lifecycle, including requirements analysis, concept design, and design for manufacture, implementation, test, build and product support. 
 What you’ll do as a Graduate Optical Engineer 
 As a Graduate Optical Engineer, you will manage your own development towards attaining Optical Engineer level through the Graduate Development Scheme over 18 months.
 To achieve this goal, you will be placed in programmes responsible progressing different parts of a product life cycle:
 New product introduction: tasked with learning the core concepts required to increase the manufacturing rate, such as modelling an existing to designs to identify root-cause analysis of observed problems and use of metrology to validate theories.
 Detailed product design: responsible for developing or improving existing designs and supporting the transfer of optical models into a detailed optical and system requirements.
 Novel concepts: to develop technologies both future and improvement of existing products.
 Throughout these placements you will learn skills required to communicate technical concepts across a wide array of disciplines. You will be expected support optical procurement and the wider product team in the creation and changing of drawings, tolerancing and how to develop of experiments to prove capability of your designs. Finally, you will be tasked performing technical reviews to assess the limits on technical capability and for creating and conducting optical tests to lower the technical risks of novel EO-Systems and solutions identified as part of wider technological reviews. 
 What you’ll bring 
 A minimum of a 2:1 master’s degree or a higher, such as a EngD or PhD.
 Relevant experience of photonics, such as summer placements, internships or research projects.
 Experience with technical writing and project planning.
 Strong analytical, modelling skills and laboratory skills.
 Evidence of successfully working in a team.
 Enthusiasm for photonics and an interest in developing your technical capabilities.
 Experience of modelling tools such as Ansys Zemax Optics Studio, Matlab, LabVIEW, and COMSOL (or equivalent) is desirable.
 Security Clearance 
 Many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years. 
 For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV). As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.

As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.

 At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something extraordinary - shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.

 At Leonardo, we develop the advanced technologies that help keep people safe. As a Graduate Firmware Engineer , you'll join a team delivering world-leading Electronic Warfare capabilities that protect fast jets, UAVs, naval vessels and land platforms operating in some of the world's most demanding environments.
 Our structured 18-month Graduate Programme is designed to accelerate your development from graduate to professional engineer. From day one, you'll contribute to real projects, work alongside industry experts, and gain hands-on experience across the full firmware development lifecycle.
 This opportunity is based in Luton , with flexible and hybrid working arrangements available. Occasional travel within the UK and overseas may be required to support technical reviews, trials and customer engagements.
