As a Research Data Scientist, you will bring a rigorous scientific approach to the continuous development and improvement of the services associated with our technology platform. You will work both independently and collaboratively with other researchers, software engineers, and customer-facing biological and operational teams to transform real-world operational data into robust
items.desc: Stingray Marine Solutions AS Stålfjæra 26, 0975 Oslo, Norge, 0975 Oslo Om jobben Lagre favoritt Stillingstittel Research Data Scientist Type ansettelse Fast, heltid 100% Antall stillinger 1 Arbeidsspråk Engelsk eller norsk Søk senest søndag 1. november Did you know that Stingray delivers world-leading Norwegian high-tech? We develop intelligent aquaculture technology for the removal of salmon lice 24/7 using machine vision and laser, as well as monitoring lice levels, measuring fish welfare and growth. Collectively, this is known as The Fish Health Hub ™. Our technology contributes to increased food production on nature's terms, without compromising the environment and animal welfare. With our services, we are proud to help shape the future of aquaculture - Made in Norway. Apply science and data to real-world aquaculture challenges We are now looking for a Research Data Scientist to strengthen our Research team and help turn complex biological and operational information into scientific insight and practical applications. As part of Stingray Aqua, the Research team acts as a bridge between technology and data specialists and customer-facing teams. Aqua Research builds and shares knowledge across Stingray and the wider aquaculture sector. It also supports the development and validation of data-driven solutions that strengthen our day-to-day services and operations, ultimately supporting better fish welfare and customer success in Norway, Iceland, and the Faroe Islands. Key Responsibilities - What will you do? As a Research Data Scientist, you will bring a rigorous scientific approach to the continuous development and improvement of the services associated with our technology platform. You will work both independently and collaboratively with other researchers, software engineers, and customer-facing biological and operational teams to transform real-world operational data into robust analytical workflows and functional capabilities that others can rely on. You will combine rigorous data analysis with iterative technical development, while keeping focus on the biological complexities associated with fish behavior and the constraints of ongoing farming operations. Your work will contribute directly to creating tools and capabilities used by our customers and employees. Your tasks and responsibilities in this role will include: Driving the iterative development of functional capabilities by developing concepts and analytical workflows to test and refine methods and assumptions, ensuring that solutions remain grounded in data and biological understanding. Designing and evaluating validation studies based on data from commercial aquaculture operations, applying appropriate experimental and statistical methods to account for biological variability and operational constraints. Analyzing extensive biological and operational datasets and developing statistical models to identify and evaluate meaningful patterns, relationships, and opportunities for improvement. Defining data requirements and independently retrieving, combining, and quality-assuring large and heterogenous data sets to build reproducible analytical workflows and reusable data pipelines, ensuring traceability and appropriate documentation throughout the process. Interpreting and communicating findings to internal and external audiences, translating complex results into practical insights that support fact-based decision-making and further development. Who we are looking for We are looking for someone with a strong quantitative and computational background who can take ownership of technically complex research problems in the context of day-to-day operations with a focus on fish welfare and behavior. You combine scientific judgement with technical discipline and are comfortable moving between exploratory research questions and the development of hands-on solutions. Most importantly, we are looking for someone who enjoys working across disciplines. You can discuss biological hypotheses with scientists, independently investigate the underlying data, and work with software engineers and customer contacts to determine how a promising research method can become a reliable functional capability. As an ideal candidate, you have: A PhD in aquaculture, biology, environmental science, or another relevant life or quantitative natural science, and preferably 3-5 years of additional relevant research and/or applied analytical experience. A solid understanding of applied research methodology, experimental design, statistical modeling and result validation. The ability to analyze complex longitudinal, time-series, or other observational datasets obtained under real-world operational conditions. Experience with behavioral or sensor data derived from computer vision, sonar, or other monitoring systems is an advantage. Strong programming, data analysis, and statistical modelling skills using tools such as R and/or Python. Experience with Power BI is an advantage. …

items.desc: About IntelliDigest IntelliDigest is a purpose-driven company working with stakeholders across the food system, from farm to fork, supporting the transition towards more sustainable and circular approaches to food production. Through technology innovation, applied research, and capacity building, we enable improved resource efficiency, soil health, and sustainable food systems. Our iDigest technology converts organic waste streams into valuable bio-nutrient outputs intended for use as soil improvers, growing media components, and fertilising products, supporting regenerative and low-input agriculture. Role Overview We are seeking a knowledgeable and motivated Plant Scientist to oversee and optimise the use of IntelliDigest bio-nutrient outputs within agricultural and controlled growing environments. The role will focus on the safe, compliant, and effective application of digestate-derived products as soil improvers, growing media constituents, and nutrient sources for food crops. The successful candidate will lead plant growth trials, evaluate agronomic performance, and generate robust scientific evidence to support product validation, farmer adoption, and regulatory compliance. Working closely with research, engineering, and operational teams, you will help translate nutrient recovery innovation into practical, scalable solutions aligned with UK agricultural and environmental standards. This role is well suited to a plant or soil scientist with a strong interest in sustainable agriculture, circular bioeconomy systems, and applied, field-relevant research. Key Responsibilities Plant Growth Trials and Agronomic Research Design, implement, and manage plant growth trials assessing iDigest bio-nutrient products as soil improvers, growing media inputs, or fertilising materials. Evaluate crop performance metrics including establishment, growth rate, nutrient uptake, yield, and produce quality. Compare bio-nutrient performance against conventional fertilisers, soil conditioners, or substrates in line with recognised agronomic methodologies. Monitor and assess soil and growing media parameters, including nutrient availability, organic matter content, pH, structure, and biological activity. Collect, analyse, and interpret agronomic, soil, and plant physiological data to inform product optimisation and application guidance. Prepare clear, evidence-based technical reports and data summaries for internal use and external stakeholders. Regulatory Alignment and Farm Integration Oversee the practical deployment of bio-nutrient products on IntelliDigest-associated farm and pilot sites. Ensure applications align with UK regulatory frameworks, including relevant requirements under PAS 110, end-of-waste criteria, and good agricultural practice. Support compliance with the Farming Rules for Water, nutrient management planning, and environmental protection standards. Develop and refine application protocols, including rates, timings, and crop-specific guidance, consistent with soil nutrient requirements and environmental safeguards. Work with farm operators to ensure correct handling, storage, and application of digestate-derived materials. Contribute to the development of documentation supporting product classification as a soil improver or fertilising product where applicable. Collaboration and Project Support Work closely with R&D scientists, engineers, and operations teams to align plant performance outcomes with process development and nutrient recovery technologies. Support cross-functional projects involving enzymatic biocatalysis, nutrient management, and sustainable food production systems. Participate in project meetings, providing scientific insight, progress updates, and evidence-based recommendations. Liaise with external partners including farmers, agronomists, research institutions, and regulatory bodies as required. Continuous Improvement and Knowledge Development Maintain awareness of developments in plant science, soil health, digestate utilisation, and sustainable nutrient management. Identify opportunities to improve trial design, data quality, and on-farm implementation practices. Contribute scientific input to grant applications, regulatory submissions, technical guidance, and impact reporting. Engage in continued professional development to strengthen expertise in applied plant and soil science. Essential Requirements Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Plant Science, Agronomy, Soil Science, Horticulture, Environmental Science, or a related discipline. Demonstrable experience designing and conducting plant or agronomic trials in agricultural, horticultural, or controlled-environment settings. Strong understanding of plant nutrition, soil fertility, and soil improver or fertiliser performance. Experience handling, analysing, and interpreting agronomic and soil data. Excellent organisational and record-keeping skills, with attention to regulatory and quality requirements. Effective written and verbal …

items.desc: About Us Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care. Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on. Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members. We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you. If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use. The Job We're looking for a talented and driven Product Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build across the whole stack, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Your goal is to shrink the time from a customer request to a deployed solution, without cutting corners on reliability or on the privacy of residents' health data. In this role, you will focus on: Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them. Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward. Fast Iteration: Break large designs and features into small shippable pieces. Get MVPs in front of users quickly, measure how they're used, and iterate or kill them. Backend & APIs: Design and build the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them. Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Build test coverage and use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on. Qualifications Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build. Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native. Comfortable working across the stack: you've built backend APIs and worked with relational databases (e.g. Postgres), not just UI. Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed. Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions. Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team. Nice to Have Experience with React Native and Expo in production. AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience. Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications. Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR). Experience shipping products across multiple markets and languages. What We Offer Participation in our warrant program (stock options). A small team where your decisions directly shape the product. Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate. Join Our Team We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

items.desc: About Us At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference. The Job Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there. In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest: Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life. OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward. Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things. Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application. Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely. Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team. Qualifications: Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs. Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices. Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers. Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards. Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT. Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team. Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus. Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus. Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus. What We Offer Participation in our warrant program (stock options). Work with state-of-the-art technology in a pioneering field. A vibrant, learning-focused work environment. A role where you can make a significant impact on healthcare delivery. Join Our Team We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

items.desc: Posizione post-doc in ambito Multimodal e Generative AI per Imaging Biomedico e Genetica Sede di lavoro: Genova Per l'Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (IIT) cerchiamo un/una PhD con competenze avanzate in machine learning e computer vision, da inserire nel team di ricerca AIGO per lavorare su modelli multimodali e generativi per l'imaging biomedico, con l'obiettivo di predire informazioni genetiche e di rischio clinico a partire da immagini mediche. Continua a leggere l'annuncio se: Hai un PhD in AI, ML, Computer Vision, Informatica, Ingegneria, Fisica, Matematica o discipline affine Hai maturato una solida esperienza di ricerca in Machine Learning, Deep Learning e Computer Vision, preferibilmente applicata all’imaging medico, biomedico o ad altri ambiti scientifici Hai lavorato su modelli multimodali o approcci capaci di integrare immagini con dati strutturati, biologici, clinici o genetici Hai già pubblicazioni su riviste e conferenze scientifiche di ML, DL e Computer Vision Non è l'annuncio per te se: Cerchi un posto a tempo indeterminato Vieni dalla genetica o dalla genomica, ma non hai mai lavorato con modelli di deep learning Hai utilizzato modelli di Machine Learning o Deep Learning prevalentemente come strumenti già disponibili, senza occuparti direttamente del loro sviluppo, addestramento o adattamento a problemi scientifici complessi Per chi ti stai candidando Le persone selezionate lavoreranno all'interno dell'Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (IIT), nato con lo scopo di promuovere lo sviluppo tecnologico del nostro Paese e l'alta formazione tecnologica, favorendo così lo sviluppo del sistema produttivo nazionale. La figura selezionata entrerà a far parte del gruppo di ricerca Artificial Intelligence for Good (AIGO), coordinato dal Prof. Vittorio Murino, punto di riferimento a livello internazionale nel campo dell'Intelligenza Artificiale. Il gruppo, composto ormai da circa 25 persone tra dottorandi, post-doc e ricercatori, si occupa dello studio di modelli di apprendimento in presenza di dati imperfetti, in particolare in scenari multimodali, affrontando contesti di apprendimento non supervisionato, semi-supervisionato, auto-supervisionato, con dati etichettati in modo debole o rumoroso, sbilanciati o distorti. Le aree di ricerca comprendono inoltre domain adaptation e generalization, few/zero-shot learning, continual learning e learning con dati biasati. Il gruppo lavora anche su modelli generativi con particolare attenzione ai più recenti foundation models multimodali, inclusi i Large Language Models (LLM) e i Vision and Language Models (VLM). Ulteriori linee di ricerca riguardano lightweight machine learning per sviluppare tecnologie AI a basso consumo energetico, anche per applicazioni su dispositivi edge (es. robot). Coerentemente con l’attenzione posta sul benessere delle persone, AIGO intende progettare fin dalle fondamenta metodi AI che incorporino aspetti etici, di privacy e fairness, nonché robustezza, orientandosi verso tecniche di deep learning che siano spiegabili, affidabili e trasparenti. Le principali applicazioni riguardano l’ambito biomedicale, biologico, neuroscientifico e sanitario in generale AIGO beneficia inoltre della collaborazione con numerose università e centri di ricerca internazionali, in particolare con le università più vicine di Genova e Verona. Il progetto La posizione è finanziata da Dompé Farmaceutici nell’ambito del progetto AI Driven Prediction of Glaucoma Linked Genetic Variants from OCT Retinal Imaging. Il progetto intende esplorare la possibilità di utilizzare immagini retiniche OCT e dati biomedici eterogenei per ricavare informazioni predittive relative a fattori genetici e al rischio di sviluppare il glaucoma. L’obiettivo della ricerca sarà sviluppare modelli capaci di apprendere dalle immagini rappresentazioni del fenotipo che possano essere utilizzate come indicatori predittivi di fattori genotipici sottostanti. Il progetto mira quindi ad andare oltre gli approcci tradizionalmente basati sull’analisi delle associazioni statistiche, facendo leva sulle capacità del Deep Learning di apprendere da dati di imaging ad alta dimensionalità e da informazioni contestuali e multimodali. Di che cosa ti occuperai: Alla persona non sarà chiesto di applicare modelli già esistenti a un dataset biomedico, ma di contribuire in team alla progettazione, allo sviluppo e alla validazione di nuove soluzioni metodologiche. Collaborando con il resto del team, la figura inserita si occuperà in particolare di: • Progettare e studiare modelli di Machine Learning e Deep Learning in grado di collegare dati di imaging medico a fattori biologici, genotipici o di rischio genetico • Lavorare su modelli multimodali e generativi, representation learning e approcci data driven applicati a immagini e dati biomedici eterogenei • Affrontare le problematiche derivanti dalla supervisione limitata, dall’eterogeneità dei dati e dalla disponibilità di differenti fonti informative • Condurre …

items.desc: The role We are seeking qualified applicants for up to a 2 year position (with possibility to extend to 4) as Research Fellow (postdoc) in Computational Linguistics on the UKRI FLF grant ‘Scaling predictability in Morphological paradigms’, led by Sacha Beniamine. The successful candidate will perform a key role in creating new software tools and employing them to measure predictability in morphology. The position is based at the Surrey Morphology Group at the University of Surrey, in Guildford, and provides the opportunity to work in the vibrant and highly collegial research environment for which the SMG is renowned. The successful candidate will be in charge of the Work Package focusing on New Models, which aims to enable precise and comparable measures of morphological predictability, in order to understand how predictability is organized in realistic, complex inflectional systems. As a core member of the team, the successful candidate will use their skills in software development to extend existing software (Qumin) which analyzes morphological lexical data and evaluates inflectional predictability. They will rely on their qualifications in linguistics to study predictability in systems which challenge existing tools and analyses, pushing the edge of what can be reliably measured and contribute to the large comparative study of macro-variation in predictability, gaining experience in linguistic typology. They will collaborate closely with the team in the writing and dissemination of papers and presentations, and be expected to take initiative in the formulation of the research agenda. About You The successful candidate will have a dual background in linguistics and software development, with a PhD in computational linguistics, natural language processing, or a related field. The candidate will have a good grasp of linguistic concepts and methods. They will have an interest in the inflectional morphology of at least one language or language family, which can serve as a test-bed for the tools they will develop. They will have experience of software development, and are fluent in Python programming. Candidates with experience programming as part of a team will be preferred. Mastery over software development tools (command line; git management; continuous pipelines and workflows; IDE) is essential. An interest in reproducibility in science will be an advantage. Experience in using these skills to answer linguistic questions is essential. How To Apply Please submit your application online: CV Contact details for 2 academic referees. Three relevant works of research (DOI/URL links if possible). Research statement of one page, describing research interests and experience, and how you think this makes you suitable for the advertised post. Please do not seek assistance from AI tools in writing this document. Interviews are planned for Tuesday the 24th of November and will be held online. Please contact Sacha Beniamine, s.beniamine@surrey.ac.uk with any questions.

items.desc: About the Role Imagine pioneering the mathematical and logical foundations that enable AI to fly safely in real-world, safety-critical aviation. As a Machine Learning Certification Researcher, you will address one of the most fundamental challenges in modern AI{{:}} proving that ML models are safe, reliable, and mathematically sound for deployment in autonomous flight. Your work will bridge the gap between cutting-edge statistical learning theory and formal aviation certification frameworks, building upon previous work (EASA CoDANN I and II, and FAA report DOT/FAA/TC-21/48), and putting real-world systems to the test. At Destinus, we are shaping the future of defense through high-speed, autonomous flight technologies. We develop next-generation unmanned aerial systems that deliver greater speed, precision, and efficiency, supporting governments and defense organizations in mission-critical operations worldwide. Daedalean AG, the AI and autonomy hub of the Destinus Group, plays a key role in this vision—developing safety-critical AI systems at the intersection of advanced research and real-world aviation. Enabling machines to perceive, understand, and make decisions in real time, we combine aerospace engineering and artificial intelligence to build the next generation of autonomous flight systems, driving innovation where it matters most. What You'll Do • AI Certification Strategy{{:}} Analyze our existing AI certification strategy and help adapt it—or pioneer entirely new strategies—to certify different supervised ML. • EASA Framework Alignment{{:}} Connect mathematical guarantees, technical arguments, and model evaluations to the EASA W-shaped process for AI certification in aviation, ensuring our research aligns with the latest regulatory guidelines. • Theoretical Foundation & Modeling{{:}} Conduct research into statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and mathematical guarantees for deep neural networks operating under dynamic real-world conditions. • Uncertainty Quantification{{:}} Apply statistics and stochastic processes to model environmental uncertainties and sensor noise, and to quantify confidence in performance metrics. • Literature & Proof Evaluation{{:}} Critically evaluate academic literature, mathematical proofs, and engineering assumptions with peer-review rigor to identify safety limitations and theoretical gaps in state-of-the-art AI. • Regulatory & Audit Justification{{:}} Construct robust, logical arguments and technical justifications that translate complex, high-dimensional empirical data into structured evidence for safety audits and certification frameworks. • Algorithmic Validation{{:}} Write clean, reproducible code in Python to test theoretical hypotheses, validate certification mechanisms, and benchmark model safety frameworks. Requirements What You'll Need Machine Learning Theory & Mathematics • ML Theory & Statistical Learning{{:}} Deep understanding of statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and the mathematical foundations of deep neural networks. • Statistics & Stochastic Processes{{:}} Strong background in advanced probability, statistical modeling, and stochastic processes. • Python Engineering{{:}} Proficiency in Python with the ability to write clean, reproducible code (can also be learned on the job provided strong theoretical foundations and basic Python coding). Research Rigor • Scientific Research Methodology{{:}} Demonstrated capability or background in conducting comprehensive literature reviews, identifying gaps in current state-ofthe-art AI, and synthesizing complex academic concepts into actionable engineering frameworks (can also be learned on the job if you possess a strong quantitative baseline). • Peer Review Expertise{{:}} Ability or experience in the peer-review process—capable of critically evaluating mathematical proofs, algorithmic assumptions, and research papers to assess their validity and limitations. Education • Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Theoretical Statistics, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related quantitative research field. Who You Are • Critical Thinking & Healthy Skepticism{{:}} You possess a strong spirit of questioning everything. You naturally challenge conventional ML assumptions, probe for hidden edge cases, and refuse to take empirical accuracy at face value without rigorous proof. • Logical Argument Building{{:}} You have an exceptional ability to construct robust, airtight logical arguments and technical justifications. You can translate complex empirical observations into structured, defensible evidence that satisfies strict engineering and regulatory scrutiny. • Thrives in Ambiguity{{:}} You are motivated by hard, unsolved mathematical problems at the intersection of theoretical computer science, safety engineering, and real-world flight operations

items.desc: Job Description Within Wandercraft’s Whole Body Control team, you will develop control algorithms for exoskeletons and humanoid robots, from mathematical formulation and simulation to deployment and validation on real robots. You will work on challenging robotics problems involving locomotion, manipulation, multi-contact control and whole-body motion generation, with a strong focus on robustness, performance and real-time execution. Reporting to the Head of Whole Body Control, you will work closely with other control engineers as well as the mechanical, electronics, perception and software teams. Depending on your background and interests, your work may include: Develop whole-body control algorithms for floating-base robots Design control strategies using linear and nonlinear control, MPC and NMPC Develop online and offline trajectory optimization and motion generation algorithms Design and improve whole-body trajectory tracking for locomotion and manipulation Model robot dynamics, contacts and interactions with the environment Develop or integrate state-estimation algorithms using sensor data Explore learning-based approaches, including reinforcement learning, when relevant Write efficient, maintainable software in C++ and Python Test, debug and validate algorithms directly on exoskeletons and humanoid robots Contribute to the architecture and long-term technical direction of the control stack Preferred Experience Diploma: Master’s or PhD degree in Robotics, Controls, Optimization, Applied mathematics, or related scientific field Required experience: Hands-on experience with robotics, control, motion generation, trajectory optimization or related algorithmic development, through industry, research or significant academic projects. Skills: Programming (C++/Python) - Autonomous level Algorithmics - Autonomous level Robotics (kinematics, dynamics, working with sensor data) - Autonomous level Control theory - Autonomous level Machine learning - Basic knowledge Who are they? At Wandercraft we pioneer intelligent robotics to help people do what they can’t do. We apply the most advanced robotics and AI to expand what’s possible for humans in the fields of healthcare and now industry. Founded in 2012, Wandercraft is globally recognized for creating the world’s first self-balancing walking exoskeleton, Atalante X, which is used in more than 100 rehabilitation centers across four continents helping individuals with disabilities re-learn how to walk, with over a million steps taken each month. Building on over a decade of real-world experience and a proprietary neural network trained on billions of steps, we’re bringing mobility beyond clinical settings and into the home. Our personal exoskeleton, Eve, is a first-of-its-kind device designed to assist wheelchair users in standing and walking in everyday life. Now we’re expanding our platform to support industrial and assistive tasks with the Calvin family of humanoid robots. Built in just 40 days, Calvin-40 is designed to relieve factory workers from hazardous labor. Future versions of Calvin will assist persons with reduced autonomy in their daily activities. Our growth into home and industrial robotics opens new horizons while reinforcing our ability to scale innovation, improve reliability, and accelerate our impact, across our entire portfolio of products and industries. From Paris and New York, our team of over 110 engineers, clinicians, researchers, and operators is united by one mission: to design robotics that improve human life, wherever people need them most! We’re not just hiring people: we’re building a team of pioneers, curious minds and problem solvers who want to change the world, step by step. Join us to shape the next generation of medical and humanoid robotics powered by AI and purpose.

items.desc: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About The Role Callosum believes that orders of magnitude improvements in AI systems will come through application-aware orchestration across heterogeneous hardware. We are building that vision: infrastructure that treats the full landscape of compute as a unified, co-evolving system, evolved beyond GPUs. Inference engines were designed for single-model inference on homogeneous GPU clusters - this role builds them beyond that. Working directly on systems like vLLM and SGLang, you will adapt and extend them for heterogeneous resources, making them hardware-aware, with deeper optimisation around scheduling, memory, and execution. The execution strategies you design - parallelism, disaggregation, caching - will define what heterogeneous inference looks like at production scale. Your work ensures that the capabilities exposed by the lower layers of the stack translate into real, measurable gains, the new standard for how inference runs on diverse hardware. What You'll Build Contribute upstream to SGLang and vLLM, and maintain internal forks where our requirements diverge Improve hardware-awareness within inference engines so that scheduling, memory management, and execution adapt to the capabilities of the underlying accelerator Design and implement bespoke parallelism and disaggregation strategies that go beyond default configurations to better exploit heterogeneous hardware Work closely with an Accelerator Systems Software engineer to ensure engine-level abstractions map cleanly onto diverse hardware capabilities What Sets You Apart Deep familiarity with the internals of SGLang, vLLM, or comparable inference serving frameworks - scheduler design, memory management, and execution pipelines Strong background in high-performance Python and C++/CUDA systems, particularly in the context of ML inference Experience designing or implementing parallelism strategies for large model serving Understanding of disaggregated serving architectures and the tradeoffs involved in separating modules of a workflow Demonstrable record of working effectively in fast-moving open source codebases with evolving APIs and design conventions What We Offer Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience Equity & Ownership Private healthcare We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all.

items.card: What you'll do Build the algorithmic core — anomaly detection, plus data profiling, SQL generation, lineage parsing, and change point detection Take a method from a research paper to a tested prototype, then to a production model running online in the engine Work out why a validator over-alerts on a metric — say one with a strong daily and weekly cycle — and reshape how it forms its expected range Tell whether a
items.desc: Validio is the agentic data management platform that automates data quality, lineage, and cataloging — so enterprises can finally trust the data behind their analytics, AI, and reporting. As a Data Scientist on our Algorithm team, you build the models at the heart of the product — the Anomaly Detection that separates good data from bad. A validator watches a metric over time; an ML model decides, for each new value as it arrives, whether it's anomalous and worth waking someone up for. These models run against tens of thousands of time series at once — unattended, unlabeled, with nobody tuning them per customer. You'll own that end to end: reading a metric from a customer's warehouse, running the algorithm online in our pipeline, and persisting the state it carries between runs, fast and reliably at scale. What you'll do Build the algorithmic core — anomaly detection, plus data profiling, SQL generation, lineage parsing, and change point detection Take a method from a research paper to a tested prototype, then to a production model running online in the engine Work out why a validator over-alerts on a metric — say one with a strong daily and weekly cycle — and reshape how it forms its expected range Tell whether a model change actually improved detection across customers, when there's no labelled set to score against Keep a validator's metrics correct and fast in SQL across multiple warehouses Work with Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Support — on the call when the customer describes the problem What you'll bring ML models you've built and deployed to production, serving real predictions to users A strong grounding in statistical modelling — the assumptions a method makes, how it estimates uncertainty, and how it fails when the data breaks them Fluent Python, and either some Rust already or the appetite to learn it here SQL well beyond SELECT — window functions, query plans, dialect differences, and why a query that flies on one warehouse is unusable on another An instinct for performance — reasoning about CPU, memory, and bottlenecks when you implement a new algorithm The range to carry a problem from a vague business need through prototype to measured impact, and to direct AI tools well — knowing what they get subtly wrong Bonus points for Time series, signal processing, anomaly detection, or unsupervised methods Inference engineering — optimising runtimes and model throughput on general-purpose hardware Our stack, and why Rust for most of the engine and backend. Python for exploration and prototyping in the Algorithm team, where modelling usually starts, and for parts of the service like the SDK and IaC tooling. SQL in every dialect that matters — we push computation down to the warehouse when we can and stream through our own pipeline when we can't. Postgres and Redis for state, Kubernetes and Helm to deploy, which lets us run Validio both as SaaS and fully air-gapped. Claude, Gemini, and Codex in daily use. Why Validio Founded in Sweden in 2019, we're trusted by data-driven enterprises like Nordea, Canva, Truecaller, Traveloka, and Deutsche Glasfaser. We raised a $30M Series A this year and grew ARR 800% in twelve months as enterprises got serious about making their data AI-ready. At around 40 people, you'll own initiatives end to end and make the call when you're closest to the problem — strict about testing and documentation, and fast about decisions. Come as you are. We hire for what you'll build with us, and we welcome applicants of every background.

items.desc: Rejoindre Davidson, ce n’est pas seulement intégrer un groupe de 3000 consultants dans 6 pays et 2 continents, c’est intégrer LA société qui a été élue par ses salariés Great Place To Work France et Europe pendant 4 ans mais aussi une des plus grandes B Corp de France, nommée Best of the World dans la catégorie “collaborateurs” en 2022 ! (Les “B Corp” formant une communauté de sociétés qui ont décidé d’être non pas les meilleures du monde mais les meilleures POUR le monde). Parce que notre développement repose sur des principes forts : Un profond respect de l’ensemble de nos parties prenantes : consultant(e)s, clients et fournisseurs. Car si le travail “ne fait pas le bonheur”, il peut cependant “faire le malheur”. Nous nous engageons donc à écouter et agir avec honnêteté. Une égalité des chances dans le traitement de nos candidatures et dans la gestion de carrière de nos salarié(e)s. Nous croyons en un milieu de travail où équité F/H, inclusion et diversité sont la norme. Une empreinte environnementale minimale, et sociétale maximale. C’est pourquoi, au-delà des missions que vous réaliserez, vous pourrez également contribuer à des projets que Davidson soutient : missions de solidarité internationale (avec Planète Urgence), bénévolat auprès d’associations (chaque Davidsonien(ne) dispose de 3 jours par an pour intervenir à leurs côtés), accompagnement d’étudiant(e)s issus de milieux peu favorisés (avec Article 1), investissement dans des startups développant des solutions innovantes, actions collectives et individuelles pour la réduction de notre impact carbone… Un Management adhocratique basé sur la mise en œuvre des principes de “l’entreprise horizontale” et du “management tribal”. Sur ce dernier point une précision d’importance : le bien-être au travail est un luxe qu’il faut pouvoir s’offrir en étant une entreprise “solide”. Ceci induit pour les Davidsonien(ne)s d’allier prises d’initiative, engagement et professionnalisme. Car “sans travail, le talent n’est qu’une sale manie”. Et cela nous incite à chercher à recruter des personnes… meilleures que nous… Nous encourageons les candidatures de personnes en situation de handicap, et nous nous engageons à répondre au mieux à leurs besoins spécifiques. Profil / Mission Dans le cadre de projets Data Science menés par Davidson pour ses clients dans des secteurs variés (Gaming, Luxe, Télécoms, Finance, etc.), tu interviendras en tant que spécialiste ML & DL. Ta mission consistera à accompagner des experts métiers sur des problématiques variées : traitement du langage naturel, reconnaissance d’images, détection de la fraude, système de recommandation, agent conversationnel, etc. À Ces Fins Tes Missions Consisteront à Animer des ateliers d’expression de besoins Identifier, intégrer et croiser les sources de données (structurées ou non structurées) Préparer et analyser des données Créer, implémenter des modèles Prototyper et valider les algorithmes Mesurer les gains obtenus Communiquer et capitaliser sur les résultats Réaliser une veille technologique ainsi que des études d’opportunités Compétences requises ou à acquérir De formation ingénieur / BAC+5, tu as déjà réussi plusieurs projets dans le domaine de la Data Science. Avec au minimum 2 ans d’expérience professionnelle (et c’est vraiment un minimum hein…) Des compétences scripting sont nécessaires. Et mieux vaut être fort en maths ! Aptitudes / Savoir-être Excellent relationnel Capacité d’analyse Curiosité Pédagogie Anglais + SQL / Python bilingue Description du pôle Métiers de la donnée La donnée est aujourd’hui un actif stratégique au cœur de la transformation digitale des entreprises et à la base de la création de multiples nouveaux services. Davidson dispose d’une expertise unique autour de la donnée qui lui permet d’intervenir de bout-en-bout pour ses clients, qu’ils soient data-driven ou cherchent « simplement » à valoriser leurs données. Nos Métiers Accompagnement à la mise en place d’une stratégie données Architecture Big Data Data visualisation Data science Notre Environnement Technique Infrastructures & Stockage : Cloud (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform), Cloudera, MapReduce, Hortonworks, mongoDB, Hadoop, Cassandra, Splunk, Redis, CouchDB Traitement de données : Spark, Scala, Kafka, Logstach, Elasticsearch, Hive, Storm, Flink Analytics : R, Python, SPSS&SAS, TensorFlow, Sickit learn Dataviz : grafana, dataiku, kibana, Tableau, Qlik, Outil propre JS Devops & containers : Docker, puppet, Jenkins, Sonar, Openshift, Kubernetes, Ansible Domaines : Machine Learning, Deep Learning

We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system. We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber. items.desc: Who we are At Yieldigo, we help leading retailers make smarter pricing and promotion decisions through advanced analytics , machine learning , and optimization . This role sits at the intersection of Data Science , Data Engineering , and Analytics . We are looking for a professional who enjoys building proprietary mathematical models , understanding data, and transforming insights into production-ready solutions. You will not only create algorithms but also help shape the data foundations and analytical capabilities that drive our platform forward. We are looking for a Data Scientist who lives for applied statistics and machine learning and wants to see their models running in a real-world product. You won’t just be “doing research” into a drawer; you’ll be a key part of the R&D team, collaborating closely with developers to power the computational engine that drives our entire application. Our tech ecosystem includes Backend, Frontend, R&D, and QA. Within R&D, your primary playground will be R and advanced statistics , with a healthy dose of Python and SQL . We breathe Agile—think bi-weekly sprints, daily stand-ups, and retrospectives—and we take code quality seriously through rigorous reviews and modern dev practices. Key Responsibility Areas Develop , test , and maintain statistical models, machine learning algorithms, and analytical solutions that power our pricing platform Design , build , and optimize data pipelines that transform raw retail data into reliable datasets for analytics and machine learning Work across the full data lifecycle, including data ingestion , validation, monitoring, transformation , and quality assurance Collaborate closely with Product , Engineering , and other teams to bring analytical solutions into production Improve automation and efficiency of data-processing and analytical workflows Participate in code reviews, architectural discussions, and continuous improvement initiatives How do we picture you You have strong analytical thinking and enjoy solving complex problems with data You graduated at CUNI MFF / CTU FNSPE (Matfyz/FJFI) – we see this as an advantage You have good understanding complex workflows with direct business impact is a challenge that entices you You have hands-on experience with R, Python , SQL, or a combination of these technologies You understand statistics, machine learning fundamentals, and data modeling concepts You are comfortable working with large datasets and building reliable data workflows You speak English and Czech – at least level C1 / Full working proficiency. What's in it for you This is a place where your work has a visible impact. The models you build won’t stay in notebooks – they’ll help some of Europe’s leading retailers make better pricing decisions every single day. Work on complex, real-world machine learning and optimization problems with direct business impact Freedom to experiment, challenge ideas, and influence how we build our product Close collaboration with experienced engineers, data scientists, and product specialists who genuinely enjoy sharing knowledge A chance to grow with a company that’s scaling internationally while keeping the agility of a smaller team Work alongside experienced professionals passionate about AI, retail and enterprise software Competitive compensation package, new offices in the heart of Karlín, Prague

items.desc: At Signifyd, we help merchants confidently grow their businesses by building trusted relationships with their customers. Our advanced technology, combined with a team genuinely invested in our clients’ success, creates frictionless shopping experiences, approving more good orders, protecting revenue, and keeping customers happy. Trusted by thousands of leading merchants across more than 100 countries, we securely process billions of transactions each year. Our people are the heart of everything we do, driving our mission forward with commitment, empathy, and creativity. Join us on our mission to empower confident, fraud-free commerce by helping online retailers provide superior customer experiences and eliminate fraud. Learn about our company values here! The Applied Decision Science (ADS) team builds production ML models and risk management tools that are the core of Signifyd's product. We help businesses of all sizes minimize their fraud exposure and grow their sales. We improve the e-commerce shopping experience for everyone by reducing the friction experienced by good buyers and blocking fraudulent purchase attempts. ADS builds and manages the entire decision stack - from designing and deploying the ML models that assess the riskiness of a transaction, to building the tools the Risk team uses to manage and fight fraud. We seek to standardize and automate repetitive work so we can spend more time on experiments and high-leverage projects. We value collaboration and team ownership. Data scientists in Signifyd are true “full stack” operators, requiring knowledge of how transaction information received via our API traverses its way through our system and into the models we are responsible for building. When you test a hypothesis at Signifyd, you’re responsible for the end-to-end development, deployment, and evaluation process. This is a massive responsibility, and no one should feel like they're solving a hard problem alone. Together we help each other develop our skillsets through peer review of experiments and code, group paper study to deepen our machine learning and statistical understanding, and frequent knowledge-sharing through live demos, write-ups, and cross-team projects. All team members are expected and encouraged to weigh in as an external reviewer on a peer's idea or approach, regardless of level. A couple quick notes on the Signifyd culture: We’re no stranger to remote work. Most of our workforce (ICs and leaders) are primarily remote. We tend to gather individual teams together once a year. There is no travel requirement for this role. We are heavy Slack users. We are heavy users of generative AI tools. We dislike token-maxxing, but enjoy the expansion of capabilities that have come with genAI. We ask that during the interview you don’t use genAI, as we want to know what you know. Responsibilities: Partner with the Business Unit Lead and their merchant portfolio to identify gaps in decisioning performance and implement solutions, with guidance from senior team members. Utilize existing, or build net new production machine learning models that identify fraud, in collaboration with other data scientists and machine learning engineers. Identify and build automation that reduces repetitive manual work. Run experiments to identify optimal decisioning strategies, balancing complexity and performance. Communicate complex ideas to a variety of audiences, from Customer Success and Sales, to limited interactions with external customers. Write production and offline analytical code in Python. Work with distributed data pipelines in Spark/Databricks/GCP. Requirements: A degree in computer science or a comparable analytical field. 3+ years of post-undergrad work experience required. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Strong machine learning and statistical background. Write code and review others' in a shared codebase in Python. Practical SQL knowledge. Design experiments and collect data. Experience with distributed analytics and data tooling such as Spark and Databricks. This role has on-call shifts, as part of our weekend rotation, Fri/Sat/Sun. While the number of shifts is subject to change, currently it works out to about six weekends a year. Nice to Have: Previous work in fraud, payments, or e-commerce. Data analysis in a distributed environment. A passion for writing well-tested production-grade code. Experience with AI coding agents and automation. Experience of running A/B tests in production environments. An advanced degree. items.desc: Word de beste versie van jezelf als AI Engineer Net afgestudeerd en klaar om écht iets met AI te doen? Heb je al wat ervaring met Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning of Generative AI en wil je je verder ontwikkelen tot een echte AI-expert? Dan is het Young Professional Track AI Engineering bij Sogeti jouw kans om impact te maken. In deze periode leer je hoe je AI slim inzet om organisaties te helpen vernieuwen en verbeteren. Je werkt met moderne technologieën, behaalt relevante certificeringen en doet ervaring op bij klanten. Jouw start bij Sogeti Je begint met een traject waarin je samen met andere starters werkt aan uitdagende opdrachten, coaching krijgt en je skills ontwikkelt zoals samenwerken, communiceren en persoonlijk leiderschap. Een periode vol groei en verbinding. Daarna start je met een inhoudelijke opleiding waarin je jezelf verder ontwikkelt op het gebied van Data & AI. Je leert werken met moderne Data & AI-tools en technieken en behaalt direct relevante certificeringen. Werken als AI Engineer Na twee maanden opleiding is het zover: je gaat het veld in. Samen kijken we welke opdracht het beste bij jou past. Je wordt gedetacheerd bij grote Nederlandse organisaties, waar je aan de slag gaat met AI. Je helpt klanten om AI-oplossingen te ontwikkelen die niet op de tekentafel blijven liggen, maar daadwerkelijk in de praktijk gebruikt worden. Je beweegt je op het snijvlak van data, AI en software engineering en werkt aan oplossingen die betrouwbaar, schaalbaar en uitlegbaar zijn. Afhankelijk van de opdracht werk je bijvoorbeeld aan het ontwerpen en ontwikkelen van AI- en ML-componenten, het bouwen van end-to-end oplossingen van proof of concept tot productie, het integreren van modellen in applicaties en processen of het verbeteren van de uitlegbaarheid en beheersbaarheid van AI-oplossingen. Je werkt samen met Data Scientists, Data Engineers, Machine Learning Engineers en stakeholders aan oplossingen die organisaties helpen beter te beslissen en te innoveren. Ondertussen blijf je jezelf ontwikkelen met trainingen, cursussen en coaching van je Talentmanager. Zo ondersteunen wij jou om de beste versie van jezelf te worden Een sterk inhouse L&D-programma, een onbeperkt opleidingsbudget en actieve vakinhoudelijke communities waar kennisdeling en groei centraal staan; Persoonlijke begeleiding van jouw Talentmanager; Werken aan impactvolle IT-projecten bij bekende organisaties; Focus op mentale gezondheid en vitaliteit, met initiatieven zoals OpenUp, sportvergoeding en vitaliteitsprogramma’s; Toegang tot inspirerende events zoals Women@Sogeti en SoPlay, waar tech en verbinding samenkomen. Je kunt daarnaast rekenen op; Startsalaris van €3730,- (incl. mobiliteitsvergoeding van €750 en vakantiegeld); 26 vakantiedagen (met mogelijkheid tot bijkopen), onkostenvergoeding en een salarisgroeimodel met elke 6 maanden kans op een verhoging binnen 1,5 jaar. Direct een vast contract; Mogelijkheid tot hybride werken (thuiswerkvergoeding); Je kunt bij ons kiezen voor de manier van reizen die het beste bij je past zoals een leaseauto (elektrisch), kilometervergoeding en je krijgt een NS-Business Card, of een combinatie daarvan. Jouw talenten en ervaringen Je staat aan het begin van je carrière en hebt zin om te leren, te bouwen en impact te maken met AI; Een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding in AI, Data Science, Computer Science of een vergelijkbare richting; Basiskennis van Python en affiniteit met AI- of ML-frameworks zoals PyTorch, TensorFlow of scikit-learn; Interesse in het bouwen van AI-oplossingen van verkenning tot implementatie, en nieuwsgierigheid naar hoe modellen in productie waarde leveren; Affiniteit met onderwerpen zoals Generative AI, Agentic AI, explainability, betrouwbaarheid en schaalbaarheid van oplossingen; Kennis van software engineering, data of cloud is mooi meegenomen, net als interesse in deployment en MLOps; Relevante stage- of werkervaring; Proactief, doelgericht en goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal (minimaal C1-niveau). Meer over Sogeti Bij Sogeti krijg je de ruimte om de beste versie van jezelf te worden - als professional, als collega én als mens. Je werkt in een hechte community van gelijkgestemden, waarin kennis delen vanzelfsprekend is: van inhoudelijke events en communities tot initiatieven als de Gamenight. Met onze sterke lokale aanwezigheid werk je aan échte projecten met impact, altijd met de ondersteuning van een betrokken People Manager die meedenkt over jouw groei. Tegelijkertijd profiteer je van de slagkracht en expertise van de Capgemini Group. Bij Sogeti geloven we in diversiteit en inclusie: iedereen is welkom en mag zichzelf zijn. Twijfel je of dit helemaal past? App ons - dan kijken we samen. Heb je vragen of wil je meer weten? Neem contact op met Savannah van Cleef (recruiter). App: 06-25641922 mail: savannah.van.cleef@sogeti.com Word de beste versie van jezelf. Become Your Best. Solliciteer bij Sogeti. Een PES-screening maakt onderdeel uit van de onboarding.

items.desc: About Us Halfords is on a journey - building the future of motoring and cycling and looking for people who want to help shape what comes next. We’re a place for cocreators: people who want to make a real impact, take ownership and be part of something that’s still evolving. Technology at Halfords is at a turning point. We’re modernising our foundations, sharpening our delivery, and ensuring every technology decision is connected to real commercial and customer outcomes. We're looking for people who act as trusted advisors to the business, take end-to-end accountability for outcomes, and can balance pace with long-term architectural integrity. Innovation here means practical, scalable solutions, not ideas that stay on whiteboards. About The Role As a Data Scientist within our Data & Analytics team, you'll play a pivotal role in helping Halfords make smarter, data-driven decisions across the business. Working on a broad range of initiatives spanning customer experience, pricing, personalisation, and operational performance, you'll use advanced analytics and machine learning to solve real business problems and deliver measurable commercial value. You'll be working on business critical projects from day one, identifying opportunities and shaping hypotheses through to data exploration, feature engineering, model development, and deployment. Working with large and complex datasets, you'll use Python, PySpark, SQL, and Azure Databricks to develop robust predictive models and analytical solutions. Just as importantly, you'll be able to explain your findings in a clear and engaging way, helping stakeholders understand not only what the data is telling them, but what actions they should take as a result. This is an exciting opportunity to join a small but ambitious team with strong backing from senior leadership and significant investment in data science. We're building the foundations for how data science is adopted across Halfords, giving you the chance to influence both the direction of the function and the impact it has on the business. From customer segmentation and churn prediction to next-best-action and pricing models, you'll work on highly visible projects that directly shape the experience of millions of customers. Key Responsibilities Develop and deploy machine learning and predictive analytics solutions that address key business challenges and deliver measurable commercial outcomes Explore, profile, and analyse large and complex datasets to identify trends, opportunities, and features that improve model performance Apply statistical techniques, feature engineering, and model tuning to create robust and scalable analytical solutions Collaborate with Data Engineers and ML Engineers to operationalise models and embed them into customer journeys, business processes, and technology platforms Communicate findings, recommendations, and model outputs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders across the organisation Contribute to the growth of data science capability within Halfords, helping shape best practices, approaches, and future opportunities About You Proven experience as a Data Scientist, with demonstrable examples of machine learning models being deployed into production and delivering tangible business value Advanced Python skills, with experience using machine learning and statistical modelling techniques in commercial environments Strong experience with Azure Databricks or similar technology, SQL, and large-scale data analysis, with the ability to work confidently across modern cloud-based data platforms Experience developing end-to-end data science items.desc: Are you looking for a new challenge? Fancy helping us shape the future of motor insurance? Prima could be the place for you. Since 2015, we’ve been using our love of data and tech to rethink motor insurance and bring drivers a great experience at a great price. Our story began in Italy, where we’ve quickly become the number one online motor insurance provider. In fact, we’re trusted by over 5 million drivers. And now we’re expanding to help millions more drivers in the UK and Spain. To help fuel that growth, we’re looking for Data Scientists to join our Pricing & Underwriting Department, the strategic engine behind Prima's growth. As part of this global team, you’ll play a pivotal role in shaping our strategy and strengthening our competitive edge. Using data, analytical thinking, machine learning and business acumen, you’ll help predict the future and set the right prices, keeping our offering both attractive and sustainable. You’ll work with your data science tools and skills to bring real-world impact, collaborating with cross-functional teams to turn insights into action and fuel innovation across the company and its different branches. Excited to make an impact? Here are the details. What You’ll Do Leverage data to identify risks, opportunities and key pricing drivers, turning complex information into actionable insights that influence strategic decision making; Leverage Machine Learning and advanced analytics to develop risk and pricing models that power real-time insurance pricing for millions of customers; Contribute directly to the company’s growth and long-term success through innovative modelling, experimentation and commercially impactful insights. What We’re Looking For Strong academic background in Mathematics, Physics, Engineering (Maths, Physics and Computer Science specialisations), Data Science, Computer Science or Statistics; Strong quantitative, logical and analytical abilities, a solid foundation in statistics, probability and advanced analytics, and a curious, proactive and innovative mindset focused on solving complex problems; Fluency in English, both spoken and written. Nice-to-Have Strong communication skills, with the ability to challenge assumptions, and drive new ideas; Possess a solid foundation in code development and machine learning, ideally in Python; Know how to create, manipulate and analyse large datasets. €38,000 - €75,000 a year Why you'll love it here We want to make Prima a happy and empowering place to work. items.desc: At Signifyd, we help merchants confidently grow their businesses by building trusted relationships with their customers. Our advanced technology, combined with a team genuinely invested in our clients’ success, creates frictionless shopping experiences, approving more good orders, protecting revenue, and keeping customers happy. Trusted by thousands of leading merchants across more than 100 countries, we securely process billions of transactions each year. Our people are the heart of everything we do, driving our mission forward with commitment, empathy, and creativity. Join us on our mission to empower confident, fraud-free commerce by helping online retailers provide superior customer experiences and eliminate fraud. Learn about our company values here! The Applied Decision Science (ADS) team builds production ML models and risk management tools that are the core of Signifyd's product. We help businesses of all sizes minimize their fraud exposure and grow their sales. We improve the e-commerce shopping experience for everyone by reducing the friction experienced by good buyers and blocking fraudulent purchase attempts. ADS builds and manages the entire decision stack - from designing and deploying the ML models that assess the riskiness of a transaction, to building the tools the Risk team uses to manage and fight fraud. We seek to standardize and automate repetitive work so we can spend more time on experiments and high-leverage projects. We value collaboration and team ownership. Data scientists in Signifyd are true “full stack” operators, requiring knowledge of how transaction information received via our API traverses its way through our system and into the models we are responsible for building. When you test a hypothesis at Signifyd, you’re responsible for the end-to-end development, deployment, and evaluation process. This is a massive responsibility, and no one should feel like they're solving a hard problem alone. Together we help each other develop our skillsets through peer review of experiments and code, group paper study to deepen our machine learning and statistical understanding, and frequent knowledge-sharing through live demos, write-ups, and cross-team projects. All team members are expected and encouraged to weigh in as an external reviewer on a peer's idea or approach, regardless of level. A couple quick notes on the Signifyd culture: We’re no stranger to remote work. Most of our workforce (ICs and leaders) are primarily remote. We tend to gather individual teams together once a year. There is no travel requirement for this role. We are heavy Slack users. We are heavy users of generative AI tools. We dislike token-maxxing, but enjoy the expansion of capabilities that have come with genAI. We ask that during the interview you don’t use genAI, as we want to know what you know. Responsibilities: Partner with the Business Unit Lead and their merchant portfolio to identify gaps in decisioning performance and implement solutions, with guidance from senior team members. Utilize existing, or build net new production machine learning models that identify fraud, in collaboration with other data scientists and machine learning engineers. Identify and build automation that reduces repetitive manual work. Run experiments to identify optimal decisioning strategies, balancing complexity and performance. Communicate complex ideas to a variety of audiences, from Customer Success and Sales, to limited interactions with external customers. Write production and offline analytical code in Python. Work with distributed data pipelines in Spark/Databricks/GCP. Requirements: A degree in computer science or a comparable analytical field. 3+ years of post-undergrad work experience required. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Strong machine learning and statistical background. Write code and review others' in a shared codebase in Python. Practical SQL knowledge. Design experiments and collect data. Experience with distributed analytics and data tooling such as Spark and Databricks. This role has on-call shifts, as part of our weekend rotation, Fri/Sat/Sun. While the number of shifts is subject to change, currently it works out to about six weekends a year. Nice to Have: Previous work in fraud, payments, or e-commerce. Data analysis in a distributed environment. A passion for writing well-tested production-grade code. Experience with AI coding agents and automation. Experience of running A/B tests in production environments. An advanced degree. items.desc: Our paywall is a model. Come and make it smarter. Schibsted | Oslo, Bergen or Stockholm (hybrid) We built our own dynamic paywall and offer engine. Now we need to make it better, understand what works, and bring it to more brands. We're looking for a Data Scientist who enjoys building models, testing ideas and finding out whether the results actually make a difference. You'll work alongside experienced data scientists, analysts and engineers, with opportunities to take ownership of your work and grow your skills along the way. Why this work matters Our democracies depend on independent journalism, and that is our business. Independent journalism needs readers who choose to pay for it. Our job in Subscription Data Enablement is to understand those readers well enough to offer them the right thing at the right time, and to leave them alone when we shouldn't bother them. Direct relationships with readers and digital profitability are how Schibsted measures success. Your models sit right in the middle of both. Who We Are We are the data and analytics team for Schibsted's Subscription business in Norway and Sweden: analysts, data engineers, an ML engineer and data scientists. We work with brands such as VG, Aftenposten, Aftonbladet, Svenska Dagbladet, Bergens Tidende and E24. Our models already cover churn, renewal, segmentation and engagement. The dynamic paywall and offer engine is the newest addition to the family. It is also a good test of how we work. The Dynamic Paywall project has many moving parts and competing priorities, and it needs people from data, product, tech, business and editorial teams in the same room. A consultant who recently worked with us said that, despite technically being a consultant, they "never really felt like one". They described a team where everyone brings different expertise, ideas get challenged, debates are healthy, and we don't always agree, but there is "always mutual respect" and a shared goal of finding the best way forward. We want you to feel the same way about us a year from now. What You Will Do Make our paywall smarter. Develop and improve the models behind our dynamic paywall and offers: who sees which offer, and when. Propensity, recommender and offer optimisation problems are all in scope. Find out what works. Design, run and analyse experiments with our brands, and report the results as they are, including what they don’t prove. Uplift modelling and causal inference are welcome tools here. Build models that get used. Take models from notebook to production with our data scientists and engineers: feature engineering, training, evaluation, testing, and monitoring once they’re live. We work with tools such as Snowflake, MLflow and Streamlit. Make the results understandable. Explain findings to commercial colleagues with clear analysis and dashboards where they help. Improve how we work. Bring ideas on modelling, tooling and MLOps as more brands come on board, including how AI can make our own work easier. Ask good questions. Including “does this actually make us money?” when someone needs to. What You Bring Python or R and SQL, used to analyse data and build models. Hands-on experience developing and evaluating machine learning models, and an understanding of what it takes to run them in production. A solid foundation in statistics and experimentation, including hypothesis testing and A/B tests. The ability to explain your work to people who don’t speak ML, and the curiosity to learn from people who know the business better than you do. How We Work We follow a short list of team principles, and we mean them: be curious and keep learning, deliver quality together, design collaboratively, help early and ask early, share generously, have fun and stay open. In practice, that means Show n Tell and Friday data talks every other week, a monthly hack day, and an expectation that you ask for help before you’re stuck, not after. We also encourage sitting in on newsroom meetings. It’s hard to build a good model of what readers value without knowing what the newsrooms think is important. What You Can Expect From Us Real ML problems, with models that influence decisions across some of the Nordics’ best-known news brands. Experienced colleagues to learn from, and room to take ownership of your work. Time and space to learn, experiment and share ideas. The practical bits Location: Oslo, Bergen or Stockholm. Hybrid. Employee terms and benefits follow Schibsted’s standards in your country, and we are happy to go through the details with you in the process. The team is spread across Norway and Sweden, so some days are on video. Working language: English We welcome applications from people with different experiences and career paths, and we focus on the skills and potential you bring. Apply Send your CV and a few lines about a data science or machine learning project you've worked on. What problem were you trying to solve, what was your contribution, and what did you learn? It …
