items.card: The Role Most companies talk about AI. We're building the infrastructure to make it stick. This role exists to close the gap between AI's potential and what our teams actually use every day. You'll embed with a team, find the highest-impact opportunities, build the tools that solve them, and train the team to run them long after you've moved on. This isn't a research or strategy role. You'll be shipping automations,
items.desc: We're Capital on Tap 👋 💳 Capital on Tap started because small businesses were underserved. Big banks were slow, their products weren't fit for purpose, and small business owners often couldn't access what they needed. We set out to fix that. Today we're a financial platform - not just a credit card company. We offer a best-in-class business credit card, SME-focused spend management platform, a savings product that hit £1 billion in funds within its first year, and a growing suite of tools and financial products that make running a small business easier. 1,000+ employees, £20bn in annual card spend, 200,000+ customers, 17,000+ Trustpilot reviews averaging 4.7 stars, and we're profitable. We've done a pretty good job so far, but we're just getting started! 📍 London (Moorgate) | 🏢 3 Days in Office The Role Most companies talk about AI. We're building the infrastructure to make it stick. This role exists to close the gap between AI's potential and what our teams actually use every day. You'll embed with a team, find the highest-impact opportunities, build the tools that solve them, and train the team to run them long after you've moved on. This isn't a research or strategy role. You'll be shipping automations, MCPs, plugins, agentic workflows, and the training that goes with them. You'll be measured on impact and weekly active users, not on launches or tools rolled out. If you'd rather be doing than advising, this is for you. What You'll Be Doing Analyse where AI can move the needle most. Map a team's processes end-to-end before proposing a single tool, and prioritise the workflows where AI can take real cost, time, or rework off the table. Build the right stack for the problem - production-grade agentic workflows that bridge LLMs, internal APIs, and case management tools, plus MCPs, Claude skills and plugins, n8n automations, and integrations with internal systems. You build it, debug it in production, and iterate live with users sitting next to you. Train the people who'll use it. Run hands-on sessions, write documentation people actually read, and coach AI champions inside every team you work with so they're self-sufficient before you move on. Roll out and measure. Active automations running unsupervised matter more than trainings delivered or pilots launched. Track weekly active AI users and impact per team, intervene when usage drops, and keep iterating until AI is part of how the team works. Maintain Capital on Tap's AI playbook. Document repeatable patterns, package them as reusable skills and templates, and make every engagement start faster than the last. Partner with senior stakeholders to decide where to point next, and what good looks like before you start. We're Looking For Deployed AI tools in environments where downtime, errors, or rework have real cost - not sandbox experimentation. Hands-on, proven experience with Claude, Cursor, n8n, Zapier, or similar in a real business context. Technical fluency across low-code/no-code tools, APIs, MCPs, and integrations; comfortable in SQL and familiar with BI tooling. 2-5 years in product ops, operations, strategy, technical programme management, internal consulting, or a similar hands-on role. Strong communicator. You can run a workshop that lands, write documentation people actually read, and translate jargon for any audience. Comfortable with ambiguity. You diagnose fast, prioritise ruthlessly, and ship a working v1 inside a week even when the team you're working with isn't yet sure what they want. High ownership. You figure out what needs doing and do it, without waiting to be told. Even if you don't have all of the necessary skills, we still encourage you to apply. Diversity & Inclusion 🌈 We welcome, consider and encourage applications from anyone who shares our commitment to inclusivity. Join us in creating a space where authenticity thrives, and everyone can do their best work. Great Work Deserves Great Perks We try not to take ourselves too seriously (all the time) so we make sure our office is decked out with a pool table, arcade machine, beer tap, and a couple of office dogs thrown in for good measure. items.card: Cosa farai con noi? Come AI Integration Engineer avrai l’opportunità di lavorare su progetti innovativi orientati all’integrazione di soluzioni di Intelligenza Artificiale Generativa all’interno di ecosistemi enterprise complessi. items.desc: Descrizione azienda MC Engineering è una dinamica società di consulenza informatica , con sedi a Torino, Milano, Roma e Bari. Lavoriamo a stretto contatto con realtà innovative nel mondo ICT, portando avanti progetti che spaziano tra vari settori. Per noi, le persone sono al centro di tutto : puntiamo su un continuo aggiornamento, sulla crescita costante e sull’ eccellenza , per affrontare insieme sfide innovative e fare la differenza nel nostro settore. Posizione Cosa farai con noi? Come AI Integration Engineer avrai l’opportunità di lavorare su progetti innovativi orientati all’integrazione di soluzioni di Intelligenza Artificiale Generativa all’interno di ecosistemi enterprise complessi. Sarai coinvolto nello sviluppo e nell’orchestrazione di integrazioni AI-based, contribuendo alla progettazione di architetture moderne basate su Large Language Model (LLM), AI Agents e sistemi di automazione intelligente. Ti occuperai dell’integrazione di modelli AI all’interno di piattaforme e applicazioni aziendali tramite API, microservizi e workflow avanzati, collaborando con team multidisciplinari per garantire scalabilità, qualità e sicurezza delle soluzioni implementate. Opererai in un contesto collaborativo e strutturato, orientato alla qualità e all’innovazione, dove il tuo contributo sarà valorizzato attraverso un percorso di crescita professionale. Requisiti Competenze richieste Laurea o diploma tecnico Esperienza di almeno 3 anni nello sviluppo software, system integration o AI Engineering Ottima conoscenza di Python Esperienza nell’integrazione di API REST e servizi enterprise Buona conoscenza dei Large Language Model (LLM) Esperienza con piattaforme AI come OpenAI, Azure OpenAI o soluzioni analoghe Conoscenza di architetture a microservizi e integrazione applicativa Familiarità con ambienti cloud (Azure, AWS o GCP) Esperienza con strumenti DevOps e CI/CD Capacità di troubleshooting e ottimizzazione di workflow AI-driven Conoscenza di database SQL/NoSQL. Lingua inglese Buona conoscenza della lingua inglese (livello B2) Modalità e/o Sede di Lavoro Modalità Full Remote Completano il profilo Un’elevata attitudine al lavoro in team Doti di precisione e flessibilità mentale Capacità proattiva nella gestione delle problematiche professionali Forte orientamento all’innovazione e all’apprendimento continuo Ottime capacità comunicative verso interlocutori tecnici e business. Altre informazioni Cosa offriamo Inserimento in organico con un inquadramento commisurato all’esperienza professionale pregressa e una retribuzione in linea con le reali capacità del candidato. Se sei una persona appassionata di tecnologia e Intelligenza Artificiale, desiderosa di crescere in un ambiente che promuove innovazione, qualità ed eccellenza tecnologica, questa è l’occasione che fa per te! Unisciti a MC Engineering: dove le idee diventano innovazione! Il presente annuncio è rivolto ad entrambi i sessi, ai sensi delle leggi 903/77 e 125/91, e a persone di tutte le età e tutte le nazionalità, ai sensi dei DLgs 215/03 e 216/03. Retribuzione Da € 25.000 a € 40.000

items.desc: Role: Machine Learning Research Scientist Engagement: Remote | Contract / Freelance Experience: 4+ years hands-on research experience; 5+ years preferred Education: Master’s degree or higher About the Role We are looking for experienced Machine Learning Research Scientists focused on experimental ML research rather than production ML engineering. The ideal candidate should have hands-on experience designing research experiments, running benchmarks and ablation studies , analyzing model behavior, and conducting research in areas such as robustness, interpretability, evaluation, or statistical machine learning . Key Responsibilities Design and execute rigorous machine learning research experiments. Develop and run benchmarks, baselines, and ablation studies . Evaluate model performance using statistically sound methodologies. Investigate model robustness, interpretability, generalization, and failure modes . Formulate research hypotheses and validate them experimentally. Conduct quantitative analysis of experimental results using Python and statistical methods. Compare models and methodologies using reproducible experimental frameworks. Document research findings, assumptions, limitations, and conclusions. Required Qualifications 4+ years of hands-on ML research experience; 5+ years preferred. Master’s degree or PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or a closely related field. Strong proficiency in Python and statistics . Hands-on experience conducting ML experiments and research. Experience with benchmarking and ablation studies . Strong understanding of statistical evaluation and experimental design. Experience in one or more areas such as: Robustness Interpretability Model evaluation Generalization Statistical machine learning Experimental ML research Active and credible professional LinkedIn profile. Preferred Background Research Scientist, ML Research Scientist, Applied Research Scientist, Researcher – Machine Learning, or Statistical ML Researcher. Important: This is a research-focused position, not an ML Engineering role .

items.desc: At Jamf, we believe in an open, flexible culture based on respect and trust. Our track record and thriving work environment all stem from the freedom we grant ourselves to get the job done right. We take pride in helping tens of thousands of customers around the globe succeed with Apple. The secret to our success lies in our connectivity, while operating with a high degree of flexibility. Work-life balance remains our priority while feeling connected is important to maintain our strong culture, achieve our goals, and thrive as #OneJamf. This role is offered as a hybrid in Brno, the Czech Republic . We are only able to accept applications for those based in the Czech Republic or who have sponsorship to live and work in the Czech Republic . What you'll do at Jamf: At Jamf, we empower people to be their best selves and do their best work. As a Software Engineer II on a new team enabling secure, governed adoption of autonomous and agentic workflows, you'll help build production systems where AI agents do real work on real code - authoring changes inside deterministic gates, with independent verification and a full audit trail. This is a greenfield build inside a mature platform, starting with Security. What you can expect to do in this role: Build the production systems where AI agents do real work on real code – authoring changes that run inside deterministic gates, with independent verification and a full audit trail behind every one. Take customer and platform problems, break them into workable pieces with your agile team, and own most of them end to end. Draw the line on autonomy: design the trust boundaries, blast radius, and least-privilege model for the automation itself, which holds elevated access to production. Build the evaluation and observability that keeps non-deterministic systems honest – measuring accuracy and catching silent degradation before anyone else does. Make the systems answer the auditor's "show me" – producing evidence that a control worked, not just the claim that it did. Work shoulder to shoulder with security engineering and PDD developers, and explain the tricky parts clearly to the rest of the organization. Bring engineering best practices to the table: ask the sharp questions, solve the hard problems, and help others level up. What we are looking for: Must-have: 3+ years building enterprise-grade software commercially, with a solid grasp of testing and QA. 3+ years of commercial experience in Java or Python. Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs and agentic frameworks – tool calling, multi-step execution, structured output – well beyond using AI coding assistants. Hands-on experience with AI-driven coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) to speed up your own work. Sound judgment about where automation should and shouldn't act on its own – and the ability to articulate exactly where that line sits. You think in trust boundaries, blast radius, and least privilege by default. You treat vulnerability management as a discipline: severity and exploitability, SLAs, and exception handling. Experience in an agile organization and with build systems like Jenkins or Bamboo. You build trust and rapport across all levels, and do your best work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Nice-to-have: Software supply chain security – SBOMs, provenance and attestation, image signing and verification, policy-as-code. Experience running AI coding agents at repository scale, and building the harness that makes their output trustworthy. Familiarity with AI governance in a security context – model-use policy, data handling, and the audit questions that follow an agent-initiated production change. Experience in a regulated environment (SOC 2, FedRAMP, or similar) and a feel for what auditors actually ask for. Why Jamf? We are progressive but laid back. You are free to be yourself and work how you work best. Here, you manage your own day and your own work style. You will have the opportunity to work with a small and empowered team where the culture is based on trust, ownership, and respect. With hybrid and remote roles, we offer an open flexible culture based on respect and trust. Benefits are a critical part of the "whole employee experience". Our benefits package includes 30 days of paid time off, 3 paid days to volunteer, Benefit Plus cafeteria, Multisport Card, and more. items.desc: Why this role exists SevenLab is an Amsterdam-based AI solutions company. We (help) build AI agents, AI applications and sovereign AI infrastructure for organisations that take data seriously: healthcare, the public sector, logistics and manufacturing. We work as an NVIDIA partner, we are ISO 27001 certified, and we deliver through a Software Development as a Service model: fixed monthly partnerships instead of hourly billing. Our entry point is a €7K fixed-scope POC. From there, clients move into a monthly partnership (Private AI, AI Applications or Governed Build). Our differentiator is that everything we build can run on EU infrastructure, backed by Sluis, our own AI governance and gateway layer with EU data residency. The demand is there. What we lack is a repeatable outbound system that identifies these organisations at the moment they start caring about AI and data sovereignty, and books a qualified conversation in our Account Executive's calendar. Building and running that system is your job. You build it, you run it, and you own the results it produces. Tasks What you'll actually do First 30 days: take over our current sales systems: Attio, Clay, our email sequences and the partner motions we already run. Audit them. Tell us honestly what's broken. Fix the worst thing and propose what else to change. Days 30–90: build our core outbound motion from scratch, starting with the Dutch market. Define the ICP per segment (public sector, healthcare, logistics, manufacturing), build the enrichment waterfall, design the signal triggers, write and test the sequences, and get the Attio data model to a state where pipeline reporting isn't a work of fiction. Day 90 onwards: you own top-of-funnel. You run experiments weekly, kill what doesn't work fast, and document what does so it survives you. You feed qualified meetings to our Account Executive and work with commercial leadership on which segments and partner channels to scale next. Requirements Must have 2–4 years of hands-on experience building and running outbound systems (GTM engineering, growth, RevOps or SDR-plus roles) Proven, practical experience with Clay, Attio (or a comparable CRM) and an outbound email tool such as Instantly, including deliverability and inbox management Track record of building signal-based lists and enrichment waterfalls, and of measuring what they produced Comfortable doing 15-minute intro calls with prospects, or a clear willingness to learn Understanding of GDPR-compliant data sourcing and able to explain the origin of every contact in a list Professional Dutch and English, spoken and written Able to work from our Amsterdam office at least two days a week Nice to have Python, or experience with Clay's HTTP API and Claygent Experience selling into the public sector, healthcare or other regulated industries Familiarity with Dutch tender and procurement signals (TenderNed, aanbestedingen) German or French Who this is for You've built outbound systems and you find the building genuinely satisfying You're allergic to spray-and-pray. You'd rather send 40 good emails than 4,000 bad ones You want to be closer to the buyer, not further from them You want a company where the thing being sold is technically interesting and adds tangible value Who this is not for Classic SDRs looking for a dialler and a script Pure RevOps people who want to stay in the tooling Benefits Practicalities Amsterdam-based (Danzigerbocht 39g), hybrid. You'll be in the office at least twice a week, more at the start. Working languages are Dutch and English. Most of our clients are Dutch organisations, so professional Dutch is required. You report to the CCO and work daily with our Account Executive and the delivery team. Compensation €3,500–€5,500 monthly base, plus OTE 8% holiday allowance 28 days paid leave per year (full-time basis) 10% pension contribution Our Process Intro Call (20-30 min) A mutual filtering session. Practical Case (2–3 hrs) You'll build a real outbound motion for our DACH launch. Live Session (45 min) Present your build, troubleshoot an issue in real-time, and conduct a mock 15-minute intro call. Final Conversation with Leadership + References The process typically takes two to three weeks from start to finish. We provide feedback and a decision after each stage. How to Apply Send us your CV along with an answer to the following question; a few paragraphs will do: Describe an outbound system you built that produced poor results. How did you discover the issue, what did you do about it, and how did you communicate this to the people relying on it? We read this answer before your CV. Applications without it will not be considered.

items.desc: Expert public de la météo et du climat, Météo-France est à vos côtés pour contribuer à votre sécurité au quotidien et vous aider à prendre les meilleures décisions, dans un climat qui change. Face à des épisodes météo dangereux encore plus intenses et plus fréquents sous l’effet du changement climatique, nos missions au service de votre sécurité sont cruciales. Nous mobilisons notre expertise, notre excellence scientifique et technologique pour vous permettre d’anticiper les phénomènes météorologiques et climatiques à enjeux, et de vous y adapter. Retrouvez-nous en ligne : https://meteofrance.com/carte-didentite-de-meteo-france Rejoindre Météo France, C'est Intégrer Une Organisation Multi-sites, Situés En Hexagone, En Outre-mer, Etc. L'organisation De Météo-France S'appuie Sur Des Directions Centrales Et Des Directions Interrégionales. Ci-dessous, La Présentation De La Direction Que Vous Pourriez Rejoindre La Direction de l'Enseignement Supérieur et de la Recherche (DESR) rassemble les entités de recherche de Météo-France (principalement CNRM, SAFIRE, LACy), l'Ecole Nationale de la Météorologie, et les services partagés de soutien administratif et informatique (PGA). Le Centre National de Recherches Météorologiques (CNRM) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche (UMR 3589) avec la double tutelle Météo-France et CNRS. Le CNRM conduit des recherches dans le domaine de la météorologie et du climat, de l'observation, la compréhension et la modélisation des processus jusqu'à la mise au point de systèmes de prévision météorologique et de projection climatique pouvant être transférés aux services opérationnels de Météo-France. Le Groupe de Modélisation et d'Assimilation pour la Prévision (GMAP), basé à Toulouse, est l'un des 6 groupes ou centres de recherche du CNRM. Sa mission est de maintenir et développer les systèmes de prévision numérique du temps (PNT) opérationnels de Météo-France et de conduire des recherches qui préparent les futures versions. L’équipe Observations (OBS) fait partie du groupe GMAP, et est en charge de l’utilisation de tous les types d’observations pour améliorer les prévisions des modèles de Prévision Numérique du Temps (PNT). Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? Embarquez pour une aventure stimulante et au service de tous aux côtés d’hommes et de femmes engagés quotidiennement face aux défis posés à notre société par la météo et le climat. Et ainsi bénéficiez des avantages suivants : horaires flexibles, RTT, télétravail, restaurant administratif ou ticket restaurant, participation à hauteur de 75% pour les transports en commun, participation pour la mutuelle, associations sportives et culturelles en fonction du site concerné, (escalade, gym, poterie, théâtre etc..). D'autres avantages vous attendent, venez les découvrir ! Le poste proposé est situé au Centre National de Recherches Météorologiques de Toulouse, unité mixte de recherche de Météo-France et du Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique (CNRS). Le candidat ou la candidate intégrera l'équipe Observations du Groupe de Modélisation et d'Assimilation pour la Prévision. Ce groupe a en charge le développement des futurs modèles opérationnels de prévision numérique du temps de Météo-France. L'équipe Observations développe l'intégration des observations météorologiques dans les modèles pour définir l'état initial de la prévision. Pour mieux tirer profit des observations dans les modèles de Prévision Numérique du Temps (PNT), les méthodes d’assimilation de données ont réalisé des progrès significatifs au cours des dernières décennies. À Météo-France comme pour les autres centres de PNT, l’utilisation d’une information ensembliste dans les algorithmes d’assimilation de données atmosphériques est désormais centrale. Le modèle global ARPEGE utilise une algorithme d’assimilation de données hybride 4DVar pour l’altitude qui utilise des covariances 3D ensemblistes issues d’un ensemble d’assimilation. Proche de la surface, de récentes avancées ont permis de mettre en place une méthode du même type, dite variationnelle ensembliste bidimensionnelle 2DEnVar, pour initialiser les variables dans le sol dans le modèle à aire limitée AROME (Marimbordes et al., 2024). Grâce à ce système, l’introduction de nouveaux types d’observations, provenant de satellites, est ainsi facilitée (Marimbordes et al., 2025). Ce système a été récemment étendu au modèle global ARPEGE. L’objectif du travail proposé est d’étudier, dans le modèle de grande échelle ARPEGE, l’intérêt d’assimiler une nouvelle observation satellitaire, la température de surface continentale provenant du sondeur IASI-NG, puis IRS, dans un système d’analyse de surface avancé, basé sur une approche variationnelle ensembliste. Ce travail s’inscrit dans le cadre d’un projet européen, nommé CHERRI (Climate Hazards Enhanced Reanalyses & Reasoning with AI), porté par le CEPMMT (Centre Européen pour les Prévisions Météorologiques à Moyen Terme) qui porte sur l'assimilation de la température de surface continentale …

items.desc: As a public weather and climate expert, Météo-France is at your side to contribute to your day-to-day safety and help you make the best decisions in a changing climate. Faced with dangerous weather episodes that are even more intense and more frequent as a result of climate change, our missions in the service of your safety are crucial. We mobilize our expertise and our scientific and technological excellence to help you anticipate and adapt to challenging weather and climate phenomena. Find us online: https://meteofrance.com/carte-didentite-de-meteo-france DESR is the research division of Météo-France (CNRM, SAFIRE, LACy), including the national school of meteorology (ENM) and shared administrative and computing support teams (PGA). CNRM is a mixed research unit Météo-France and CNRS. CNRM leads research in meteorology and climate, observation, process understanding and modeling until the development of operational weather forecasting and climate models that can be transferred to operational services. GMAP is a research group at CNRM (National Centre for Meteorological Research) affiliated with Météo-France and CNRS (National Centre for Scientific Research). GMAP develops numerical forecasting software packages for Météo-France. The OBS team is in charge of the assimilation of observations in the global and regional NWP models of Météo-France. Why join us? Embark on a stimulating adventure in the service of all, alongside men and women committed to the daily challenges posed to our society by the weather and climate. And enjoy the following benefits: flexible working hours, RTT, telecommuting, administrative restaurant or luncheon voucher, 75% contribution to public transport, contribution to health insurance, sports and cultural associations depending on the site (climbing, gym, pottery, theater, etc.). Other benefits await you, come and discover them! The position is opened at the Centre National de Recherches Météorologiques in Toulouse, UMR Météo-France and CNRS. The candidate will be recruited in the Observations team in the Groupe de Modélisation et d'Assimilation pour la Prévision (GMAP). This group is in charge of the development of future Météo-France operational numerical weather prediction models. The Observations team develops the integration of meteorological observations into model to define the initial state of forecasts. Data assimilation methods have made significant progress in the past decades and are now able to ingest a large variety of observations from different observing systems with the aim of improving Numerical Weather forecasts at different scales. At Météo-France as well as in other NWP centres, the use of ensemble information in data assimilation algorithms is now central. ARPEGE global model uses a hybrid 4DVar data assimilation algorithm for upper-air assimilation with the use of 3D ensemble covariances. Near the surface an ensemble variational method has been recently developed to initialise soil variables in the AROME limited-area NWP model (Marimbordes et al., 2024). With this system, the introduction of new types of observations from satellites is now made easier (Marimbordes et al., 2025). This system was recently extended to the ARPEGE global model. The objective of this work is to study the possibility of assimilating a new satellite observation, the land surface temperature from IASI-NG and/or IRS sounder into the ARPEGE global model using an advanced surface data assimilation system based on an ensemble variational approach. This study happens in the framework of CHERRI European project (Climate Hazards Enhanced Reanalyses & Reasoning with AI) lead by ECMWF (European Centre for Medium range Weather Forecast). Assimilation of land surface temperature in the global NWP model ARPEGE with a bidimensional ensemble variational method (2DEnVar) in the framework of CHERRI Horizon Europe project. The study will be divided into four steps Assessement of land surface temperature observations from IASI-NG and/or IRS quality to prepare their assimilation. Assimilation of these observations into a surface data assimilation system based on a variational ensemble approach (2DEnVar). These developments will take place in the ARPEGE global model. Evaluation of results and sensitivity tests to find the configuration that improves low atmospheric forecasts. Preparation of a report and a scientific publication. Presentation of results at conferences in the framework of CHERRI project. Additional Information This position is open to people with disabilities. Office hours. Fixed-term contract of 24 months. Remote work available: 1 day a week maximum. You hold a master's degree or a doctorate Experience in data assimilation is required. Solid knowledge in programation langages as Fortran/C++/Python is required. Knowledge in meteorology or numerical weather prediction is a recommended. items.desc: About The Program The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings researchers and scientists together to tackle consequential problems in AI. In partnership with Scale Labs, we are building a small cohort of researchers to work on the empirical foundations of AI safety. That work includes finding where models fail, checking whether safety controls hold up under pressure in realistic settings, and studying how AI agents (mis-)behave over long-horizon tasks. Scholars take open research questions like these and turn them into work that improves how frontier AI systems are evaluated and safeguarded. Each scholar owns a substantial part of a safety research project. You'll work alongside a mentor from the research question through the experiments to deciding what to test next. Research Areas Mentors will guide Research Scholars on projects in selected AI safety research areas in select AI safety research areas, such as: AI control and chain-of-thought monitoring: Developing techniques to oversee and constrain AIs, including detecting harmful intent or deception. Alignment auditing and evaluations: Building scalable methods to test whether models have hidden goals, misaligned behaviors or unsafe tendencies. Multi-agent safety: Studying the risks that emerge when multiple agents interact, such as collusion, coordinated failures, or unexpected collective behavior. Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) safety: Investigating how to keep AI systems safe and aligned as AIs increasingly contribute to their own development. Science of Evaluations: examining when and how models recognize they're being tested, and how situational awareness affects the reliability/validity of evaluations. Misuse risks and evaluations: Developing methods to assess how AI systems could be exploited by malicious actors, including evaluating their potential to enable harmful activities. Projects are matched to demonstrated expertise; we don’t expect any candidate to cover every area. Representative Research ASPI: 728 task–attack scenarios testing how clarification-seeking changes prompt-injection vulnerability in LLM agents. PropensityBench: simulating real-world pressure to choose between safe or harmful behavior BioRiskEval: evaluating whether safeguards for open-weight bio-foundation models remain robust under fine-tuning and probing. See more work from the Human Frontier Collective. What You'll Do Projects are mentor-guided. By default, you will be given a list of research proposals and match you with one based on your research interests and background. You’ll meet weekly with a Scale researcher who sets the direction and gives feedback, and you will drive the day-to-day work. Own research end to end: Turn a high-level safety question into hypotheses, baselines, and controlled experiments, and produce work that others can inspect and build on. Build the measurement: Implement and debug evaluation harnesses, agent environments, datasets, monitoring methods, or post-training experiments. Exercise research judgment: Identify confounds, separate what a model can do from what it tends to do, make sense of negative results, and decide what to try next without step-by-step direction. Make the work legible: Produce reproducible code, experiment logs, analysis, and precise technical writing. External outputs, where appropriate, remain subject to research, security, and communications review. Outputs also include research papers, which will be submitted to top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR). Who We're Looking For You may be a good fit if you: are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems; are interested in technical safety research, such as alignment evaluations, AI control, monitoring, multi-agent safety, or open-weight model safety; are pursuing or have completed a PhD in CS, ML, statistics, mathematics, or a related field (we also encourage researchers with an equivalent track record to apply); can make progress with high-level guidance, including implementing, debugging, getting unstuck, interpreting results, and proposing next experiments; communicate research clearly and handle confidential information and internal systems responsibly. Application Process Apply: Submit your resume or CV, your Google Scholar profile if you have one, and one research project you substantially owned, with 2–3 sentences on your contribution. Research background discussion: Walk us through a past project, including what you tried, what didn't work, and what you learned. Research design: Work through a research problem with us and propose how you'd approach it. Onboarding: Successful candidates complete the applicable recruiting, work-authorization, security, and project-onboarding steps. PLEASE NOTE: Our policy requires a 90-day waiting period before reconsidering candidates for the same role. This allows us to ensure a fair and thorough evaluation of all applicants. items.desc: Vous êtes une personne passionnée par l’interaction laser-matière à haute intensité et de l’optique relativiste et souhaitez contribuer à l'excellence scientifique ? Rejoignez le laboratoire PHI (Physique à Haute Intensité) en tant que chercheur·euse afin d'exercer une activité scientifique expérimentale de haut niveau. Vous serez notamment en charge du développement et de l’optimisation de miroirs plasmas pour manipuler la lumière extrême, ainsi que de sources de particules pilotées par laser utilisant des approches prometteuses. vous exploiterez les caractéristiques uniques de la plateforme UHI100 (laser Ti:Sa de classe 100TW dont la puissance sera prochainement portée à 200TW) du LIDYL, ainsi que d’autres plateformes expérimentales accessibles de type multi-PW en France et/ou à l’étranger. L’activité, principalement expérimentale, pourra s’accompagner d’une composante numérique et dans tous les cas pourra bénéficier d’un soutien fort des membres du groupe spécialistes de la modélisation numérique, qui développent leur propre code PIC exploitant au mieux les nouvelles générations de supercalculateurs. Vous aurez en particulier l’opportunité de développer une activité en lien avec le projet ERC Synergy NP-QED (« Probing the non perturbative regime of Quantum Electrodynamics with extrem light »), piloté par Henri Vincenti, visant à explorer les limites de l’électrodynamique quantique (QED) en champ fort (SF-QED). Vous intégrerez un environnement de recherche international de premier plan au sein du groupe PHI. Vous développerez des projets de recherche innovants, contribuerez au montage de financements nationaux et européens, et participerez à l’évolution de la plateforme UHI100. Le poste implique une forte interaction avec des partenaires académiques et industriels, ainsi qu’une participation active à la vie scientifique du groupe et à la formation des jeunes chercheurs (stagiaires, doctorants et post-doctorants). The Optoelectronics Section provides functional support to ESA projects and carries out technological research (R&D) in the field of optoelectronic device technologies and applications. In particular, the Optoelectronics Section deals with the specification, development and characterisation of photonic component subsystems and active optical instruments, such as detectors and lasers operating in the UV to FIR wavelength ranges, fibre-optic sensors, lidars, optical communication systems and quantum technologies. The Section is staffed with around 25 engineers supporting all ESA projects and offers a unique opportunity to contribute on the challenges relating to optoelectronic technologies required for ESA missions, spacecraft, instruments and equipment. Duties Reporting to the Head of Section and within the technical fields described above, your main tasks and responsibilities will include: providing expert technical support and consultancy to ESA projects, programmes and general studies involving optical atomic clocks, optical frequency combs, lasers and integrated photonic technologies for space and related technologies and testing techniques throughout all project phases; participating in feasibility studies, project reviews and the evaluation of procurement proposals; identifying critical development problems and assisting in their resolution; contributing to the definition of technology development requirements and work plans for the Agency’s technology programmes; defining, initiating and managing R&D activities covering both long- and short-term needs; fostering new application areas for multidisciplinary activities, placing emphasis on innovative concepts, cutting-edge technologies and system architectures; laboratory activities, as required; monitoring applicable scientific and technological trends and maintaining state-of-the-art expertise; contributing to the dissemination of the results of the activities performed and the transfer of knowledge across the Agency. Your duties may also include supporting other activities within your field of competence. Technical competencies General background and specific experience in the technical domains covered by the position optical atomic clocks, including related subsystems, such as frequency combs, ultra-stable lasers, cavities, metrology and T&F distribution related quantum and photonics technologies, such as atom/ion trapping and cooling, photonic integrated circuits and fibre optics Experience with laboratory and field testing of relevant technical equipment and hands-on hardware experience Understanding of related technologies, R&D trends and industrial landscape Project support experience in a relevant domain Experience in the coordination and preparation of procurement activities for technology development and innovation, such as statements of work and proposal evaluation Behavioural competencies Result Orientation Operational Efficiency Fostering Cooperation Relationship Management Continuous Improvement Forward Thinking For more information, please refer to the ESA Core Behavioural Competencies guidebook. Education And Professional Experience A master’s degree in physics, photonics, optoelectronics, optical engineering or a related discipline is required for this post, together with at least four years of relevant professional experience. Additional Requirements Solid experience in the design, definition, development and testing of complex optoelectronics systems. The following will be considered assets: Knowledge of environmental testing of space hardware. Knowledge of working on projects with a formal security framework. A PhD in a relevant discipline. items.desc:
Help shape the scientific software that powers bioinformatics research worldwide. 
 At EMBL-EBI, our bioinformatics services help researchers access and work with biological data at scale. As our Bioinformatics Software Engineer & Scientific Lead, you’ll combine hands-on software development with scientific and technical leadership, helping guide the evolution of Job Dispatcher and other core software products. 
 You’ll work closely with scientists, engineers and infrastructure specialists to shape product strategy, prioritise development and deliver reliable, sustainable services that meet the changing needs of the global research community. 
 About the team 
 The Software Team within EMBL-EBI’s ITS Service and Operations department develops and maintains centrally provided scientific software, including Job Dispatcher, which provides structured access to run bioinformatical analysis tools on our high performance compute clusters and FiRE, which manages the storage and archiving of over 120Pb of scientific data . Working at the intersection of software engineering, scientific computing and bioinformatics, the team delivers services that support researchers in working with biological data and running computational analyses. 
 The Role 
 You’ll combine hands-on software development with scientific and technical leadership, helping shape the strategy, development and long-term sustainability of Job Dispatcher and other software products owned by the team. 
 Primary Tasks & Responsibilities: 
 Lead software development: Develop, maintain and improve production bioinformatics services and scientific software as an active member of the team. 
 Shape product strategy: Work with the team project lead and Head of Services and Operations to define and deliver product roadmaps, technology direction and longer-term development priorities. 
 Guide scientific direction: Provide specialist bioinformatics expertise to ensure services remain scientifically relevant, useful and aligned with the needs of the global user community. 
 Manage priorities and delivery: Help curate and prioritise the development backlog, coordinating projects, dependencies, risks and technical deliverables. 
 Coordinate service updates: Work with EBI service teams to plan and coordinate data updates, particularly for Job Dispatcher. 
 Collaborate across teams: Work with scientists, software engineers, infrastructure teams and other stakeholders to deliver and improve reliable scientific services. 
 Provide technical leadership: Represent the services in regular tools committee meetings, contribute to the wider ITS leadership community (TMC Plus) and support the evolution and modernisation of bioinformatics services. 
 Share knowledge and impact: Promote services through training, conference presentations, scientific publications and service updates, helping users understand and make effective use of the tools. 
 You Will Have: 
 A degree in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Computer Science or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience. 
 Professional experience in bioinformatics, scientific computing or software engineering, with the ability to apply software development expertise to scientific applications and services. 
 Strong programming experience developing and maintaining production software and RESTful APIs, using languages such as Java, TypeScript/JavaScript and Python. 
 Experience developing modern web applications using Angular or an equivalent framework. 
 Experience with scientific workflow technologies and high-performance computing environments, including Nextflow and job schedulers such as SLURM. 
 Experience packaging and deploying bioinformatics tools using containers such as Docker and Singularity/Apptainer. 
 Strong experience with Git-based version control, GitLab and CI/CD automation, alongside Linux, scripting, job scheduling, monitoring and production software operations. 
 You May Also Have: 
 Experience developing or maintaining large-scale, widely used bioinformatics services. 
 Experience communicating scientific work through peer-reviewed publications, presentations or other technical and scientific outputs. 
 Experience working with biological sequence data, including format conversion, processing and database indexing. 
 Familiarity with ServiceNow or similar IT service-management systems and processes, including incident and change management. 
 Contract Length: 3-Year fixed-term Staff Member contract, renewable to 9 years. 
 Working Pattern: This role offers a hybrid working arrangement, with 1-2 days per week on site, including one designated team day to support collaboration and connection. 
 Salary: Grade 6 or Grade 7, depending on experience. Monthly salary from £3,861.91 (grade 6) or £4,395.66 (grade 7) after tax, plus generous benefits and financial allowances based on individual circumstances. Excluding 12.99% personal pension and insurance contributions.

OUR STORY 
 At STMicroelectronics, we believe in the power of technology to drive innovation and make a positive impact on people, businesses, and society. As a global semiconductor company, our advanced technologies and chips form the hidden foundation of the world we live in today. 
 When you join ST, you will be part of a global business with more than 115 nationalities, present in 40 countries, and comprising over 50,000 diverse and dedicated creators and makers of technology around the world. 
 Developing technologies takes more than talent: it takes amazing people who understand collaboration and respect. People with passion and the desire to disrupt the status quo, drive innovation, and unlock their own potential. 
 Embark on a journey with us, where you can innovate for a future that we want to make smarter and greener, in a responsible and sustainable way. Our technology starts with you. 
 YOUR ROLE 
 We are seeking a highly motivated Metal Process Engineer to join our Power Front-End Technology R&D team. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of advanced metal processing technologies and materials solutions for next-generation products. This position is ideal for recent Master's graduates interested in applying their knowledge of materials science, metallurgy, and process engineering in an innovative research environment.
 The engineer will work closely with senior researchers and cross-functional teams to support process development, experimentation, characterization, and technology transfer activities.
 Process Research & Development 
 Support the development and optimization of metal processing technologies.
 Conduct laboratory experiments and evaluate process performance.
 Assist in designing and executing Design of Experiments (DOE).
 Collect, analyze, and interpret experimental data.
 Materials Characterization 
 Perform materials characterization using analytical and microscopy techniques.
 Investigate relationships between process conditions, microstructure, and material properties.
 Support root cause analysis of material and process-related issues.
 Innovation Projects 
 Participate in R&D projects focused on new materials, advanced manufacturing processes, and technology development.
 Review technical literature, scientific publications, and emerging technologies.
 Contribute to technical reports, presentations, and project reviews.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration 
 Collaborate with process engineers, product developers, manufacturing, and quality teams.
 Support prototype builds and technology demonstration activities
 partecipate in knowledge sharing and continuous improvement initiative 
 YOUR SKILLS & EXPERIENCES 
 Master's Degree in: Materials Science and Engineering
 Metallurgical Engineering
 Mechanical Engineering
 Chemical Engineering
 Physics or related disciplines
 Candidates should demonstrate knowledge in several of the following areas:
 Physical metallurgy and materials science fundamentals.
 Metal processing technologies and manufacturing principles.
 Materials characterization techniques.
 Statistical data analysis and experimental methodology.
 Thermodynamics, kinetics, and phase transformations.
 Mechanical properties and microstructure characterization.
 Basic data analysis tools (Excel, MATLAB, JMP, Python, or equivalent).
 Hands-on experience acquired through academic research or laboratory activities.
 Knowledge of: Metallography
 SEM/EDS
 XRD
 Mechanical testing
 Surface characterization techniques
 Experience with Design of Experiments (DOE) during research projects.
 Exposure to scientific writing and technical presentations.
 Basic understanding of semiconductor, electronics, automotive, aerospace, or advanced manufacturing applications.
 Key Competencies
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Curiosity and passion for research and innovation.
 Ability to learn quickly and adapt to new technologies.
 Effective teamwork and communication skills.
 Initiative and willingness to work in a multidisciplinary environment.
 Strong attention to detail and scientific rigor.

Research and Teaching Assistant 
 chevron_left 
 Übersicht 
 Research and Teaching Assistant
 100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print 
 Drucken 
 The newly established Chair of Global Security, held by Prof. Annette Idler, is part of the Department of Humanities, Social and Political Sciences (D-GESS) at ETH Zurich. The Chair examines global security, especially in relation to armed conflicts, the global illicit economy, transitions from war to peace, and the interconnections between local conflict dynamics and global shifts in order and power. Its mixed-methods research programme integrates macro-level theory with detailed, contextualised fieldwork across world regions, combines qualitative, quantitative, and computational approaches, and bridges the social sciences with complexity science and other disciplines. The Chair’s international research group engages closely with international organisations, governments, and civil society. From 2029, Prof. Idler will additionally assume the Directorship of the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich.
 The Chair holder, Prof. Annette Idler, is seeking to appoint, as soon as possible or by agreement, a research and teaching assistant (100%).
 Job description
 You will prepare the Chair’s courses each semester, manage the online learning environment for the Chair’s courses and help with grading. You may be asked to represent the Chair on the departmental Teaching Committee. You will also support Prof. Idler with research for teaching and research projects – including literature and background research, data collection and management, editorial support and preparing presentations – and maintain the Chair’s teaching records.
 Profile
 You hold a Master’s degree in Political Science, International Relations or a related discipline, with specialist knowledge of international politics and global security, and are familiar with the relevant research institutes and publication outlets. You have an excellent command of written and spoken English; knowledge of German is an advantage. Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methods, a high degree of independence and very good IT skills round off your profile.
 This position is an ideal entry point after completing a university degree and is fixed-term for about two years. You can look forward to varied and challenging work in a stimulating and motivating environment at a world-leading university. You will work closely with Prof. Idler, gain insight into teaching and research at a newly established chair at ETH Zurich and engage with a wide range of global security issues. There is also scope to develop a small independent research project of your own, for example towards a PhD proposal.

items.desc: A 2.5-year Postdoctoral Research Associate position is available for an outstanding and ambitious scientist to study transition metal molecular spin qubits using pulse EPR spectroscopy and related methods. This position, funded by an UKRI grant managed by Dr Floriana Tuna (https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/floriana.tuna/), involves close collaboration with the University of Rhode Island (Huh group) and Brown University (Robinson group) under an UK-US research partnership to explore quantum information science concepts in metal organic systems. As part of the project, the successful applicant will interact closely with experts at the UK National EPR Facility at Manchester (Prof David Collison, Prof Eric McInnes) and access state-of-the-art instrumentation for cw and pulse EPR (1-34 GHz), rapid scan, light-induced EPR, and SQUID magnetometry (https://www.chemistry.manchester.ac.uk/epr/). Recent publications relevant to the project: J. Am .Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 15000; Nat. Commun. 2019, 10, 3330; Chem. Sci. 2024, 15, 3003, Chem.Eur.J. 2026, e71619, Inorg. Chem. 2026, 65, 6544. Purpose of the Job The role holder is expected to characterise the electronic structure and coherence properties of a series of d-block metal complexes to a standard suitable for publication, using pulse EPR and magnetometry, and to supervise junior researchers in the research group. Candidates should have or expect to obtain a PhD qualification in chemistry, physics, or a closely related field. They should have experience in performing advanced spectroscopic and/or magnetic measurements. Experience of EPR spectroscopy and handling and measuring highly air-sensitive samples, using glove boxes, d/f block chemistry, and being adept at a variety of characterisation techniques and calculations, are all highly desirable. The successful candidate will be a highly capable, motivated and independent researcher who is able to manage a group of PhD and undergraduate students working on a variety of spectroscopy and magnetism projects. You will be part of a larger research team working across synthesis, measurements and calculations to characterise qubits and establish the electronic structures of paramagnetic complexes. You will be expected to take a leading role in the research group, including coordination with the Huh group at Rhode Island University involved in chemical syntheses, organising group meetings, and presenting findings at international conferences. The start date is 1 February 2027, or soon after, and the position is available for up to 2.5 years. The Department of Chemistry is strongly committed to promoting equality and diversity, including the Athena SWAN Charter for gender equality in higher education. The School of Natural Sciences holds a Silver Award, which recognises their good practice in relation to gender; including flexible working arrangements, family-friendly policies, and support to allow staff to achieve a good work-life balance. We particularly welcome applications from women for this post, who are currently under-represented at this grade. Appointment will always be made on merit. For further information, please visit: https://www.manchester.ac.uk/connect/jobs/equality-diversity-inclusion/awards/athena-swan/ The University will actively foster a culture of inclusion and diversity and will seek to achieve true equality of opportunity for all members of its community. (Grades 6-9) Our benefits include: Generous employer contribution pension 29 days annual leave plus bank holidays, along with Christmas closure Ride to work and EV car scheme available For more information, please see University of Manchester Benefits. You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working here. We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our Freedom of Speech Policy. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. items.desc: About us The Curie Institute Research Center France’s leading cancer research and treatment centre, Institut Curie unites a renowned research centre and a specialist hospital, fostering close collaboration between scientists, clinicians and healthcare professionals. It offers an environment of excellence where expertise comes together around shared values: care, humanity, openness, collaboration, efficiency, innovation, solidarity and commitment. Mission Laboratory The ATOMIC team “Advanced Therapy in radiation Oncology and Molecular Imaging Characterization” (CNRS UMR9029/Inserm U1353/Université Versailles Saint-Quentin) develops new strategies to increase the therapeutic index of radiotherapy. The team brings together biologists, medical physicists and radiation oncologists. FLASH radiotherapy, discovered at Institut Curie ( Favaudon et al., Science Translational Medicine, 2014 ), delivers the dose in a fraction of a second. It reduces toxicity to healthy tissue while maintaining anti-tumour efficacy comparable to that of conventional radiotherapy: this is known as the “FLASH effect”. As part of the FRATHEA institutional project , Institut Curie is developing a new FLASH irradiator using very high-energy electrons (VHEE), designed to reach deep-seated tumours. You will conduct the preclinical studies needed to validate this equipment, working closely with the team’s physicists and radiation oncologists: a rare opportunity to take part, from the very beginning, in the development of an innovative radiotherapy technology. The position is based at Institut Curie’s Orsay site, at the heart of the Université Paris-Saclay campus, which brings together research teams in radiobiology and medical physics as well as the Institut Curie Proton Therapy Centre. Main responsibilities Design and implementation of in vivo experiments : plan and carry out irradiation protocols in mouse models to assess the effects of FLASH radiotherapy, in compliance with regulations and animal welfare standards (3Rs principle); contribute to drafting project authorisation applications (APAFiS, the French ethics approval system). Animal care and monitoring :), weighing, substance administration, anaesthesia, monitoring of clinical parameters. Irradiation sessions : prepare, anaesthetise and position animals on the FLASH irradiator, in coordination with the physicists (dosimetry, scheduling of beam time). Biological analyses : collect organs and samples; take part in analyses (histology, immunofluorescence, genotyping, flow cytometry) with other team members. Data analysis and reporting : collect, organise and statistically analyse data; keep the electronic laboratory notebook; present results at team meetings and contribute to publications. Profile Education and skills Master’s degree (MSc) or engineering degree in biology, biotechnology, physiology or life sciences. Significant initial experience in vivo required (final-year internship, work-study programme or previous position); 2 or more years of professional experience is an advantage. Regulatory training in animal experimentation required: French “Applicator” certificate or equivalent (EU Function B); training in “Conceptor (EU Function C, project design) is an advantage and may be funded as part of the position. Proficiency in rodent handling techniques Knowledge of histology, immunofluorescence and molecular biology (PCR, genotyping); experience in flow cytometry is a plus. Basic skills in statistical analysis (GraphPad Prism, R or equivalent). Experience in radiobiology or in an irradiation environment is appreciated. Personal qualities Scientific rigour, observational skills and critical thinking Strong organisational skills and autonomy Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team (researchers, physicists, PhD students, clinicians) Good writing and communication skills; scientific English (reading articles, discussions in meetings). What we offer A pioneering project: the preclinical validation of a new FLASH radiotherapy technology. A multidisciplinary biology – physics – clinical environment, on one of Europe’s leading research campuses. Funded training (flow cytometry, statistical analysis, etc.). Recognition of your work, with co-authorship of publications according to your contribution. items.desc: Location: Teagasc, Animal & Grassland, Research and Innovation Centre, Grange, Dunsany, Co. Meath. Research Salary: Research Officer with a Salary Scale of €42,921 to €81,218 Closing Date: 06/11/2026 12:00 PM Permanent Full Time Job Summary Duration: Permanent . A panel may be formed from which future similar vacancies may be filled; such a panel will remain active for a maximum period of 12 months. Basic Function: To develop, lead and implement a state of the art research programme in the production of suckler beef cattle with particular focus on the following: Genetic and nutritional factors influencing the productivity of suckler beef cows and their progeny Key maternal, reproductive and health related traits Increasing animal performance and efficiency from both grazed and conserved forages Impact of both genetics and nutrition on environmental sustainability of suckler beef production systems Background: The beef industry is a major contributor to the value of Ireland’s agri-food sector. For example, the output value of the Irish cattle sector is typically in excess of €3 billion annually. Additionally, beef cattle production is a significant enterprise on over 94,000 farms, which are widely dispersed throughout the country. In particular the suckler beef sector, built around a national herd of ca. 800,000 beef cows, is central to the production of premium quality beef destined for high value international markets. Teagasc plays a key role in developing and supporting competitive, profitable and sustainable systems of Irish beef production. These production systems must maximise the use of grazed grass to capitalize on Ireland’s natural competitive advantage in grass production, and to contribute to the high quality, grass-fed reputation of Irish beef worldwide. Teagasc are seeking to appoint a highly qualified and enthusiastic researcher to develop and lead a cutting edge research programme to underpin the continued development and sustainability of the Irish suckler beef production sector. The successful candidate’s research programme will have particular emphasis on, but will not be limited to, investigating the impact of animal genetics and nutrition on the biological performance of suckler beef cows and their progeny, and how these management interventions influence both economic and environmental sustainability. The programme will also investigate how to further increase animal performance from grazed and conserved forage. This will be a key appointment for Teagasc with national significance in further developing our beef industry over the coming years. The Grange campus is part of the Animal & Grassland Research and Innovation Centre in Teagasc and has extensive facilities for field and laboratory research. These include pasture and overwintering facilities for in excess of 1100 cattle including in excess of 200 beef cows and their progeny to finish. Field and laboratory resources include state of the art electronic individual feed intake and methane emissions measurement equipment; a feed digestibility research unit and a suite of animal nutrition, animal health and molecular biology based laboratories to support a world-class beef cattle research programme. Indeed, Teagasc has an international reputation for research and development in grass-based systems of livestock production and the successful candidate will work with a dynamic and multidisciplinary team of researchers and knowledge transfer specialists across Teagasc’s Animal & Grassland Research and Innovation Programme at Moorepark, Grange and Athenry. Job Objectives Develop, lead and implement a cutting edge research programme on aspects of the breeding and nutrition of suckler beef cattle Design and manage experiments; statistically analyse and publish the resulting data. Manage staff and resources assigned to the research programme. Identify opportunities for cutting-edge research to address key knowledge gaps. Lead successful submissions for external funding, that are consistent with the Teagasc research programme, with the objective of developing critical mass in the area by building and supervising a dynamic team of post-doctoral researchers(s) and post-graduate student(s). Develop and maintain active collaboration with relevant national and international research organisations. Work closely with Teagasc Knowledge Transfer Specialists to ensure effective dissemination of research findings to advisors and stakeholders. Supervise, in conjunction with academic collaborator postgraduate students to Masters and PhD level. Interpret and publish research results in the scientific and popular press, at conferences (nationally and internationally) and to stakeholders Contribute to the teamwork and team spirit in the Animal & Bioscience Department, and foster and add to further collaboration and integration To assist Teagasc in meeting the commitments of the Quality Customer Service Charter and Action Plan. items.desc: Andersen is hiring a DevOps Engineer with Italian for a project supporting web and mobile applications and enhancing CI/CD processes, security, and operational reliability. items.desc: Join the research project Past to Future (P2F), an ambitious Horizon Europe research consortium. The project’s overarching goal is to radically advance our capacity to anticipate future climate changes and tipping points by utilizing Earth's deep climate history. As Impact & Stakeholder Coordinator, you will play a key role in connecting our groundbreaking research with the right audiences. Additionally, you will help ensure the project runs smoothly by supporting the management team with project-related tasks. Your job As Impact & Stakeholder Coordinator, you will be the link between P2F’s scientific advancements and their application in policy and society. Your role is essential for translating complex research into actionable insights for diverse audiences. You will join the Management Team of the P2F project. The research consortium consists of 22 European partners and 3 international associated partners. You will be based at Utrecht University (UU), working alongside two dedicated Project Managers. A core component of this role is to serve as a bridge to Cardiff University, working in close daily collaboration with P2F’s Senior Public Engagement and Impact Manager who coordinates the overall Dissemination, Exploitation and Communication (DEC) of P2F. This partnership is vital for aligning our management and outreach teams in Utrecht and Cardiff. The position therefore includes one or two work visits to Cardiff to strengthen these operational links and co-develop project-wide strategies. Key Responsibilities Stakeholder engagement: Monitor and coordinate the overall stakeholder engagement strategy to non-scientific target groups, including stakeholder mapping, in close collaboration with the Cardiff team. Support the dissemination of project results to relevant scientific stakeholders and maintain active communication with the project’s Scientific Advisory Board (SAB), particularly to promote the uptake and long-term impact of the project’s core outcomes. Communication and Outreach: Collaborate with the communications officer from the related EMBRACER project to reach diverse target groups within the Netherlands, and potential role-out of activities to European partners. Set up and supervise student projects to produce visual communication materials, interviews, and other creative outputs regarding P2F research. Further develop the P2F website, manage and track the project’s social media presence and translate complex scientific papers into engaging and accessible content for the website and social media channels. Join relevant working groups, e.g. joint-policy initiatives from the Climate Research Communication Network. Project Support & Reporting: Maintain the continuous EU reporting of DEC project activities in the EC Funding & Tenders Portal, ensuring all outreach events and publications are accurately logged. Provide general consortium management support to the UU leadership team, particularly during reporting peaks and the organization of General Assembly Meetings. Your qualities Academic background (Master’s degree at a minimum) in climate/environmental science, climate policy, climate communication, or a closely related field; Experience in building networks and facilitating collaboration across different organizational cultures and with diverse external stakeholders. Strong communication skills, with a proven ability to translate complex scientific jargon into accessible narratives for the general public and policymakers. Familiarity with the Dutch and/or European climate research and policy landscape, and experience engaging relevant stakeholders. An established network in these fields is an advantage, as the role requires building connections and developing effective engagement activities within a relatively short project timeframe. Digital proficiency, including experience managing website content and utilizing social media tracking/amplification tools. Fluency in English (the project’s working language) is required. While not mandatory, proficiency in Dutch is a strong asset for engaging with local stakeholders and aligning with national projects. Nice to have: Project coordination experience, specifically in supervising student groups or managing small-to-medium scale events. Experience with EU project management or reporting (Horizon Europe/H2020), specifically regarding DEC plans and impact tracking. Our offer a position for one year (0.4 – 0.6 FTE), with the possibility of an extension until the end of the project on 1 March 2029, after a positive evaluation; a gross monthly salary, depending on qualifications and experience, between €3.706 and €5.760 (salary scale 10 under the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO NU)). The salary is based on a 38-hour working week; 8% holiday pay and 8.3% year-end bonus; a pension scheme, partially paid parental leave and flexible terms of employment based on the CAO NU. items.title: Own the cloud platform that makes cargo talk
items.card: What you'll do Own our Azure cloud platform end to end: architecture, ingestion, data, cost, and the calls about what we run and why. Push AI-assisted development further than most dare. Claude writes most of our code and a human owns every merge - you'll define how far that goes for production infrastructure, and build the guardrails. Scale ingestion and the data tier for a fast-growing fleet - without per-device
items.desc: Surfact AS Kjelsåsveien 141, 0491 Oslo Om jobben Lagre favoritt Stillingstittel Platform Engineer Type ansettelse Fast, heltid 100% Antall stillinger 1 Arbeidsspråk Engelsk eller norsk Vis flere detaljer We make cargo talk. Why? Because a third of all food and pharma produce is wasted on the way to consumers, and we're out to change that. Our smart tracker Emma - made from recycled ocean plastic - travels with temperature-sensitive shipments for enterprise customers in food, pharma and seafood across 20+ countries. We're looking for a seasoned engineer to own the platform behind it, and to build it for ten times the fleet we run today. What you'll do Own our Azure cloud platform end to end: architecture, ingestion, data, cost, and the calls about what we run and why. Push AI-assisted development further than most dare. Claude writes most of our code and a human owns every merge - you'll define how far that goes for production infrastructure, and build the guardrails. Scale ingestion and the data tier for a fast-growing fleet - without per-device cloud cost rising with it. Make reliability unremarkable: no reading silently lost, late and backfilled data handled gracefully, and monitoring that spots trouble before a customer does. Grow the data platform so questions about the fleet or a single shipment are answered in seconds, not filed as tickets. Our stack A cloud-native platform on Azure: event-driven IoT ingestion, serverless services, and both operational and analytical data stores. CI/CD carries much of what we ship, a human reviews every change, and turning more of our infrastructure into code is a job we want you to own. AI runs through development, operations and analysis, and we are leaning into what is now just possible. We're ISO 27001 certified and our customers are audited, so security shapes real engineering decisions. We'll go through the details with you in the interview. What you bring Deep experience in building and operating production cloud infrastructure - Azure, or another major cloud and the appetite to go Azure-deep. Real conviction about AI-assisted development, with the judgement to know when to slow down and verify. A curious, fast-learning mind - being a jack-of-all-trades is a real plus here. Fluency with infrastructure as code, CI/CD and observability. Strong Postgres and SQL, and sound instincts for modelling time-series data at volume. Nice to have: IoT or telemetry at fleet scale, cellular (LTE-M, NB-IoT), ISO 27001/SOC 2 environments, Python, and cloud cost engineering. What we offer Competitive salary, good pension, and share options - own a piece of what you build. Flexible hours and location; a welcoming office at Kjelsås Stasjon with parking and good transit. Our team tends to spend about half their time at the HQ. Your choice of tools, plus best-in-class AI tools with generous quotas. This job is based in Oslo, Norway. Norwegian/EEA work permit required. Relocation support is not provided. Om bedriften Born in Norway. Built for the world. Surfact transforms temperature-sensitive logistics with sensor technology built for the cold chain. We are backed by strong partners and we cut waste and safeguard vital cargo, shipment after shipment. We build our own electronics, our own firmware, our own software. It is all engineered, built and assembled in Norway to survive the harshest environments on earth. We hire generalists with depth, give them real ownership, and trust them to make decisions. The work is serious, with pharma, food, lives and livelihoods at stake, but the way we do it is grounded, honest and unmistakably Norwegian. Be part of an excellent multidisciplinary research center with the HRS4R badge. Location on the Can Ruti Campus, a first-class translational research environment in the Barcelona area, in a very stimulating scientific environment. The IGTP offers a supportive, friendly and collaborative ecosystem to promote professional development and help you achieve your research goals. FOR MORE INFORMATION https://www.germanstrias.org/en/research/infectious-diseases/3/innovation-in-respiratory-infections-and-tuberculosis-diagnosis. HOW TO APPLY Interested persons must attach to the application: Motivation letter explaining their interest in the position. Updated CV. Contact of 2 references. Applications will be evaluated in accordance with the guiding principles and objectives of the supply systems, following the process described below: Curricular evaluation : analysis of the curriculum vitae to assess aspects related to training, professional career and experience in positions related to the job position under selection. Personal interview : once the résumé has been evaluated, the selected candidates will be called for a personal interview to verify and expand on the information detailed in the résumé and to evaluate aspects related to experience and professional skill s. Applications that do not meet the requirements, that are not included in the cases foreseen or that are not processed in accordance with the established procedure will not be considered in the selection process. DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS The call for applications will close on 26th of October 2026 About us The Germans Trias i Pujol Research Institute (IGTP) is a public research centre located in Badalona.
