items.desc:
About kaiko 
 Picture Laura, 58, with a cough that will not clear. It takes four specialists and a year to find her lung cancer, though the signs were in her file from the start, spread across scans, lab results and reports. No doctor had the whole picture, or the time to weigh it.
 kaiko is named after a deep-sea vessel that went 10,911 metres down, to the bottom of the ocean, and came back with what was there. Our clinical AI does the same with a patient’s record and the medical evidence, so doctors have the whole picture when they decide. It is built on our own foundation models and used daily at leading European hospitals.
 We are a well-funded team of more than a hundred people in Amsterdam and Zurich. Join us so the next patient like Laura is diagnosed months sooner, with a better chance of a long and healthy life.
 About the role 
 As kaiko brings its clinical AI to clinicians, the decisions on where we invest depend on data we can trust. That data has to follow each user from a first visit to our website, through sign-up and first use, to the colleagues they bring in.
 There is no marketing technology stack for this yet, so you design and build it from the ground up: tracking and consent, the connection between product and marketing data, event-triggered email next to our CRM, and the data layer the team reports from. Working closely with product, engineering, data and security, you keep clinical data out of every marketing tool by design. You document what you build and hand it over to the growth team in working order, ready for new European markets.
 We’re looking for someone who has built a measurement and messaging stack from nothing for a product-led company, and who is as comfortable writing an event specification with engineers as setting up a CRM integration or modelling data in a warehouse.
 This is a freelance engagement until mid-2027, starting as soon as possible. 
 Some areas of responsibility 
 Design and build our marketing measurement from the ground up: the tracking plan, consent and server-side tracking, attribution, and the definitions the team reports on.
 Connect product and marketing data with product engineers: event specifications, one event pipeline, and one view of each user across website, product and CRM.
 Set up event-triggered lifecycle email next to our CRM, with reliable deliverability and clear rules for which tool reaches whom.
 Build the data layer and dashboards the growth team decides from, then document the stack and hand it over in working order.
 About you 
 4 to 8 years in marketing operations, growth engineering, analytics engineering, or martech consulting, including building a stack from scratch for a self-serve or product-led company.
 You have set up an event-triggered messaging tool such as Customer.io , Braze, or Iterable next to a CRM such as HubSpot, and connected both to a product.
 You set up and model a data warehouse with SQL and a tool such as dbt.
 Privacy by design: you build tracking under GDPR and ePrivacy and keep sensitive data out of marketing tools.
 A hands-on builder who works as one team with product and engineering. You document your work so others can run it.
 Nice to have: 
 Experience in healthcare, life sciences, or another regulated sector.
 Experience measuring referral loops, or setting up tracking across countries and languages.
 Working knowledge of Dutch.
 Why kaiko 
 At kaiko, we believe the best ideas come from collaboration, ownership and ambition. We’ve built a team of international experts where your work has a direct impact. Here’s what we value:
 Ownership: You’ll have the autonomy to set your own goals, make critical decisions, and see the direct impact of your work.
 Collaboration: You’ll have to approach disagreement with curiosity, build on common ground, and create solutions together.
 Ambition: You’ll be surrounded by people who set high standards for themselves and others, who see obstacles as opportunities, and who are relentless in their work to create better outcomes for patients.
 Our interview process 
 Our interview process is designed to assess mutual fit across skills, motivation, and values. It typically includes the following steps:
 Screening call: A short conversation to align on your motivation, professional goals, and initial fit for the role.
 Technical interview: A deep dive into your problem-solving approach through a technical challenge, case study, or role-specific scenario.
 Onsite meeting (optional): You’ll meet team members across functions to explore collaboration dynamics, team fit, and day-to-day context.

Scientific Assistant in Industrial Robotics and Manufacturing 
 chevron_left 
 Übersicht 
 Scientific Assistant in Industrial Robotics and Manufacturing
 100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print 
 Drucken 
 The Advanced Manufacturing Lab (am|z) at ETH Zurich, led by Prof. Markus Bambach, is seeking a highly motivated Scientific Assistant to contribute to research and development in industrial robotics, automated manufacturing, and metrology.
 We are looking for a candidate who combines strong programming skills with hands-on experience in robotic hardware, enjoys solving challenging technical problems, and can independently develop and implement robotic solutions.
 The position offers the opportunity to take ownership of experimental robotic systems, develop innovative automation solutions, and contribute to scientific research in advanced manufacturing.
 Project background
 The Advanced Manufacturing Lab at ETH Zurich investigates innovative manufacturing technologies by combining robotics, automation, process engineering, and data-driven methods.
 Our research aims to make industrial robotic systems more flexible, accurate, autonomous, and reliable. Applications include robotic manipulation, pick-and-place operations, and manufacturing processes such as welding, adhesive bonding, and drilling.
 Beyond conventional robot programming, we investigate methods for improving robotic capabilities through sensing, metrology, calibration, process monitoring, and data-driven approaches. Our work combines the development of practical robotic systems with experimental validation and scientific investigation.
 Job description
 Your main responsibilities will include:
 Independently develop, program, and operate industrial robotic systems for automated manufacturing and manipulation tasks
 Design and implement robotic applications, including pick-and-place operations, welding, adhesive bonding, drilling, and related manufacturing processes
 Integrate robotic hardware, including end-effectors, sensors, measurement equipment, tooling, and peripheral systems
 Develop and maintain software for robot control, motion planning, and automation, using version control, automated testing, and deployment workflows
 Design and implement automated data acquisition and processing workflows to collect, synchronize, visualize, and analyze robotic and manufacturing process data
 Integrate metrology and sensing technologies to evaluate and improve robot positioning accuracy, calibration, repeatability, and process quality
 Independently plan and conduct experiments, troubleshoot technical challenges, and evaluate system performance
 Contribute to scientific research by developing and validating novel methods, analyzing experimental results, and preparing scientific publications
 Collaborate with researchers, students, and industrial partners on robotics and manufacturing projects
 Profile
 We are looking for an independent, technically skilled, and research-oriented engineer who enjoys working with real robotic systems and transforming ideas into functioning experimental solutions.
 You should have:
 A Master's degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation, or a closely related field
 Hands-on experience in programming, operating, or integrating robotic systems, gained through research, academic projects, or industry
 Strong programming skills, particularly in Python, C++, or comparable languages, with experience in developing and maintaining software for robotics and automation
 A solid understanding of robotic kinematics, coordinate transformations, motion planning, and control principles
 Practical experience with robotic hardware, including the integration, configuration, or troubleshooting of sensors, actuators, end-effectors, or mechanical components
 Proficiency with Git and version control, along with familiarity with software testing and continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) workflows
 Experience with experimental work, data acquisition, and analysis of measurement data
 The ability to independently solve technical problems, combined with creativity, initiative, and a systematic approach to engineering challenges
 A strong interest in scientific research and the development of innovative robotic technologies
 Fluent English, both written and spoken
 Knowledge of German is an advantage

 Experience with industrial robots, such as ABB, KUKA, FANUC, or similar platforms
 Familiarity with the Robot Operating System (ROS/ROS 2) or other robotics frameworks
 Experience with robotic manufacturing applications, including manipulation, assembly, welding, adhesive bonding, machining, or drilling

 Experience with machine vision, force/torque sensors, laser measurement systems, industrial communication interfaces, or real-time data acquisition

 Photonic EEEE Engineer in the Components Section, Avionics and EEE Division, Electrical Department, Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality.
 The Components Section provides functional support to ESA projects and carries out technological research and development (R&D) in the field of electrical, electronic, electromechanical and electro-optical (EEEE) components with a strong focus on technologies and processes, development and reliability as well as on ground qualification activities. In addition, the Section is responsible for ESCC (European Space Component Coordination).

items.desc: The AI Teams at Agile Robots are looking for a Robotics Software Engineer (m/f/d) AI Tools & Integration , who will integrate AI models with robot hardware and build the applications and tooling around them. Customers and partners reuse this stack through open-source releases, so it has to keep working with messy data, limited compute, and real hardware. Responsibilities Robot Integration: Integrate trained AI models with single-arm and dual-arm robots through ROS 2, and maintain the runtime that runs them on hardware. Application Development: Build robot applications on top of the AI stack, including agentic workflows that chain AI models and robot skills into multi-step tasks. Tool Interfaces: Build UI, API, and CLI tools such as dataset viewers, training dashboards, and benchmark viewers. End-to-End Testing: Build test suites that run real user workflows from data through training to inference, including stress tests with messy data and limited compute. Release Readiness: Maintain nightly regression runs on the reference workflows and run reliability checks before demos and open-source releases. Documentation: Write and maintain the documentation customers and partners use to adopt the tooling. Essential Skills Engineering Background: Degree in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent qualification plus professional experience building comparable software systems. Python Engineering: Professional experience building and maintaining Python software that other engineers depend on. ROS 2 Integration: Hands-on experience integrating and debugging software on physical robots through ROS 2. Containers & CI: Hands-on experience with Docker and CI pipelines such as GitHub Actions for reproducible builds and releases. Testing: Hands-on experience designing integration and end-to-end test suites and debugging failures across the full stack. Backend Services: Experience building backend services and APIs, for example with FastAPI or gRPC. Beneficial Skills C++ Development: Experience writing C++ for robot-side or performance-critical code. Agentic Systems: Experience building applications that combine language or vision-language models with robot skill execution. Frontend Development: Working experience with React or Next.js for building data-heavy interfaces. ML Workflows: Working understanding of how training and inference pipelines for robot learning models fit together. What we offer A dynamic high-tech company, combined with financial soundness and world-class investors. Join an interdisciplinary, international team with 60+ different nationalities in a collaborative work environment. Lots of development opportunities as we continue to grow. Challenging tasks and impactful projects alongside experts that enable professional and personal growth. Corporate Benefits Program covering health, mobility, and learning for 100€ net per month. Modern office facilities with a rooftop terrace overlooking Munich, free drinks & fruits, and regular company events contribute to a good working environment About us Agile Robots SE is an international high-tech company based in Munich, Germany with a production site in Kaufbeuren and more than 3500 employees worldwide. Our mission is to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and robotics by developing systems that combine state-of-the-art force-moment-sensing and world-leading image-processing technology. This unique combination of technologies allows us to provide user-friendly and affordable robotic solutions that enable intelligent precision assembly. This is made possible by our employees, who bring out the best in each and every day with creativity and enthusiasm. Become part of this team and shape the future of robotics with us! We are proud of our diversity and welcome your application regardless of gender and sexual identity, nationality, ethnicity, religion, age, or disability.

L'obiettivo di Over è quello di garantire luoghi dove i residenti possano mantenere le proprie abitudini, la propria socialità, la propria indipendenza ma con una protezione costante ma discreta, supportata dalle moderne tecnologie alla portata di tutti. Posizione: Operiamo nel settore socio sanitario e stiamo investendo con decisione sull'innovazione digitale, siamo certificati ISO/IEC 27001 e abbiamo inoltre avviato un percorso di conformità all'AI Act europeo. Non ci limitiamo ad adottare la tecnologia, ma la sviluppiamo internamente con un team dedicato alla progettazione di soluzioni AI-native, che vogliamo far crescere con giovani talenti. I nostri team lavorano a stretto contatto con gli operatori sanitari per progettare e fornire strumenti che semplifichino la presa in carico del paziente e la relativa cura. Siamo alla ricerca di un/a Junior Web Developer & AI Integration per le seguenti attività: Supporto alla manutenzione e all'evoluzione dei siti web aziendali (front-end e back-end), imparando a curare performance, sicurezza e accessibilità. Partecipazione all'integrazione di siti e flussi digitali con il centralino basato su AI (instradamento chiamate, automazioni conversazionali) e con il CRM (contatti, lead, appuntamenti, flussi paziente). Sviluppo di integrazioni API/webhook tra siti, CRM, centralino, marketing automation, gestionali e sistemi sanitari interni, affiancato da colleghi senior. Collaborazione con il team AI su automazioni, agenti e integrazioni che vanno oltre il "semplice sito", imparando sul campo. Attenzione alla qualità tecnica: codice pulito e manutenibile, documentazione essenziale, rispetto delle regole su sicurezza dei dati e GDPR. Requisiti: Competenze tecniche Laurea o diploma in informatica o ITS; prima esperienza anche breve (stage o progetti) nello sviluppo web. Buone basi di HTML/CSS/JavaScript e di un linguaggio back-end (PHP, Node.js, Python); gradito React o Vue. Concetti base di API REST e webhook. Attitudine AI (il nostro requisito distintivo) Utilizzo già abituale di AI coding assistant (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor o simili) nei tuoi progetti o nello studio. Spirito critico nell'uso dell'AI: capire il codice che l'AI propone, verificarlo e non accettarlo a scatola chiusa. Interesse a conoscere API di LLM, prompt e automazioni agentiche (non serve essere già esperti). Curiosità reale, voglia di imparare e di sperimentare con strumenti in continua evoluzione. Approccio: voglia di crescere, attitudine al lavoro in team, disponibilità ad ascoltare e a chiedere, capacità di dialogare con referenti clinici e amministrativi, precisione e attenzione alla qualità. Titoli preferenziali: tirocini o progetti in ambito sanitario o in contesti regolamentati; interesse per le normative sul trattamento dei dati sanitari; progetti personali o di studio basati su AI. Altre informazioni: COSA OFFRIAMO Un percorso di crescita strutturato, con affiancamento costante da parte di colleghi senior e formazione continua. Lavoro su progetti reali di AI applicata in un'azienda in forte crescita innovativa, per sviluppare competenze che vanno oltre il web development tradizionale. Un ambiente in cui le idee vengono ascoltate e la tecnologia ha un impatto concreto sulla cura delle persone. RAL 35.000€-45.000€ SEDE DI LAVORO: GENOVA. Lavoro in sede

Collaborare
items.desc: Trento, IT, 38122 Società: Gruppo Cassa Centrale Cassa Centrale Banca è Capogruppo dell’omonimo gruppo bancario cui fanno capo altre società attive in ambito finanziario ed in grado di completare l’offerta rivolta alla soddisfazione di molteplici esigenze delle banche clienti. Cassa Centrale Banca è una “Banca per le banche” che si impegna a lavorare per la rete delle banche affiliate e clienti condividendone valori, cultura, strategie e sistema organizzativo per rendere sempre più efficiente e competitivo il sistema sul mercato. La missione del Gruppo Cassa Centrale è contribuire allo sviluppo della vita economica e sociale dei territori delle banche di credito cooperativo. Il Gruppo Cassa Centrale ha il proprio headquarter presso la storica sede di Trento, e filiali territoriali nelle maggiori città italiane. Scopri di più sul sito della corporate http://gruppo.cassacentrale.it/ L'Intelligenza Artificiale sta trasformando il settore bancario e finanziario, creando nuove opportunità di innovazione, efficienza e servizio ai clienti. Entrando nel team AI Promotion & Governance, contribuirai alla definizione e all'evoluzione del modello di adozione dell'AI del Gruppo, collaborando con funzioni business, tecnologiche e di controllo per favorire uno sviluppo responsabile, sicuro e orientato al valore delle soluzioni di Intelligenza Artificiale. Chi stiamo cercando Cerchiamo una persona curiosa, analitica e motivata, con una buona preparazione sui temi dell'Intelligenza Artificiale e un interesse genuino per il settore bancario e finanziario. Valutiamo sia neolaureati con una solida preparazione accademica sia professionisti alle prime esperienze che desiderano crescere in un contesto in forte evoluzione, lavorando all'intersezione tra tecnologia, innovazione, business e governance. Cosa farai Supportare l'identificazione, la valutazione e la prioritizzazione di iniziative di Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI e Agentic AI, analizzandone benefici, impatti operativi e rischi. Contribuire all'evoluzione del framework di AI Governance del Gruppo, supportando la definizione di ruoli, processi, controlli, policy e strumenti necessari per un'adozione responsabile e scalabile dell'AI. Collaborare alla valutazione dei casi d'uso AI, anche in relazione agli aspetti di rischio e sostenibilità operativa. Monitorare l'evoluzione tecnologica, normativa e di mercato in ambito AI, predisponendo analisi e sintesi a supporto delle decisioni aziendali. Supportare attività di AI Literacy, formazione e comunicazione interna, contribuendo a diffondere conoscenza e consapevolezza sull'uso dell'AI all'interno del Gruppo. Partecipare a workshop, gruppi di lavoro e momenti di confronto con stakeholder interni ed esterni sui temi di innovazione e AI adoption. Requisiti Laurea in Informatica, Ingegneria, Matematica, Statistica, Economia o discipline affini. Conoscenza dei concetti fondamentali di Machine Learning, Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLM) e AI Agents Interesse per i temi di AI Adoption, Responsible AI, AI Governance e innovazione tecnologica Interesse o prima esposizione al settore bancario e finanziario, maturata attraverso studi, tesi, progetti o esperienze professionali Esperienza professionale compresa tra 0 e 2 anni Buona conoscenza della lingua inglese Competenze che apprezziamo Pensiero critico e capacità di analizzare problemi complessi Capacità di tradurre concetti tecnici in messaggi chiari per interlocutori non specialistici Attitudine alla collaborazione e al lavoro in team multidisciplinari Proattività, autonomia e orientamento al risultato Interesse per la trasformazione organizzativa e l'innovazione nei servizi finanziari. Per questa posizione è previsto un trattamento economico non inferiore ai minimi tabellari stabiliti dal CCNL applicabile per l’inquadramento indicato. Indicazione economica minima (base): a partire da €35.650 RAL (minimo contrattuale per Terza Area Professionale Primo Livello). Sede di lavoro: Trento La suddetta ricerca è aperta a candidature di qualsiasi orientamento o espressione di genere, orientamento sessuale, età, etnia e credo religioso, in ottemperanza e nel rispetto del d.lgs. 198/2006. Per i valori a cui ci ispiriamo, prestiamo particolare attenzione alla diversità, all’inclusività e alla tutela dell’equilibrio fra vita privata e vita professionale.

About the job We are looking for Fullstack Engineer to help QVAC application teams develop, review, test, and deliver reliable software with less friction. Your focus will be our desktop and mobile applications and their shared runtime, AI harness, and skills packages. You will build and maintain developer tools, integrate AI agents into engineering workflows, and improve code quality and delivery automation. This is a hands-on engineering role with room to shape the tooling roadmap. You will work with engineers to identify useful improvements and own them from implementation through adoption and ongoing support. Success means shorter feedback loops, dependable automation, and tools that developers trust and use. Responsibilities Evaluate, integrate, and maintain developer tools and AI agents, including the repository guidance and integrations they need to work effectively. Build and operate agents in CI and scheduled workflows that investigate failures, propose fixes, and give engineers evidence they can act on. Improve automated pull request reviews, evaluating finding accuracy and reducing noise for reviewers. Develop code quality scripts and checks for complexity, function and file size, dependency cycles, and performance regressions. Work with package owners on practical thresholds and targeted refactoring. Improve development environments, testing, and build and release workflows so engineers and agents can verify changes reliably. Prioritize improvements with engineering teams, support adoption through documentation and onboarding, and measure effectiveness, reliability, and operating costs. Example projects include agents that investigate CI failures, diagnose compatibility and performance regressions, and flag changes that affect package interfaces or architecture. You will choose and refine these workflows with the engineers who use them. Experience building and maintaining developer tools or engineering automation used by others, with strong JavaScript/TypeScript and Node.js skills. Hands-on experience using and integrating AI coding tools or agents, with sound judgment about their limitations, output validation, and human review. Experience with Git, CI/CD, automated testing, and systematic debugging of build, test, or integration failures. A strong approach to code quality: maintainable code, useful automated checks, and refactoring that preserves behavior. Ability to work independently, collaborate with engineers, and communicate clearly in English within a remote, globally distributed team. Important information for candidates Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. items.desc: Location: Krakow, Lesser Poland, Poland Job ID: R0147165 Date Posted: 2026-10-15 Company Name: HITACHI ENERGY SERVICES SP. Z O.O. Profession (Job Category): General Management Job Schedule: Full time Remote: No Job Description: The AI Research Engineer brings research discipline to practical technology validation at Hitachi Energy. The role interprets emerging AI research, methods, frameworks, models and evaluation approaches, and turns the most relevant developments into practical validation questions. It performs hands-on prototypes, benchmarks and comparisons to produce evidence before architecture, platform, acceleration or delivery commitments are made. How you will make an impact Review AI research, publications, benchmarks and model documentation, and identify developments that merit practical testing. Translate research insight into validation questions, fair experimental designs and baselines, together with the Experimentation Engineer and Opportunity Lead. Run research-led prototypes, benchmarks and comparisons, and interpret the results with clear limitations and proportionate recommendations. Exchange methods and learnings with Hitachi Group, DAAI peers, vendors and external research communities. Publication is not a standing expectation. Keep reusable methods, benchmarks and test assets where they prevent repeated work. Turn one finding into a concrete question, for example whether a new technique beats what we use today on our kind of data. Design the experiment: baseline, tasks, how success is judged, and what would invalidate the result. Run benchmarks and research-led prototypes in Python (LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, fine-tuning, responsible-AI checks). Your Background 3+ years in applied AI research, AI engineering or ML research, in a company, consultancy or research institution. Strong Python, with hands-on AI/ML experimentation, benchmarking and evaluation. Familiar with LLMs, generative AI, fine-tuning, RAG, agentic AI and responsible-AI evaluation. MSc or PhD in AI, machine learning or computer science, valued when combined with practical work. The Role As an AI Innovation Lab Experience Specialist, you will bridge interaction design, engineering, and research to transform client opportunity briefs into tangible, working prototypes and evidence-backed human-AI experiences. Operating under the engagement direction of the Associate Director and Director, you turn ambiguity into momentum—taking customer concepts from brief to service blueprint, agent concept, coded interface, and physical or voice touchpoints. items.desc: Intro px dynamics is a small quantitative trading firm in Berlin and Cologne. We are four people. We trade European short-term power markets systematically, on our own account, and we sell trading signals to a few trading desks. We build and run everything ourselves: the data, the models, the execution and the servers. We are looking for one more person to research and run trading strategies with us. The problem What we try to understand is price formation in a physical system. The European power market is a stack of many technologies, from nuclear and gas to wind, solar and batteries, each with its own economics, interconnected across borders so that the price in one zone depends on the weather in another. The mix shifts continuously as the energy system transforms, and the market trades it down to the last minutes before delivery. It's a fantastically complex problem and nobody has run out of things to learn. A well-traded short-term market helps a system with a lot of wind and sun run efficiently, and we like that our work has that effect. What you would work on Price models for the intraday market, built from weather model output, fundamentals and our own order-book history. Trading strategies for the continuous intraday market, together with the sizing and the risk limits that go with them. Running what you build in production, and comparing what it did with what the backtest said it would do. You take each of these from the first idea to live trading, so we don't split the work much along the value chain. How we work The team has backgrounds in machine learning, particle physics, information systems and economics, and together over two decades of experience in energy markets. Everyone works across research, trading systems, data and infrastructure. We think people do their best work when it is truly theirs. Everyone also does the ordinary work, from scheduling to the occasional invoice, because we want to stay small, and a small team only works if everyone chips in. Live systems need looking after, so monitoring on weekends and holidays rotates through the team. Our stack is open source and our own code from top to bottom, and we run it ourselves, so anyone here can read and change every part of it. We write most of that code with AI coding assistants, and the repository, the documentation and the data are organised so that both people and models can work with them. Who you are You have a strong academic background in physics, statistics or another quantitative field, typically a PhD, but a master's degree and real work with real data count just as much. We care more about how you think than about the title. You want to understand the energy system itself, not only the methods you apply to it. The domain matters to us as much as the modelling. While you'll find plenty of support and knowledge in the team, you are comfortable taking ownership for your learning journey. You have a very strong understanding of statistics and genuinely view the world probabilistically. We value that more than familiarity with any particular class of models. You know what clean code and a clean architecture look like, and you hold the code to that standard whether you or an assistant wrote it. Writing Python by hand matters less than it used to; knowing when to do it anyway, for example when you are iterating on a statistical model, matters more. You do not need to be a software engineer. You would rather be corrected than be wrong, and you can take an idea all the way to production yourself. If you are unsure whether you meet all of this, apply anyway. We would rather see your application than not. Nice to have Experience in power markets or as a quant trader. Time series modelling. R, where it is the better tool. You are at home on Linux. Some familiarity with Rust or C. What we offer Hybrid work from our Berlin office 30 days vacation VSOP (virtual shares) Core hours roughly 9 to 5, and flexibility when life happens A small team where your models trade Practicalities English is our working language; German is helpful but not required. We welcome applications regardless of gender, background or where you studied, and we particularly welcome applications from women.

items.desc: The Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam (AIP) is dedicated to astrophysical questions ranging from the study of our Sun to the evolution of the cosmos. The research focuses on the area of stars, the Sun and exoplanets, galactic and extragalactic astrophysics, and cosmology. A significant share of the work involves research and development in the area of astrophysical spectroscopy, astrophotonics and the research data infrastructure. The AIP fulfils its research mission through numerous national, European, and international collaborations. The institute is the successor to the Berlin Observatory, founded in 1700, and the Astrophysical Observatory Potsdam, founded in 1874, which was the first institute in the world to devote itself expressly to astrophysics. Since 1992, the AIP has been a member of the Leibniz Association. Around 200 people work at our institute, set in a beautiful park landscape in Potsdam, not far from Berlin. At the department of Galactic and Extragalactic Astrophysics, we are looking for a Tenure-track scientist (m/f/d) in the field of Dwarf galaxies with particular attention to the Magellanic Clouds. The successful applicant is expected to develop an independent research programme that well fits the scope of the Research group “Dwarf Galaxies and the Galactic Halo” led by Prof. Maria-Rosa Cioni. This includes the exploitation of data from space-based imaging (e.g. Euclid, Roman, HST/JWST) and large-scale spectroscopic (e.g. 4MOST, (Blue)MUSE, MOSAIC) facilities to study the assembly history and dynamical evolution of Dwarf galaxies. In particular, using resolved stellar populations of field and star clusters, in the Magellanic Clouds and their analogs. The appointment will be for an initial period of five years, with a tenure review to be carried out in the 4th year of the appointment. The successful candidate must have a Doctoral degree or equivalent in Physics, Astronomy, or a related field as well as Post-doctoral research experience and a proven trackrecord in astronomy research, preferably on the subject of dwarf galaxies or the Magellanic Clouds. The candidate is expected to attract external funding to support junior members and act as supervisor of undergraduate and graduate research projects. The AIP offers a modern working environment, spacious and well-equipped offices, travel support, an open collegial working atmosphere and good opportunities for internal and external training. Salary is based on professional experience and expertise following the German public service collective agreement (TV-L) with a pay grade of E14. Social benefits include health insurance, contributions to the German Pension Insurance and the company pension VBL, disability and survivors’ benefits as well as a subsidy for the public transport ticket. The position is suitable for part-time employment and the start date is foreseen for the summer or fall of 2027. To apply for this position, please submit a cover letter, a curriculum vitae including a list of publications, a research statement including future research directions (max. 3 pages), plus the names and contact details of three potential reference letter writers. Letter writers will be requested to upload their recommendation only for candidates that advance to the second stage of the selection process. Please use the AIP job Application Portal to submit your application: https://jobs1.aip.de/rec101. Equal opportunities are an integral part of staff and organisational development at the AIP; therefore, applications from all genders are equally welcome. People with disabilities will be given preferential consideration where they have the same professional qualifications and skills. Your application documents will be made available to a selection committee, relevant bodies and officials. They will also be kept for a period of at least three months following the conclusion of the recruitment process. Applications received by 15th December 2026 will receive full consideration. However, applications received after this date may still be considered until the post is filled. In case of questions, please contact Prof. Cioni using the email address bewerbung-2026-08@aip.de. items.desc: Job Purpose As Research Analyst of the Kuehne Climate Center (KCC), you will support the Knowledge Hub’s applied research and analytical work on logistics, freight transport, and supply chains. The position covers the full knowledge-development workflow: retrieving and packaging information, framing questions, identifying evidence, collecting and structuring data, quantitative analysis, visualization, and actionable insights. The role combines structured research with strong quantitative problem solving and effective use of AI and digital tools. You will work closely with the Knowledge Hub Team and support analytical needs across the KCC Program Lines. What you will do Conduct applied research on logistics, freight transport, and supply-chain topics in the context of climate action Translate research and advisory questions into analytical approaches, indicators, and data needs Review scientific and industry sources and identify relevant datasets Collect, clean, structure, and document datasets; ensure quality and traceability Conduct quantitative and statistical analysis and modelling, and run scenario analyses as required Build dashboards, visualizations, and practical analytical tools Use AI-assisted tools for research, coding, analysis, and evidence synthesis Automate recurring research and analytical workflows where useful Support KCC’s database infrastructure and emerging intelligence platform Contribute to methodologies, models, and analytical toolkits Translate findings into reports, presentations, data stories, and recommendations Collaborate with Program Lines, research institutions, technology partners, and other stakeholders in generating new information and insights You‘re good at Conducting applied research independently and systematically Structuring complex questions into solvable analytical problems Applying quantitative, logical, and problem-solving skills Working with complex, incomplete, and multi-source data Learning new analytical, digital, and AI tools quickly Working reliably, diligently, and with attention to detail Translating evidence into clear insights and visual narratives Dealing with ambiguity Collaborating proactively in an international team You bring 2-5 years of relevant experience in applied research, either in consulting, the logistics industry, or in a relevant analytics role related to supply chains and logistics Master’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, Statistics, or a related field Good understanding of logistics, freight transport, and supply chains Strong quantitative reasoning and hands-on experience working with data, analytical methods, and models Advanced proficiency in Excel and Power BI / Tableau; experience with Python or R is highly desirable Familiarity with standard research methods and tools in the industrial context Confident use of modern AI tools for research, analysis, coding, and automation; SQL, Git/GitHub, APIs, Power Automate, SharePoint, GIS, Azure, MCP, or similar tools are an asset Strong data storytelling and communication abilities; fluency in English and German You will work with The Research Analyst reports to the Head of Knowledge & Analytics and works closely with the Senior Data Analyst, the Data Analyst, the Communications Department, the Management & Operations Team, and the Program Line leaders to deliver applied research, analytical outputs, data products, and knowledge products supporting KCC’s programs and strategic initiatives. What you can expect Work in an enthusiastic and highly motivated international team committed to making a real positive impact on climate action A high degree of creative freedom High agility and speed of implementation A stimulating and diverse range of work within a strong Foundation network Personal and professional growth driven by your own initiative and engagement Additional information The Kuehne Climate Center (KCC) is a subsidiary of the Kuehne Foundation in Schindellegi, Switzerland. Established in 1976 by the Kuehne family, it is one of the largest foundations in the German-speaking world. As an operational foundation, it is involved in the areas of logistics, medicine, culture, and, since the beginning of 2023, climate action. The Foundation is independent, operational, and international. The KCC implements the Foundation’s climate action mandate. Its mission is to accelerate climate-compatible development within and through logistics systems. KCC works through applied research and thought leadership, project and advisory work, training and capacity building, with a particular focus on countries of the Global South. KCC is a globally operating think-and-do tank headquartered in Hamburg’s vibrant HafenCity. From here, we manage and support all our global projects, actively partnering with our regional teams and with institutions from around the world. items.desc: Temporary Consultant Histopathologist required for hospital in the West of Ireland. The successful candidate will provide high-quality diagnostic histopathology services, participate actively in site-specific Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) meetings, support National Cancer Control Programme (NCCP) clinical pathways, and contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education and research. Key Responsibilities & Clinical Duties 1. Clinical Service Delivery Provide diagnostic reporting on surgical pathology specimens, biopsies, and cytopathology (where applicable) across general and subspecialty areas. Participate actively in site-specific Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) meetings for cancer diagnosis, staging, and treatment planning. Provide expert consultative opinions on complex cases at the request of clinical colleagues. Provide an autopsy service in line with regional hospital requirements. Ensure rapid turn-around times and quality standards in compliance with ISO 15189 accreditation requirements and INAB guidelines 2. Management & Service Development Collaborate with the Clinical Lead, Laboratory Manager, and Senior Medical Scientists to optimize laboratory workflow, quality assurance, and digital pathology integration. Education, Training & Research Supervise and mentor Specialist Registrars (SpRs), Non-Consultant Hospital Doctors (NCHDs), and trainee Medical Scientists. Participate in undergraduate medical teaching in conjunction with the University of Limerick School of Medicine. Engaged in clinical research, clinical trials, and academic publications supported by the Clinical Education & Research Centre (CERC). Professional Qualifications Specialist Registration: Full registration in the Specialist Division of the Register of Medical Practitioners maintained by the Medical Council in Ireland in the specialty of Histopathology (or eligibility for immediate registration at the time of appointment). Experience & Competencies Possession of FRCPath (or equivalent recognized higher qualification in Pathology). Demonstrated high-level expertise in general diagnostic surgical pathology and subspecialty reporting. Strong track record of active participation in clinical audit, clinical governance, and multidisciplinary team working. Excellent interpersonal, leadership, and communication skills. Proficient in clinical teaching, NCHD supervision, and educational delivery.

items.desc: The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers top-level education and research in one of the most relevant and exciting scientific disciplines of the 21st century: engineering health. In combining engineering and life sciences, through challenge-based learning and a multidisciplinary approach in collaboration with hospitals, industry and others, the department addresses the great challenges of the future, striving to improve healthcare and society as a whole. Introduction Do you enjoy bringing structure to complex projects and working with researchers in an innovative academic environment? Are you organized, communicative and curious about research and new technologies? Would you like to contribute to innovative research projects while developing your knowledge of research funding and project development? If so, we are looking for you. Within the Project Development Office (PDO), you will help researchers navigate the different stages of a research project, from identifying funding opportunities and preparing grant proposals to facilitating a smooth transition towards project implementation. The PDO supports researchers throughout this process, ensuring that funding opportunities are identified, proposals are well prepared and projects can move smoothly from development to implementation. We are looking for a proactive and organized Junior Project Development Officer to strengthen our research support team. In this role, you will support researchers, project coordinators and experienced Project Development Officers with grant preparation, project administration, consortium coordination and project management activities. You will help ensure that funding applications and research projects run smoothly by keeping track of deadlines, documentation, communication and administrative processes. Job Description As a Junior Advisor Research Funding, you support researchers and experienced Project Development Officers in the preparation and coordination of research proposals and projects. You help ensure that the practical, administrative and organizational aspects of funding applications are handled accurately and efficiently, keeping track of deadlines, documentation and communication. A key part of your role is keeping track of the many moving parts involved in grant applications. You coordinate input from researchers and consortium partners, organize meetings, follow up on action points, monitor deadlines, perform compliance and completeness checks, and help set up applications in funding portals such as the European Commission Funding & Tenders Portal. You also maintain application records, project documentation and internal systems, and support communication activities where needed. Once a project is awarded, you help ensure a smooth transition from proposal development to project implementation. You will support the administration and coordination of running research projects, for example by monitoring deadlines and deliverables, organizing meetings, supporting reporting and maintaining collaborative project environments such as SharePoint. Within the Project Development Office of the Department of Biomedical Engineering, you will work closely with researchers, project coordinators and colleague Project Development Officer. You will be part of a team that supports innovative research throughout the project lifecycle. This role offers an opportunity to learn about research funding, project development and the research conducted within Biomedical Engineering, while contributing to the continuous improvement of research support processes. Job Requirements We are looking for a proactive and organized colleague who is eager to learn and interested in supporting innovative research. You bring: A Bachelor's or Master's degree, preferably in Biomedical Engineering, a related field, or another relevant discipline. Strong organizational and administrative skills, with an eye for detail and the ability to keep an overview of multiple tasks and deadlines. Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal. A proactive and hands-on approach: you take initiative, follow up on actions and make sure things keep moving. The ability to work effectively with different stakeholders, including researchers, colleagues and external partners. An interest in research, innovation and research funding, and the curiosity to learn how research projects are developed and funded. Affinity with digital tools and new technologies, and an interest in exploring how AI and other tools can improve the way we work. Experience with academic research, project management, research funding, or tools such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint and online grant submission systems is a plus, but not required. If you are concerned that you don’t meet all the requirements sufficiently, but the job does excite you, then be sure to respond, we would love to look at your profile. items.desc: About Turing: Turing is one of the world’s fastest-growing AI companies, accelerating the advancement and deployment of powerful AI systems. Turing helps customers in two ways: Working with the world’s leading AI labs to advance frontier model capabilities in thinking, reasoning, coding, agentic behavior, multimodality, multilinguality, STEM, and frontier knowledge; and leveraging that work to build real-world AI systems that solve mission-critical priorities for companies. Role Overview: We are looking for candidates with strong analytical and English comprehension skills. The ideal candidate should have the ability to read, summarize, and break down large content into smaller logical blocks, conduct research online, validate claims made in the content through online research, and work with the LLM (Large Language Models) to solve puzzles! Your role is critical in helping fine-tune and improve large language models (like gpt), and will make you an expert on how to leverage AI to be a better analyst. This is your chance to future-proof your career in an AI-first world! What does day-to-day look like: You would spend time answering a variety of interesting analytical questions and creating scenarios that can train the LLM models to get better. Here are a couple of examples which models might get wrong and you would have to give the correct answer and explanation to enable the models to learn. Based on a given distribution of sales by month across locations, could you analyze which location has grown the most? (Hint: what time period should we look at? should we account for sudden variability at the beginning?) In a small town, there are four distinct neighborhoods: Oak, Pine, Maple, and Elm. A postman is assigned to deliver mail and can only deliver to two neighborhoods in one day, with certain rules (e.g. Oak is always visited before Pine). If he delivers to Oak and Elm on the first day, which neighborhoods does the carrier deliver to on the second day? Note: No other prior specialized domain experience is needed. Requirements: Multilingual capabilities are mandatory (English and Norwegian). Analytical Skills: Good research and analytical skills. Feedback Skills: Ability to provide constructive feedback and detailed annotations. Creative Thinking: Creative and lateral thinking abilities. Communication: Excellent communication and collaboration skills. Independence: Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote setting. Commitment: Ability to commit to 40 hours per week for the contract duration overlapping US hours. Technical Setup: Desktop/Laptop set up with a good internet connection. Preferred Qualifications: Bachelors degree or undergraduate in Engineering, Literature, Journalism, Communications, Arts, Statistics, or a related field. We are open to candidates who do not have a Bachelor's degree but have experience in the area. Experience writing professionally (business analysts, research analyst, copywriter, journalist, technical writer, editor, translator, etc). Understanding of Excel and Google Suite. Proficiency in Data interpretation, Logical reasoning and Basic arithmetic is highly desirable. Benefits: Competitive compensation based on experience and expertise. Flexible working hours and remote work environment. Opportunity to work on cutting-edge AI projects with leading LLM companies. Potential for contract extension based on performance and project needs. Offer Details: Engagement type: Contractor assignment/freelancer (no medical/paid leave). This role will require some overlap with UTC-8:00 (2-5 hrs/day) America/Los_Angeles.

items.desc: The Institute The Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) is an international biomedical research institute of excellence, based in Barcelona, Spain, with more than 400 scientists from 44 countries. The CRG is composed of an interdisciplinary, motivated and creative scientific team which is supported both by flexible and efficient administration and by high-end and innovative technologies. In September 2026, the Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) has received the renewal of the 'HR Excellence in Research' Award from the European Commission. This is a recognition of the Institute's commitment to developing an HR Strategy for Researchers, designed to bring the practices and procedures in line with the principles of the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers (Charter and Code). Please, check out our Recruitment Policy The role We are seeking a Health Data Sharing and Governance Specialist, AI and Research to support the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) at the intersection of law, biomedical research, data governance, open science and emerging technologies. The selected candidate will contribute to the development and implementation of legal, ethical and governance frameworks for the responsible sharing and reuse of human genomic, phenotypic and other sensitive biomedical data. The role will focus on translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical policies, agreements, procedures and guidance for researchers, data access committees and research infrastructures. Key areas will include data access and secondary use of biomedical data, data-sharing agreements, consent, data-use conditions, data protection, AI governance and emerging regulatory frameworks. The candidate will work closely with multidisciplinary EGA teams, EMBL-EBI and international partners, and contribute to European-funded projects related to biomedical data sharing, federated access, FAIR data and responsible AI. About the EGA The European Genome-Phenome Archive (EGA, www.ega-archive.org) is a secure service for the permanent archiving and sharing of sensitive genetic, phenotypic, and clinical data resulting from biomedical research projects. It currently hosts more than 16 petabytes of data, including over 3,700 studies and 8,600 datasets. Jointly managed by the Centre for Genomic Regulation (www.crg.eu)) in Barcelona and the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI, www.ebi.ac.uk) in Cambridge, the EGA is an active partner in numerous international and national projects and contributes to establishing global standards in genomics and health research. It plays a central role as a core data resource for ELIXIR (www.elixir-europe.org), a driver project of the Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH,www.ga4gh.org), and a major contributor to precision medicine initiatives. The EGA team at the CRG is a diverse group of around 25 professionals, including bioinformaticians, developers, helpdesk officers, and project managers, working across disciplines to advance biomedical data sharing. Based at the Barcelona Biomedical Research Park (PRBB, www.prbb.org), and supported by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC, www.bsc.es) and Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF,www.upf.edu), the EGA provides advanced services to the international research community and continues to grow steadily in both scale and impact. Whom would we like to hire? Professional experience Must Have A degree in Law, with an advanced postgraduate degree in a relevant area such as health law, data protection, technology law, artificial intelligence governance, bioethics or biomedical data governance Research experience at the intersection of law, artificial intelligence, and data governance, including legal and ethical analysis of biomedical data sharing, AI regulation, and emerging governance frameworks Experience developing data access policies, data-sharing agreements, consent templates, and governance best practices, with a focus on translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical frameworks for health-sector and research stakeholders. Knowledge of legal and ethical issues surrounding the collection, access, sharing and secondary use of health, genomic or other sensitive research data Familiarity with the GDPR, European Health Data Space, EU AI Act and related European regulatory frameworks Ability to communicate legal and regulatory concepts effectively to audiences without a legal background Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing policies, reports, guidance documents, agreements or scholarly outputs Nice to have: A doctorate or ongoing doctoral research related to health law, AI, technology governance, open science or data governance Qualification or professional experience as a lawyer Knowledge of international approaches to health-data governance and cross-border research data sharing Experience with organisations or initiatives working on …

items.desc: About the role: About our Vacancy We are seeking to appoint suitably experienced Teaching Assistants to work in our Early Years and Primary phases. The ideal candidate should possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Experience of working with children with special needs, including those with autism, is essential. The successful candidates will join a friendly, supportive team with opportunities for further training. There is potential for this role to become permanent. We offer a comprehensive and bespoke CPD programme. throughout the year and have a good record of upskilling staff at all levels. As all children have an EHCP and are working significantly below age-related expectations, the role is more likely to suit those who are trained/experienced within Early Years , Primary or Special settings. We operate an EYFS/Primary model of teaching up to and including Year 13 with some specialist teaching in Y10-13. We are particularly keen to hear from you if you have experience of delivering tailored and personalised learning programmes for children with SEND About Us About the Trust London South East Academies Trust is a growing and ambitious Multi-Academy Trust, currently comprising mainstream, special and alternative provision academies, alongside an outreach service and a music hub. Our schools are located across Bromley, Bexley, Sussex, Lambeth and Surrey, serving a wide range of communities and educational contexts. Across the Trust, our schools share a strong commitment to raising attainment, encouraging aspiration and supporting social mobility for every pupil, throughout their educational journey and beyond. We take a holistic but personalised approach to education, recognising that children thrive when their individual strengths, needs and circumstances are properly understood and supported. This enables pupils to flourish and achieve their full potential, whatever their starting point. We believe that great schools are built by great people. As a Trust, we invest in our staff through strong professional development and leadership opportunities, clear expectations and supportive structures. We actively encourage collaboration and the sharing of best practice across schools, supported by high-quality, cost-effective central services that allow leaders and teachers to focus on what matters most: improving outcomes for pupils. London South East Academies Trust sits within the Elevare Civic Education Group, which also includes a multi-campus further and higher education college, London South East Colleges and a charitable foundation, Elevare Education Foundation. This unique structure provides meaningful progression pathways for pupils and families, as well as broad development and career opportunities for staff across the wider Group. Our teams are united by a shared belief in the power of education to change lives. By continuing to grow our Trust and welcoming new expertise and perspectives, we aim to strengthen our schools further and extend the positive impact we have on our communities. Equal Opportunities London South East Academies Trust is fully committed to being an Equal Opportunities Employer and to creating a diverse, inclusive and respectful working environment, free from discrimination and harassment. We welcome and encourage applications from all, regardless of race, nationality, ethnic origin, religion or belief, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, parental status or marital or partnership status. As a Disability Confident Committed employer, we will offer an interview to applicants who declare a disability and meet the essential criteria for the role. If you have accessibility needs or require any reasonable adjustments to support you through the application or interview process, please let us know. Please note that if a suitable applicant is identified, we may close the advert before the published closing date. If you have any specific queries about the role, please contact us at lseathr@lsec.ac.uk. As the Trust supports children and vulnerable adults, all roles are exempt from Section 4(2) of the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974. Appointments are subject to an enhanced DBS check and, where relevant, a Children’s and/or Adult’s Barred List check. Any offer of employment may be withdrawn if these checks are unsatisfactory. Self-disclosure is required as part of the recruitment process, and failure to make a full disclosure or to provide sight of a DBS certificate is likely to result in withdrawal of an offer. The Trust’s DBS policy on the recruitment of ex-offenders is available on request. All appointments are also subject to verification of the right to work in the UK, in line with Home Office requirements. Original documentation will be required prior to commencement of employment.

items.desc: About Nomad Digital Nomad Digital is the world's leading provider of passenger and fleet connectivity solutions to the railway industry. Founded in 2002, and headquartered in the UK, currently serving more than 80+ global customers - in more than 40 countries - Nomad designs, builds, deploys and manages passenger Wi-Fi and on-board passenger infotainment systems. Nomad also provides remote online condition-based monitoring and maintenance solutions for optimising fleet management, operational performance and improving fuel economy. When you join Nomad Digital, you will join a forward thinking, fast-growing, fun environment with access to some of the very latest technology in its field. You will work with experts who innovate collaboratively, creating an environment of team work and trustworthiness. Overview: Working within an agile R&D product team (developers, QA, DevOps), you will be the team’s expert in CI/CD automation, currently built on GitLab. You will take the automation code produced by the wider R&D team (today mainly Puppet modules and Ansible playbooks, and in future whatever tools best fit the job) and turn it into reliable, automated deployment pipelines, so that every planned and patch release is rolled out safely, repeatably and at scale rather than by hand. Because much of the estate is remote, resource-constrained and intermittently connected, every change must be automated, tested, controlled and reversible. You will also help the team adopt AI-assisted engineering tools in a safe, secure and auditable way. The role requires an individual with 3+ years of relevant experience and a strong sense of ownership for production quality. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Deployment automation Use and configure the team’s configuration-management and automation code (currently Puppet and Ansible) to deploy, update and maintain systems across the whole hybrid estate. Maintain customer-specific configuration and data so deployments stay consistent, parameterised and free of duplication. Turn manual or operator-run deployment and update procedures into automated, pipeline-driven workflows. Plan and carry out controlled rollouts of both planned and patch releases, using staged and rolling deployments, pre- and post-deployment health checks, automatic stop on failure, manual approval gates where needed and tested rollback to a known-working version. Ensure deployments are safe for remote, resource-constrained and intermittently connected systems. Coordinate releases across the estate so related changes ship together under one versioned release, with the deployed state recorded and reported. Work closely with the developers who build the automation code: test new versions, report defects with clear evidence, and feed back deployment requirements and improvements. Evaluate and adopt new automation, deployment and infrastructure-as-code tools as the needs of the estate and the business evolve. CI/CD pipelines and release engineering Act as the team’s subject-matter expert for CI/CD (currently GitLab CI/CD): design, build and maintain pipelines, reusable templates, runners and pipeline images. Choose the right deployment model for each part of the estate (push, pull or GitOps), with CI/CD testing and promoting releases, and orchestration tools carrying them out where appropriate. Build automated quality gates into deployment pipelines, e.g. linting, dry runs and configuration diffs, and acceptance testing on reference or virtual systems. Make greater use of virtual machines inside CI/CD pipelines (e.g. KVM / QEMU / libvirt, cloud-init, Packer) to create disposable test environments, run automated tasks and tests against them, and tear them down automatically. Automate release workflows end to end: versioning and tagging, release notes generated from the issue tracker, documentation publishing and promotion of changes between environments. Keep pipelines secure: protected and masked secrets and variables, protected branches and tags, least-privilege runner and token access, and secret and dependency scanning. Measure and improve pipeline speed, reliability and the developer experience for the wider team. AI-assisted engineering Use AI coding assistants productively to write, review, test and document pipelines, deployment configuration and scripts. Apply and help define safe-use practices: use only company-approved tools; never share secrets, credentials or customer data with AI tools; treat AI output as untrusted until reviewed and tested; keep human approval on every change that reaches production. Ensure AI-generated changes go through the same review, CI quality gates and change control as any other change, with clear traceability. Share good practice with the team and help evaluate new AI tooling against our security and compliance requirements. items.desc: The opportunity Bring research discipline to practical technology validation, so that Hitachi Energy can distinguish credible AI advances from hype before it invests. As AI Research Engineer in the Technology Validation team, part of Hitachi Energy's Data, Analytics & Artificial Intelligence (DAAI) organization, you interpret emerging AI research, methods, models and evaluation approaches, turn the most relevant developments into practical validation questions and answer them through prototypes, benchmarks and comparisons. Your evidence informs architecture, platform and delivery teams. The team builds to learn and demonstrate, not to operate production systems. How You Will Make An Impact Monitor and interpret AI research, publications, benchmarks and model documentation. Identify developments that merit practical testing. Translate research insight into concrete validation questions and fair experimental designs, with explicit baselines, success criteria and the conditions that would invalidate the hypothesis, together with the AI Experimentation Engineer and AI Opportunity Lead. Run research-led prototypes, benchmarks and comparisons across LLMs, RAG, agentic AI, fine-tuning and responsible-AI evaluation. Interpret results with methodological rigor and state the limitations clearly. Recommend a proportionate next step: stop, keep watching, test further or hand over to the team that should build it. Exchange methods and learnings with Hitachi Group colleagues, DAAI peers, vendors and external research communities. Preserve reusable methods, benchmarks and test assets so that work is not repeated. Your background A genuine passion for AI: you try new tools and models on your own initiative and can show a recent example of something you built or tried. 3+ years of experience in applied AI research, AI engineering or ML research, in a company, consultancy or research institution. Strong programming skills (Python preferred) with hands-on AI/ML experimentation, benchmarking and evaluation. You know LLMs, generative AI, fine-tuning, RAG, agentic AI and responsible-AI evaluation. Familiarity with cloud AI platforms (Azure preferred, GCP or AWS) is an advantage. Ability to read research and technical claims critically and translate them into practical, enterprise-relevant experiments. Clear communication of research-level topics and their limitations. You have experience collaborating across research, engineering and business communities. Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience and fluent English. An MSc or PhD in AI, machine learning or computer science is an advantage when combined with practical work. items.desc: AI macht uns schneller. Das Denken nimmt sie uns nicht ab. Was AI produziert, überprüfen wir. Für alles, was rausgeht, stehen wir gerade. Beim Ausprobieren sind wir schnell, beim Ausliefern gründlich. Du liest ein Paper und willst wissen, ob die Idee hält. Also klonst du das Repo. Läuft es nicht, folgst du dem Stacktrace in den Quellcode. Und widersprechen die Daten deiner Hypothese, stutzt du kurz und freust dich: Jetzt wird es interessant. Ein schönes Ergebnis macht dich dagegen erst mal misstrauisch. Zufall? Bug? Oder hält es? Bei smartclip arbeitest du mit Messdaten von Dutzenden Millionen Geräten, eigener GPU-Infrastruktur und Sidekicks, unserer AI-Initiative für Wissensfragen und echte Workflows. Du verantwortest deine Fragestellung vom ersten Experiment bis zum belastbaren Prototyp. Den baut Engineering mit dir zum Produkt aus. Unser Stack basiert auf Linux, Open Source und freier Software. Du kannst nachvollziehen, was unter der Haube passiert. Deine Mission Eine Stelle, zwei Schwerpunkte. Ob du einen vertiefst oder beide, entscheiden dein Können und deine Vorlieben. AI gehört immer dazu. 1. Knowledge Agents & Agentic Retrieval Wie beantwortet ein Agent eine Frage, deren Antwort über Tausende Dokumente verteilt ist? Wie erkennt er Widersprüche zwischen Entwürfen und finalen Fassungen? Und wie belegt er seine Antworten zuverlässig? Entwickle Agenten, die Informationen über große Dokumentbestände hinweg erschließen. Untersuche, wie sich Vollständigkeit, Widersprüche und die Qualität von Quellen bewerten lassen. Sorge dafür, dass Antworten nachvollziehbar bleiben und Unsicherheiten sichtbar werden. 2. Machine Learning at Scale Wir messen das Werbegeschehen bei mehr als 150 TV-Sendern in Europa. Unser Ziel: lineares Fernsehen so planbar und messbar machen wie digitale Werbung. Entwickle Prognosemodelle für die Leistung von Werbeblöcken. Bewerte Unsicherheiten, Messfehler und die Aussagekraft deiner Modelle. Verarbeite große Datenmengen mit Spark auf unserem Cluster und untersuche, wo Datenqualität oder Verarbeitung die Ergebnisse beeinflussen. In beiden Bereichen machst du aus einer guten Frage etwas, das läuft: Experimentiere und evaluiere: Formuliere Hypothesen, entwirf aussagekräftige Tests und lerne aus Ergebnissen, auch wenn diese nicht deine Erwartungen erfüllen. Übernimm Verantwortung: Entwickle deinen Ansatz eigenständig bis zum belastbaren Prototyp. Hol dir einen zweiten Blick oder denk mit deinem Team am Whiteboard weiter. Arbeite mit Engineering: Begleite die Überführung deines Prototyps in ein Produkt und bringe dein Wissen über Problem und Lösung ein. Unterstütze andere Teams: Bewerte Datenfragen, zeige sinnvolle Einsatzmöglichkeiten von AI auf und liefere je nach Bedarf eine fundierte Empfehlung oder einen Prototyp. Deine Skills Fundierte technische Grundlagen: Bring Kenntnisse in Informatik, Softwareentwicklung oder Data Science mit – erworben durch Studium, Promotion oder praktische Erfahrung. Du kannst deine Methodenwahl begründen und Ergebnisse kritisch bewerten. Verständnis für AI: Du musst keine Modelle in PyTorch trainieren. Erkläre aber beispielsweise den Unterschied zwischen Prefill und Decode und dessen Auswirkungen auf Latenz und Kosten. Eigenständiges AI-native Development: Nutze Coding-Agenten, um schneller zu entwickeln. Validiere den generierten Code, teste die Ergebnisse und verstehe, wie deine Anwendung und ihre Komponenten funktionieren. Strukturiertes Experimentieren: Formuliere klare Specs, definiere eine Definition of Done und prüfe mit passenden Tests und Evaluationen, ob deine Umsetzung das richtige Problem löst. Offene Zusammenarbeit: Teile Wissen, diskutiere technische Entscheidungen und gib respektvolles, direktes Feedback. Ein Plus, kein Muss: Erfahrung mit NLP/Computerlinguistik, Agentic Retrieval oder der Entwicklung von LLM-Agenten. Unser Stack Knowledge Agents: Python (Pydantic AI), TypeScript, vLLM/SGLang Daten und Pipelines: Spark, Trino, StarRocks, Postgres und Prefect Infrastruktur und Observability: OpenTelemetry, Docker/Kubernetes Kennst du eher Ray, LangChain, Airflow, passt das genauso: Die Konzepte zählen, nicht die Logos. Was dich bei uns erwartet Remote Work mit gezielten Treffen: Wir arbeiten überwiegend remote und kommen gelegentlich für Workshops, Team-Sessions und den gemeinsamen Austausch in unserem Tech-Office in Berlin zusammen. Außerdem veranstalten wir über das Jahr verteilt Team-Events, darunter unser jährliches Company Offsite, das jedes Jahr an einer anderen Location in Deutschland stattfindet. Die Bereitschaft, für diese Treffen anzureisen und daran teilzunehmen, gehört zur Rolle. Eigenverantwortung statt Mikromanagement: Übernimm Verantwortung für deine Themen und bringe sie selbstständig voran. Build > Talk: Früh ausprobieren, früh danebenliegen, früh dazulernen. Hohe Ansprüche, wenig Ego: Wir geben direktes Feedback und arbeiten offen und respektvoll zusammen. Weiterentwicklung: Nutze Hackathons, Konferenzen und …

items.title: Researcher in AI-Assisted and Computational Social Science Research
items.card: Political science at the Swedish Defence University is unique in its special focus on security and crisis management. The subject is at the same time theoretically broad, and draws on a wide range of related fields, such as international relations, political communication, public administration, and political theory as well as drawing inspiration from other research within and outside of political science.
items.desc: Political science at the Swedish Defence University is unique in its special focus on security and crisis management. The subject is at the same time theoretically broad, and draws on a wide range of related fields, such as international relations, political communication, public administration, and political theory as well as drawing inspiration from other research within and outside of political science. Description The position is focused on AI-assisted social science research, computational social science and quantitative methods. The research may, for example, address information influence, political and strategic communication, media and narratives. A central part of the position is to develop and evaluate scientifically rigorous ways of using large language models (LLMs) and other AI-based methods in social science research. The researcher will work in a team that conducts commissioned research on information influence and disinformation. Duties The researcher is expected to plan and conduct both independent and collaborative research and to contribute to scientific publications and conference presentations. The researcher will work in a research team conducting commissioned research on information influence and disinformation. A central part of the position is also to strengthen the research group’s competence in AI-assisted research, computational social science and quantitative methods. The researcher is therefore expected to actively train and supervise other researchers in the group and to contribute to building long-term methodological capacity. Duties Include, Among Other Things plan and conduct independent and collaborative research using AI-based, computational and quantitative methods; develop and evaluate methods involving LLMs, quantitative text analysis, machine learning and NLP; explore the use of local and open-source language models with research data, with particular attention to validation and reproducibility; strengthen the research group’s methodological competence through workshops, individual guidance, and support in programming and analysis; contribute to scientific publications, conference presentations and research funding applications. Qualifications Applicants must hold a doctoral degree, or an equivalent international degree. The Following Qualifications Are Also Required experience of quantitative and/or computational social science methods, including computational text and/or image analysis and processing of social media/platform data, as well as the ability to use Python and/or R for analysis and research experience of machine learning, NLP or quantitative text analysis, with particular emphasis on LLM-based methods a good understanding of research design, validation and reproducible research; excellent ability to communicate in English. Experience of local or open-source language models, RAG, fine-tuning, multilingual NLP or advanced quantitative methods is considered an advantage. Experience of research in political science, political psychology, media studies, computational social science, or another relevant social science field is considered an advantage. Great importance will be attached to the ability to communicate advanced methodological issues clearly and pedagogically, and to collaborate effectively with researchers with varying methodological backgrounds. Experience of supervision, training or methodological support is considered an advantage Knowledge of Swedish or another Scandinavian language is considered an advantage. Great importance will be attached to personal suitability. We are looking for a researcher who is independent, proactive and communicative and who has a strong ability to collaborate with researchers from different methodological backgrounds. Application The Application Must Include a cover letter explaining why you are qualified for the position; a CV including a list of scientific publications or a project portfolio copies of official academic degree certificates. Applications must be submitted via the Swedish Defence University’s recruitment system by clicking on the ‘Apply’ link on the job advertisement page. The recruitment system contains a number of screening questions to be answered. Here you should enter your experience and qualifications and upload any supporting documents you wish to submit in support of your application. The complete application must be received by the Swedish Defence University no later than midnight on the closing date, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time). Terms om Employment The position is a full-time fixed-term appointment for 12 months. Location: Stockholm. Employment at the Swedish Defence University may be subject to security screening in accordance with the Swedish Protective Security Act (2018:585). Starting date January 1, 2027, or by agreement. The Swedish Defence University applies individual salary setting You are welcome to submit your application until October 18th!
