items.desc: De flesta organisationer har redan startat sina AI-piloter. Frågan är inte längre om de ska investera, utan var, och hur de ser till att värdet faktiskt realiseras. Det är där vi arbetar. Om Influence Influence är ett managementkonsultbolag som kombinerar strategi med förmågan att genomföra den. Vi mäter kvaliteten på en strategi i vad som händer sedan. Vi arbetar nära våra kunder, med genuin omtanke och modet att säga det som behöver sägas, så att varje uppdrag lämnar efter sig en skarpare organisation och inte ett beroende av oss. Vi är en del av Newground, en allians av specialistbolag under ett gemensamt tak. Det ger oss djup inom AI, data och teknik när vi behöver det, och kollektiv intelligens som grund för allt vi gör. Om rollen Vi är varken ett utbildningsteam för AI eller en systemintegratör. Vi hjälper ledningsgrupper att fatta bättre beslut: var de ska satsa, vad de ska låta bli, hur de går från experiment till skala och hur strategi, organisation och arbetssätt måste förändras för att värdet ska bli verkligt. Du arbetar direkt med kundernas seniora beslutsfattare. Du prioriterar möjligheter, bedömer om organisationen faktiskt kan realisera dem, formar transformationsroadmaps, designar operating models och styrning, och leder kunder från enskilda initiativ till effekt i hela verksamheten. Du är bryggan mellan affärsledning och tekniska specialister. Du förstår AI och teknik tillräckligt väl för att ifrågasätta antaganden, leverantörslöften och orealistiska use cases, men din styrka ligger i affärsmässigt omdöme och förändring. Du är rösten i rummet som utmanar önsketänkande, och du gör det på ett sätt som bygger förtroende. Du bygger också affär. Att utveckla kundrelationer, forma nya uppdrag och driva vårt erbjudande inom Tech-Driven Reinvention framåt är en central del av rollen. Vem du är 5–10 års erfarenhet från management consulting eller en strategisk transformationsroll Du förstår AI, data och teknik ur ett affärsperspektiv och är trygg i att utmana tekniska antaganden utan att själv äga leveransen Du har drivit verklig förändring, inte bara strategi på papper: nya operating models, arbetssätt, governance eller förmågebyggande Du är van vid komplexa organisationer och har trovärdighet hos ledningsgrupper Du kan skilja det som är strategiskt attraktivt från det en organisation faktiskt kan genomföra Du balanserar tydlig riktning uppifrån med experimenterande och ägarskap nära verksamheten Du skapar samsyn mellan affär och teknik, och du har kommersiellt driv Du är flytande i svenska och engelska Erfarenhet av AI- eller data governance, portföljstyrning, digital- eller mjukvarustrategi eller storskalig transformation är meriterande. Du arbetar med några av de mest avgörande frågorna ledningsgrupper står inför just nu, med stora och medelstora bolag inom retail, industri och tjänstesektorn, och med Newgrounds specialister vid din sida. Och du gör det i en kultur som folk stannar för. Vi lever efter det vi säger: great minds, genuine hearts, sustainable results. Vi går igenom ansökningar löpande. Välkommen med din. Influence. For a wiser tomorrow.

items.card: About the Role We’re looking for a Talent Acquisition Partner to join our growing team in Stockholm and help us build the engineering, product and design teams behind Tandem. items.desc: Build something monumental for Healthcare! At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care. We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you! About the Role We’re looking for a Talent Acquisition Partner to join our growing team in Stockholm and help us build the engineering, product and design teams behind Tandem. You’ll be at the heart of our mission - connecting brilliant people with meaningful work that’s reshaping how healthcare works. This role is all about people and impact. You’ll partner closely with our CTO and Engineering, Product and Design leaders to attract and hire exceptional builders - from software, security, data and AI engineers to product managers and designers. You’ll craft creative sourcing strategies, champion a high-touch hiring experience, and act as a true partner to the business as we scale our product and technology organisation. This is a demanding role with real substance. Our hiring bar is very high, the talent we go after is some of the most sought-after in Europe, and you’ll be trusted with real ownership from day one. You don’t need a decade in recruitment to thrive here - what matters most is your drive, how fast you learn and how much you want to push yourself. We’re growing fast - new products, new teams, new opportunities to make an impact. That means you’ll play a key role in building the foundations of how we hire tech talent at scale while keeping the heart of Tandem’s culture alive. If you love connecting people to purpose, thrive in high-growth, fast-paced environments, and want to help shape the team that’s transforming healthcare across Europe - this role is for you. What You Will Do Partner with Tech, Product and Design leaders to understand their needs, define what great looks like, and bring the right people into every conversation. Own end-to-end hiring across tech, product and design roles - from first outreach to signed offer. Take real ownership of your searches: run them yourself, make the judgement calls, and be accountable for outcomes, not just activity. Craft and experiment with creative sourcing strategies to reach world-class engineers, product people and designers beyond the obvious channels, including passive and highly sought-after talent. Build a thoughtful, inclusive, and seamless candidate experience from first touch to offer, including technical interviews, case work and on-site visits. Help shape and scale our recruitment processes as Tandem grows - balancing speed with quality, and keeping the bar very high, and holding an uncompromising bar, even when that means saying no to a good candidate while we wait for a great one. Use data to keep our funnels healthy, share market insights with hiring managers, and continuously improve how we hire. Strengthen our employer brand among technical talent by telling authentic stories about our people, our product and our mission. Be a culture carrier: bring energy, curiosity, and passion into every interaction. What You Bring Proven experience as a Talent Partner or Technical Recruiter, ideally in a high-growth, international environment. Years matter less than results: we care about what you’ve achieved, how much responsibility you’ve already taken on and how quickly you’ve grown. A track record of hiring engineers, product managers and/or designers, including senior and specialist profiles. An appetite for hard problems and high standards: you hold yourself to a bar most people find uncomfortable, and you actively seek out more responsibility. Deep curiosity and creativity when it comes to sourcing - you find the people others overlook, and you know how to start a conversation that gets a reply. Enough technical fluency to understand what different engineering, product and design roles actually involve and to hold credible conversations with candidates and hiring managers. You’re excited by the plethora of Talent Acquisition enablement tools and embrace AI-driven tech and sourcing innovation to work smarter and uncover hidden talent. Strong stakeholder management skills - you build trust fast, push back when needed and communicate with clarity. A passion for creating a great candidate experience and championing diversity in every process. Comfort with ambiguity and change - you thrive where things are moving fast and are energised by high pace. Bonus points Experience hiring for Stockholm’s tech/AI scene or competitive talent markets Experience building or improving hiring processes in a scale-up Location We believe the best ideas happen when we’re together. Your role As a Systems Engineer within Air Traffic Management, you will build and improve reliable test and proof-of-concept environments for advanced products used by airports and air navigation service providers around the world. You will be working closely with developers, system engineers and testers and set up, configure and maintain test and concept environments. Our product portfolio primarily consists of software solutions developed in-house, complemented by proprietary hardware and selected commercial off-the-shelf components. The breadth of the role offers a unique opportunity to work across multiple disciplines and gain a deep understanding of complex systems. items.desc: Do you want to build the data-driven engine taking Avanza into Denmark? At Avanza, we are driven by making savings cheaper, better, and simpler. To succeed, we need data that is not only accessible, but accurate, smart, and actionable. We are currently operating as an internal startup at Avanza, building a brand-new platform to expand our business into Denmark. We combine startup speed with corporate strength, taking an AI-first approach to everything we do. We are now looking for a Data Engineer who is ready to step outside their comfort zone, interface seamlessly with software engineering teams, and help build the foundation for our next big journey. Working at Avanza As a Data Engineer in our expansion team, you will help transform raw data into business value through robust pipelines and sustainable data models. We work according to data mesh principles, meaning you will both provide and consume data in a decentralised landscape. Our tech stack rests on BigQuery, Kafka for real-time streaming, and dbt for transformation logic. You will become part of an autonomous team with a strong mandate to shape both architecture and ways of working. We value the craft of data engineering and apply core software development principles such as traceability and scalability—often through pair programming and close cross-functional collaboration. Who You Are You are a curious and proactive team player who loves solving complex problems together with others. You turn ideas into action and see learning from mistakes as a natural part of growth. You actively contribute to maintaining a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment within the team, where asking for help is just as natural as offering it. We Believe You Have (Note: You don't need to check every single box to apply!) Solid experience with SQL, data modeling, and modern data tools such as BigQuery and dbt. Experience with streaming data and message queues (e.g., Kafka). Strong background in software engineering (e.g., Java) and API design in distributed environments—you have your primary focus in data, but can code application logic when needed. An interest in systems monitoring, observability, and analytics support. A humble, solution-oriented mindset where you prioritise team success and knowledge sharing. Professional working proficiency in English, Swedish is a bonus but not a must. Bonus Points If You Have Previous experience working with both user behavior data (e.g., clickstream, event tracking, product analytics) and core platform/financial data, with a track record of combining them to build holistic insights. Experience working with Python for advanced data automation or AI/ML integrations. A curiosity and passion for taking an AI-first approach to problem-solving and software/data development. Prior experience working in a regulated environment such as banking or fintech . What Success Looks Like at Avanza & in this Role We have many customers and they love the product! Success means building reliable, high-impact data pipelines that power our Danish expansion, collaborating seamlessly across tech domains, and fostering an environment where innovation and knowledge-sharing thrive. Ready to Build the Future of Banking with Us? We apply a hybrid workplace model and love seeing each other at our renovated office at Regeringsgatan 103 about 2–3 days a week. If you're excited to help bring Avanza to Denmark with an AI-first mindset, we’d love to hear from you! We review applications continuously, so feel free to apply today. Ready to get started? items.desc: Klarna, briefly At Klarna, we’re building an everyday finance network, helping over 120 million consumers across 26 countries save time and money, and worry less about their finances. Working here means taking on problems most companies never get to solve, and being hands-on enough that the interesting part of the work lands with you, not someone else — you’ll build with AI, not watch it happen. This is the stretch zone. Come find out what you’re capable of. About the role Klarna Bank AB is authorised in Sweden and operates in other EU markets through branches. That means Klarna answers to Finansinspektionen (FI), our home regulator, and to the host regulators in each of those markets, and what we tell one of them has to match what we tell the others. You’ll join the Regulatory Interactions team in Stockholm, work alongside a senior colleague who leads these supervisor relationships, and take on part of that portfolio. You’ll report to the Global Lead, Regulatory Interactions. The position also has a build side: you’ll design tools with AI and upgrade the processes the team already runs. Within your first year, those tools and processes should be in everyday use across the team, and you should be the person maintaining them. The brief moves with the team’s priorities rather than following a fixed task list. What you’ll do You’ll handle regulator correspondence for your part of the portfolio, answering each request accurately and on time. You’ll log every interaction, so Klarna holds a complete record of what we have said and when. You’ll prepare material for submissions and supervisory meetings, in Swedish where the matter calls for it. You’ll keep the team’s registers current: the rules that apply to us, the positions we have taken with regulators, and the periodic reports we owe, to whom and by when. You’ll design new tools with AI and upgrade existing processes, for example a workflow that logs and summarises inbound correspondence, or a check that compares a draft response with the positions we have already taken with that regulator. You’ll build every tool within Klarna’s data and security controls from the start, because much of the material is confidential and some of it is legally privileged. You’ll find out what the colleagues using your tools need, check that what you deliver works for them, and keep it running after launch. You’ll work with Compliance, Risk, Legal, the market teams in the countries you cover, and the owners of our regulatory reporting data in Financial and Regulatory Reporting and Analytics. You’ll also coordinate with the colleagues covering the FCA in the UK and BaFin in Germany. Who you are You’ve worked in or close to financial services regulation, for example in a regulatory, compliance, legal or analyst position at a bank, payments firm or other regulated institution, at a supervisory authority, or at a consultancy or law firm advising them. You understand how regulated firms work with their supervisors, from answering information requests to meeting reporting deadlines and keeping positions consistent across authorities, and you pick up new EU regulation quickly enough to apply it to a live request. You’ve built something with AI or code that other people use, such as an automation, an internal tool, a tracker or a dashboard, and you can explain how it works and where it is likely to break. You work comfortably with data and spreadsheets, and you structure information so others can find and use it. You’re fluent in Swedish and English, written and spoken: English for formal correspondence with regulators across the EU, and Swedish for correspondence with FI and work with Swedish colleagues. You write precisely in both languages, keep track of detail across many open items without missing a deadline, and handle confidential material with discretion. You notice when a process could work better and fix it rather than work around it, you raise problems early, and you’re at ease working with senior people. Bonus points for A degree in law, economics, finance, business, data or a related field. A Swedish law degree (juristexamen) is welcome but not required. Experience building with LLM APIs or agent workflows, or designing prompts and tests for AI used on confidential material, using tools such as Claude, Cursor or Google Apps Script. A recognised compliance or regulatory qualification, for example from the International Compliance Association. Experience rolling out a tool you built and training colleagues to use it. Further EU languages, since several of the regulators you will cover correspond in their own language. German is especially useful given the team’s BaFin coverage. Things you should know before applying This position is based in Stockholm. We are open to someone earlier in their career who shows clear ability, as well as someone who already runs their own workstream with limited supervision. No certifications are required. Working together: we value co-located …

items.desc: At Capgemini Engineering, the world leader in engineering services, we bring together a global team of engineers, scientists, and architects to help the world’s most innovative companies unleash their potential. From autonomous cars to life-saving robots, our digital and software technology experts think outside the box as they provide unique R&D and engineering services across all industries. Join us for a career full of opportunities. Where you can make a difference. Where no two days are the same. YOUR ROLE We are seeking an experienced Mechanical Design Engineer to support the design, development, and implementation of custom tooling and equipment for aseptic fill & finish operations within an isolator environment. The role focuses on developing solutions that maintain First Air protection, support Annex 1 compliance, and improve operator safety, ergonomics, and process robustness. The successful candidate will work closely with Process Engineering, Manufacturing, Automation, Validation, Quality, and external equipment suppliers. Your Responsibilities Design and develop custom isolator tools, fixtures, change parts, and operator aids for aseptic fill & finish operations. Ensure designs comply with Annex 1 principles and maintain protection of critical zones and First Air. Create and review 3D CAD models, assemblies, drawings, and technical documentation. Perform design reviews, risk assessments, and feasibility studies. Evaluate operator interventions and develop engineering controls to minimize contamination risks. Support FAT, SAT, commissioning, and implementation activities. Collaborate with equipment suppliers and engineering partners during development and procurement phases. Apply hygienic design principles and GMP requirements throughout the design lifecycle. Support continuous improvement initiatives for isolator operations and aseptic processes. YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline. Several years of experience in machine design, special-purpose machinery, pharmaceutical equipment, or aseptic manufacturing environments. Strong CAD skills (SolidWorks or equivalent). Experience creating manufacturing drawings and technical documentation. Understanding of mechanical design, materials, tolerances, and fabrication methods. Ability to work independently in multidisciplinary project teams. Preferred Qualifications Experience with pharmaceutical fill & finish equipment. Knowledge of isolator technology and aseptic processing. Understanding of EU GMP Annex 1 requirements. Experience with airflow concepts, contamination control, and First Air protection. Experience supporting qualification and validation activities in GMP environments. Familiarity with ergonomic design and human-machine interactions within isolators. Key Competencies Strong engineering judgement Problem-solving mindset Risk-based decision making Excellent communication skills Ability to challenge designs from a contamination control perspective Hands-on approach during testing and implementation WHAT YOU’LL LOVE ABOUT WORKING HERE? At our engineering academy, you’ll have access to over 60,000 hours of world-class training - designed to fuel your growth from day one. Whether you're diving into Generative AI, data science, or sustainability, our digital campus supports your learning journey every step of the way; Experience the benefits of hybrid working, offering flexibility and ensuring work-life balance; Harness the strength of diverse teams, fostering innovation and inclusive collaboration; We offer additional benefits such as 5 weeks of vacation, Employee referral bonus, Company shares program and Annual contribution to a fitness subscription. Capgemini is a global business and technology transformation partner, helping organizations to accelerate their dual transition to a digital and sustainable world, while creating tangible impact for enterprises and society. It is a responsible and diverse group of 340,000 team members in more than 50 countries. With its strong over 55-year heritage, Capgemini is trusted by its clients to unlock the value of technology to address the entire breadth of their business needs. It delivers end-to-end services and solutions leveraging strengths from strategy and design to engineering, all fueled by its market leading capabilities in AI, generative AI, cloud and data, combined with its deep industry expertise and partner ecosystem.

The role supports Strategy development, undertaking research and analysis on relevant global health, financing and development issues and synthesizing evidence and stakeholder perspectives to inform strategic choices and decision making. It also supports analysis and delivery across strategy or policy priorities, working with relevant teams to develop evidence, assess options and implications, and support the development, review and evolution of organizational positions and policies. Support development of succinct and strategic materials to guide stakeholder input and decision-making on topics relevant to strategy development and ongoing updates in organizational strategic direction. Support relevant teams across the Secretariat to prepare for new Strategy operationalization and changes in organizational strategic direction including but not limited to Global Fund funding model ,the allocation methodology, KPIs, the grant lifecycle and Secretariat operations. Demonstrated understanding of topics and innovations at the forefront of international development, particularly HIV, TB, malaria, resilient and sustainable systems for health and other relevant sectors. Experience distilling and synthesizing the key strategic points of research, analysis, written input and extended discussions. Experience drafting concise reports capturing the key salient points of extensive discussions or meetings. Experience developing high-quality presentations to effectively communicate strategic messages based on analysis or stakeholder input. Experience with effective stakeholder engagement in complex organizational processes. Experience with responsible use of AI tools in research and evidence synthesis. Desirable: Over 2 years relevant professional experience within an international management consultancy, public health or development organization, major multilateral or bilateral organization, not-for-profit or related setting. Es besteht auch die Möglichkeit, eine Dissertation zu verfassen. Die Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter am ILE-HSG forschen an der Schnittstelle von Recht und Wirtschaft. Wir bieten Ihnen Eine abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit in einem jungen, dynamischen und interdisziplinär ausgerichteten Forschungsinstitut und in einem Team, das Ihre Arbeit aktiv begleitet. Sie wirken an spannenden Projekten mit, haben Freiraum für eigene Forschung und die Aussicht auf eigene Publikationen. Dann sind Sie bei uns genau richtig. Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung. Ladislava Metzger Administrative Institutsleitung Ich würde mich sehr freuen, Sie bald in unserem Team begrüssen zu dürfen. Bei Fragen stehe ich gerne zur Verfügung. items.desc: The Newcastle Genetics Laboratory forms part of the North East and Yorkshire Genomic Laboratory Hub, (NE&Y GLH) alongside our partners in Leeds and Sheffield. There are ongoing Clinical Scientist vacancies to join our friendly laboratory teams, (see https://ney-genomics.org.uk/for-professionals/careers2/ ) and applications are invited for a band 7 Clinical Scientist post in the Newcastle Genetics Laboratory. This is an exciting time to work in genomics, and an opportunity to be at the forefront of improving outcomes for patients. Candidates should ideally be either State Registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) or should achieve State Registration within the first year. State Registration will be required for full assimilation onto Band 7 (successful candidates within one year of HCPC registration would be appointed at 75% of Band 7 until registration was achieved). All applicants should have direct experience of the work of a diagnostic genetics service. Interview Date Monday 23 November 2023 37 Hours 30 Minutes/Week You will be redirected to Trac to apply for the vacancy. Please expand the job details section and read all of the information before applying for the vacancy NO AGENCIES PLEASE We provide testing for a wide variety of inherited and acquired conditions for a local population of over three million people, as well as services provided for the North East and Yorkshire Genomic Laboratory Hub. In addition we provide specialised services to patients throughout the UK and internationally. The Newcastle Genetics laboratory is housed in purpose built accommodation at the Institute of Genetic Medicine near to Newcastle city centre, and has a close association with the high profile academic groups working in the Institute of Genetic Medicine research laboratories. The successful candidate will be a motivated and reliable individual and will join a team of around 100 Scientific and Technical staff in the Genetics laboratories in Newcastle. They will be required to deliver coordination of testing for a range of genetic conditions, in addition to preparing reports and liaising closely with clinical colleagues and Genetic Technologist staff. A broad knowledge of diagnostic genetics and good communication, team working and supervisory skills are essential. This is a new post, and a major component of the role will be in supporting the coordination and delivery of testing in acquired cancer. As a flexible working friendly organisation, we want to be sure that you can work in a way that is best for us and for our patients, and for you. Speak to us about how we might be able to accommodate a flexible working arrangement. If it works for the service, we will do our best to make it work for you. With around 2 million contacts with patients every year, we deliver care from: Royal Victoria Infirmary (RVI) Freeman Hospital Newcastle Dental Hospital Cramlington Manor Walks Urgent treatment centres Newcastle Fertility Centre Northern Centre for Cancer Care, North Cumbria Northern Genetics Service These include a range of flagship services which deliver cutting-edge care (supported by state-of-the-art diagnostic services in both radiology and pathology) and are a catalyst for innovation to support pioneering clinical practice in the NHS. We also have offices at Regent Point in Gosforth and community sites. Please see attached information on what Staff Benefits we have to offer at our Trust under ‘Documents to download’ or ‘Supporting documents’. For further information on Careers at The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust please visit our website: Newcastle Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust Analysis, interpretation and reporting of genetic tests for a broad range of inherited disorders and acquired cancers guided by clearly defined policies and procedures. Service development in own area. Limited responsibility for an additional component of the genetics service. Providing specialist advice to clinicians on specific genetic tests. Supervision of technical, junior and trainee staff in section. Practical and theoretical training of scientific & technical staff.

items.desc: The School of Chemistry at the University of St Andrews is seeking an experienced Scientific Officer with expertise in small molecule crystallography to join its single-crystal diffraction facility. Working closely with Dr David Cordes (X-ray Crystallographer) the postholder will use advanced diffraction instrumentation to tackle challenging structural problems and help deliver high-quality structural solutions across a diverse range of research projects. You will work directly with researchers across the School, providing specialist expertise and helping them make the most of the facility’s capabilities. In addition, the postholder will become familiar with the School’s powder X-ray diffraction facilities, providing essential support for their effective operation. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced crystallographer who enjoys scientific problem-solving, advanced instrumentation and collaborative research, and who would like to play a key role in supporting an important resource for the School’s research activities. We are looking for a collaborative scientist who will contribute to the School’s research environment and share our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Dr David Cordes at dbc21@st-andrews.ac.uk, or Professor Sharon Ashbrook, Head of the School of Chemistry, at chem-hos@st-andrews.ac.uk. St Andrews offers more than just a place to work—it is a place to belong. We value collegiality, inclusion, and wellbeing, and we are committed to creating a workplace where staff can thrive and perform at their best. In addition to the salary on offer for this position, there are a wide range of benefits for staff working at the University of St Andrews. We are committed to creating a fair, inclusive and supportive workplace, reflected in our participation in national diversity charters and awards, including Athena Swan, Carer Positive and the Race Equality Charter. We particularly welcome applications from people from Black, Asian, minority ethnic and minority religions The University encourages all interested candidates to apply, and all applications received are assessed against the essential and desirable criteria listed in the further particulars. The successful candidate will have to demonstrate their right to work in the UK prior to commencing employment and where required, the University can support with visa sponsorship. items.desc: Department Department of Public Health, Environments & Society Salary £40,784 to £46,643 per annum pro rata inclusive Closing Date Friday 30 October 2026 Reference PHP-PHES-2026-16 The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice. We seek a quantitative researcher with experience in policy evaluation, statistical analysis, healthcare data, and information governance. The candidate will join the NIHR-funded CoSine project, which evaluates health outcomes associated with energy-efficiency upgrades for low-income households in London (UK) using linked housing and healthcare data. The role offers experience in analysing large-scale administrative datasets while engaging with climate resilience and energy poverty research questions. The team develops best practices when setting up a new platform and the candidate will have responsibilities for authoring a technical handbook and organising an event for user feedback. The candidate will also be involved with writing research reports, evidence synthesis, knowledge mobilization as well as other reasonable duties in relation to teaching and administration. You should hold a relevant first degree and, ideally, Masters in the field of epidemiology or related quantitative field with grounding in statistics or data science. You should have relevant experience in policy impact evaluation and public health, relevant analytical skills in statistical programming, e.g. Stata or R and evidence of good organisational skills, including effective time management is essential. Further particulars are included in the. The post is full-time 35 hours per week, 1 FTE and fixed-term until 31 May 2028. The post is funded by the NIHR and is available from 01 November 2026. The salary will be on the LSHTM salary scale, Grade 5 in the range £40,784 - £46,643 per annum (inclusive of London Weighting). The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part-time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in London. Applications should be made on-line . Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet each of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable. Please note that if you are shortlisted and are unable to attend on the interview date it may not be possible to offer you an alternative date. The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine is committed to being an equal opportunities employer. We believe that when people feel respected and included, they can be more creative, successful, and happier at work. While we have more work to do, we are committed to building an inclusive workplace, a community that everyone feels a part of, which is safe, respectful, supportive and enables all to reach their full potential.

items.desc: Job Summary We are seeking a dynamic and detail-oriented QA Analyst to join our innovative technology team. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the quality and functionality of software applications through rigorous testing, automation, and analysis. Your proactive approach will help deliver seamless user experiences, optimize system performance, and uphold the highest standards of software quality assurance. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work with cutting-edge tools and methodologies in a fast-paced environment dedicated to continuous improvement and excellence. Responsibilities Develop, execute, and maintain comprehensive test cases and test plans based on detailed requirements gathering and analysis. Design and implement automated testing frameworks using tools such as Selenium, TestNG, Cucumber, and Jenkins to streamline testing processes. Perform various types of testing including functional, system, regression, load, performance, user acceptance testing (UAT), and API testing to validate software quality across platforms like Android, iOS, web, and desktop. Conduct root cause analysis to identify issues related to software bugs, system failures, or performance bottlenecks; collaborate with development teams for effective troubleshooting. Integrate testing procedures within the SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle) using DevOps practices and tools like GitHub, GitLab, TFS, Jenkins, Maven, Ant, and Waterfall methodologies. Support release management activities by verifying software builds and coordinating deployment processes across environments such as AWS or Azure. Collaborate with business analysts and developers to understand requirements thoroughly and ensure test coverage aligns with project goals. Experience Proven experience in software testing with a strong understanding of SDLC methodologies including Agile Scrum and Waterfall models. Hands-on expertise in test automation using Selenium WebDriver, TestNG, Cucumber, JUnit, or similar frameworks across various programming languages such as Java or C#. Familiarity with performance testing tools like LoadRunner or JMeter to evaluate system scalability under load conditions. Solid knowledge of APIs (RESTful & SOAP), web services (XML & JSON), and service-oriented architecture (SOA) principles for integration testing. Experience working with databases such as MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB or DB2; proficient in writing complex SQL queries for data validation. Strong debugging skills combined with experience in troubleshooting issues related to Windows/Linux operating systems and network configurations. Ability to analyze requirements from multiple sources including business analysis documents and technical specifications; excellent data analysis skills are essential. Join us if you’re passionate about delivering high-quality software solutions! We value innovative thinkers who thrive on continuous learning and enjoy working collaboratively within a fast-paced environment committed to excellence in quality assurance. Pay: £35,500.00-£65,100.00 per year Benefits: Casual dress Company events Company pension Free fitness classes Gym membership Private medical insurance Sick pay UK visa sponsorship Work from home Work Location: Hybrid remote in London EC1Y 8LZ

items.desc: A bit of background on Rotageek Rotageek helps businesses optimise staff scheduling through data-driven technology. By combining machine learning and advanced algorithms, we help organisations forecast demand, improve workforce management and give employees greater control over their schedules. Our solutions drive operational efficiency, improve customer experiences and help reduce staff turnover across the retail and healthcare sectors. Rotageek is now part of the ELMO Software group, strengthening our ability to deliver industry-leading workforce management solutions as part of a broader HR technology ecosystem. Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. But we’ll let you in on a secret: there’s no such thing as a “perfect” candidate. Rotageek is a place where everyone can grow. So, however you identify and whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come into work every day. Our values: what we live by Start With People : You champion the customer experience, create psychological safety and help the whole team deliver with confidence. Own It, Together : You take responsibility for quality outcomes, collaborate across disciplines and help turn incidents into learning. Clear Is Kind : You make defects, risks, coverage and quality decisions clear, actionable and respectful. Why this role is so important Our customers rely on Rotageek to support important workforce decisions. As a Software Engineer, you’ll help build the services, APIs and integrations that make those experiences reliable, secure and easy to extend. You’ll take ownership of well-scoped features and components, turning clear requirements into simple, robust and maintainable C# and .NET solutions. You’ll work closely with Engineering, QA, Product and Data colleagues from design through to production. This is a role for an engineer who cares about the whole journey, not just the code. You’ll think about testability, security, performance, observability and the way application data moves into reliable customer-facing experiences. You’ll also use AI-assisted engineering tools as part of your delivery workflow. You’ll use them to accelerate implementation, testing and refactoring, while applying your judgement to validate the output for correctness, security and architectural fit. ️ What you’ll be doing Break down well-scoped features into deliverable tasks, identifying dependencies and communicating progress, risks and decisions. Write automated tests covering core behaviour and common edge cases, working with QA to ensure the right coverage at the right level. Apply established security practices, including OWASP principles, secure handling of data and appropriate escalation of risks. Use logs, metrics and traces to monitor, troubleshoot and improve production behaviour. Participate in constructive code reviews that improve logic, style, performance and security while helping colleagues grow. Work with Data Engineering colleagues on interfaces, data contracts, data quality and operational failure modes. Contribute to incident response, post-incident learning and continuous improvement of the services you support. Document technical decisions and operational knowledge so the team can understand, support and extend what you build. What you’ll bring Professional experience building software with C# and .NET. Strong fundamentals in object-oriented design, APIs, SQL, automated testing and debugging. Experience delivering medium-complexity features within an established architecture. A practical understanding of secure development, performance, reliability and observability. Confidence participating in code reviews and explaining technical decisions clearly. The ability to take ownership of work from a well-scoped ticket through to production, including testing, documentation, monitoring and follow-through. A collaborative, customer-focused approach to agile delivery. The judgement to use AI productively while validating and owning everything it produces. Nice to have, but not essential Experience working closely with Data Engineering, Data Architecture or analytics teams. Practical understanding of data modelling, data quality, lineage, data contracts or transformation pipelines. Experience building reliable ingestion or integration workflows, event-driven services or messaging-based systems. PURPOSE OF THE ROLE Join BBC MediaTech DevOps team as a DevSecOps Engineer. You'll help build, operate and improve the software, platforms and automation that support secure software delivery across Media Technology. The role spans software engineering, cloud infrastructure, security tooling, CI/CD, vulnerability management and engineering automation. You'll work on practical engineering problems alongside experienced engineers and engineering teams. The role is intended to give you exposure to different parts of DevSecOps and security engineering rather than specialising in a single platform or security discipline. WHY JOIN THE TEAM You'll work on practical engineering problems alongside experienced engineers and engineering teams. You'll be expected to independently deliver well-scoped pieces of work, while working with senior engineers on larger or more complex technical changes. The role is intended to give you exposure to different parts of DevSecOps and security engineering rather than specialising in a single platform or security discipline. YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT Build integrations that connect security, engineering and organisational data to make findings easier for teams to understand and act on. Build, maintain and improve backend services, integrations, automation and internal engineering tools. Work with AWS infrastructure and Infrastructure as Code to deliver and operate secure cloud-based services. Help integrate security checks and controls into CI/CD workflows, including dependency scanning, code scanning, secrets detection and container or infrastructure security tooling. Apply secure engineering practices around identity and access management, secrets, logging, monitoring, data handling and least-privilege access. Help operate and improve security and vulnerability-management platforms used by engineering teams. Investigate technical issues across services, integrations, cloud infrastructure and security platforms, and implement appropriate fixes. Write automated tests, documentation and operational tooling to support reliable production services. Deliver well-defined engineering changes independently, from implementation through testing and deployment. Work with senior engineers on larger pieces of work, contributing to technical design, estimation and implementation. Work with engineering teams to understand security or operational problems and help implement practical solutions. Contribute reusable code, patterns, documentation and automation where these can help other teams. items.desc: Site Reliability Engineer About the role The Site Reliability Engineer will ensure highly reliable, secure and scalable application platforms by applying SRE practices on cloud native systems built on AWS, Kubernetes and Springboot microservices using Java. The role focuses on observability with Splunk, performance optimization and incident prevention for complex hybrid environments in day shift with a strong focus on continuous improvement and service resilience. Location: Glasgow, UK Work Arrangement: This is a fully onsite role, requiring attendance at the Glasgow office 5 days per week . Mandatory Skills Java, Springboot, Microservices, Kubernetes, Dynatrace and Splunk. Certifications Required: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer and Certified Kubernetes Administrator and Splunk Core Certified Power User Additional eligibility requirements: Candidates must be available to start within 4 weeks of receiving an offer. Candidates must currently reside in the UK. In this role, you will: Design and implement highly available and resilient application infrastructure on AWS to ensure business critical services run reliably and efficiently across hybrid environments. Optimize Kubernetes based container platforms by tuning resource usage, scaling strategies and deployment pipelines to maintain consistent performance under varying workloads. Develop and enhance Springboot microservices in Java to improve reliability, modularity and fault tolerance while aligning with best practices for cloud native architectures. Conduct detailed root cause analysis for production incidents and implement robust corrective actions to prevent recurrence and improve overall system resilience. Document runbooks, operational procedures and reliability patterns to support consistent incident response and knowledge sharing across global teams. Partner with stakeholders supporting asset and wealth management processes to understand domain specific reliability needs and translate them into technical solutions. Drive continuous improvement initiatives by analyzing reliability metrics, identifying bottlenecks and proposing targeted enhancements that support organizational goals. Ensure security, compliance and governance requirements are integrated into SRE workflows so platforms remain protected while delivering dependable services. Qualifications -Show proven experience working as a Site Reliability Engineer in complex environments for eight to twelve years with consistent focus on reliability and performance. Demonstrate strong hands on expertise in AWS services such as compute, storage, networking and managed application components used to host production workloads. Exhibit practical experience implementing SRE frameworks including observability, incident management, error budgets and service level definitions in large scale systems. Display advanced skills using Splunk for log management, custom dashboards, alerts and analytics to support proactive detection of issues and trends. Provide solid experience managing Kubernetes clusters including configuration, scaling, workload orchestration and troubleshooting in production contexts. Show deep proficiency building and maintaining Springboot based microservices using Java with emphasis on modular design, resilience and maintainability. Highlight any background in asset and wealth management domains where reliability and integrity of transactional systems and client facing platforms are critical.

This role combines incident response, cloud security and stakeholder engagement, requiring the ability to identify, contain and investigate sophisticated cyber threats across traditional, hybrid and cloud-hosted environments. You will investigate incidents across cloud, endpoint, network and identity platforms, analysing security telemetry and attacker activity to determine scope, impact and root cause. Working alongside threat intelligence, detection engineering and force stakeholders, you will provide technical advice to support incident response, recovery and organisational decision-making. Key Responsibilities Incident Response & Investigation Lead and support investigations into cyber security incidents affecting UK policing, including ransomware, malware, unauthorised access, data compromise and insider threats. Conduct technical investigations across endpoints, servers, cloud environments and identities to determine the scope, root cause and impact of incidents. Support containment, eradication and recovery activities through evidence-based recommendations. Develop and maintain investigative methodologies, playbooks and procedures aligned to recognised incident response frameworks. Cloud Security Lead and support investigations into cyber incidents affecting Azure, AWS and GCP environments. Analyse cloud telemetry, audit logs, identity events and security alerts to identify malicious activity and support incident response activities. Investigate attacks targeting the identity control plane, including Microsoft Entra ID and other identity providers (IdPs), identifying compromised accounts, privilege escalation and unauthorised access. Support response activities across cloud infrastructure, workloads and SaaS platforms, providing technical expertise during active incidents. Work closely with threat intelligence, detection engineering and force stakeholders to improve investigative outcomes and situational awareness. Translate lessons learned into improvements to cloud security controls, detections, playbooks and response procedures. Stakeholder Engagement Act as a trusted advisor to police forces and policing organisations during cyber incidents. Deliver clear technical and strategic briefings to senior stakeholders, including Chief Officers, CIOs, Heads of IT and Heads of Cyber Security. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure effective incident management throughout investigations. Support national coordination activities where incidents have cross-force or sector-wide implications. Threat Analysis & Continuous Improvement Apply threat intelligence, attacker TTPs and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK to support investigations and response activities. Identify trends, lessons learned and opportunities to improve cyber resilience across UK policing. Contribute to the development of detection capabilities and incident response processes through post-incident reviews and technical findings. Support knowledge sharing, mentoring and capability development across the wider NMC function. What you need to succeed in the role Experience investigating and responding to cyber security incidents within enterprise environments. Experience investigating ransomware, malware, unauthorised access, cloud compromise and data breach incidents. Experience analysing telemetry from cloud, endpoint, network and identity platforms to determine attacker activity, scope and impact. Experience working with Azure, AWS or GCP environments. Experience investigating identity-based threats involving Microsoft Entra ID and other identity providers (IdPs). Strong understanding of attacker tactics, techniques and procedures, and the incident response lifecycle. Experience using EDR, SIEM and cloud security tooling to support investigations and response activities. Ability to communicate technical findings and recommendations to senior stakeholders. items.desc: Solution Architect (London) AND Introduction At AND, we accelerate the development of digital capabilities. In practice, that means helping ambitious leaders and organisations build the teams, products, processes and even operational structures they need to close the digital skills gap within their organisation today, so that they thrive tomorrow. Clients rely on our experience, agility and craft skills across tech and business strategy, software development and product management to address some of the toughest challenges facing their businesses. We bring aboard thinkers, tinkerers, passionate software craftspeople and inspiring technologists to help us solve these challenges. Together, we’re united by a sense of pragmatism, purpose and a deeply-held belief that digital products and technology alone won’t transform a business or save the world: it’s the people that count. About You As a Solution Architect Lead, you will provide solution architecture expertise, supporting our clients to deliver their digital objectives. As a result, you will need to be able to: Analyses and translates business, information and technical requirements into an architectural blueprint that outlines solutions to achieve business objectives for our client Work with our clients to provide solution architecture expertise, supporting our clients to deliver their digital objective Work with enterprise architecture, application and infrastructure teams to produce an optimal designs for the technology to support the product and identifies and designs dependencies with other systems in the enterprise Manage and lead the target design, policies and standards, working proactively to maintain a stable, viable architecture and ensure consistency of design across designated projects Provide hands-on support alongside the Dev Team for complex solutions and code migrations Coach and develop the AND Digital Product Developers across the squads To do that, it’s essential you bring the following: Broad understanding of the key layers of IT architecture including enterprise, data, application and solution, specific to enterprise level platforms A track record of delivering end to end solution architecture for large and complex multi-channel digital projects Experience in cloud technologies such as AWS and Azure, Saas and Iaas, cloud infrastructure and multiple programming languages Experience of best practices processes and frameworks such as TOGAF and architectural patterns / models Experience in a consulting role and confident in presenting /working and building relationships with all levels of seniority, from clients to dev teams. It’s helpful if you also have: Good knowledge of open source technologies (in full-stack environments) and stretching into code management, testing and deployment tools You have worked for a professional services business, in a solution architecture role for leading corporate clients Commercial awareness of implementing software i.e. cost of system, ownership, impact of new tech into established organisation Good experience and knowledge of the Agile /Scrum delivery process Understanding of IT organisations, functions, roles, activities Joining AND From the work we deliver, to the way we serve and support our people, we work hard to ensure that there’s nowhere quite like AND. But joining a company is a two-way street: the fit has to work on both sides. So before you apply, here’s three key things to understand about us: We’re built for people - like, real humans. Not ‘resources’ or ‘staff’. That means happiness and wellbeing really do matter to us, and we hate unnecessary hierarchy and bureaucracy. There’s no well-trodden path ahead: AND is growing fast and forging a new trail. That’s exciting, and gives us all the autonomy and opportunity we love - but bear in mind it also demands focus, patience and resilience. Diversity is a priority. After all, to build great products that a wide variety of different people love to use, we need a wide variety of people to help us build them. So diversity is more than a policy or a word: it’s business critical for us. Still sound good? Great! Fill out the short application form below and we’ll be in touch.

Support services across AWS, Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365. Maintain patching, monitoring, backups, access controls and secure configurations. Support identity and access management, including onboarding and offboarding. Investigate infrastructure and security issues and escalate where appropriate. Maintain accurate system documentation, inventories and operational procedures. Support backup restoration testing, disaster recovery and infrastructure improvement activities. Security assessments Prepare responses to security questionnaires, due diligence requests and client or partner assessments. Work with internal stakeholders to verify responses and gather evidence. Maintain a library of approved security responses and supporting documentation. Track deadlines, follow-up questions and resulting actions. Escalate gaps, unclear requirements or significant commitments for review. Essential experience and skills Experience working in systems administration or an infrastructure-focused IT role. Experience with on-premises servers and virtualised environments. Hands-on experience with AWS or Microsoft Azure, with familiarity with the other. Experience supporting Microsoft 365. Good understanding of networking, identity and access management, backups, patching and secure administration. Strong troubleshooting, organisation and documentation skills. Clear written and verbal communication. An interest in information security and ISO 27001. Ability to work independently while recognising when escalation is required. Desirable experience Proxmox, VMware, Hyper-V or similar virtualisation platforms. Administration across both AWS and Azure. Microsoft Entra ID, Intune and Defender. Windows Server and Linux. ISO 27001, audit preparation or compliance evidence gathering. Security questionnaires or supplier assessments. Vulnerability management, disaster recovery or business continuity testing. PowerShell, Bash or other scripting experience. Relevant Microsoft, AWS or information security certifications. Support and development You’ll work closely with the Head of IT and have the opportunity to develop your experience across infrastructure, cloud technologies, information security and ISO 27001 compliance. We welcome applicants with strong systems administration foundations who are still developing experience in some of the technologies or compliance areas listed above. What success looks like Internal systems are secure, reliable and well documented. Maintenance and compliance activities are completed on time. Audit evidence and compliance records are organised and up to date. Security and remediation actions are followed through to completion. Client and partner security assessments are completed accurately and consistently. Why Join Code Wizards? We're passionate about building technology that powers great games, but we're equally passionate about building an environment where talented people can do the best work of their careers. Strengthen collaboration between Data Governance, Architecture, Technology, and Business teams to embed governance considerations from design through implementation while supporting successful delivery. Promote awareness and adoption of Data Governance principles and Data Minimum Standards across project and delivery teams, building strong relationships with project managers, business stakeholders, data owners, architects, and technology teams. Experience participating in enterprise governance forums such as architecture review boards, change approval boards, or platform review boards (Required). Familiarity with governance artefacts such as data readiness checklists and metadata capture templates (Preferred). Skills …

items.desc: 56 Dean Street is an award winning HIV and Sexual Health service based in Soho in the heart of London’s West End. We are looking for a skilled and dynamic Health Adviser to join our team. You must be able to offer skilled compassionate advice and care to our service users and be able to work in a busy environment. To see clients diagnosed with sexually transmitted infections including HIV, for information, health education, partner notification, health promotion and risk reduction. To undertake PEP assessments, offer sexual health screening (including venepuncture) and issue PEP and PrEP under a PSD. To see clients in a Sexual Health setting for time limited 1:1 work specifically around risk reduction and behaviour change. To provide time limited support for clients newly diagnosed with HIV. To take on specific project work as negotiated with the senior sexual health adviser. Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of England's top-performing and safest trusts. We operate two main acute hospital sites—Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and West Middlesex University Hospital—along with award-winning clinics across North West London. Our nearly 7,500 staff care for a diverse population of 1.5 million, providing full clinical services, including maternity, A&E, and children’s services, plus specialist HIV and sexual health clinics. The Care Quality Commission rates us 'Good' in safety, effectiveness, care, and responsiveness, and 'Outstanding' in leadership and resource use. We continually invest in our facilities, including a £30m expansion of critical care at Chelsea and Westminster and an £80m Ambulatory Diagnostic Centre at West Middlesex. We welcome applications for flexible working arrangements, accommodating requests where possible to support our staff and patient needs. The Trust is committed to equality and welcomes applications from all, regardless of background. Adjustments can be made for disabled candidates. Early application is advised as vacancies may close once sufficient applications are received. If you haven’t heard from us within three weeks of the closing date, your application was likely unsuccessful. Employment is subject to a six-month probationary period. Some roles may require weekend shifts at multiple sites. Clinical Practice Provide information and health education for clients diagnosed with sexually transmitted infections, including HIV, providing support and onward referral as required. To manage the process of partner notification/management for these clients in order to encourage, with the client’s consent, the attendance of all potentially infected sexual contacts to a Sexual Health clinic. To provide time limited work for clients specifically around risk reduction and behavior change, using evidenced based tools such as Motivational Interviewing and Behavioral Change models. The post holder is responsible for assessment of care needs of patients, planning programmes of care, implementation and evaluation of these programmes with direct supervision. They will be working independently autonomously and at times without direct supervision, accountable for their own professional actions. items.desc: A twelve-month Locum Consultant Anaesthetist position is available to start as soon as possible. We are delighted at your interest in joining our Anaesthetics department at the Royal Surrey Hospital. We are a department that provides a consultant-led service to dynamic surgical teams at the cutting edge of surgical innovation. Our department prides itself in allowing individuals to develop and bring their own areas of expertise and interest to what is already a very diverse mix of special interests. These include the more conventional areas such as examinerships, deanery roles, quality improvement, editorships, fellowship leads etc; but have expanded to medical examiner roles, mortality reviews, clinical risk, project management, ethics, management roles within the trust and even Magistracy. There is increasing demand for anaesthetic support for procedures away from theatres, with endoscopy, interventional radiology and radiotherapy being at the forefront of expansion recently. These are relatively new areas of demand, and along with an expansion of elective obstetrics and obstetric clinics offers a new consultant niche areas to organise and streamline. We are also expanding our pre-assessment service including a greater provision of consultant-led high-risk anaesthetic clinics and CPET. The department has historically led the way in holding senior deanery roles and we would look to new consultants to join our group of educational supervisors. Work has started on a purpose built, modular, ambulatory care centre – the Cancer and Surgical Innovation Centre (CASIC) - in the grounds of the RSFT that will give us additional capacity of 6 new theatres and associated facilities. Expected to come online in 2026, this exciting development opens up new opportunities to appointees. This will include involvement in planning new protocols and pathways for the area. Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us. We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients’ homes across Guildford and Waverley. We work in partnership with Ashford & St Peter’s Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust through a collaborative Group Model, supporting joined-up services, workforce flexibility and development opportunities. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has rated us as Outstanding. We are proud of our achievements and continue to invest in our people and infrastructure. To learn more about life at Royal Surrey, please watch our short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R96pMboIYdo Adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. For further details on the role, please see attached job description and person specification attached.

items.desc: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated and dynamic Research Nurse to support the delivery of high‑quality clinical research and trials across Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. As a Research Nurse, you will play a vital role in supporting the development and delivery of both commercial and academic research studies across a range of specialities. Working with strong leadership skills, you will collaborate closely with colleagues within the Research Team and the Medical and Surgical Division to build and sustain a diverse portfolio of clinical trials and research studies. You will actively facilitate the implementation of Good Clinical Practice (GCP) , ensuring that all research activity across the division consistently meets these standards. As a research‑active organisation, LTHTR is committed to giving patients access to innovative treatments, improving clinical outcomes, and supporting colleagues to develop their research delivery skills. Ensure the safe planning, delivery and evaluation of care for patients participating in clinical trials and research studies Act as a clinical expert in research delivery, ensuring patient safety is paramount at all times Communicate effectively and confidently with multidisciplinary teams , sponsors, external partners and patients Demonstrate excellent organisational skills , attention to detail and accurate data management Uphold Good Clinical Practice (GCP) principles across all research activity Support the development of a strong research culture within the Trust Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (LTHTr) is one of the largest and busiest acute Trusts in the North West, providing high‑quality care to the communities of Lancashire and South Cumbria. We are proud of our strong research culture and our ambition to become a recognised Centre of Excellence, particularly in women’s health and maternity research. As part of our Research & Innovation (R&I) team, you will join a supportive and dynamic department committed to building research capacity, improving patient outcomes, and reducing health inequalities. We work closely with regional partners, national research networks, and academic institutions, including Tommy’s Research Centre and local universities, to ensure our patients have access to cutting‑edge studies and innovative care pathways. LTHTr is dedicated to supporting the development of our staff. You will have access to training, mentorship, and opportunities to expand your clinical and academic skills. Our Trust values compassion, teamwork, and continuous improvement, and we foster an environment where staff feel empowered, respected, and encouraged to contribute to meaningful change. Joining us means becoming part of an organisation that is passionate about making a real difference—both to the patients we serve and to the future of women’s health research across our region. The post holder will support the Research and Innovation department to provide high‑quality, compassionate and patient‑focused care for people taking part in research within the Lancashire Clinical Research Facility and across clinical services. They will make sure care is planned, delivered and reviewed in line with Trust values, national standards, Good Clinical Practice and evidence‑based guidance. The role involves leading and coordinating safe research care, reducing risks, keeping clear and accurate records, and ensuring patients are treated with dignity, involved in decisions and kept safe. The post holder will act as a positive role model, supervising and supporting staff and students, helping with recruitment, training, appraisals and performance management, and promoting a respectful and inclusive working culture. They will also help manage the clinical environment and resources, support governance activities such as audits, incidents and complaints, develop and follow Standard Operating Procedures, promote equality, health education and wellbeing, and support the set‑up and delivery of commercial and academic clinical trials alongside Principal Investigators and multidisciplinary teams, ensuring all research meets regulatory requirements and high quality standards.

You will be closely aligned and work with colleagues within GP practices as well as Health in Mind (NHS Talking Therapies- NHS TT). The MHP role will provide a critical function in triaging referrals into the service as well as those in NHS TT, providing timely and consistent assessments, brief interventions and onward referral as required. Liaison with key stakeholders and third sector organisations also forms part of this role. This post offers the Trust's £2,000 Golden Hello or Relocation Incentive for Band 6 Nurses & Practitioners, (pro rata and subject to terms and conditions; please see attached Protocol Document for full details). You will be working closely with a range of professional groups, including Mental Health Practitioners based within GP surgeries, NMHT colleagues, partner organisations, VCSE providers, and other aligned services within the Neighbourhood as well as NHS Talking Therapies Teams. Xelix is a fast-paced scale-up – things move fast and expectations are high. We raised our Series B with Insight Partners in June 2025 and are expanding aggressively. This is a hands-on 1role focused on the systems that power our products, rather than internal BI or building a company-wide data warehouse. Build reliable pipelines with tools such as Prefect. Optimise PostgreSQL performance and data models. Choose the right storage, search and processing tools. Improve data quality and retention practices. Deliver changes alongside product, AI and DevOps teams. Strengthen data access, retention and auditability in partnership with security, compliance and engineering teams. What you’ll bring Professional experience owning the architecture of production data systems in AWS and their improvements. Experience with data access controls, retention and auditability requirements in regulated environments (SOC 1, SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001 or similar). Good judgement on storage and processing trade-offs. Clear communication and a hands-on, collaborative approach. A focus on reliability, data quality and security. Strong SQL, PostgreSQL and data modelling skills. Experience with NoSQL databases (like MongoDB, DocumentDB or DynamoDB) and warehousing solutions (like DuckDB, ClickHouse, Redshift) Solid Python and data pipeline engineering skills. Confidence using AI tools for development, investigation and documentation, with sound judgement about their value and limitations. The role
items.desc: Location Swindon / Wiltshire Salary Circa £67,500 Contract Permanent (Full Time ) Reference 4967 Closing Date 29 October 2026 Job description The Infrastructure Private Cloud Engineer will join the platform team who are responsible for the operational support, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Nationwide private cloud. Working within an ITIL-aligned operating model, the engineer will ensure platform stability, security, availability, and compliance while supporting the delivery of platform services to consumers. The role requires operational knowledge of VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) and associated infrastructure technologies, combined with the ability to challenge existing processes, improve engineering standards, and provide technical leadership across the team. We are happy to consider flexible working approaches to help you perform at your best. At Nationwide we offer hybrid working wherever possible. More rewarding relationships are supported through our hybrid approach, bringing colleagues together across our UK wide estate, whilst also supporting generous access to home working. We value our time in the office to solve problems, to learn, and to feel connected. For this job you'll spend at least two days per week, or if part time you'll spend 40% of your working time, based at our Swindon office. If your application is successful, your hiring manager will provide further details on how this works. You can also find out more about our approach to hybrid working here. Whilst these locations are where we are primarily looking to fill the role, if you’re an internal applicant based in a different location we would welcome your application and if successful, your hiring manager will provide further details on how this could work for this specific role. You can also find out more about our approach to hybrid working here. If we receive a high volume of relevant applications, we may close the advert earlier than the advertised date, so please apply as soon as you can. What you’ll be doing You will be responsible for maintaining the operational health, stability, and performance of the Hosting Landing Zone (HLZ) platform, ensuring services are delivered reliably and in line with agreed service levels. Working as part of an ITIL-aligned engineering team, you will lead the investigation and resolution of incidents, drive problem management activities, oversee technical changes, and support service requests across the platform estate. You will take ownership of complex technical issues, using your experience and judgement to identify root causes, implement sustainable fixes, and prevent recurring problems. You will be expected to continuously improve operational processes, reduce manual effort through automation, and help embed engineering best practices across the team. A key aspect of the role is providing technical leadership without direct line management responsibility. items.desc: Brynawel is the leading residential centre for the treatment of alcohol and drug dependencies in Wales. Our mission is to be a centre of excellence in the provision of high-quality professional support and assistance for people experiencing alcohol or other drug dependency issues. Brynawel is committed to providing high quality, evidence-based recovery interventions and care. We are a learning partnership which promotes staff training, development and competence. Our Clinical Governance committee oversees governance within the organisation. We promote staff training, development and competence. Job purpose: As an Aftercare and Resettlement Coordinator you will utilise your communication, organisational and networking skills to provide support and discharge planning for clients. The post holder should be able to demonstrate a high level of personal and professional accountability, leading in the operational delivery of after care services and taking responsibility for the development of new ideas, initiatives and ways of working within the team.
