items.desc: Job Description Pagero has recently joined Thomson Reuters. Together, we are building the world’s largest, open business network. With our cloud-based network, customers can reach any business, anywhere in the world – no matter how many borders their operations may cross. We take care of the technical and regulatory requirements across the entire order-to-cash, purchase-to-pay and freight processes, to give customers data accuracy and security, transparency, and real-time visibility. All this through a single connection. We are seeking a highly skilled Identity & Access Management (IAM) Engineer to join our global IAM team as we undertake a complete transformation of our identity landscape — a cornerstone of our enterprise security posture. In this role, you will be responsible for administering secure and scalable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) , Access Governance , MSFT EntraID , and SSO/Federation solutions. You will drive operational excellence across IAM platforms, with a focus on continuous improvement, automation, and high availability. Key Responsibilities In this opportunity as IAM Engineer , you will: Administer and implement security across IAM technologies including product MEMORITY, Microsoft Entra, Active Directory, Access Governance , and LDAP directories Configure and troubleshoot Single Sign-On (SSO) for enterprise applications using SAML, OAuth, Kerberos, and NTLM Implement OpenID Connect (OIDC) and OAuth 2.0 solutions using MEMORITY tools Manage and maintain MEMORITY Directory Server , including cluster management and timely replication of configuration changes across Test and Production environments Administer and performance-tune MEMORITY/MSFT EntraID to support high-traffic enterprise workloads Deploy and support highly available, scalable MEMORITY infrastructure on AWS and on-premises , enabling SSO and federation for internal access Configure MEMORITY Access servers, Gateways, and Agents to protect enterprise resources Manage federation services between SiteMinder and MemorityFederate for SAML and WS-FED based application migrations Work with multiple Memority Federate adapters including HTML Form, x509, Kerberos, OpenToken, Memority ID, and Composite adapters Coordinate with server hosting and MemorityFederate vendor teams to resolve hardware and software issues Lead vulnerability mitigation and patch management activities, including version upgrades Prepare comprehensive documentation and operational runbooks for the Operations team Act as first-level escalation support for IAM operational teams and other IT security functions Drive development of automation and integration capabilities within IAM solutions Required Qualifications You’re a fit for the role of IAM Engineer if you have the following required qualifications: 3+ years of experience designing, develop Memority, and implementing IAM security technologies including MEMORITY, Entra, Active Directory, Access Governance, and LDAP Strong hands-on experience with SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), Kerberos, NTLM, LDAP, and RADIUS Proven experience integrating, develop Memority, and automating MFA and authentication protocols Deep understanding of Identity domains: Authentication, Authorization, Access Management, and Attestation Experience with Memority Federate including adapter configuration, Service Provider/Identity Provider connections, metadata management, and SSL certificate handling Hands-on experience with Memority Access integration with Memority Federate to protect applications using Memority Access Tokens Demonstrated experience with API security concepts, including integration with Open AM, SiteMinder, OAuth 2.0, JWT tokens, and certificate-based authentication Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS preferred) and an understanding of dynamic computing's impact on Identity Proven ability to deliver Proof of Concepts (POCs) for identity and API security integrations Preferred Qualifications Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting skills in complex, large-scale enterprise environments Experience designing and engineering identity solutions in a large global enterprise #LI-EH2 What’s in it For You? Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment (2-3 days a week in the office depending on the role) for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected. items.desc: Job Description We are looking for an Integration Test & Validation Engineer to join a growing technical team in Gothenburg. This position will be responsible for providing overall services and test support to our SE Site in terms of TSP infrastructure, functional capabilities, and information security. Key Responsibilities • Validate system interactions and data consistency between: o TSP backend services (Microservices) o Vehicle side (TCU/TCAM/In-Vehicle Infotainment) o Mobile applications (iOS/Android) • Actively query and verify databases (SQL/NoSQL) to ensure data integrity, correct state transitions, and accurate business logic flow during integration. • Analyze backend logs and APM tools (e.g., Kibana, Splunk) to identify root causes of business errors, communication failures, and API mismatches. Investigate data flow and communication between systems to ensure correct orchestration and messaging. • Design and execute integration test scenarios covering real-world use cases (e.g., remote commands, vehicle status, OTA, eCall, and remote diagnostics). • Support defect analysis and troubleshooting, bridging the gap between frontend, backend, and vehicle teams to drive complex cross-functional issues to closure. • Collaborate closely with backend developers, vehicle teams, and app teams in an international environment. Verify API behaviors, message flows, and communication protocols (e.g., MQTT, HTTP/HTTPS, Protobuf). • Prepare test reports, validation documentation, and quality assessments for release readiness. Requirements & Technical Proficiency • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Telecommunications, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. • Minimum 3 years of experience in integration testing, joint debugging, or system validation, preferably in the telematics or connected vehicle domain. Deep understanding of connected car business logic and architecture (TSP / TCAM / Mobile App interaction flow). • Proficient in database operations, with the ability to write SQL queries independently (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL, or Oracle) for data verification and troubleshooting. • Proven experience in log analysis and issue investigation across distributed systems (e.g., tracing a remote command failure from App, TSP, Vehicle). • Solid knowledge of networking and communication protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, MQTT, or other messaging queues. Familiarity with API testing tools (e.g., Postman, JMeter, curl) and log management tools (e.g., ELK stack, Kibana). Preferred Qualifications• Experience within OEM or Tier-1 automotive telematics projects (e.g., handling T-Box/TCU registration, activation, or TSP lifecycle management). • Familiarity with common backend business error codes and exception handling mechanisms. • Basic scripting skills (Python, Shell) for log parsing, data preparation, or test automation support. Experience with cloud-based backend systems (e.g., AWS, Azure) and microservices architecture. Personal attributes• Strong analytical mindset with a structured, end-to-end problem-solving approach. • Excellent communication and coordination skills, with the ability to effectively drive joint- debugging sessions across different technical teams. • Proactive, self-driven, and highly quality-oriented. Fluent in English (written and spoken) for daily collaboration in international teams. What We Offer A supportive and learning-oriented work environment Opportunity to gain hands-on experience in IT operations within the automotive domain Career development path towards IT Manager or other IT roles Competitive salary and benefits in accordance with Swedish standards Öppen för alla Vi fokuserar på din kompetens, inte dina övriga förutsättningar. Vi är öppna för att anpassa rollen eller arbetsplatsen efter dina behov.

items.desc: Do you want to drive new business opportunities based on cutting edge technology? At CPAC Systems, you will combine technical curiosity with commercial drive and build customer relationships that help shape the next generation of machines and vehicles. At CPAC Systems, we work with electrification, automation, and connected solutions that make our customers’ products smarter, safer, and more efficient. We bring the entire product development process together under one roof, with close collaboration across disciplines and short decision paths. We are now looking for a Business Developer to join our Industry & Integration team. You will play a key role in growing existing accounts and developing new business, with a particular focus on agriculture, mining, heavy material handling and other industrial vehicle segments. Your role You will drive business from the first conversation and identified need through to agreements and long-term growth. You will own a portfolio of OEM customers, meaning manufacturers of products such as machines and vehicles, and Tier 1 suppliers. You will build relationships across engineering, product management, procurement, and senior management. By understanding your customers’ operations, technology, and future plans, you will identify where we can create value. Together with our engineers and project managers, you will turn those needs into solutions and business opportunities across hardware, software, and services. The role combines long-term account development with active prospecting. You will report to the Sales Director, Industry & Integration, and represent CPAC Systems at customer meetings, trade fairs, and industry events. You will primarily work from our office in Mölndal, with the flexibility to work remotely one day per week. The role includes travel to customers, trade fairs, and industry events. Key responsibilities Grow our key accounts. Develop long-term account plans, run regular business reviews, and identify opportunities for upselling, new projects, and continued collaboration. Develop new business. Identify and approach new OEM customers, primarily in agriculture and construction machinery, while exploring opportunities in other relevant industries. Lead commercial negotiations. Prepare proposals, negotiate pricing and terms, and secure profitable agreements, renewals, and long-term supply commitments. Demonstrate customer value. Build business cases and ROI calculations that show the value of our technology, and structure paid pilots and proofs of concept. Connect customers and technology. Work with engineering, project management, and operations to support deliveries that meet expectations on cost, quality, and timing. Bring market insights into CPAC. Follow customer roadmaps, technology shifts, and competitors, and contribute these insights to product and business development. Keep sales activities structured. Maintain account plans and opportunities in CRM, prepare sales forecasts, and track account growth. You will share knowledge and experience with your colleagues and use AI tools to support activities such as account research, meeting preparation, and customer communication. Who are you? You combine commercial drive with a genuine interest in technology and your customers’ operations. You have a solid technical understanding, stay curious, and keep up with new developments. You want to understand how your customers’ machines and products work, the challenges they face, and how our solutions can help. You spot opportunities when a customer develops a new platform, updates a product, or needs to solve a technical challenge. You take initiative, open doors, and move business forward. At the same time, you know that lasting partnerships are built on trust, listening, and delivering on your promises. You are confident in negotiations and can explain the value of a technical solution to both engineers and commercial decision-makers. Qualifications At least five years of experience in business development, technical sales, or Key Account Management. A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field. Experience leading complex negotiations with multiple decision-makers and closing deals. An understanding of embedded hardware and software, with the ability to explain the value of technology based on customer needs. Fluency in English. Nice to have Experience selling to OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers. An established network of contacts at OEMs in relevant markets. Experience selling electronics, embedded systems, or industrial technology. Experience working with a CRM tool. Experience working with customers in agriculture or construction machinery. Fluency in Swedish. Why CPAC? At CPAC, you will work close to both the technology and the people behind it. You will collaborate with experienced colleagues, follow solutions from idea to finished product, and see how they are used in real machines and vehicles. We have a flat organisation where …

We help partners and clients understand and reduce the environmental impact of their products and systems, from the first design choices to end of life. Our work centers on three services: ISO 14044-compliant LCA studies, customized life cycle tools, and prospective LCA (pLCA) with scenario modeling. We work alongside research and industrial partners in and outside Switzerland. The role We are looking for an engineer with a genuine interest in sustainability to join us as a Life Cycle Engineer. You will build and run life cycle models in Python, contribute to funded research projects, and help turn results into clear insights for partners and clients. It is a hands-on role at the intersection of engineering, data, and sustainability research. Start date: January 2027 or by arrangement Duration: 1 year, with the possibility of extension Workload: 80–100% Location: Dübendorf, Zurich What you will do Build, run and document LCA models in Python, using Brightway Collect, clean and structure data from partners and the literature Contribute to research projects in the mobility, construction and energy sectors Help develop customized life cycle tools and data workflows for clients Prepare clear results, figures and reports for technical and non-technical audiences Support proposal writing and literature reviews for new research projects Competencies A bachelor's and master's degree in environmental, mechanical, civil, or another relevant engineering discipline 0–3 years of relevant professional experience. Recent graduates are encouraged to apply. Proficiency in Python. Hands-on experience building tools, models, or data workflows is a plus. A solid understanding of life cycle assessment methods and the ISO 14040/14044 framework is a strong plus, as is familiarity with Brightway. A strong motivation to work on sustainability, with interest in research on circular economy and sustainable infrastructure, especially mobility, construction and energy Strong statistical and analytical skills are considered a plus, particularly the ability to interpret complex data and derive actionable insights. Proficient English, written and spoken; German or French is a plus Based in Switzerland, with a valid Swiss work permit What you bring Strong ability to understand and analyze complex, interconnected processes across different systems. A structured, careful way of working with data, and the curiosity to dig into technical systems Excellent analytical skills, keen attention to detail, and accuracy in data handling. Strong communication skills, able to present complex information concisely and effectively. Self-motivated, proactive, agile, and a team player. What we offer You will work in a small team on an interactive and personal level. Our biggest asset is our team, and you get to shape your own place in it. The opportunity to help shape a new research branch from an early stage and grow your expertise in sustainability and system analysis A role with direct, visible impact, where innovative thinking and new ideas are encouraged Research projects with leading Swiss and European research partners A dynamic, international team of 20 professionals Mentorship and guidance from experienced professionals in LCA and circular economy, and accelerated personal growth Flexible working hours and up to 40% home office An office and workplace in Zürich (Dübendorf) How to apply Please upload your CV, and if you have LCA or Python work to share, such as a GitHub repository, thesis, or project report, we would love to see it. Our process includes a short online call, an in-person interview, and a short technical task tailored to your background. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, and especially encourage FLINTA* persons to apply. Work Location: In person

items.desc: Job title: Formulation Scientist - Composition, Particle & Process Design Location: Kaiseraugst, Switzerland As a Formulation Scientist, you will drive the development of innovative formulations for food, dietary supplement, and oral pharmaceutical applications. Manage and evolve AWS infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform & Terragrunt). Operate and scale containerised workloads on EKS, alongside serverless workloads on Lambda. Design, secure, and maintain AWS networking — VPCs, subnets, security groups, routing, and load balancing.
items.desc: Description We’re looking for a mid-level DevOps Engineer to join our engineering team and help us build, automate, and scale the AWS infrastructure that underpins our products. You’ll work closely with development, platform, and security teams to improve deployment velocity, system reliability, and operational visibility. This is a hands-on role for someone who is comfortable owning infrastructure as code, maintaining CI/CD pipelines, and championing automation and observability across the software delivery lifecycle. We place a high value on clear, well-maintained documentation, and you’ll be expected to document your work to a standard that helps the whole team. You’ll have enough autonomy to make meaningful technical decisions, with the support of a senior team to grow into. Key Responsibilities Build, maintain, and improve CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions) to enable fast, safe, and repeatable deployments. Manage and evolve AWS infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform & Terragrunt). Operate and scale containerised workloads on EKS, alongside serverless workloads on Lambda. Design, secure, and maintain AWS networking — VPCs, subnets, security groups, routing, and load balancing. Manage relational databases on RDS and Aurora, including performance, backups, and resilience. Handle secrets and sensitive configuration securely using AWS Secrets Manager. Implement and maintain monitoring, logging, and alerting to ensure system health and rapid incident response (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, ELK, Datadog). Collaborate with development teams to improve deployment practices, environment consistency, and developer experience. Contribute to security and compliance efforts — secrets management, patching, access control, and secure-by-default configurations. Take part in our support and on-call arrangements and help shape them as they mature. Automate manual and repetitive operational tasks through scripting and tooling. Produce and maintain clear, accurate documentation — architecture diagrams, runbooks, onboarding guides, and operational procedures — and champion a culture where knowledge is written down and shared rather than siloed. Skills, Knowledge & Expertise Essential Skills & Experience 3+ years in a DevOps, SRE, Platform, or infrastructure-focused engineering role. Solid hands-on experience with AWS. Practical experience running Kubernetes in production, ideally EKS. Experience building and deploying serverless functions with AWS Lambda. Good working knowledge of AWS networking — VPCs, subnets, security groups, routing, and load balancing. Experience operating relational databases on RDS and/or Aurora. Experience managing secrets with AWS Secrets Manager (or equivalent). Proficiency with Docker and containerised workflows. Practical experience with Infrastructure as Code using Terraform and Terragrunt. Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, ideally with GitHub Actions. Strong scripting ability in at least one language (Bash, Python, or Go). Good understanding of Linux systems administration and networking fundamentals. Familiarity with monitoring and observability tooling. Comfortable working with Git and modern version control workflows. A genuine commitment to good documentation — able to write clear, concise runbooks and technical docs that others can follow. Willingness to take part in an on-call rotation and contribute to a maturing support function. Desirable Relevant certifications (e.g. AWS Associate/Professional, CKA/CKAD, Terraform Associate). Experience with service mesh, GitOps (ArgoCD/Flux), or progressive delivery. Exposure to security and compliance frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2, or similar). Experience with database backup/DR strategies and Aurora failover. Experience establishing or improving on-call and incident management processes. Experience introducing or improving documentation practices (e.g. docs-as-code). Understanding of cost optimisation and FinOps practices. Job Benefits Hybrid working arrangements 26 days holiday (plus 8 public holidays) Enhanced family friendly benefits Private medical insurance Onsite gym A supportive and collaborative work culture About Restrata Restrata was originally founded as the technology arm of one of the world’s largest security services companies, providing design, prepare and respond solutions in high threat areas over many decades. We witnessed first-hand the extreme pain of data siloes and system-hopping and the negative impact on response efforts that endangered lives, put business assets at risk and disrupted continuity. This deep industry expertise led us to build resilienceOS, one end-to-end platform built from the ground up to unify your data, gain insights and take action to protect what matters.

At Torchbox, we work with organisations that are making the world a better place. From charities and nonprofits to ambitious, purpose-driven organisations, we bring together talented people across design, technology, marketing and delivery to create digital experiences that make a real impact. We're always keen to connect with brilliant freelancers who share our values, love what they do and might be interested in collaborating with us. Whether you're an experienced independent consultant, a creative problem-solver, a technical specialist or someone who brings a fresh perspective to digital challenges, we'd love to hear from you. Who we're looking to connect with We work across a wide range of digital disciplines and are particularly interested in hearing from freelancers with experience in: UX, Research & Design: user research, UX design, UI design, service design, accessibility, content design and creative / brand design. Software Engineering & Development: frontend and backend development, Python, Django, Wagtail, JavaScript, React and technical architecture. Digital Marketing: SEO, paid media, PPC, paid social, digital strategy, content marketing and campaign management. Data, Analytics & Optimisation: web analytics, GA4, Google Tag Manager, data visualisation, dashboards, CRO and digital performance measurement. Delivery & Project Management: digital project management, agile delivery, programme management and product management. Strategy & Consultancy: digital transformation, AI & innovation, product strategy, discovery, research and strategic consultancy. This isn't an exhaustive list. If your skills sit somewhere within the digital space and you think you'd be a great fit for Torchbox, we'd still love to hear from you. What it's like to work with us We're a certified B Corp and employee-owned digital agency, and we care deeply about both the work we do and the people we do it with. We believe great work comes from collaboration, curiosity, openness and bringing different perspectives together. When working with our freelance partners, we aim to create an experience where you feel welcomed, valued and part of the team, with clear communication, meaningful collaboration and the opportunity to contribute your expertise to projects that matter. Depending on the project, opportunities might range from short-term specialist support to longer-term engagements working alongside our internal teams. What we value We're particularly interested in connecting with people who: Care about producing thoughtful, high-quality work. Enjoy collaborating with multidisciplinary teams. Communicate openly and take ownership of their work. Bring curiosity, creativity and a problem-solving mindset. Are comfortable working in a remote-first, collaborative environment. Share our commitment to inclusion, accessibility and creating positive impact through digital. Experience working with charities, nonprofits or purpose-driven organisations is a bonus! Interested in freelancing with Torchbox? We'd love to learn more about you. Share a little about your experience, your areas of expertise, the types of projects you enjoy and your availability. Links to your portfolio, website, LinkedIn profile or examples of previous work are always welcome. Please note: This is an ongoing expression of interest rather than an advertisement for a specific live project. We review our freelance network as project needs arise and will get in touch if we identify an opportunity that aligns with your experience and availability. If you'd like to be part of our extended talent community, we'd love to hear from you.

items.desc: Proximie is on a mission to improve healthcare by transforming the world’s operating rooms into connected ecosystems of people, devices, and data. Our Intelligence Suite transforms operating room (OR) performance, keeping teams in sync and workflows on track to maximise throughput. Simultaneously our computer vision and AI capabilities capture real-time data and detect surgical events – improving quality of data outputs. The result: ORs are optimised like never before – with predictive analytics and automated notifications ensuring patients and staff are in the right place at the right time. Once practitioners are in the OR, our Surgical Suite enables real-time remote access and creates a secure video record of every procedure; improving training, education, and collaboration. It is an intuitive asset which helps instil a culture of continuous learning, accelerates the adoption of cutting-edge medical devices, and enhances surgical performance across the entire global workforce – improving outcomes and saving lives. Proximie was commercialised in 2019 and is available in over 500 facilities globally. Check out our Founder and CEO Nadine’s Origins Story here: https://www.proximie.com/about-us/ Position Overview With hospitals and health systems around the world increasingly adopting Proximie’s Surgical Suite and Intelligence Suite, we are seeking a skilled and agile Data Integration Engineer to spearhead the integration of our platform with customer Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems. This is a pivotal, high-ownership role responsible for driving healthcare data integration across the UK and META. You will be instrumental in enabling scalable, secure, and reliable data exchange between Proximie and its partners, accelerating clinical insights, enhancing workflows, and delivering operational efficiency at scale. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in healthcare data integration and industry standards (including HL7), with the ability to independently analyze and interpret complex data sets. Success in this position requires exceptional communication skills, technical leadership, and the agility to thrive in a fast-paced, global, and highly collaborative environment. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, and maintain HL7 interfaces (ADT, ORU, ORM, etc.) to support real-time and batch data exchange with customer EHR systems. Rapidly stand-up file-based and HL7-based integrations to meet customer onboarding timelines and scalability needs. Develop and manage ETL pipelines for transforming and validating clinical data from diverse sources. Collaborate with customer IT teams to define integration requirements, troubleshoot issues, and ensure successful deployment. Perform data analysis and validation to ensure completeness, accuracy, and consistency of exchanged data. Work closely with internal product, engineering, and customer success teams to align integration efforts with platform capabilities and customer goals. Document integration workflows, data mappings, and technical specifications for internal and external stakeholders. Requirements 3+ years of experience in healthcare data integration, preferably with EHR systems (Epic, Cerner, Meditech, etc.). Strong hands-on experience with HL7 v2.x messaging standards and interface engines (e.g., Mirth Connect, Rhapsody, Cloverleaf). Proficiency in ETL tools and scripting languages (e.g., Python, SQL) for data transformation and validation. Familiarity with healthcare data standards (FHIR, CDA, CCD) and privacy regulations (HIPAA, GDPR). Ability to analyze complex data sets and troubleshoot integration issues independently. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, especially in customer-facing technical discussions. Experience working in fast-paced, agile environments with cross-functional teams. Experience integrating with cloud-based platforms and APIs is highly desirable. Knowledge of surgical workflows and clinical documentation practices is highly desirable. Nice to Haves Familiarity with software engineering practices, including version control (e.g. Git), deployment processes, and release workflows — enabling effective collaboration with engineering teams and a smoother path from integration development to production. Proximie is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under the law.

Teamwork: You work well with colleagues across Sales, Support and Customer Success. Right to work: You are eligible to work in the UK. Software-as-a-service (SaaS) or subscription experience: Exposure to account management, customer success, inside sales or renewals in a software or information services business. The post holder will work in partnership with our Neonatal Community Outreach Team to ensure timely referral to this service to facilitate early discharge home for all babies when every possible. The role involves liaison with many other community teams including but not exclusive to: community children's nursing, perinatal mental health, substance misuse teams, children's centres, family support workers, social workers, housing support officers and community midwives. items.desc: We are seeking an enthusiastic Senior Community Practitioner (Nurses) to join the Nottinghamshire Virtual Ward! We are recruiting one full time position. Virtual Wards deliver hospital‑level care at home using remote monitoring, digital tools and multi‑disciplinary community support. Our service is part of a system‑wide collaborative across Nottinghamshire Healthcare, NUH, Sherwood Forest Hospitals, Doncaster & Bassetlaw Teaching Hospitals and CityCare, ensuring seamless care across acute and community settings. We support pathways including frailty, respiratory and admission avoidance. As a Band 6 Senior Community Practitioner, you will provide timely assessments, person‑centred care and advanced clinical decision‑making in patients’ homes, working both autonomously and within an established MDT. This role offers opportunities to develop advanced assessment skills, contribute to innovative virtual care models and play a key part in system transformation. We welcome applications from nurses passionate about acute community care, digital innovation and supporting people to recover safely at home. Deliver timely, person‑centred assessments and provide high‑quality clinical care to patients on the Virtual Ward for up to 14 days. Work autonomously and within the MDT (including Matrons, Nurses, AHPs and support staff) to prevent unnecessary hospital admissions and support safe early discharge. Interpret remote monitoring data, undertake face‑to‑face clinical reviews, identify deterioration and initiate appropriate interventions or escalation. Lead and coordinate safe, effective discharge planning and contribute to daily MDT discussions on treatment and risk. Support junior staff through supervision, role‑modelling and clinical guidance. Maintain accurate documentation on SystmOne and uphold professional standards, governance, and patient safety. Work flexibly across respiratory, frailty and admission avoidance pathways, following lone‑worker and dynamic risk assessment procedures. #TeamNottsHC comprises over 11,000 dedicated colleagues who #MakeADifference every day. We deliver intellectual disability, mental health, community health, forensic, and offender healthcare services across Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire, and South Yorkshire. Our care is provided from over 200 sites, spanning community locations, acute settings, and secure environments, including prisons. We are one of the largest mental health and community Trusts in the East Midlands and one of Nottinghamshire's biggest employers. We also host national and regional services, such as the National High Secure Deaf Service and the Nottingham Centre for Transgender Health. We offer a variety of employee-led staff networks, including Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) groups, the Green Champions network, the Freedom to Speak Up network, the Health and Wellbeing Champions network, and the Menopause Champions network. These networks play a vital role in supporting our diverse workforce and promoting a culture of inclusivity. The health and wellbeing of colleagues is a top priority. We invest significantly in this through our in-house occupational health and staff counselling services, supported by a dedicated Health and Wellbeing team. The Trust is committed to reducing its carbon emissions, with a specialised Energy and Environmental team working to ensure compliance with environmental legislation, enhance our environmental performance, and achieve our net-zero commitment. We are looking to recruit a dynamic, flexible, and compassionate Senior Community Nurse to join this new and exciting service within the localities of Mid Nottinghamshire and/or Bassetlaw. You will work within the Virtual Ward Team and in collaboration with system partners such as City Care, as part of a supportive multi-disciplinary clinical team with a dedicated focus of delivering excellent patient centred care and innovation. You must be able to work flexibly over 7 days including weekend and bank holidays. Shifts are 8am -8pm You will be providing care to patients in a community setting, who require high quality holistic evidence-based care that is responsive, effective, and efficient in line with the virtual ward model. We would love to hear from you if: You possess community nursing experience or acute care experience with a passion for learning, demonstrate excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to be adaptable, reliable, resourceful, and approachable, evidencing high levels of personal and clinical credibility, being able to instantly establish effective working relationships in a range of work settings. You have a thirst to use digital and remote technologies within your assessments. You demonstrate high levels of care and compassion to promote independence, prevent hospital admission or admission to care, support early discharge from hospital and to help people to receive the care they require within the places they call home. …

About The Rainbow Foundation The Rainbow Foundation is an active ageing charity which has worked to improve the health and wellbeing of our communities for over 32 years, and now supports more than 7,000 people each year across Wrexham and North East Wales. We have provided Social Prescribing across Wrexham since 2019 and contributed to the development of the Welsh Government Social Prescribing Framework. Our awards include Best Mental Health Support Service (Wales) 2024, the GSK IMPACT Award with The King’s Fund and Bevan Commission Exemplars, and we are rated Excellent for Wellbeing by Care Inspectorate Wales (2025). Job summary We have been awarded the contract for the Wrexham-wide Social Prescribing and Community Wellness Service, commissioned by Wrexham County Borough Council (WCBC) in partnership with Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB), for residents aged 25 and over. It builds on what already works and is delivered with Citizens Advice Wrexham as our specialist advice partner, addressing the needs of residents across the whole of the County. Social Prescribing connects people with non-clinical support for the social, economic and environmental factors affecting their health. Our System Ready model works around the person: psychologically and trauma-informed practice; practitioners embedded in GP practices and neighbourhoods; and integrated working across health, social care and the voluntary sector. The service is non-clinical and preventative – it does not provide counselling, crisis response or clinical treatment. The new service brings more outreach into rural communities and areas of highest need, Citizens Advice integrated into the pathway, and a presence at the Wrexham Wellbeing Hub, Adult SPOA and Wrexham Maelor Hospital. We follow the nationally aligned pathway – What Matters conversation, co-produced wellbeing plan, warm handovers, review and planned closure – in line with the National Framework for Social Prescribing and the HEIW Competency Framework. Role Responsibilities: Referrals and access Receive self-referrals and professional referrals (GP practices; BCUHB teams including Wrexham Maelor, the Emergency Department and Minor Injuries Units; Adult SPOA; Adult Social Care; housing and community partners) – a ‘no wrong door’ approach. Offer pre-referral advice to professionals and keep referrers and GPs (with consent) updated, including a closure summary. Deliver support in trusted community venues and through outreach into rural communities and areas of highest deprivation with flexible, non-digital and home-visit options where appropriate and safe. Person-centred support Hold structured ‘What Matters’ conversations and co-produce strengths-based wellbeing plans. Work in a trauma-informed way within the boundaries of a non-clinical service, escalating promptly where specialist clinical, safeguarding or urgent needs are identified. Provide multi-contact support, review and planned closure, with warm handovers and supported introductions to community groups, peer support, volunteering, learning and activities. Address the wider determinants of wellbeing (housing, income, employment, transport, caring), referring to Citizens Advice for debt, benefits, housing or legal issues while retaining case ownership, and to community outreach for practical support. Promote statutory advocacy, and make reasonable adjustments for people with additional needs, including dementia, caring roles, neurodivergence, learning disability or sensory impairment. Deliver the Welsh Language Active Offer and arrange translation for other community languages where needed. Partnership and community connection Build effective relationships with GP practices and clusters, WCBC, BCUHB, AVOW, Citizens Advice and networks such as Ageing Well Wrexham and the Wrexham Poverty Action Collaborative. Use DEWIS Cymru as the primary directory of community assets and help keep it up to date. Identify gaps and share evidence so that partners can develop community-led responses (the service enables, rather than directly delivers, community activities). Promote the service across Wrexham, with a focus on seldom-heard and under-represented …

items.desc: Gloucestershire Health and Care NHS Foundation Trust are looking for experienced GPs to join the Integrated Urgent Care Service (IUCS). The overall aim of the Integrated Urgent Care Service is to provide a consult and complete model of care for people needing urgent care. The key features of the service include NHS 111, Clinical Assessment Service and Out of Hours services (face-to-face base and home visiting). The NHS 111 service will be provided by Health Advisors and Clinical Advisors hosted by our partner organisation, IC24. Where a senior clinical review is indicated, this will be completed within the Clinical Assessment Service, which will be jointly delivered by GHC Senior Clinical Leads based at Edward Jenner Court, Gloucester and remotely by IC24 CAS clinicians. The post holder will act as the Senior Clinical Lead for CAS and be part of the rota covering the service 24/7. This role is offered on a permanent basis. We currently have a range of hours and shifts available during the week and at weekends, between 08:00-00:00. These can be offered as a fixed pattern. Please note that enhancements are offered, please see attached, for out of hours working and any CAS Senior Lead hours attract 3% if salaried before the enhancements are then added. For any bank hours you will see the different rates attached for the two types of roles. The qualification, training & experience requirements for the role are underlined in the Job Description/Person Specification. The postholder will work collaboratively with the service team and have oversight of all clinical queues across the IUCS pathway to direct patients without delay to the correct parts of the urgent care system utilising the Gloucestershire Directory of Service. The Senior Clinical Lead will provide support and guidance to all colleagues across the service ensuring everyone is confident and supported to work to the top of their license. As a GP working within the service they will use their clinical expertise and professional knowledge to assess and manage patients as part of clinical telephone triage, working as part of a multi-disciplinary team to deliver high quality and patient centred service when in hours General Practice is closed. Where required and available, the CAS will have access to direct booking into the Out of Hours bases and Home visiting service and work closely with other community services within GHC such as Minor Injury and Illness Units, Rapid Response and Evening and Overnight District Nursing. The CAS will provide an enhanced assessment supported by the NHS Pathways Clinical Consultation Support (PaCCS) module to identify clinical need/risk. It will also oversee and take actions relating to any abnormal urgent pathology results communicated by Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHFT) Pathology Service during the OOH period. We have a skilled and dedicated workforce of over 5000 colleagues working in a diverse range of services over 55 sites and within people’s homes. We strive to enable a welcoming workplace culture that builds and celebrates civility, inclusivity and diversity, while providing a sense of belonging and trust. Annual staff surveys, regular Pulse surveys and other engagement opportunities provide our people with lots of opportunity to tell us about their experiences of working with us. In the latest staff survey, 61% of colleagues gave us their views. It was great to hear that: 72% of colleagues would recommend the Trust as a place to work, ranking us 1st for Provider Trusts in the South West region on this question. 76% would recommend the standard of care provided in our services if a friend or relative needed treatment, also ranking us 1st in the South West region. 81% said that care of patients and service users is the Trust’s priority, compared with an average in comparable NHS Trusts in England of 64%. This high-level overview shows we are in a healthy position, with higher scores than average for comparable organisations, alongside a great response rate, indicating good staff engagement. However, we also know we have plenty of room for improvement in many areas. To that end, we continue to prioritise and invest in our commitment to genuinely becoming a Great Place to Work with consistent top-quartile performance in the annual staff survey and Pulse surveys. Come and work for us! We are delighted to be able to offer a Band 6 Mental Health practitioner post to a dynamic and caring professional with a passion for working with children and families. This is a 30 hours per week, permanent post based in the Havant & Petersfield CAMHS team. We are a warm and compassionate multi-disciplinary team who are united in the commitment to provide the highest quality care to the children, young people and families using our service. HIOW CAMHS is currently undergoing an exciting transformation so that we are better able to meet the mental health needs of our communities going forward, and you will be an active part of this process. They will have a robust knowledge of evidence based therapeutic interventions relevant to the care group including education, clinical care, wellness recovery action plans and discharge planning. Our mental health services include community-based support and early intervention in psychosis (EIP) for both adults and young people, alongside a network of specialist inpatient wards covering forensic, learning disability, eating disorder and older person's care. We deliver extensive physical health services too, from urgent community response teams helping frail and older patients remain safely at home, to hospitals at home teams providing acute-level care in familiar surroundings. Our neurological services offer rehabilitation and treatment for conditions including Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's Disease, Motor Neurone Disease, Head Injury, Cerebral Palsy and Stroke. Across Hampshire, our community hospitals provide inpatient rehabilitation as a step down from acute care, and our dedicated teams also staff Treetops Sexual Assault Referral Centre in Portsmouth, offering expert, compassionate support. items.desc: As the Booking Coordinator, your responsibilities will include booking of new/follow up appointments and clinics for various specialties within local and national booking guidelines. You will be responsible for delivering an excellent customer service to patients whilst showing empathy and understanding to their situation. On a daily basis, you will be using your great communication skills by liaising with outpatient reception teams, secretaries and other internal stakeholders in the hospital. You will be able to work in a calm, logical and methodical way and be able to multi-task on a variety of different urgent queries. You will be familiar with the data protection act and responsible for maintaining patient confidentiality. The department works in line with a number of the government targets around patient waiting time and would suit someone who is familiar with challenging but rewarding targets. To perform role of an Outpatient Booking Coordinator, ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of the appointments centre; making and rescheduling appointments for patients according to available clinic capacity, dealing efficiently with all enquiries from staff, referring practitioners, patients and other health service organisations. Ensuring full utilisation of all available outpatient clinic slots and liaising with key internal stakeholders to raise concerns when patients cannot be booked an appointment within a timely manner. The post holder should have the ability to manage and prioritise their workload whilst being able to work under pressure, and have the ability to communicate with staff at all levels. Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us. We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients’ homes across Guildford and Waverley. items.desc: Are you passionate about developing nursing practice? Do you love helping others reach their full potential? If so we want to hear from you! An exciting opportunity has arisen within The Private Care Division at the Royal Marsden, for a part time (30h/week) band 7 Clinical Practice Educator in medical and surgical oncology field. The post holder will work alongside with the Charge Nurses of different departments (Markus ward, Granard House wards and Private Day Surgery) to support the full development of the nursing staff . As part of our private care team, it is expected that the candidate will work alongside others Private Care Clinical Practice Educators to support nursing staff across all our areas. The candidate is also expected to closely work with the RMH Clinical Education Team. The successful candidate should have considerable experience in Oncology nursing, at medical and surgical level, as well as in practice-based teaching at least at a senior staff nurse level and a post registration qualification in Oncology or another relevant speciality. The post holder will demonstrate safe, clinical decision-making and expert care, whilst acting within professional boundaries and supporting the delivery of Trust policy and procedures. The post holder will be responsible for delivering a high-quality evidence based education to staff within Private Care areas as inpatient wards and day areas. This will include supporting the education and training of nurses to become clinically competent in the care of cancer patients, facilitate the induction, clinical mandatory updates, and continuing professional development for all levels of nursing. The post holder will also be responsible for promoting high standards of care through the demonstration of clinical expertise and the creation of a clinical environment that encourages learning and professional development. The post holder will also work closely with the Charge Nurse of the departments to foster a supportive working environment and maintain staff morale. The post holder will work closely with the Trust Lead Nurse for Clinical Education and support the training at Trust level for all staff working across Trust. In addition, the post holder will support the Ward Sisters / Charge Nurses and the Medical Devices Coordinator with the Monitoring and review of staff compliance with medical devices and mandatory training. The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust is a world-leading cancer centre. Our role is to offer our patients the best cancer care available anywhere in the world, and to continue to make a global contribution to finding better ways of diagnosing and treating cancer. We employ over 4,500 staff in a diverse range of careers including nursing, medical, science, radiography, pharmacy, occupational therapy, finance and administrative services. We have two hospitals – one in Chelsea, London, and one in Sutton, Surrey – as well as a Medical Daycare Unit in Kingston Hospital. At The Royal Marsden, we deal with cancer every day, so we understand how valuable life is. When people entrust their lives to us, they have the right to demand the very best. That's why the pursuit of excellence lies at the heart of everything we do. At the heart of the hospital is our dedicated team. We offer a stimulating and dynamic working environment, a wide range of staff benefits, learning and development opportunities and clear career pathways. There are opportunities to work flexibly across a range of areas and specialities and we welcome flexible working requests from point of hire to support employees work life balance. We are looking for employees who aspire to excellence, share our values and can play a crucial role in our on-going achievements. We are growing aggressively as we look towards 2030. Our Business Consulting team is focused on speeding drug development, launching treatments more effectively, and shaping the best engagement for our customers. We are seeking great people to help shape the future of the industry with the world’s leading software, data, AI, and expertise at their back. The Role We are hiring recent university graduates to grow the next generation of consultants through our Business Consultant Development Program (BCDP). We believe in pushing high potential people to achieve excellence. Our program is specifically designed to provide a challenging environment to learn quickly and deliver value early. You will collaborate with experienced team members on customer-facing engagements to create high-impact business solutions. In our structured 20 month program, we equip you with the resources to develop the core consulting skills, deep domain expertise, and leadership foundation for long-term career success at Veeva. BCDP spans five core practice areas: Analytics, Commercial, Content, R&D, and Quality. As an Associate Consultant you will align to one of those practices, allowing you to build targeted industry expertise. You will be asked to choose your preferred practice in the application process. You can learn more about our practices and the work we do here. The anticipated start date is September 2027. What You'll Do Support and deliver all components of customer engagements (e.g., customer communications, workshops, stakeholder interviews, process and data analysis, managing timelines) Collaborate with Business Consultants to create deliverables that optimize customer operating and engagement models, processes, and business performance Leverage Veeva’s software and data to pull through tangible business and operational solutions REQUIREMENTS | We are looking for graduates who meet the following requirements: Desire to work within an intense, challenging program and environment Excellent verbal and written communication skills A process-driven person who loves digging into operations, numbers, and other data to find opportunities for improvement Upcoming 2027 university graduate with strong academic performance Fluent in written and spoken English High work ethic. Veeva is a hard-working company High integrity and honesty. Veeva is a PBC and a “do the right thing” company, and we expect that from all employees Willingness to travel up to 20% of your time per year. Travel varies per customer engagement, coworking, internal meetings, and events with your team Explore More Generation Veeva Roles: We welcome you to apply to all roles that align with your skills and interests. See all open opportunities here: Generation Veeva Careers THE PROCESS | Our process is different than most. It is designed to be fast, efficient and respectful. Here are the steps: Application: You submit your resume, short cover letter of questions, and take a personality test. Within one week we will notify you via email if we would like to move you to the next stage Leader Interview: The next step is an interview with a leader of the practice Case Exercise: If we proceed, you will be invited to complete a case exercise within a week Offer: Within one week after completing your case exercise, we will extend you an offer or let you know that we do not wish to move forward. You will have two weeks to make your final decision. If you accept, we will hold a spot for you and expect you to show up on your start date. Accepting an offer and continuing to interview would be an ethical violation in our view Compensation Starting Salary: 45,000 GBP After one year, if you perform well, you will receive a significant salary increase and be granted equity Work Authorization: Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United Kingdom. Veeva is unable to provide sponsorship for employment visas for this position. Work Environment: Veeva is a Work Anywhere company. You can choose to work in an office or remotely from home on any given day of the week - it’s up to you! Although Veeva is Work from Anywhere, Associate Business Consultants must live within a maximum commuting distance of 45 minutes to 1 hour from Veeva’s London Office. #LI-Hybrid #LI-Entry Veeva is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender …

items.title: Community Matron
items.card: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Community Matron to join our Community Nursing Teams across North Northumberland; the Community Matron will be responsible for identification of vulnerable patients who are at risk and also those frequently admitted to hospital by proactive case management working with Specialist Nurses, Medical colleagues, Palliative Care, Intermediate Care, Social Care and AHPs, the aim is
items.desc: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Community Matron to join our Community Nursing Teams across North Northumberland; the Community Matron will be responsible for identification of vulnerable patients who are at risk and also those frequently admitted to hospital by proactive case management working with Specialist Nurses, Medical colleagues, Palliative Care, Intermediate Care, Social Care and AHPs, the aim is to reduce admissions and improve quality of life. They will provide support into the care homes. Northumbria Healthcare Trust are committed to lifelong learning and offer support to enhance your knowledge and skills, to role model compassionate and inclusive leadership in order to shape the creation of a collective leadership culture within the trust. This means demonstrating a consistent leadership style which (a) engages, enables and empowers others (b) uses coaching to promote ownership of learning and quality improvement and (c) facilitates team working and collaboration within teams / departments and across organisational boundaries. Please note we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the closing date once the required number of suitable applications have been received. The Community Matron undertakes advanced clinical assessment, identifying needs, planning, case management and coordinating of care for patients with highly complex needs and co- existing long term conditions, working in partnership with other professionals and agencies to improve patient outcomes. The post holder will provide clinical leadership for staff within the Community Nursing service, supporting the development of staff roles with regular training and supervision and will contribute to the assessment of competence for registered and non registered staff. We manage three major locality hospitals at North Tyneside, Wansbeck and Hexham, plus a number of smaller community hospitals and clinics from Tynemouth to Berwick on Tweed, covering one of the largest geographical areas of any NHS trust in the country. Leading in innovation and quality – opening a state of the art Northumbria Specialist Emergency Care Hospital, the first of its kind in England. Do you want to work in one of the best performing NHS organisations in England? Work in an organisation that supports its staff and focuses on staff experience as much as it does the experience of its patients? You can live and breathe in an area that has the cleanest air, cost effective living, great nightlife, some of the best schools with a wealth of history available on your doorstep. Sound too good to be true? Well it isn’t, this is what you get when you work for Northumbria Healthcare, this is the Northumbria Way! Please read ‘applicant guidance notes’ before submitting your application. To clinically supervise and demonstrate specialist community healthcare knowledge and skills to develop the skill set of community nursing staff, students, patients and carers within a cluster of community teams. To role model compassionate and inclusive leadership where team members are supported to work and develop clinical practice across all localities acting as joint supervisors to all Nurse Practitioners where needed. The post-holder will undertake advanced clinical assessment, needs identification, planning, case management and co-ordination of care for individuals with highly complex needs and co-existing long-term conditions. The post-holder will work towards advanced professional practice including advanced clinical skills, medicines management, leadership, supporting self-care management and forge interagency and partnership working to improve outcomes for patients with co-existing long-term conditions. In addition, the post-holder will work proactively to reduce unplanned hospital admissions and facilitate earlier discharge from hospital for patients identified through multi-disciplinary team meetings, high risk patient programmes or proactive care management. To role model compassionate and inclusive leadership in order to shape the creation of a collective leadership culture within the trust. This means demonstrating a consistent leadership style which (a) engages, enables and empowers others (b) uses coaching to promote ownership of learning and quality improvement and (c) facilitates team working and collaboration within teams / departments and across organisational boundaries.

items.desc: About the Role: Grade Level (for internal use): 11 The Team: Product Platform Design (PPD) is responsible for the design, build, and evolution of SPDJI’s core product platforms that support index creation, calculation, rebalance, analytics, and distribution. PPD operates using a product-led, service-based delivery model and is organised into value streams aligned to major business domains. The team works closely with Index Management, R&D, Operations, and Technology to deliver scalable, reusable platforms that support the full index lifecycle across asset classes. This role sits within the Equity value stream and will focus on the data functionality embedded within T3, SPDJI’s core equity index calculation platform. T3 supports key parts of the index lifecycle, including corporate actions, data capture, validation, transformation, and rebalance implementation. The team is evolving its platforms to improve automation, simplify legacy processes, and align with the broader Data Platforms strategy where appropriate. This creates an opportunity for a Product Owner / Business Analyst who can connect business needs, data dependencies, operational workflows, and technology delivery in a practical and structured way. The Impact: We are recruiting a Technical Product Owner – Equity Calculation on a 12 month fixed term contract to help shape and deliver enhancements across equity index calculation and related data capabilities. This is a hybrid Product Owner / Business Analyst role, working closely with the Value Stream Lead and agile delivery teams to define priorities, translate requirements, and support delivery of platform improvements. The successful candidate will play a significant role in improving efficiency within the equity index calculation domain by using product ownership, business analysis, and analytical judgement to simplify complex workflows, improve data quality, and support more scalable platform delivery. This role requires someone who can work with incomplete or evolving information, identify practical options, and communicate complex topics clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. The individual will also be expected to build strong relationships across PPD, Index Management, R&D, Operations, Technology, and Data Platform teams, influencing peers and immediate leadership to achieve defined goals. Responsibilities: Partner with the Value Stream Lead on roadmap input, prioritisation, and delivery planning. Gather, analyse, and translate business requirements into epics, features, user stories, and clear acceptance criteria. Own and manage the agile team backlog in Azure DevOps (ADO), ensuring work is clearly defined, prioritised, and ready for delivery. Work closely with Index Management, R&D, Operations, Technology, and Data Platform teams to understand requirements, dependencies, and delivery impacts. Act as a translator between business and technology teams, tailoring communication for different audiences and simplifying complex information. Support agile ceremonies, including refinement, planning, reviews, and retrospectives. Perform hands-on user acceptance testing (UAT) to confirm delivered functionality meets business requirements. Assess embedded and legacy data processes within T3 and identify opportunities to improve automation, reduce manual effort, and simplify operational workflows. Use analytical judgement to evaluate different solution options, make recommendations, and influence stakeholder buy-in based on business value, risk, and delivery impact. Identify cross-platform dependencies and collaborate with other Product Owners across PPD to support alignment and avoid fragmented ownership. Support longer-term platform evolution while balancing short-term operational stability and business continuity. Contribute professional expertise to help improve team knowledge, support junior colleagues where appropriate, and model S&P Global’s purpose and values in day-to-day work. All employees are required to work from the office a minimum of 2 days per week. What We’re Looking For: Basic Required Qualifications: Experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, or hybrid PO/BA in an agile environment. Strong understanding of index products, index calculation workflows, and operational processes. Experience working with data-heavy platforms, workflows, or systems where data ingestion, validation, transformation, and quality are important to business outcomes. Comfortable engaging in technical discussions and translating complex requirements into clear, actionable delivery items. Experience managing backlogs using ADO or equivalent tools. Strong analytical skills, with the ability to assess requirements, identify dependencies, and recommend practical solutions. Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build relationships across teams and influence peers and immediate leadership. Ability to work effectively with incomplete, changing, or conflicting information …

items.desc: Are you organised, proactive, and passionate about delivering excellent support services? Do you enjoy building relationships, solving problems, and helping services run smoothly behind the scenes? We're looking for a Medical Workforce Advisor – Rotas & Compliance to join our friendly and supportive Medical Workforce team. In this varied and rewarding role, you'll play a key part in ensuring our resident doctors are effectively rostered, supported, and compliant with national contractual and regulatory requirements. Working closely with doctors, managers, rota coordinators, and senior stakeholders, you'll help maintain safe staffing arrangements while providing expert advice on rota management, exception reporting, workforce systems, and compliance processes. Managing and maintaining resident doctor rotas and work schedules. Supporting compliance with Working Time Regulations and national Terms and Conditions. Acting as a key contact for exception reporting and rota compliance queries. Providing training, guidance, and support on rostering systems and processes. Monitoring workforce data and producing reports to support decision-making. Working collaboratively with clinical and operational teams to resolve rota issues. Supporting service improvement initiatives and the development of innovative workforce solutions. Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us. We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients’ homes across Guildford and Waverley. We work in partnership with Ashford & St Peter’s Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust through a collaborative Group Model, supporting joined-up services, workforce flexibility and development opportunities. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has rated us as Outstanding. We are proud of our achievements and continue to invest in our people and infrastructure. To learn more about life at Royal Surrey, please watch our short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R96pMboIYdo Adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. For further details on the responsibilities associated with this role, please refer to the attached job description.

items.card: you will provide visible clinical and operational leadership for our nursing teams across the Staffordshire sites of Queens Hospital Burton, Samuel Johnson and Sir Robert Peel Hospitals, ensuring the delivery of safe, effective, and responsive services. You will work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, senior clinicians, operational managers, and corporate departments to improve patient experience,
items.desc: We are seeking an experienced, compassionate, and highly motivated Outpatient Matron to lead and develop our outpatient services. This is an exciting opportunity for an inspirational nursing leader who is passionate about delivering high-quality, patient-centred care and driving continuous improvement across a diverse range of specialties. As an Outpatient Matron, you will provide visible clinical and operational leadership for our nursing teams across the Staffordshire sites of Queens Hospital Burton, Samuel Johnson and Sir Robert Peel Hospitals, ensuring the delivery of safe, effective, and responsive services. You will work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams, senior clinicians, operational managers, and corporate departments to improve patient experience, clinical outcomes, and service efficiency. We are looking for an ambitious and talented individual who is looking to take the next step in their nursing career in the NHS. This will be a demanding role with influence and impact across the sites, so it will require good stakeholder management skills via clear communications and visible leadership. You will therefore need to provide professional nursing leadership across outpatient services. Ensure the highest standards or patient safety, quality and experience. Lead service improvement initiatives. Manage clinical governance, risk management and compliance with regulatory standards. Act as a role model for professional nursing practice and leadership. You will also be joining us at a time of unprecedented change as we look to revolutionise our Outpatient Services, we are currently engaged in an ambitious improvement programme including the introduction of a new electronic patient record systems (EPR). These programs of work will allow us to become more agile and efficient in our response to change and to getting things right first time. This will require you to have experience and knowledge of effective change management tools and techniques. You will champion service improvement and support the Trust’s ambition to deliver outstanding care, whilst at the same time ensuring that the patient is at the centre of everything you do. If this sounds like just the challenge you've been looking for, then we look forward to hearing from you. For an informal discussion about this role, please contact Thamina Parveen via email thamina.parveen1@nhs.net . If shortlisted, you will be expected to visit prior to your interview. Closing date of applications: 29 October 2026 Interview date: 12 November 2026 As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together. Our fundamental Values of Compassion, Openness and Excellence underpin how we intend to work as a Trust and the associated behaviours are becoming embedded in all aspects of how we work. In return we will offer: Development opportunities, both professional and leadership development On-going support from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond. Staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes Key Facts: We see on average 4810 OP appointments a day. We are the 4 th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England – an average of 2077 per week. An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day – 3rd largest in the country. Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily. Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres. We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres. We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day. UHDB is a research active University Hospital with a large and varied portfolio of clinical trials and research opportunities for all staff. Please see attached Job description and Person Specification. To apply please click APPLY FOR THIS JOB – this link will take you to the TRAC Recruitment Site. You will need to register if you do not already have an account. UHDB is committed to fair and transparent recruitment. We welcome authentic applications that reflect your own skills, experience and motivations for the role. While we understand that candidates may use AI tools for grammar, formatting or accessibility purposes, applications that appear to be substantially AI‑generated may be subject to additional review. If this applies to your submission, we will let you know and may ask for clarification. Please ensure your application accurately represents your experience and is written in your own words.
